GTA 6's first downloadable PC port is here — ScarlettPort boots Leonida on Windows, no compiling required

By Matt

Every GTA 6 PC port until now made you build it yourself. ScarlettPort doesn't: it's a public download with its own launcher that boots the Xbox version on Windows, gets past the menus and puts you in control in the opening area — at around 20 frames per second. It's the first one anyone can actually download and run.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The GTA 6 PC port race just changed shape. Until today, every project in this saga came with homework: clone the repository, compile the build yourself, hope you got it right. ScarlettPort skips all of that. It is a public release with its own launcher — download the ZIP, run it, and the Xbox version of GTA 6 boots on Windows.

Game Rant, DSOGaming and eTeknix all reported the release on November 27, and the details line up across them. This is the first unofficial port of the game that anyone can simply download.

What ScarlettPort actually is

ScarlettPort is a compatibility layer, not a rebuilt game. It runs the Xbox Series X version of GTA 6 on a PC by translating the game's graphics code for desktop GPUs, and it ships with none of Rockstar's files — you have to supply data from your own copy of the game.

The current build, at version 0.5.3, gets through the legal screens, the menus and the save screens, then reaches the game world and hands you control of your character in the opening area. DSOGaming's breakdown of the 0.5.2 update describes lit rooms, ambient and sky lighting and full textures rendering in that opening stretch — a long way from the single-frame-at-a-time renders this saga started with earlier this week.

It also behaves like a PC game in the small ways. There is experimental mouse-and-keyboard support with mouse look, and the port reads PlayStation controllers — DualSense and DualShock 4 — directly. The launcher shows shader progress live as it builds, leaves two CPU cores free for the desktop, and can install its own updates with one click.

The catch is the frame rate

None of that makes it a good way to play GTA 6 yet. Community testing documented on the project's GitHub page puts a Radeon RX 9060 XT at a median of roughly 19 to 22 frames per second, and eTeknix's reading of open-world tests drops to around 7 frames per second away from the opening area. Game Rant's testing notes an RTX 5070 Ti averaging 12.8 frames per second in the jail sequence. The developers have not verified that the full story can even be completed this way.

So the honest summary is: it boots, it loads, you can walk around the opening — and that is the milestone. A week after launch, the barrier between PC players and Leonida is no longer "can it run at all." It is "can it run well," and that is a much shorter argument.

The warning that comes with every one of these posts

ScarlettPort's executable is not digitally signed, and that matters. Take-Two's November 24 DMCA sweep already erased one port project's entire repository network, and DSOGaming warns that torrent sites are currently full of fake GTA 6 PC downloads. An unsigned program that asks for your copy of the biggest game on Earth is exactly the shape malware hides in, and nothing about this release changes the standing advice: the leaked Xbox files circulating online were distributed without authorization, using them is piracy, and Rockstar has announced no PC version of GTA 6 at all. The game is officially a PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S title. The only official-PC timing in circulation is an unconfirmed report pointing at the first quarter of 2027.

What is verified is the trajectory, and it keeps steepening. In eight days the unofficial port went from leaked files, to a frame every couple of seconds, to rendering in-game, to a mod menu, to multiplayer in a private fork — and now to a public download with a launcher that updates itself. The takedowns are landing on schedule. The releases are landing faster.

Sources: Unofficial GTA 6 PC Port Is Now Live, No Building Required (Game Rant) · First Unofficial GTA 6 PC Port Available for Download (DSOGaming) · First Unofficial GTA VI Port Available for Download on PC (eTeknix)

Captain Price is coming to the big screen — probably: Peter Berg teases the Call of Duty movie's most famous face

By Matt

Director Peter Berg told Variety the Call of Duty movie is set in the Modern Warfare universe — and that fans can 'probably expect to see Captain Price.' Casting is just beginning, and the film hits theaters June 30, 2028.

The most famous face in Call of Duty is probably headed to the movies. Director Peter Berg, speaking to Variety while promoting his new World War II film The Mosquito Bowl, said the long-awaited Call of Duty movie is set in the Modern Warfare universe — and dropped the tease fans have been waiting for.

"We've already said that we're basing it on the 'Modern Warfare' universe," Berg said. "So you can probably expect to see Captain Price, I would think."

That is not a confirmation. It is the closest thing to one anyone has gotten. Price has been the spine of Modern Warfare since the original Call of Duty 4 in 2007, when he debuted as captain of the 22nd SAS Regiment, and he has appeared in every installment of the original trilogy and the reboot series since. He is the one character a movie version of Modern Warfare simply has to get right — and Berg just told the world he knows it.

Where the movie stands

Berg is directing and co-writing the film with Taylor Sheridan, the Yellowstone creator and Sicario writer, who is also producing. Berg called Sheridan "the best possible partner I could have in the whole world," and said Paramount chief David Ellison and Activision have been "really smart about how they want to do it."

Casting is "beginning," Berg said, with no actors announced yet. The film is slated to open in theaters on June 30, 2028. As for when fans will hear more — casting, plot, the rest of the Task Force 141 lineup — Berg put a rough clock on it: "Check in with me, I'd say, in four months."

The casting question is the whole movie

Price's most recent incarnation is Barry Sloane, who has played him through the reboot series and again in this year's Modern Warfare 4 — including the voice, the motion capture, and a face modeled closely on the actor. Fans have already been campaigning for Sloane to reprise the role on screen, and it is easy to see why: he is the version of Price an entire generation of players knows.

But nothing is settled, and Berg's wording leaves the door open for a different choice. That is the gamble of the whole project. Modern Warfare's characters are so defined by their voices and faces that recasting Price with a movie star would be felt instantly — for better or worse. Get him right and the film has instant credibility with the franchise's core audience. Get him wrong and it spends its opening weekend apologizing.

Why the timing is perfect

The movie arrives at the strongest moment the franchise has had in years. Modern Warfare 4, which released October 23, is the highest-rated Call of Duty in 15 years, according to Metacritic. The game puts Price front and center too — a vengeful captain waging a personal war from the shadows while a North Korea–South Korea conflict erupts around him. The film and the game are now selling the same character from opposite directions, and the audience for both is the same.

The adaptation was announced in late 2025, and details have been scarce ever since — the Modern Warfare setting was the main thing anyone knew for certain. Now there is a character, a casting window, and a timeline for real news. Four months from now, we should know who is wearing the boonie hat.

The Witcher 3 Remastered just got a wave of new console mods — including a fan-made expansion with a dozen quests

By Matt

Patch 5.02 is live on PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2, and its headline is the mod library: a big batch of new cross-platform mods, led by an expansion-sized quest pack.

CD Projekt Red is still feeding The Witcher 3. Patch 5.02 went live November 26 across PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2 — and while the notes are full of fixes, the real story is the mod library: more than 40 new cross-platform mods are now live in the game, with CD Projekt Red promising more on the way. Console players, who had far fewer options than PC players when the Remastered version launched at the end of September, just got the gap closed in a big way.

The Remastered edition's in-game Mods menu — powered by mod.io, free for owners of the game — lets players browse and install community creations from the main menu after linking a CD Projekt Red account. Until now, the console catalog was thin. This patch changes that.

What's in the new mod wave

The headliner is "Tales of the Witcher: Cintra," an expansion-sized mod that adds a dozen quests to the game. Around it, the new batch covers the full spread of what console modding is for: "Glowing Witcher Eyes" gives Geralt a more lore-accurate, unsettling look; there are new hairstyles for Geralt, alternative looks for Ciri, extra monster hunts, and added narrative content — plus, for the truly committed, a boat race.

It's a meaningful moment for a game that is eleven years old and still being played like it's new. The Remastered version, which launched September 29, was the first time The Witcher 3 ever had official mods on consoles. Patch 5.02 is the first real proof that CD Projekt Red intends to keep growing that catalog rather than letting it sit.

The fixes underneath

The patch is also a heavy round of repair work. Installing or uninstalling mods no longer empties merchant inventories, Geralt's inventory, or his storage — a bug that could wipe hours of progress. Outdated PC mods now get disabled with a warning instead of crashing the game with a compilation error. Merchant interaction, broken for some players, is restored.

The visual fixes read like a blooper reel: Geralt could turn bald after enabling HairWorks, grow a beard that made his head invisible with the Rabble-rouser hairstyle, or end up missing faces and body parts. All fixed. Meditating for less than a minute could send time running backwards indefinitely; that's fixed too. Photo Mode gets a round of improvements, and the game now supports 32:9 super-ultrawide displays.

Why this one matters

The Witcher 3 is in a strange, strong position: a decade-old game with a remaster that keeps getting better, a mod scene that finally reaches consoles, and a future mapped out in public. Polygon reports the Songs of the Past expansion arrives next year — about the size of the 2016 expansion Blood and Wine, and a finale to Geralt's adventures — with The Witcher 4, starring Ciri, to follow in 2028. A fan-made quest pack landing on consoles today is a decent way to spend the wait.

Sources: The Witcher 3 Remastered's Mod Library Just Got a Massive Update (Polygon) · The Witcher 3 Wild Hunt Remastered Adds 40 Cross-Platform Mods in New Patch (GosuGamers) · Patch 5.02 for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered is live! (CD Projekt Red) · Witcher 3 Remastered Patch 5.02 Fixes Mod Installs That Emptied Geralt's Inventory (Tech Times)

Arkheron is out now — the ex-Blizzard team's ten-year PvP project hits Early Access

By Matt

Bonfire Studios' team-based PvP game launched in Early Access today on Steam, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S — and everyone can play the full game free all weekend.

Ten years of work is finally playable. Arkheron, the debut game from Bonfire Studios, entered Early Access today, November 27, on Steam, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S with crossplay — and the studio is throwing the doors open: everyone can play the full game free over the opening weekend, November 27–29, no purchase needed.

Bonfire is the studio founded by Blizzard veteran Rob Pardo, the former chief creative officer behind Diablo, Overwatch, StarCraft, and World of Warcraft. Arkheron is its first game, and it launched live on the show floor at DreamHack Stockholm, with 84 PC stations running it all weekend.

What Arkheron actually is

Arkheron is a fast-paced, isometric team PvP game. Teams of three fight their way up a mysterious Tower, collecting items mid-match that reshape their builds on the fly, and taking on rival teams along the way. The pitch is Diablo-style action with a build-crafting twist: the loot you grab changes how you play, every match.

The Early Access version costs $24.99 on Steam, with a $49.99 Supporter Edition for players who want to back the studio further. Bonfire has said every Collection — its version of a battle pass — will be earnable for free during Early Access. From early 2027, the game will run in Books of about six months, each split into three roughly two-month Chapters, with the Eternal roster changing every Chapter.

How to play free this weekend

There are three ways in without paying. The opening weekend, November 27–29, is free for everyone with no limits. A free Friend Pass lets your friends join you if you own the game. And Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers get the full game in Game Preview for the first three months. Anyone who buys any edition by December 1 gets the Armored Swan Pack free.

Why this one matters

New PvP games live or die on their first weekend, and Bonfire is doing everything it can to lower the barrier: free weekend, free friends, Game Pass from day one. The pedigree is real — Pardo's team built some of the most-played games ever made — but Arkheron is an unproven new IP in a genre that chews up new arrivals. This weekend is the test: if the Tower hooks people while it's free, Bonfire has a foundation. If it doesn't, the ten-year build becomes a much harder story to tell.

Warframe: Tau has a date — December 9, and it's the biggest swing in the game's history

By Matt

Digital Extremes dated Warframe: Tau at Devstream 199: a free trip to a second star system on December 9, with a mob-run casino city, a new Warframe, and the game's first card game.

Digital Extremes finally put a date on it. At Devstream 199 today, the studio confirmed that Warframe: Tau launches December 9, 2026 — free on PC, console, and mobile — taking players to a second star system for the first time in the game's 13-year history.

Tau has lived in Warframe's lore for years, teased most heavily in the pivotal conversation in The New War. Now it's a place you can actually go. Creative Director Rebecca Ford called it "the biggest swing we could do" — and stressed that December 9 is only the start.

A second star system

Tau arrives with two regions at launch. First is Perita, a sandstorm-scoured desert home to descendants of the Dax, running six game modes — including a Survival variant with environmental hazards and an ecological system where you hunt larvae and bugs for a young scientist named Catylac. The developers' working codename for it was "Mad Max Dax," and it shows.

The headline region is Fornax, a ringed Sentient city run like a mob casino town — Digital Extremes describes the vibe as cyber Detroit crossed with Atlantic City, with Mass Effect, The Sopranos, and Boardwalk Empire among the inspirations. It's Warframe's first interconnected social hub system, with three connected hubs: the Last Bloom Lounge casino, the Manifold 90-BF industrial district, and a third hub still kept under wraps. You move between them by running bounties, launching missions from the star chart, driving the Highway Network — a car-combat mini-game where mob cars chase you down Sentient highways for resources — or taking a Night Walk, a first-person, non-combat stroll through the city with a hound at your side.

Fornax runs on a single syndicate, The Fornax Informer, a trio of newsies who know and publish everything happening in the city. At rank three, players can start detective work — collecting clues to solve a scandal at the Last Bloom Lounge for an exclusive reward. The city also has its own permanent skill-progression system, with buffs that apply in Fornax missions.

Brysko, Kullervo Prime, and a card game

The new Warframe is Brysko, the 67th frame — a Sentient Warframe brought back to life by Albrecht Entrati, silent to the world but alive in inner monologue voiced by Matthew Mercer. He fights with brass-knuckle melee, explosive playing cards, and an Exalted revolver magnum.

Kullervo Prime launches alongside Tau as the Prime Access, with increased armor and energy and two new Prime weapons: the Rauta Prime shotgun and the Vitrica Prime heavy blade. Like all Prime gear, it can be earned free through gameplay or unlocked instantly.

And Warframe is getting its first card game. Portau is a poker-style game you can play against the house, against other players, or with your squad — and a roulette game follows early next year. The mission lineup gets new flavors too: Spy returns after years away as a vault heist where you memorize codes and passwords, Mayhem is a brand-new mode about destroying the mob's property — including blowing up its limousines — and Racket sends squads to recover stolen funds and return them to extorted neighborhoods. The Tau quest itself runs roughly two hours, and the update ships with a full album of new music Ford described as "EDM meets trip hop meets acid wash."

Why this one matters

Ford's framing is the story: building a second star system took everything Digital Extremes has learned over 13 years, and the studio is treating Tau as a foundation, not a finish line. It lands right after the Epoch Operation: Taubound — which ended with the Infested home world Eris being consumed, and which the studio says was the most participated-in event in Warframe's history. The Infested get their response in 2027, when the developers plan a deep dive back in the Origin System.

The game now counts more than 90 million players, and it's nominated for Best Community Support at The Game Awards. Watch Geoff Keighley's show on December 10 for 30 minutes with a linked Twitch account and you get a free Caliban. December 9 is twelve days away. The Tenno are leaving the Origin System.

NFL · Nov 27, 2026 · 7:11 PM ET

No Rodgers, no problem: Steelers crush Broncos

By The Stat Line

T.J. Watt and Jalen Ramsey each scored a defensive touchdown as Pittsburgh routed Denver 27-5 on Black Friday — the Steelers' first game since releasing Aaron Rodgers.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The Pittsburgh Steelers capped the wildest week of their season with a 27-5 rout of the Denver Broncos on Black Friday at Acrisure Stadium, winning their first game since releasing Aaron Rodgers — and they barely needed their offense to do it.

Mason Rudolph started in Rodgers' place and played safe, mistake-free football. The defense did the rest, scoring twice off Bo Nix turnovers while holding Denver out of the end zone all afternoon in the rain.

The defense scored twice

The tone was set on Denver's second possession. Nix dropped back under heavy pressure from T.J. Watt and Nick Herbig, the ball slipped out of his hand as he was sacked in the end zone, and Watt fell on it for the first touchdown of the game at 6:03 of the first quarter.

Rudolph then directed a quick 85-yard drive — rookie Germie Bernard turning a crossing route into a 58-yard catch-and-run — and lofted a back-shoulder fade to DK Metcalf for a 22-yard touchdown with 1:40 left in the first. It was Pittsburgh's first 14-0 first-quarter lead since 2019.

Denver's only points came on a safety and a field goal. Alex Singleton blew up a run and dropped Jaylen Warren in the end zone at 11:14 of the second quarter, and Wil Lutz's 44-yarder cut the lead to 14-5. Chris Boswell answered with a 47-yard field goal, and 18 seconds later Ramsey stepped in front of a Nix pass and weaved 36 yards down the left sideline for a 24-5 halftime lead. Boswell's 33-yarder in the fourth closed the scoring.

Q1, 6:03: T.J. Watt recovers Nix fumble in the end zone; PIT 7-0

Q1, 1:40: Rudolph 22-yard TD pass to DK Metcalf; PIT 14-0

Q2, 11:14: Alex Singleton safety (Warren tackled in end zone); PIT 14-2

Q2, 5:10: Wil Lutz 44-yard field goal; PIT 14-5

Q2, 1:55: Chris Boswell 47-yard field goal; PIT 17-5

Q2, 1:33: Jalen Ramsey 36-yard interception return; PIT 24-5

Q4, 11:19: Chris Boswell 33-yard field goal; PIT 27-5

Rudolph did what was asked

Rudolph completed 9 of 15 passes for 142 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions, good for a 113.8 passer rating. Pittsburgh took a conservative approach early, running on eight of its first 11 plays, and never asked its backup quarterback to win the game on his own.

Metcalf finished with three catches for 36 yards and the score, his leaping grab at the goal line standing as the game's only offensive touchdown. Rico Dowdle added 71 yards on 11 carries.

Nix had his worst day as a pro

Nix completed 22 of 40 passes for 169 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions — Ramsey's pick-six and a second one by Daylen Everette — and was sacked three times. Denver managed just 205 total yards and never reached the end zone.

The loss ends the Broncos' six-game winning streak and drops them to 8-3, raising questions about how far they can go with Nix at quarterback after a game in which the offense never found any rhythm.

What it means

Pittsburgh improves to 7-4 and snaps a two-game skid, with the losses to Cincinnati and Philadelphia that set the stage for Rodgers' exit now firmly behind them. The Steelers played with an energy that had been missing in those two defeats, and they did it less than 48 hours after the franchise removed the signs and pictures of No. 8 around Acrisure Stadium.

It was the first game of a difficult stretch that includes meetings with Houston and Jacksonville. If the defense plays like this, the post-Rodgers Steelers look like a playoff team.

NHL · Nov 27, 2026 · 6:18 PM ET

Linus Ullmark just did something no goalie in NHL history has ever done — twice

By Matt

Linus Ullmark stopped 18 shots in Ottawa's 6-2 win over Tampa Bay on Friday, improving to 13-2 on the season — and becoming the first goaltender in NHL history to win at least 13 of his first 15 games in a season multiple times.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Nobody has ever done it twice. Now somebody has.

Linus Ullmark stopped 18 shots in the Ottawa Senators' 6-2 win over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Friday, and with the win he became the first goaltender in NHL history to win at least 13 of his first 15 games in a season multiple times.

Read that again. Not the first to do it once. The first to do it twice.

Ullmark has allowed two or fewer goals in 13 of his 15 starts this season. The Senators are rolling behind him, and the rest of the Atlantic is now chasing a team with a five-point lead at the top of the division.

He did this before — in his Vezina season

The reason the record says "multiple times" is that Ullmark already did this once. He started 13-1-0 through 15 games in 2022-23 with the Boston Bruins — the season he won the Vezina Trophy as the league's best goaltender, finishing 40-6-1 with a 1.89 goals-against average.

That was supposed to be the career year. The once-in-a-lifetime start. Three seasons later, in a different uniform, he has matched it — and now he owns the only repeat in league history.

Ullmark entered Friday at 12-2-0 with a 1.63 goals-against average and a .935 save percentage across 14 appearances. Wednesday had been the one crack in the armor: he surrendered four goals for the first time all season in a 5-3 loss to the Florida Panthers. Friday was the answer — 18 saves, two goals against, and a place in the record book that nobody else has ever reached twice.

The night in Tampa

Ottawa scored on its first shot of the game and never looked back. Ridly Greig opened the scoring at 3:37 of the first period with a side-angle shot from outside the left circle, and Tim Stutzle finished off a Michael Amadio pass for a short-handed goal at 12:47 to make it 2-0.

Amadio made it 3-0 at 6:20 of the second period, and Stutzle grabbed a rebound on an odd-man rush at 17:37 to make it 4-0. Artem Zub — scoring for the first time this season — and Claude Giroux scored 1:38 apart early in the third to stretch it to 6-0 before Jake Guentzel got Tampa Bay on the board twice.

Stutzle scored twice to bring his team-leading goal total to 15. Amadio finished with a goal and two assists, and Greig and Giroux each had a goal and an assist.

Tampa Bay, meanwhile, is sliding. The Lightning have lost three consecutive games in regulation and finished a six-game homestand 2-4 — after starting the season with eight consecutive wins at home. Dennis Hildeby stopped 15 of 21 shots in the Tampa net. The Lightning also placed forward Pontus Holmberg on injured reserve with a lower-body injury that will keep him out four weeks, while Ottawa welcomed back Andre Burakovsky after a 12-game absence.

What it means for Ottawa

The Senators have now won six of their last eight and opened up a five-point lead at the top of the Atlantic Division standings. They suffered their first regulation loss since November 1 on Wednesday in Florida. Friday was the response.

And the response came from the same place it has come from all season: the crease. Ullmark is 33 years old, in his second season in Ottawa, and playing the best hockey of his life — again.

The first time he started a season like this, he won the Vezina. The second time, he made history no other goalie has ever made. The question now is what the third act looks like — because nobody in NHL history has ever had to answer that one before.

UFC · Nov 27, 2026 · 5:45 PM ET

Cody Garbrandt says his UFC farewell is set — one last fight in Cleveland on Feb. 13

By The Stat Line

Former bantamweight champion Cody Garbrandt told MMA Junkie his Feb. 13 fight in Cleveland will be his last in the UFC — twelve years after he debuted, and with one fight left on his deal.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Cody Garbrandt is picking his ending. The former UFC bantamweight champion told MMA Junkie on Friday that he plans to fight one last time in the UFC — at UFC Fight Night 299 in Cleveland on Feb. 13, 2027 — and then walk away from the promotion for good.

"We're looking for February in Cleveland. No opponent yet, but that looks to be the date and my farewell from the UFC. It's bittersweet," Garbrandt said.

The plan

Garbrandt has one fight left on his UFC contract, and he has already talked with matchmaker Sean Shelby about filling it on the Cleveland card at Rocket Arena in his home state of Ohio. No opponent has been confirmed, and his place on the card has not been made official yet. The event is headlined by Joe Pyfer vs. Bo Nickal.

The 35-year-old's record stands at 15-8 in MMA, 10-8 inside the octagon.

Why now

Garbrandt framed the decision around family and timing. He has a 10-month-old daughter and an 8-year-old son, and his wife is expecting their third child in February — the same month as the planned farewell.

"At the end of the day, I competed at the highest level, became a world champion and I wasn't supposed to make it this far in life and where I'm at. I'm OK with it," he said. "You can't fight forever."

The run

Garbrandt debuted in the UFC as an undefeated fighter in January 2015 and climbed to the bantamweight title in under two years — a rise he still measures himself against. "A lot of people spend their whole career chasing what I was able to accomplish in under two years in the UFC," he said.

The back half of his run was harder. His most recent fight was a first-round TKO loss to Adrian Yanez at UFC 329 in July, and he has not fought since. His dream final opponent, he said, is a third fight with longtime rival T.J. Dillashaw — though he acknowledged that fairytale endings don't always happen.

What's next

Garbrandt is not leaving combat sports entirely. He makes his Real American Freestyle wrestling debut on Saturday at RAF 15 in Chicago, facing former Bellator titleholder Sergio Pettis — and wrestling, his first sport, is where he sees his future.

"I would love to jump in and wrestle as much as I can. It was my first love and the first sport I did," he said. "There's some unfinished business I want to do in wrestling, and I'll want to compete until I can't anymore."

He left the door slightly open on fighting MMA again outside the UFC, but he was clear about the direction: "I don't see myself really wanting to compete any more after that."

What it means

Twelve years after he arrived as an undefeated prospect, Garbrandt is choosing to close his UFC chapter on his own terms, at home in Ohio, with a third child on the way. The opponent is still to be determined — but the date, and the decision, are set.

MLB · Nov 27, 2026 · 5:17 PM ET

Jazz Chisholm Jr. is a Blue Jay — one year, $20 million, and a $40 million option behind it

By Matt

Toronto adds the first big-name second baseman of the offseason on a bet-on-himself deal — and takes him from the Yankees in the process.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The deal

The Blue Jays are in agreement with Jazz Chisholm Jr. on a one-year contract that guarantees him $20 million, FanSided's Robert Murray first reported, with ESPN's Jeff Passan first with the terms and MLB.com's Mark Feinsand, The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and the New York Post's Jon Heyman all confirming the structure. The guarantee breaks down as a $6 million signing bonus and a $12.5 million salary for 2027, plus a $1.5 million buyout. Chisholm holds a $16 million player option for 2028; if he declines it, the option converts to a $40 million club option for Toronto. Exercising the player option locks in $34.5 million over two years; the club option would take it to $58.5 million.

The Yankees never made it a contest. They declined to extend Chisholm the $23.15 million qualifying offer, so Toronto signs him without losing a draft pick — and the team that let him walk watches him land with a division rival.

The player

Chisholm is 28 and turns 29 in February, a two-time All-Star who has spent seven big-league seasons putting up one of the strangest profiles in baseball: huge tools, huge variance.

The ceiling showed up in 2025, his first full year in the Bronx. He hit 31 homers, stole 30 bases and posted an .813 OPS across 130 games, good for 4.1 WAR — the second All-Star berth of his career. Then came the platform year. In 2026 he hit 19 homers with 55 RBIs and 41 stolen bases, but his OPS fell to .711 over 137 games, just below league average. The career line sits at .245/.315/.444 with 14.3 WAR.

He is also the first major free-agent second baseman to sign this offseason, and he did not lack for suitors — the Nationals and Padres were both reportedly in the mix before Toronto closed it. The market clearly priced him as a rebound candidate, and the structure of the deal says Chisholm agrees with that read: take the one-year guarantee, bet on the 2025 version showing up again, and hit the market at 30 with a much bigger number attached.

The fit

Toronto needs him everywhere, which is the point. The Jays stumbled to a 79-83 finish in 2026, a year after reaching Game 7 of the World Series, and the lineup was the problem as much as the rotation. Shortly after the season, general manager Ross Atkins told Toronto media that second baseman Ernie Clement — a 2025 playoff hero and a 2026 All-Star — would have to earn an everyday role in 2027. That was the opening, and Chisholm walks straight through it.

He settled in at second base with the Yankees over the past two seasons after struggling defensively at third in 2024, and he has also played shortstop and center field in his career. The Jays have questions at all of those spots: they traded Daulton Varsho out of center field, Addison Barger missed almost all of 2026 injured, and Brett Bateman's late-season audition in center was encouraging without being definitive. Chisholm gives them a starter at second and a fallback in center, with the speed to change a game from either spot — 41 steals in a down year is not a fluke, it is who he is.

What it means

This is the second big swing of Toronto's week, three days after the club landed Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, and it follows the same logic: buy the upside before the market catches up. The Jays get the 2025 version of Chisholm at one-year money with a club option behind it — if he repeats last season, they can walk away for the price of the buyout; if he repeats 2025, they hold a $40 million option on a 29-year-old entering his prime. Chisholm gets a full-time job in a lineup that needs his bat, a ballpark where his pull power plays, and a clean shot at free agency again next winter.

There is a clock on all of it. The collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, with a lockout expected to freeze player movement the moment it does — which is why the Jays are closing deals on a holiday weekend instead of waiting for the winter meetings. Toronto has now added a front-line starter and a starting second baseman in four days. The team that lost the World Series in seven games a year ago is not waiting around to find out whether the window is still open.

NHL · Nov 27, 2026 · 5:09 PM ET

Devils extinguish Flames in comeback

By The Stat Line

Jack Hughes piled up four points and his brother Luke scored twice as New Jersey erased a third-period deficit to beat Calgary on Black Friday.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Jack Hughes willed the New Jersey Devils past the Calgary Flames on Black Friday afternoon, finishing with a goal and three assists as New Jersey scored three unanswered goals in the third period to win 5-3 at Prudential Center in Newark.

The Devils trailed 3-2 entering the final frame and erased a pair of deficits on the day. It was their third straight win — and their league-leading 10th comeback victory of the season.

The Hughes brothers ran the show

Jack Hughes' night was the seventh four-plus-point game of his career, and the fourth of those to come in calendar year 2026. His brother Luke scored twice, including the empty-netter that sealed it, and the pair combined for six points and three goals.

Luke opened the scoring burst for New Jersey less than a minute into the second period, carrying the puck from the blue line to the left dot and picking the top far corner over Devin Cooley's glove. That was his eighth goal of the season, tying his brother Quinn for fourth-most by a defenseman in the NHL.

Twelve seconds later, Timo Meier buried a backdoor feed from Jack Hughes into a vacant cage — the fastest two goals of the season for New Jersey, flipping a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead in the opening 68 seconds of the period.

Meier makes Swiss history

Meier's tally was the 249th of his career, making him Switzerland's all-time leading goal scorer in the NHL. He passed Nino Niederreiter, who sits at 248 — and who faces the Devils on Saturday.

How the third period turned

Calgary had reclaimed the lead before the second intermission. Matt Coronato tied it at 2-2, then Zach Whitecloud's rising wrister beat Jake Allen late in the period to put the Flames up 3-2.

Jack Hughes answered midway through the third with the goal of the game. He collected a pass in the neutral zone, sped around Whitecloud one-on-one, fell to one knee in the slot, and still got a shot off from a bad angle as his momentum carried him across the crease.

> "Not how I wanted to play the 1-on-1. (Whitecloud) gave me some gap because was on the ice, so I got around him. The second part, I don't really know." — Jack Hughes

With under four minutes to play, Connor Brown gave New Jersey the lead for good, poking home a loose puck at the crease after a pretty passing sequence between Jack Hughes and Meier. Luke Hughes added the empty-netter with 11 seconds left.

The win was nearly undone late: Jonas Siegenthaler took a tripping minor with 2:22 left, and the Devils' penalty kill — already down two regular killers in Johnathan Kovacevic and Brenden Dillon — held to preserve the lead.

2nd: 0:56; Luke Hughes (NJD) — 1-1

2nd: 1:08; Timo Meier (NJD) — 2-1

2nd: —; Matt Coronato (CGY) — 2-2

3rd: 12:25 left; Jack Hughes (NJD) — 3-3

3rd: 3:58 left; Connor Brown (NJD) — 4-3

3rd: 0:11 left; Luke Hughes (NJD), empty net — 5-3

What it means

The Devils keep stacking comeback wins — ten of them now, the most in the league — and this one came with a patched-up blue line. Vladislav Kolyochonok and Anton Silayev drew in with Dillon suspended and Declan Chisholm ill, and David Rittich was recalled to back up Allen, who was making his first start in 17 days and earned his first win since Nov. 7.

For Calgary, Yegor Sharangovich had two assists against his former team in a losing effort. The Flames fall to 11-14-2.

New Jersey is right back at it Saturday night at Prudential Center, hosting Winnipeg at 7:08 p.m. ET, with Connor Hellebuyck facing his former team.

Gaming · Nov 27, 2026 · 4:50 PM ET

Stage 2 is set at the PGL Singapore Major — 100 Thieves take the last spot as NAVI, G2 and Astralis enter

By Matt

Stage 1 is done in Singapore: 100 Thieves, Imperial and Lynn Vision won the last three deciders on Friday, and the eight survivors join NAVI, G2, Astralis and five more invited teams in Stage 2 starting Saturday.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Stage 1 of the PGL Major Singapore is over, and Stage 2 has its field. 100 Thieves took the last of the eight qualifying spots on Friday, beating M80 2-1 in a 2-2 decider — Dust2 13-6, Inferno 10-13, Mirage 13-5 — to extend their first-ever Major appearance into a second stage. They needed a title at the FiRe Last Chance qualifier just to secure Europe's final invitation to Singapore, then survived two elimination series in a row to get here.

Alex "poiii" Nyholm Sundgren led the decider with a 1.28 rating and a 50-27 K-D, and Nicolai "device" Reedtz added a 1.27. For M80, the loss ends a run of four straight Majors reaching Stage 2 — they had won their first two series in Singapore, over 9z and HEROIC, before dropping three in a row.

The last three deciders

Imperial were the first of the three to go through, beating Wildcard 2-1 after a series full of swings — Dust2 13-11 on Wildcard's pick, Mirage 11-13 after Wildcard led 11-1 at the half, then Cache 13-8 to close it. Kaiky "noway" Santos was the difference with a 1.34 rating and 57 kills, and Imperial salvaged a 2-0 start that had slipped away before rallying in the decider. Wildcard finish 25th to 27th.

Lynn Vision took the second spot with the cleanest result of the day, sweeping HEROIC 2-0 — Nuke 13-11, Dust2 13-6 — behind a 1.45 rating from Junjie "EmiliaQAQ" Tang. The Chinese squad are the second Asian team through after FlyQuest's surprise 3-0 run, and the win ends HEROIC's tournament one day after HEROIC ended FaZe's season.

The eight who made it

Ninjas in Pyjamas and FlyQuest led the way at 3-0. PARIVISION, Eternal Fire and Team Liquid went through at 3-1, and Imperial, Lynn Vision and 100 Thieves all finished 3-2 after going the distance in the final round.

The names Stage 1 already claimed are the story of the week so far: FaZe went out 1-3 to HEROIC, Oleksandr "s1mple" Kostyliev's BC.Game roster — playing as GOSH — finished 0-3, and 9z, who made the playoffs in Cologne, also went home at 1-3.

Who is waiting in Stage 2

Eight invited teams enter on Saturday: FUT, Nemiga, G2, 1win — competing as THE ONE — Natus Vincere, Astralis, The MongolZ and MIBR. The opening round is all best-of-ones, starting at 05:00 CET (11 p.m. ET Friday):

• FUT vs. FlyQuest

• The MongolZ vs. Lynn Vision

• Astralis vs. Imperial

• Nemiga vs. Ninjas in Pyjamas

• G2 vs. Team Liquid

• 1win vs. Eternal Fire

• Natus Vincere vs. PARIVISION

• MIBR vs. 100 Thieves

Stage 2 runs November 28 to December 1, and the top eight move on to Stage 3 from December 2 to 6, where MOUZ, Vitality, Aurora, Spirit, BETBOOM, Falcons, FURIA and Legacy are waiting. The playoffs follow from December 10 to 13 at the Singapore Indoor Stadium, with $500,000 of the $1.25 million prize pool going to the winner. It is the second Counter-Strike Major of 2026, the first ever held in Southeast Asia, and the 25th Counter-Strike Major overall.

Collectibles · Nov 27, 2026 · 3:09 PM ET

Fans Reject Universes Beyond in Rosewater's 2026 Set Poll

By Matt

Reality Fracture won Mark Rosewater's fan poll of 2026 Magic sets in a landslide, while all four Universes Beyond sets combined barely matched the runner-up.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Magic players have spoken, and the message is loud: they want Magic to feel like Magic.

Reality Fracture won Mark Rosewater's end-of-year poll of 2026 sets on his Blogatog, taking 44.8% of the 2,695 votes cast. The next closest set, Secrets of Strixhaven, managed 15.9% — meaning the winner nearly tripled the runner-up. All four Universes Beyond sets combined barely cleared that runner-up's share.

The full results

Reality Fracture: 44.8%

Secrets of Strixhaven: 15.9%

Lorwyn Eclipsed: 15.1%

Marvel Super Heroes: 6.3%

Star Trek: 4.3%

The Hobbit: 2.5%

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: 2.2%

The three in-universe sets swept the top three spots. The four crossovers — Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Marvel Super Heroes, The Hobbit, and Star Trek — finished at the bottom of the ballot, combining for just over 15% between them. TMNT, the year's first crossover, finished dead last.

Why the winner won

Reality Fracture was the year's story set. Released October 2, it closed out the three-year Metronome arc with Jace Beleren's Echoverse — a "What If…?" take on the Multiverse where familiar characters and schools show up as twisted mirror versions of themselves. Every booster carried a character and their Echoverse counterpart, and Limited players have been praising the draft format since launch.

It was also the set fans had been asking Rosewater for for years. The "What If" concept was one of the most requested ideas in the game's history, and the design team built the whole set around making it work.

The vote matches the sales

This isn't just a poll of Blogatog regulars — the buying public agrees. Earlier this month, Rosewater revealed that the three in-universe sets of 2026 are the three top-selling in-universe sets of all time: Lorwyn Eclipsed, Secrets of Strixhaven, and Reality Fracture. Hasbro's third-quarter results added that Reality Fracture shipments exceeded expectations, with Magic revenue topping $600 million in a quarter for the first time.

That context matters because 2026 was the year Universes Beyond took over the calendar. Four of the year's seven premier sets were licensed crossovers — the most ever — and Hasbro CEO Chris Cocks has said the company is still in the "early innings" of the initiative, with crossovers planned out through the early 2030s. The poll doesn't change that strategy. But it does show the gap between what Wizards is selling and what its most engaged players actually love: the three sets built from Magic's own world took roughly 75% of the vote, the four borrowed worlds took just over 15% between them, and the rest went to a refuse-to-pick option.

The caveat is the sample. Blogatog is Rosewater's personal blog, and 2,695 votes is a small, self-selected slice of the player base — the kind of players who follow the head designer closely enough to vote in his poll. Still, the direction is hard to argue with: the set that leaned hardest into Magic's own lore won by nearly 30 points.

Gaming · Nov 27, 2026 · 2:15 PM ET

GTA 6 sold an estimated 53 million copies in its first week — $4.7 billion, and it's already the 13th best-selling game ever

By Matt

Alinea Analytics estimates Grand Theft Auto 6 sold 53 million copies in its first week on sale, for roughly $4.7 billion in revenue — a week-one total that would already put it 13th on the all-time best-sellers list, before GTA Online or a PC version even exist.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

One week in, Grand Theft Auto 6 has sold an estimated 53 million copies. That's the week-one figure from Alinea Analytics, published Friday, November 27, and it works out to roughly $4.7 billion in revenue — from a single-player game, on two consoles, with no PC version and no online mode yet.

The estimate is not an official number from Rockstar or Take-Two, and it matters to say that plainly: the only figures the publisher has confirmed are $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales and 32.5 million units sold before release. Alinea's number is an independent estimate of sell-through to players, built from its own market data. But it is consistent with everything else we've seen this week — the same firm's estimate through the launch weekend was 44.9 million, and the jump to 53 million means roughly 8 million more copies moved in the four days after that.

The PlayStation split, and why it matters

Of the estimated copies sold, 75.7% were on PlayStation 5 — about 40.1 million — with the remaining 24.3%, roughly 13 million, on Xbox Series X|S. The revenue split tilts even further toward Sony, with PS5 accounting for 76.1% of the money, a gap Alinea attributes to regional pricing.

That is the payoff of Rockstar's PlayStation marketing deal, which positioned GTA 6 as playing best on Sony's console. PlayStation does hold roughly 75% of the console market, so the split is close to proportional — but the deal still delivered, and Sony has already struck a similar arrangement with CD Projekt Red for future releases, including The Witcher 4, according to Polygon.

The Xbox share has been shrinking steadily since launch day, from 25.8% on November 21 to 24.3% now.

The comparison that puts it in perspective

GTA 5 sold 29 million copies in its entire first month. GTA 6 nearly doubled that in seven days. GTA 5 has since gone on to sell more than 230 million copies across its lifetime — a number that took thirteen years and three console generations to reach. At this pace, the conversation about whether GTA 6 catches it is a question of when, not if.

On the all-time best-sellers list, the week-one estimate would already place GTA 6 13th, ahead of games that have been selling for a decade or more.

People aren't just buying it — they're living in it

The same Alinea report found nearly 7 million players have already logged more than 50 hours in the game, with around 250,000 past 100 hours. The game has been out for eight days.

The launch also swallowed the rest of the industry whole. On PlayStation, sales of several other major releases — including 007 First Light, Resident Evil Requiem and Marvel's Wolverine — fell 34% during GTA 6's release week, though Alinea notes typical post-launch sales decay accounts for part of that drop. Call of Duty's daily active users fell 42% around the launch, from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million.

What comes next

None of this includes GTA Online, which hasn't launched yet, or a PC version, which Rockstar still hasn't announced. The unofficial PC port scene keeps making headlines — the latest is a 209GB torrent repack of the leaked Xbox build — but there's no official word on when PC players get in. Whenever those two things arrive, they'll be selling into a player base that is already tens of millions strong.

For now, the first week is done — and the next chapter, Online and PC, hasn't even started.

NHL · Nov 27, 2026 · 1:17 PM ET

Kyle Palmieri tore his other ACL — 364 days after the first one ended his season

By Matt

The Islanders announced Friday that Kyle Palmieri is out six to eight months with a torn ACL and meniscus in his right knee — the other knee from the one that ended his season last November.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The other knee

Kyle Palmieri is out for the season. Again. On the other knee.

The New York Islanders announced on Friday, November 27, that Palmieri tore the ACL and meniscus in his right knee, and he will be sidelined six to eight months. Head coach Pete DeBoer put it plainly: Palmieri is out for the regular season, and the team will see about after that.

The injury came in the second period of Monday's 4-2 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs. Palmieri got tangled with Toronto forward Easton Cowan, and his right leg caught on the goalpost. He did not return to the game, and the Islanders placed him on injured reserve the next day, listing it only as a lower-body injury.

Friday, the diagnosis came out — and it was the worst version of it.

364 days later

This is the second time in barely a year that Palmieri has torn an ACL. He tore the one in his left knee on November 28, 2025, against the Philadelphia Flyers, after colliding with defenseman Jamie Drysdale — and still recorded an assist while limping his way back to the bench before leaving the game.

That injury ended his season after 25 games. He spent the months after it grinding through rehab to get back for this season, and he did — returning to the Islanders' top line, where he had been playing alongside Bo Horvat.

DeBoer, who watched Palmieri's comeback from the other bench last season before taking over behind it, called the news heartbreaking.

"It's emotional," DeBoer said. "People don't see the work that he put in to come back from what he went through last year, in order to get to the point he got to this year. And then to have it happen like that to the other leg on such a fluky kind of thing, it's heartbreaking, emotional, all those words."

What the Islanders lose

Palmieri had nine points — four goals and five assists — in 23 games this season, a consistent presence on the top line. He is 35 years old, an alternate captain, and a veteran of 948 career games over 17 NHL seasons. He is also in the final year of his contract with the Islanders, a two-year deal worth $4.75 million per year, set to become an unrestricted free agent after this season.

The Islanders acquired him from the New Jersey Devils at the 2021 trade deadline, and he scored seven goals during that spring's run to the Stanley Cup Semifinals. Mathew Barzal, who played on a line with him during that run, called him a warrior — the kind of player who brings it every night, goes to the gritty areas, and scores around the crease.

"He brings an element that's hard to find," Barzal said. "He goes to gritty areas. He forechecks hard and he's got skill along with that and good goal scoring."

Young defenseman Matthew Schaefer said the whole room looks up to Palmieri, and that the veteran was always smiling and checking in on the team even while he was rehabbing last year's injury around the facility.

Now the Islanders will be the ones checking in on him.

"To have it happen again second in a row, it's not fair and it's not fun," Schaefer said. "I know Palms knows we're all with him, and he's gonna do the same thing again. He's gonna keep grinding, and then he's gonna keep coming back."

Two ACL tears, two knees, two seasons in a row. The first one took his season. The second one just did the same.

CoreJJ leaves Team Liquid after eight years — the end of an LCS era

By Matt

Team Liquid confirmed on Tuesday that Jo 'CoreJJ' Yong-in is leaving after eight years, seven titles and two MVP awards — ending one of the longest and most decorated runs any player has had with a single North American team.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Eight years, seven titles, and one of the defining runs in North American League of Legends is over. Team Liquid announced on Tuesday that Jo "CoreJJ" Yong-in is leaving the organization, ending a partnership that began in November 2018 and turned a Korean import into the face of the LCS.

The announcement came in a farewell video posted to Team Liquid's X account, with a message that said everything about what he meant to the org: "Eight years of leadership and dedication. You helped shape who we are today." The official LoL Esports account shared the news soon after, under the line "AFTER 8 YEARS."

What eight years looked like

CoreJJ arrived in North America already a world champion. He won the 2017 World Championship with Samsung Galaxy, then switched from AD carry to support and joined Team Liquid on November 20, 2018. He won both LCS splits in his debut season and was named Spring Split MVP — and he never really stopped winning.

Across eight seasons, CoreJJ won seven titles with Team Liquid: LCS championships in Spring and Summer 2019, Spring and Summer 2024, and Summer 2026, plus the LCS Lock-In tournament in 2021 and 2022. He was named LCS MVP a second time in Summer 2020, and he earned eight First-Team All-Pro selections — the most recent in Summer 2026, his final split with the team.

He was also the shotcaller and the steady hand. Through roster turnover, coaching changes and the league's rebrand from LCS to LTA, CoreJJ was the constant — the player Liquid built its bot lane, and often its whole identity, around.

The one thing he never got

For all the domestic dominance, the international breakthrough never came with Liquid. CoreJJ never reached the knockout stage of Worlds with the organization, despite winning the league five times. His final season told the same story: a fourth-place finish at the LCS Lock-In, a Spring Split grand final swept 3-0 by LYON, a 3-0 loss to T1 in the MSI 2026 Play-In stage, and a 1-3 Swiss-stage exit at Worlds 2026 in front of a home crowd. His last match in a Liquid jersey was the 2-1 defeat to Brazilian champions LOS that knocked North America's top seed out of the tournament.

That gap is the only blemish on the résumé — and it's the reason the departure lands the way it does. He didn't leave because he declined. He left as the reigning Summer Split champion, still playing at an All-Pro level, because after eight years the run had simply reached its end.

Where he goes next

Neither Team Liquid nor CoreJJ has said where he will play next, and Liquid has not named a replacement. The reporting, though, has been consistent for weeks: Sheep Esports reported on November 12 that CoreJJ and longtime bot-lane partner Sean "Yeon" Sung are set to join Cloud9 for the 2027 LCS season, and followed up on November 23 that Cloud9 has finalized its planned 2027 lineup, with CoreJJ and Yeon joining returning players Robert "Blaber" Huang and Park "Loki" Jong-hoon. That move has not been confirmed by either team, and Yeon's departure has not been announced either — but if it lands, Cloud9 would be getting the most proven support in the league's history, already paired with the ADC he has played beside since 2023.

Liquid, meanwhile, is reportedly turning to the team that ended its Worlds run. Sheep Esports reported on November 18 that Argentine support Gabriel "Ackerman" Aparicio — who won the 2026 CBLOL title with LOS — is set to take over as Liquid's starting support.

Eight years is an eternity in esports. Most players don't get eight years in the league, let alone eight years with one team. CoreJJ got both, won nearly everything there was to win at home, and walks out the door still at the top of his game. Wherever he lands next, the LCS just lost one of the players who defined it.

Thanksgiving Grandma story becomes a Lifetime movie

By Matt

A wrong-number Thanksgiving text in 2016 turned into a decade-long friendship — and now Wanda Dench and Jamal Hinton's story is becoming a Lifetime movie, aiming for a November 2027 release.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The announcement

Ten years after a wrong-number text turned two strangers into family, the story is becoming a movie. Wanda Dench and Jamal Hinton have signed the rights to their story to Lifetime, which is developing a dramatization under the working title The Thanksgiving Grandma. Producer Jack Leslie is aiming to start filming in early 2027, with a November 2027 release.

Hinton confirmed the deal on Instagram on November 19, writing that he was "very excited to officially be in business with Lifetime." Dench told The Arizona Republic on November 16 that the two had recently signed over the rights, and that Lifetime told them up front the film would be based on their story.

The text that started it

In November 2016, Dench meant to text her grandson an invitation to Thanksgiving dinner. He had changed his number, so the message landed on the phone of Hinton, then a 17-year-old high school student in Arizona who had never met her. When he asked who was texting, she replied, "It's your grandma."

Hinton sent back a selfie and a question that made the whole thing famous: "You're not my grandma. Can I still get a plate though?" Dench's reply — "Of course you can. That's what grandmas do… feed everyone" — turned a mix-up into an invitation. He showed up at her home in Mesa that Thanksgiving, and he has been at the table every year since.

A friendship that outlasted the viral moment

What makes the story worth a movie is everything that happened after the screenshot faded. The two stayed in each other's lives through the hard parts: Dench's husband Lonnie died in 2020, and Dench faced a breast cancer diagnosis in 2024. She is now cancer-free, and the pair still meet every year around the holiday, their families growing into each other's.

Both have put the attention to work. Hinton is developing a nonprofit called Bounce Back, focused on youth sports and skills, while Dench runs neighborhood support efforts. The film is expected to cover more than the original mix-up — how they supported each other through the losses and the diagnosis, and what a decade of showing up actually looks like.

The movie

Screenwriter Glen Dolman is writing the script and recently spent a weekend at Dench's home getting to know the pair. Production is expected to begin in early 2027, with a possible shoot in the Phoenix metro area or New Mexico. No cast has been announced.

This isn't the first screen adaptation of the story — Netflix announced its own version, The Thanksgiving Text, back in December 2021. The Lifetime film is the one moving now, with Dench and Hinton involved directly and a release targeted for next Thanksgiving.

ArcheAge Chronicles studio XLGames faces 'extensive restructuring' — and possible closure

By Matt

XLGames, the studio behind ArcheAge Chronicles, is preparing for large-scale restructuring and has told staff it must even consider going out of business — weeks after the MMO's early-access launch fell short of the sales it needed.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

XLGames is in trouble. The Korean studio behind ArcheAge Chronicles is preparing for what its own CEO calls "extensive restructuring" — and has told employees it must even consider the possibility of going out of business entirely, weeks after the MMO's early-access launch fell short of what the company needed it to be.

According to reporting from Korean outlet MTN, covered in English by Massively Overpowered, CEO Choi Kwan-ho announced the plan in a letter to staff. Complaints about the early-access launch keep coming, sales are trending downward, and layoffs are likely as the company shrinks toward what the letter calls "minimum viability" — drastically cutting business operations and keeping only essential functions and a minimal workforce. Choi also said the company will try to find additional funding so there are no disruptions to severance pay and benefits for those who leave.

"We must prepare for extensive restructuring by drastically reducing business operations and focusing on essential functions and a minimal workforce," the letter reads. "The company is currently at a critical crossroads where we must even consider the possibility of going out of business."

The launch that was supposed to save the studio

The numbers tell the story of why this happened now. ArcheAge Chronicles sold 100,000 copies in its first 10 days of release, bringing in about 4 billion KRW — just under $3 million. For most games that would be a fine start. For XLGames, a studio that had already sold off most of its flagship ArcheAge IP to stay liquid, it wasn't enough of a tailwind.

The game started life as ArcheAge 2, in development as far back as 2020, and went through a long run of delays and problems before finally reaching early access. In October, XLGames sold the ArcheAge IP and the separate ArcheAge S development business to Align Studio, a developer funded by Kakao Games, for roughly 39.2 billion KRW — a deal the company said was about securing liquidity and improving its financial structure. That effectively put the company's entire existence on Chronicles doing numbers at launch. It didn't.

The game isn't done yet

For players, the immediate picture is less bleak than the headlines. The game is still being updated — a November 25 patch raised monster gold and experience and opened a loot trade route after a shop-price cut that had angered players — and a major update is still due December 10, with the Azhra raid, a female Warrior class and the Gladius weapon, according to a November 26 letter from executive producer Yongjin Ham. The Steam page still lists an expected early-access run of nine to twelve months.

But the studio behind it is now openly talking about its own survival, and that's the part that matters. A game can keep getting updates while its developer shrinks to a skeleton crew — the question is for how long, and at what cost to the roadmap. XLGames is betting that a December update and new funding can steady the ship. The CEO's own letter says the alternative is on the table.

GTA 6 has a second story softlock — Raul never calls Lucia, and the fix starts with a jewelry job

By Matt

A second game-breaking softlock is stopping GTA 6 players from finishing the story — this time in Chapter 4, where Raul's call to Lucia never comes. Rockstar's first patch didn't fix it, but players have found a workaround, and in a lot of cases the call is just waiting on unfinished jobs.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

GTA 6 has a second story softlock, and this one hits even later than the first. Players reaching Chapter 4 are getting stuck on a mission called Raul's Plan, where Lucia is supposed to wait for a phone call from Raul — and for some players, the call simply never comes, no matter how much in-game time passes. The story stalls at roughly three-quarters complete, with dozens of hours already sunk into the save.

Rockstar's first post-launch patch, update 01.002.002, went out November 23 and specifically fixed story-related phone calls that weren't triggering. This one survived it. Rockstar has not acknowledged this particular bug, and there is no dedicated patch for it yet — so for now, players who hit the wall are relying on a community workaround.

First, make sure it's actually a bug

Before you assume your save is broken, check the jobs the game is quietly waiting on. Raul's Plan is a waiting mission, and the call won't come until earlier Chapter 4 tasks are finished — even ones that look optional.

The checklist, as reported by GameRant, TalkEsport and PlayerOne: finish all three of Yasmani's jewelry jobs, including the optional ones where you pay him for robbery tips; pay Abe Gonzalez's $75,000 lawyer fee; and answer every text, missed call and reminder on Lucia's phone. In a lot of cases, the call is being held back by one of those — not by a bug at all.

If you've done all of that, waited an in-game day or two, and the phone still hasn't rung, your save has most likely hit the softlock.

The workaround players are using

The fix that has worked for players comes from the community, and GameRant's own writer used it to save a stuck playthrough. The steps:

1. Finish any outstanding Yasmani jobs, including the optional paid-tip ones.

2. Clear every notification and reminder from Lucia's phone.

3. Make sure Jason and Lucia are split up, not hanging out together.

4. Make a manual save as Lucia inside her Vice City hotel room.

5. Fully shut down your console — hold the power button for 10 to 30 seconds, not rest mode — then turn it back on.

6. Load the save and leave the hotel room as Lucia, alone.

If it works, the first call Lucia gets isn't from Raul at all — it's Valentina, with a new main story mission. Finish that, pay the lawyer fee if you haven't already, and Raul's call finally comes through. It isn't guaranteed, and players who are still stuck should report the bug to Rockstar Support and keep an older save in a separate slot in case a future patch needs a clean starting point.

Not the same softlock as the last one

This is a different bug from the Chapter 3 Missing Persons softlock we covered on November 26, where Jason stays greyed out on the character wheel after the side case ends. That one is still live too, and its only reliable way out is an older manual save. Two separate story blockers, both unpatched, both in the biggest game of the year — and both with the same advice attached: make a manual save in a new slot before every major mission, because story missions can't be replayed.

Ghanaian GTA VI reenactment goes viral on TikTok

By Matt

A group of Ghanaian creators staged GTA VI scenes in a real car park — and the clip passed 1.5 million TikTok likes in a day, with viewers arguing over whether it was real life, gameplay, or AI.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

A group of Ghanaian creators turned a car park into Vice City — and the internet couldn't tell the difference. Their real-life GTA VI reenactment passed 1.5 million TikTok likes by Friday, November 27, a day after the Daily Mail shared the clip and declared that the cameraman deserved an Oscar.

The clip is a straight-faced imitation of the game's most familiar sights. A man in a white singlet, blue cap, and denim shorts walks across the car park with the swagger of a GTA protagonist before approaching a black Dodge Challenger. Around him, bystanders play along as non-player characters, mimicking the stiff, repetitive movements the games are famous for. An Intercity STC bus sits in the background, placing the scene firmly in Ghana.

Why it took off

The numbers piled up fast. By Friday the clip had gathered more than 1.5 million likes, over 12,600 comments, and more than 226,000 shares — all within about a day of the Daily Mail posting it.

The reaction was the giveaway that the bit worked. Commenters from around the world said they genuinely couldn't tell whether they were watching real footage, actual gameplay, or AI. That confusion is the whole joke, and the creators nailed it: the walk, the NPC extras, the car, the framing — all of it reads like a phone video of a game that happens to be happening in real life.

The timing helped

The reenactment landed a week after GTA VI itself arrived. Rockstar released the game on Thursday, November 19, and Ghana has been part of the launch story from the start — Ghanaian music features in the game, putting the country's sound in front of a global audience of players. The creators built on that moment, staging their own version of the game's famous scenes rather than just playing it.

It's a reminder of how the launch has played out beyond the sales numbers: the game is so embedded in the culture now that a car park, a Challenger, and a few friends acting like NPCs can pass for Vice City — at least long enough for 1.5 million people to tap like.

Sea of Sorrow has a date — Silksong's free expansion sails December 11

By Matt

Team Cherry closed its first-ever showcase, Cherry Time!, with the news Silksong players have waited eleven months for: the free Sea of Sorrow expansion launches December 11, with new areas, bosses, tools — and fishing.

Team Cherry finally ended the wait. At its Cherry Time! presentation this morning, the studio confirmed that Sea of Sorrow, the first major expansion for Hollow Knight: Silksong, launches December 11, 2026 — free for everyone who owns the base game.

The expansion takes Hornet to a new aquatic region of Pharloom, and Team Cherry is billing it as a grand tale of high-seas adventure, full of new characters, items, and bosses. The debut trailer showed off new areas, new enemies, new tools to master, and what appears to be a new crest based on how Hornet moves in the footage. And yes — there's a fishing minigame coming to the Soulslike Metroidvania.

Eleven months of "2026"

Sea of Sorrow was first teased in December 2025 with nothing but a vague 2026 window attached, and Team Cherry has said almost nothing about it since. That silence is the studio's trademark — it communicates in long gaps broken by sudden drops — which is why a scheduled showcase with a named time was itself news when it was announced on November 25. The presentation delivered: the 2026 window holds, and players get the expansion two weeks from today.

Silksong itself launched in September 2025 after years as one of gaming's most anticipated sequels, and it lived up to the wait. A free, major expansion landing three months later is the kind of post-launch support that keeps a game in the conversation — and December 11 puts it right in the middle of the holiday break, when players actually have time to dive back in.

Team Cherry's surprise second act

Sea of Sorrow wasn't the only news. Cherry Time! also revealed that Team Cherry is moving into publishing, showing off three indie games from other teams. First was Blokkan: Secret of the Walking City, a hand-drawn adventure about a robot detective investigating cases, pitched as a love letter to the golden age of adventure games. Next came Radio Rain, a 2D pixel-art side-scroller where you play a young girl named Cass, trapped in a ruined, rainy world, searching rain-spattered streets for a way home with her spirit companion. The reveals closed with The Botanist and the Translator, in which plant detective Hatti investigates a planet-spanning plant mystery alongside her translator, Oliver.

That's a real statement of intent from a studio that has spent its whole life making exactly two games. Team Cherry isn't just shipping its own expansion — it's putting its name behind other developers' work.

Why this one matters

For Silksong players, the wait is over and the price is zero. For the rest of the industry, the takeaway is bigger: the most famously silent studio in games just ran its first showcase, dated its biggest expansion, and announced a publishing arm — all in one morning. December 11 is two weeks away. Hornet goes fishing.

Marc Márquez announces his retirement from MotoGP — the reigning champion walks away at 33

By Matt

Marc Márquez announced Friday morning at Valencia that this weekend's Grand Prix will be his last race, closing his MotoGP career as the reigning world champion — and walking away from a Ducati contract that ran through 2028.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The announcement

Marc Márquez announced Friday morning at Valencia that he is retiring from MotoGP, delivering the news himself in the Ducati pit box just minutes before the opening practice session of the season finale — holding up a series of placards to the television cameras.

"We'll talk later, but first … Thank you to everyone who's been part of this journey … I hope you've enjoyed it as much as I have. … This will be my last race in MotoGP. … We made history."

Ducati confirmed it on Friday: the Valencia Grand Prix, this Sunday, will be his final race as a professional rider and with the Ducati Lenovo team.

The shock is the timing. Márquez is not fading out. He clinched the championship last Sunday at Portimão, his second straight title with Ducati, and he held a contract that ran through 2028. He is leaving at the top, on his own terms.

Why now

Márquez made the decision in October, after winning the Japanese Grand Prix at Motegi, and told almost nobody. His brother Álex was the only person who knew; his father found out on Wednesday, Ducati on Thursday, and his mother on Friday morning. He kept it quiet so he could fight for the championship without the retirement talk draining him.

The reason, in his own words at the press conference that followed, is risk. "I feel competitive, I feel fast, but the reason is the risk," he said. "Sometimes you need to have a balance between risk and compensation. And right now, the compensation, or the thing that I can achieve is, OK, to win one more [title]. Maybe. But it was not the time to do it."

The injuries behind that calculation are extensive. He has had seven operations on his right arm and shoulder since 2019, the latest in May to remove two bent screws pressing on a nerve. And the double vision that first appeared after his crashes has returned — after the Indonesian Grand Prix crash last October and a highside at Le Mans this year. He admitted he has started to feel fear — not of the bikes or the speed, he stressed, but of what the injury could become.

The career

Márquez arrived in MotoGP in 2013 and leaves as one of the two most decorated riders the premier class has ever seen: eight premier-class world championships, a total matched only by Giacomo Agostini, and 10 world titles across all classes — moving him past Valentino Rossi's nine.

This final season was the comeback that sealed it. He started the year still carrying the effects of the Indonesian crash, missed races after the Le Mans crash, and at one point trailed the championship leader by 102 points. He closed the gap with seven Grand Prix victories and 10 sprint wins, clinching the title with a race to spare — and retires with 80 premier-class race wins, nine behind Rossi's 89.

What it means

Sunday's race in Valencia is now a farewell. Márquez goes out as the reigning champion, in front of a home crowd, with nothing left to prove — and MotoGP heads into its new 850cc era in 2027 without its biggest star.

"I arrived in MotoGP in my way, and I will go in my way," he said at the press conference. He did exactly that.

GTA 6's unofficial PC port just got multiplayer — two Jasons in one Leonida, before GTA Online even exists

By Matt

The unofficial GTA 6 PC port now has working multiplayer: two players sharing one Leonida, driving cars at each other, talking over proximity voice chat — at a claimed 25 to 30 frames per second. The build is private, the footage is verified, and Rockstar still hasn't announced a PC version at all.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The unofficial GTA 6 PC port has multiplayer now. Not a menu, not a launcher — two players, in the same Leonida, at the same time.

French developer TeK posted footage on November 26 showing two Jason Duvals meeting at an airport, driving cars toward each other and interacting in one shared game world, with proximity voice chat running. TeK says the build runs at a stable 25 to 30 frames per second. The community tracker PortWatch VI says it has verified the footage is genuine — though it has not verified the frame-rate figure, which comes from the developer.

One week after launch, modders have built the thing Rockstar hasn't even announced.

What the footage actually shows

The clip is short and the demo is small: two players, one airport, cars, and voice. Notebookcheck, VideoCardz, Dexerto, and WCCFTech all covered the same footage on November 26, and the details line up across them. The build supports character and vehicle synchronization plus proximity voice chat, according to TeK. PortWatch's report notes the menu also allows teleporting around the map and spawning vehicles — this is still a developer's debugging playground, not a server browser.

There is a limit worth stating plainly. The demo shows two players. It does not establish how the build performs with more players, in busier parts of the map, or over a longer session. And some skeptics have suggested the second Jason could be a spawned NPC using Jason's model — PortWatch's verification is the counterweight there, but nobody outside TeK's group can test the build themselves, because the code is not public.

A fork of the build Take-Two already killed

TeK's multiplayer runs on a private fork of CGBJ's build — the same CGBJ whose repository vanished from GitHub on November 26, minutes after going public. Take-Two's DMCA notice on November 24 took down the Leonida project's network of 3,007 repositories, and CGBJ was one of the first projects the publisher targeted. The code TeK is building on was public only briefly before going offline.

That is the pattern of this whole saga now. The work spreads into private forks faster than the takedowns can reach it, and each private fork pushes the state of the art a little further. Three days ago the port needed one to two seconds to draw a single frame. On November 26 the public forks were running the open world at around 20 frames per second with a mod menu already built. Now a private fork has two players in the same world.

For scale, PortWatch's leaderboard puts the fastest verified public build — Belobug's AMD fork — at about 22 frames per second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT with 64 GB of RAM. The private CGBJ build that TeK's group forked averages about 25 frames per second in single-player. TeK's 25 to 30 claim for multiplayer sits just above that, and it is unverified.

Still not a game you can play — and still not legal to get

None of this is an official port, and Rockstar has announced no PC version of GTA 6. The game is listed only for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Reports have pointed at an official PC release in early 2027 with GTA Online to follow, but that is speculation, not an announcement.

And the warning from every previous post in this saga still stands: there is no playable PC version of GTA 6, and there is no safe way to get one. The leaked files have not been independently authenticated. Downloading them is piracy, and files circulating from strangers carry real malware risk — the port tracker is already flagging fake repositories distributing malware under the guise of GTA 6 port tools. TeK's build is private. Nobody can download it, test it, or verify the frame rate but TeK's group.

What is verified is the direction of travel. The port went from a single frame every two seconds to two players sharing a world in four days. The takedowns keep landing. The private forks keep moving anyway.
