Story of Seasons maker Marvelous is cutting console jobs — even as its profits soar

By Matt

Marvelous is offering voluntary retirement to 65 people on its console team, even after reporting operating profit up more than tenfold this year — a restructuring that leans harder on outsourcing for its Story of Seasons and Rune Factory games.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Marvelous — the Japanese publisher behind Story of Seasons, Rune Factory and Daemon X Machina — is cutting jobs on its console team, and the timing is what makes it sting. The company announced a voluntary early-retirement program on Friday that aims to shrink its console business by 65 people, weeks after reporting a huge jump in profits.

The program, which Marvelous calls its External Career Transition Support Program, is part of a restructuring of its console division — the part of the company that makes full-price, non-mobile games. Applications open December 14 and run through January 8, 2027, and anyone who takes the offer will leave by March 31, 2027, the end of the company's fiscal year. Those who go get a lump-sum retirement payment on top of standard severance, plus help finding a new job through an outside firm if they want it.

Why now — and why it looks strange

Marvelous says the move is about the changing shape of game development: bigger projects, longer cycles, and a need for a more flexible structure that mixes in-house development with outsourcing to external studios. Console development stays a core business, the company insists — the team is just getting smaller and more reliant on partners.

The awkward part is the money. For the six months from April through September 2026, Marvelous reported operating profit up 1,105.3% year on year, according to Automaton — a surge driven by its games business. The company still expects the retirement program to cost it about ¥220 million, roughly $1.37 million, which it will book as an extraordinary loss in the third quarter.

What it means for the games

For players, the near-term question is what happens to the pipeline. Marvelous is still working on Eternal Anima, its upcoming title, and the Story of Seasons and Rune Factory series remain the company's best-known console brands — Grand Bazaar, the latest Story of Seasons, only just arrived. A smaller in-house team with more outsourced work doesn't automatically mean fewer games, but it does mean the next ones will be made differently.

This is the same pattern the industry has been running all year: even healthy publishers are trimming headcount while they restructure around longer, more expensive development. Marvelous just did it in the most Japanese way possible — nobody is being fired, the door is open for volunteers, and the company is paying for the privilege.

Space Marine 2's Decimation update is live — Weekly Clash PvP, a Vanguard rework, and six new Heroic weapons

By Matt

Patch 16 is Space Marine 2's last big update of 2026, and it's a PvP-first one: a rotating Weekly Clash mode, a new Chaos Siege sector, a full Vanguard rework, and a half-dozen Heroic weapons to chase.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2's Decimation Update is live now — Patch 16, free on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC, and the last major update Saber Interactive has planned for 2026. After a year of operations, sieges and class reworks, this one is aimed squarely at the PvP crowd, with a new mode, a reworked class, and a fresh pile of gear to unlock.

Weekly Clash shakes up PvP

The headline addition is Weekly Clash, a new mode for Eternal War that rotates the rules every week. One week a match might be restricted to a single class, the next to a single weapon — and some variants hand out near-unlimited grenades. Saber says more modifiers are coming, and private lobbies can already craft their own rule sets.

It's a direct answer to the problem every live PvP mode eventually hits: the meta goes stale. Weekly Clash doesn't add maps or modes so much as it changes what the existing ones feel like, week to week.

Siege gets harder, Vanguard gets better

Chaos Siege, the wave-survival mode introduced in the Anniversary Update, gets a third sector that kicks in from wave 11 onward — plus a new enemy, the Loyalist Tactical Space Marine, whose Auspex Scan increases the damage you take. Surviving the late waves just got meaner.

The Vanguard class gets the rework treatment this time around. The Grapnel Launcher can now be used at close range, a batch of perks has been reworked and repositioned, and there's a new Revenge status effect: hitting an enemy afflicted with Revenge also damages nearby enemies. The Heavy is next in line for a rework, in Patch 17.

The loot

Six new Heroic Weapons join the Armoury — the Omnissian Axe, Bolt Rifle, Las Fusil, Plasma Incinerator, Heavy Bolt Pistol and Infernus Heavy Bolter — alongside four new helmets to unlock with Accolades, including the Space Wolves Iron Priest helm and Mk VI and Mk VII Hybrid variants. Season Pass III owners also get two new cosmetic packs today: the Deathwatch Champion Pack and the Mortifactors Cosmetic Pack.

There's a community event running alongside the patch, too. From November 26 through December 8, players can collectively recover 300,000 Gene Seeds to earn the Victrix Honour Guard Greave.

What's next

Saber has already sketched the road ahead: Patch 17 lands in the first quarter of 2027 with the Apothecary class and the Heavy rework, and the Year Three battle plan runs through Patch 19. For now, Decimation closes out 2026 with the game's PvP loop refreshed and its hardest mode made harder — which, for a game about being a giant in power armor, feels about right.

Walmart's Iono's Bellibolt ex box hits 3,924 stores, one per person

By Matt

Walmart put the Pokémon TCG: Iono's Bellibolt ex Premium Collection on shelves at 3,924 stores at 6 a.m. local time on Black Friday — one box per person, no Walmart+ membership needed.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Walmart opened its doors at 6 a.m. local time on Black Friday with one Pokémon box on the shelf that collectors have been waiting weeks for: the Pokémon Trading Card Game: Iono's Bellibolt ex Premium Collection, available at 3,924 participating stores while supplies last. The limit is one box per person, and you don't need a Walmart+ membership to buy one in store.

The price at the shelf is $49.97, according to Polygon — a markup over the $39.99 MSRP listed by Pokémon. That gap is worth knowing before you go, because the sealed box has been trading well above both numbers: TCGplayer market price sat at $62.42 as of November 26. Even recent eBay sales of sealed boxes ranged from $31.40 to $56.99 between November 16 and 20, so Walmart's in-store price lands in the middle of the real market — not a steal, but a fair shot at a box that's been hard to find at retail.

What's in the box

This isn't a new product. The collection first launched on April 11, 2025, built around Iono — the streamer gym leader from Pokémon Scarlet and Violet — and her electric partner Bellibolt. Per Pokémon, each box contains:

• 1 full-art foil promo card featuring Iono's Bellibolt ex

• 1 foil card featuring Iono's Tadbulb

• 1 sheet of acrylic standees featuring Iono, Bellibolt, and more

• 1 double-sided backdrop display

• 1 photo sticker featuring Iono and Bellibolt

• 6 Pokémon TCG booster packs

• A code card for Pokémon TCG Live

Polygon reports this restock's packs come from sets such as Chaos Rising and Pitch Black. Pokémon doesn't name the packs, and the original 2025 release carried different sets, so check the back of the box before you assume what's inside.

Why this one matters

The Bellibolt box is the centerpiece of Walmart's second Pokémon wave of the season. The first wave landed November 12 with 30th Celebration ex boxes and tins, and the retailer has more coming online for Cyber Monday, November 30 — including the 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collection. For collectors who struck out on the November 12 drop, this is the second real chance at a marquee box in two weeks, and the only one that requires showing up in person.

The promo card itself is the draw for players, too. Iono's Bellibolt ex carries the Electric Streamer Ability, which lets you attach extra Lightning Energy to Iono's Pokémon — a card that has stayed relevant in the Delta Reign format, where it pairs with the new Mega Rayquaza ex.

Before you drive over

Two warnings from the early reports: some Walmart stores put the boxes out ahead of schedule, so your local store may already be picked over — and some stores had Bellibolt signage up while actually selling the Garchomp box. Look at the box in your hand, not the sign above it. With the limit in place, the odds are decent if you get there early, but this is a while-supplies-last drop, and there's no online backup for this one.

TSL Bets: The Black Friday parlay (~+236) — Coleman anytime TD, Freiermuth OVER 21.5 receiving yards

By Matt

Jonah Coleman owns Denver's backfield with J.K. Dobbins suspended, and Pat Freiermuth has cleared 21.5 receiving yards in three straight games. Two legs, about +236, in the rain in Pittsburgh.

The game

Denver Broncos (8-2) at Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4) — 3:00 PM ET, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh, PA (Prime Video)

Broncos -4.5 (-110), total 36.5 (Over -114 / Under -106), moneyline Broncos -235 / Steelers +194 (BetMGM via USA Today Sportsbook Wire, November 26). Forecast: 90% chance of rain, low 40s, windy.

Injuries — Denver: S Taylor Rapp OUT (quadriceps). DE Sai'vion Jones OUT (hamstring). RB Tyler Badie QUESTIONABLE (thumb). RB J.K. Dobbins SUSPENDED for this game. S Brandon Jones returns after missing two games (hamstring — no game status). CB Pat Surtain II CLEARED.

Injuries — Pittsburgh: LB Alex Highsmith OUT (ankle). G Gennings Dunker OUT (knee). LB Cole Holcomb QUESTIONABLE (heel). WR Ben Skowronek on injured reserve (calf). QB Mason Rudolph starts — his first start of the season, after Aaron Rodgers was benched Tuesday night and released Wednesday. WR Michael Pittman Jr. activated from injured reserve (foot), no designation. WR DK Metcalf CLEARED.

Storylines: The Black Friday game is pure chaos on one sideline and a machine on the other. Denver arrives riding six straight wins and sitting in the thick of the AFC's top seeds. Pittsburgh is clinging to the final wild-card spot after two straight losses, and the week has been a storm: Rodgers benched, Rodgers released, Rudolph — making his 21st career start — thrown in against one of the league's best defenses in the rain. The Steelers will lean on the run and the short passing game, which is exactly where both of these legs live. Coleman has seen his share of Denver's backfield grow in each game since coming off injured reserve four games ago, and he was a one-man wrecking crew in Week 11: three touchdowns and 129 total yards. With Dobbins suspended, the backfield is his outright.

Leg 1 — Jonah Coleman anytime touchdown

Coleman has six touchdowns this season and just put up three in one game last week, and now the only other back who was taking his goal-line work is suspended. Denver is a 4.5-point favorite with a run-first game plan in bad weather — the exact script for a lead back to find the end zone. Line: anytime touchdown (-130, BetMGM via USA Today Sportsbook Wire; -135, DraftKings).

Leg 2 — Pat Freiermuth OVER 21.5 receiving yards

Freiermuth has cleared this number in three straight games — 39 yards at Philadelphia, 35 at Cincinnati, 35 against Cleveland — and he is the safety valve a first-time starter leans on: short routes, quick throws, move the chains. Rudolph will be under pressure from Denver's pass rush all afternoon, and the tight end is where the ball goes when the pocket collapses. He has 32 catches for 309 yards and 5 touchdowns this season. Line: OVER 21.5 receiving yards (-111, BetMGM via USA Today Sportsbook Wire).

The bet

Jonah Coleman anytime touchdown (-130, BetMGM) + Pat Freiermuth OVER 21.5 receiving yards (-111, BetMGM) — about +236. A $10 ticket returns about $33.63.

Why these legs

Both legs clear on their own. Coleman is the lead back on a 4.5-point favorite in a run-weather game with the goal-line work to himself, and Freiermuth is a yardage prop with a three-game floor and a quarterback who needs him. Neither leg depends on the other — different players, different sides of the ball, different markets. That is the juice rule working as intended: two props with real trend edges, about +236 instead of the chalky +150 you get from stacking favorites.

The honest caveats

The weather is the shared risk — rain, low 40s and wind in Pittsburgh can turn this into a slog where neither offense sustains drives, and Freiermuth's leg is the exposed one. Both legs live in the same game, so one bad afternoon in the rain sinks both. The total is just 36.5, so points are expected to be scarce, and Freiermuth's target volume is thin — two to five targets a game — so one quiet half can end it. And a parlay needs both legs — either one can sink it alone. The edge is real, but it is an edge, not a lock.

The record

TSL Bets is 23-45 in November, 27-66 all-time.

Eklund ties it with 3 seconds left, Islanders edge Blues in shootout

By Matt

Rookie Victor Eklund buried a one-timer with 2.3 seconds left to force overtime, and Bo Horvat and Mathew Barzal converted in the shootout as the Islanders beat the Blues 3-2 at UBS Arena.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Victor Eklund had 2.3 seconds to save the game, and he used every one of them. The 20-year-old rookie buried a one-timer from just above the right circle to tie the St. Louis Blues 2-2 on Wednesday night at UBS Arena, and the New York Islanders finished the job in the shootout for a 3-2 win.

It was the Islanders' seventh game-tying goal within the final three seconds of a game in franchise history — and the first since Anders Lee did it on March 3, 2015.

The final seconds

The Islanders pulled Ilya Sorokin for an extra attacker with a little over two minutes left, trailing 2-1 after Mason McTavish had put St. Louis ahead with six minutes to go. The pressure built, but the breakthrough didn't come until the very last shift.

Brayden Schenn collected a loose puck below the goal line and fed it up top to Eklund, who beat Joel Hofer blocker side with the one-timer. It was the Islanders' first 6-on-5 goal of the season — and it kept both points on the table.

After the game, Eklund earned the team's postgame oar for the moment. Asked by MSG's Shannon Hogan what he was thankful for with American Thanksgiving coming up, the rookie answered: "I'm thankful to be an Islander!"

How the game got there

Jean-Gabriel Pageau opened the scoring 5:37 into the second period, deflecting a Calum Ritchie feed past Hofer with his skate. St. Louis answered at 15:24 of the same period, when Dylan Holloway took a pass off a Robert Thomas faceoff win and beat Sorokin from the high slot.

McTavish's go-ahead goal came at 14:00 of the third, collecting a loose puck near the right post after a blocked shot and lifting it past Sorokin. The Blues, riding a four-game winning streak, looked poised to close it out on the road — until Eklund's shot changed everything.

Sorokin stopped 21 shots through overtime, then made two more saves in the shootout, including a glove stop on McTavish — the same player who had given St. Louis its late lead.

The shootout

Mathew Barzal scored in the first round, faking a shot and lifting the puck past Hofer's right arm. Bo Horvat followed in the second round, motoring through the middle of the slot before lifting a shot over Hofer's stick and right arm. Jake Neighbours scored the only shootout goal for St. Louis, and Horvat's tally stood as the winner.

What it means

The win moved the Islanders to 5-1-3 in their last nine games, and it snapped the Blues' four-game winning streak. For Eklund, a rookie still earning his place in the lineup, it was the kind of night that sticks — a game-tying goal in the final seconds of a game his team had no business winning, on a night the franchise hadn't seen anything like it in more than a decade.

The box score

Final: 3 (SO); 2

Goals: Pageau (2nd), Eklund (3rd, 59:57); Holloway (2nd), McTavish (3rd)

Shootout: Barzal, Horvat; Neighbours

Goalie: Sorokin — 21 saves + 2 in shootout; Hofer

Trail Blazers spoil Wemby's 44-point night in NBA Cup play

By Matt

Victor Wembanyama dropped 44 points and 16 rebounds in Portland, but Deni Avdija's 33 and a banked dagger three in the final minute gave the Trail Blazers a 116-111 NBA Cup win — San Antonio's first road loss of the season.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Victor Wembanyama did just about everything a single player can do in a basketball game on Wednesday night at Moda Center — and it still wasn't enough. The San Antonio star put up 44 points and 16 rebounds, but the Portland Trail Blazers held on for a 116-111 win in NBA Cup group play, handing the Spurs their first road loss of the season.

It was his third monster night in three weeks — and his second in four days. He went for 52 points and 24 rebounds against Dallas on November 4, then 50 points and 19 rebounds against New Orleans on November 21. This one was nearly as loud, and it still ended in a loss — a reminder that even an MVP-frontrunner season doesn't guarantee wins when the other side gets hot from deep.

The closing sequence

The game turned on the final three minutes, and Wembanyama was at the center of all of it. His turnaround jumper with 3:02 left cut Portland's lead to two, and after Stephon Castle tossed the ball high for an alley-oop dunk, the game was tied at 109 with two minutes remaining.

That's when Deni Avdija took it over. He made two free throws to put Portland ahead 111-109 with 1:45 left. Then, with 38.6 seconds on the clock and the shot clock winding down, Damian Lillard drove, saw Wembanyama waiting, and fired the ball back out to Avdija — who banked in a 25-foot three-pointer to stretch the lead to five. San Antonio never caught up again.

Avdija finished with 33 points, 12 rebounds and 7 assists, shooting 11 of 21 from the field and 5 of 8 from three. Lillard added 29 points, 7 assists and 5 threes of his own.

How Portland won it

The Blazers won this one from the arc. They took 50 of their 94 field-goal attempts from three-point range and drained 19 of them, shooting 38 percent from deep despite a rough 39.4 percent night from the field overall. Portland outscored San Antonio 32-24 in the fourth quarter, and the Moda Center crowd — in the building for the Blazers' first home game since November 11 — got the finish it came for.

Wembanyama set the tone early in the second half, scoring the first 12 San Antonio points of the third quarter and capping the run with a three that gave the Spurs a 69-66 lead. But Portland kept answering from deep, and the Spurs couldn't find a second scorer to match him down the stretch.

The box score

Victor Wembanyama: Spurs; 44 PTS, 16 REB, 3 AST, 2 BLK (17-30 FG, 3-9 3PT, 7-10 FT)

Deni Avdija: Trail Blazers; 33 PTS, 12 REB, 7 AST (11-21 FG, 5-8 3PT)

Damian Lillard: Trail Blazers; 29 PTS, 7 AST, 5 3PT

Stephon Castle: Spurs; 20 PTS, 9 AST, 6 REB

Sidy Cissoko: Trail Blazers; 16 PTS

What it means

Portland improved to 12-6 and moved to 2-1 in NBA Cup group play with a +7 point differential, keeping the Blazers in the hunt for a wild-card spot in the knockout round. San Antonio fell to 15-4 — second in the Western Conference behind the 15-3 Lakers, and 9-1 in its last 10 — but the loss stings in a group where four teams now sit at 2-1, including Golden State and the Lakers.

The two teams don't have to wait long for the next chapter of group play: Portland hosts Golden State and San Antonio hosts the Lakers on Friday night, both at 8:30 p.m. CT.

NFL · Nov 27, 2026 · 1:08 AM ET

Bass boots 57-yard walk-off as Bills edge Chiefs

By The Stat Line

Tyler Bass drilled a 57-yard field goal as time expired to cap a rainy Thanksgiving night and lift Buffalo past Kansas City, 13-10.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Tyler Bass drilled a 57-yard field goal as time expired to give the Buffalo Bills a 13-10 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, closing out the holiday tripleheader in heavy rain at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park.

It was a kicker's night in miserable conditions — and Bass was the only one who looked comfortable in them.

How the final seconds played out

Kansas City went three-and-out from its own 11 with 15 seconds left and was forced to punt. Buffalo linebacker Joe Andreessen got a hand on Matt Araiza's punt, and Greg Dortch returned it 17 yards to the Chiefs' 39, where he was tackled with four seconds on the clock.

That was all the time Bass needed. He sent the kick through the uprights from 57 yards out as the clock hit zero, and the Bills improved to 10-1 — the first team in the NFL to reach 10 wins this season, and the leader in the race for the AFC's top seed.

The winner came about 12 minutes after Bass had already rescued Buffalo once, nailing a 54-yarder with 11:58 left in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 10. Both kicks were struck in the same direction, into the same wind and rain.

The contrast on the other sideline was stark. Harrison Butker missed a 46-yard attempt wide right earlier in the fourth quarter — his eighth missed field goal of the year — a kick that would have given Kansas City the lead with just under six minutes to go.

The weather was the story

Neither offense could find much rhythm all night. Heavy rain fell for most of the game, the temperature sat at 34 degrees at kickoff, and gusts reached 35 mph, making it feel like 23. Both quarterbacks struggled to complete passes in the second half, and Buffalo turned the ball over twice.

Patrick Mahomes finished 16-of-29 for 174 yards. The Chiefs' best work on the ground came from Emmett Johnson, who ran for 72 yards and a touchdown — his sixth score of the season — to give Kansas City a 10-7 lead in the third quarter.

Cook carried the offense

With the passing game grounded by the weather, James Cook was Buffalo's offense. He ran for 117 yards and scored the Bills' only touchdown, a 5-yard run that opened the scoring. It was his 11th touchdown of the season.

Final score: 13; 10

Record after the game: 10-1; 8-3

James Cook rushing: 117 yards, 1 TD; —

Patrick Mahomes passing: —; 16/29, 174 yards

Emmett Johnson rushing: —; 72 yards, 1 TD

What it means

The win extends Buffalo's run of regular-season success against Kansas City — six straight regular-season meetings — even as the Chiefs remain 4-0 against Josh Allen in the playoffs. More immediately, it gives the Bills separation at the top of the AFC with six weeks left, while Kansas City falls to 8-3 and loses ground in the conference race.

For the Chiefs, the loss was a special-teams failure more than anything else: a deflected punt on the penultimate play and a missed field goal in the fourth quarter, in a game their defense had kept within reach all night.

Gaming · Nov 26, 2026 · 11:48 PM ET

End of an era: Boaster and Alfajer leave Fnatic — Gentle Mates' VCT 2027 superteam is official

By Matt

Gentle Mates confirmed the worst-kept secret in VALORANT at their 2027 Keynote: Jake 'Boaster' Howlett and Emir 'Alfajer' Beder are leaving Fnatic — and the French org is building its whole 2027 project around the duo that won two international titles together.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The worst-kept secret in VALORANT is official. Gentle Mates confirmed at their 2027 Keynote on Tuesday that Jake "Boaster" Howlett and Emir "Alfajer" Beder are leaving Fnatic to headline a rebuilt VALORANT roster for the VCT EMEA 2027 season — ending a Fnatic era that delivered two international titles and made the pair the faces of European VALORANT.

Boaster spent nearly six years with Fnatic, joining from SUMN FC in February 2021 when the org launched its VALORANT division. Alfajer arrived from Surreal Esports in May 2022, and the two of them spent four years together as the core of the roster. The announcement was made during Gentle Mates' Keynote presentation, and the org confirmed the full roster on X the same day.

The end of Fnatic's golden era

There is no overstating what this duo meant to Fnatic. Boaster became the face of the org's greatest spell, winning VCT LOCK//IN São Paulo and Masters Tokyo in 2023, plus three EMEA titles along the way. He reached the VALORANT Champions playoffs five times — more than any other player in the game's history.

Alfajer was named Masters Tokyo MVP, and the pair finished runners-up at Masters Toronto and at Champions in Paris in 2025. They were, for four years, the identity of the team: Boaster the mastermind in-game leader who always knew how to get the best out of a roster, Alfajer the mechanically gifted gunner who could flex across agents.

The split follows a 2026 season in which Fnatic missed every international event. The club announced on September 8 that Boaster had been granted permission to explore his options before his contract expired, and the writing was on the wall from there.

Boaster did not dress it up when he spoke to Sheep Esports after the announcement. "For sure. Fnatic is where I built a lot of my history. It was difficult, but I felt like it was the right time to try a different project. I'd been there for ages and I wanted to wear a different color jersey."

He once said his ambition was "to be the greatest leader of all time in VALORANT." The next chapter of that chase starts in Paris.

The new Gentle Mates roster

Gentle Mates did not just sign two stars — they built a whole project around them. The confirmed 2027 lineup is Boaster as in-game leader, Alfajer, Uğur "Ruxic" Güç from NAVI, 16-year-old Romanian duelist Denis-Stefan "kozzy" Aionitoaei, and Martin "MAGNUM" Penkov. Former Sentinels head coach Adam "kaplan" Kaplan takes charge, with Casper "Desmo" Rasmussen as his assistant.

The pieces fit together deliberately. Ruxic was the 2025 VCT EMEA Controller of the Year and joins after NAVI missed out on the 2027 partner slots. MAGNUM played alongside Boaster at Fnatic in 2021 and 2022, so this is a reunion for him too. And kozzy is the swing for the future: he posted 245 ACS in Stage 2 of VCT EMEA this year, and Gentle Mates are betting that a 16-year-old duelist with that kind of ceiling is worth building around.

There is one catch, and it is a real one. Kozzy was born on February 22, 2010, which means he does not turn 17 until that date in 2027 — so he will miss the EMEA Kickoff and Masters Seoul, which starts on February 20. Gentle Mates will have to field a sixth player for the start of the season, and they have not announced who that substitute is yet.

The roster is still pending Riot Games approval, which is standard for partner-team signings.

Gentle Mates are going bigger than VALORANT

The Keynote was not just a roster reveal. Gentle Mates also confirmed they are entering Rainbow Six Siege esports through Ubisoft's R6 Share partnership program for the 2027 season, and that they will host the first Call of Duty League Major of 2027 in Paris, scheduled for February 12–14 at the Plenitude Arena.

It is a statement of intent from an org that tore up its entire 2026 roster and coaching setup after Riot confirmed it as one of the eight VCT EMEA partner slots on a two-year deal. Gentle Mates finished runner-up at the EMEA Kickoff in 2026 and played at Masters Santiago, then fell apart in Stage 2 and finished 13th–16th after Play-In losses to Enterprise and Eintracht Frankfurt. The rebuild is total, and Boaster and Alfajer are the foundation of it.

What Fnatic do now

Fnatic are not standing still. They have already signed marteen for 2027, days after Alfajer's own four-year run with the org came to an end. But replacing Boaster is not a one-signing job — he was the in-game leader, the face of the team, and the player who had been there since the division began. Whoever takes the reins inherits a roster that missed every international event in 2026 and now has to rebuild its identity from scratch.

The 2027 VCT EMEA season just got a lot more interesting. Gentle Mates, with Boaster and Alfajer leading the way, an experienced hand in MAGNUM, and two players with something to prove in kozzy and Ruxic, have built a roster that can aim at the top of the region — and the reunion of the duo that won Tokyo together is the storyline that will follow them all year.

Pokémon Black Friday Deals 2026: Best Cards & ETBs

By Matt

TCGplayer's Cyber Weekend pays 10% back in store credit from Black Friday through Cyber Monday — and the Delta Reign Booster Box is the best per-pack value in the set's lineup.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Black Friday for Pokémon collectors in 2026 isn't about slashed prices — it's about store credit. TCGplayer's Cyber Weekend promotion runs from Friday, November 27 at 9 AM ET through Monday, November 30 at 11 PM ET, and it pays 10% back in future store credit on eligible purchases. Subscribers get 12% under TCGplayer's official terms. And the best value in the newest set, Delta Reign, is the booster box — at the November 26 market snapshot it worked out to about $5.33 a pack, well under what the ETB or booster bundle cost per pack.

The TCGplayer Cyber Weekend deal

The promotion covers all eligible products — singles, sealed product, accessories — with a few exclusions: gift cards, taxes, shipping, and anything bought before the window opens don't count. Preorders do qualify.

The fine print matters here. The credit is not a discount at checkout; it lands in your TCGplayer account 3–5 business days after the purchase, and it's only good on a later order. Credit is capped at $50 per qualifying item and $1,500 per account for the whole promotion. So a single big-ticket item tops out at $50 of credit no matter the price, and you'd need $15,000 of eligible buying to hit the account cap.

Subscribers get the better rate, but only if you subscribe before you buy — the perk isn't retroactive.

Delta Reign, by the numbers

Delta Reign launched November 6, and it's still the set everyone is chasing — largely because of the Mega Rayquaza cards. Here's how the sealed products stacked up in the November 25–26 TCGplayer market snapshot:

Delta Reign Booster Box: 36; $191.93; $5.33; $161.64

Delta Reign Elite Trainer Box: 9; $74.41; $8.27; $49.99

Delta Reign Booster Bundle: 6; $42.92; $7.15; $26.94

The box is the clear winner on per-pack cost, and it's the only one of the three that comes close to its list price — it sits about 19% over MSRP, while the ETB is roughly 1.5x its $49.99 list price. At the box's market price, the Cyber Weekend promo would return roughly $19.19 in future store credit.

Prices have been falling since presale, which is the real story of this set's launch. The ETB was $106.29 on presale and the booster box $238.91; by the November 24 check they were down to $74.95 and $191.35. The trend has been steady, not a Black Friday cliff — if you're buying to open, the box at its current price is already the deal.

The honest context

Don't walk into the weekend expecting sealed Pokémon at or below sticker price. On November 26, zero of the 31 core sealed products tracked by The Lab TCG sold at or under MSRP on TCGplayer. That's the market you're shopping in.

The exception is at retail, not on the marketplace. Best Buy had the Delta Reign Booster Box at $160.99 — a hair under its $161.64 MSRP — through its invitation system. Walmart listed the ETB at $79.77, which is actually above the $74.41 market price, so it's only worth it if you'd rather buy from a retailer than the marketplace. Target has a Pokémon trading card drop scheduled for Saturday, November 28 as part of its Black Friday event. Best Buy is the spot where an actual below-market price shows up; everywhere else, the "deal" is the store credit coming back to you later.

The rule of thumb for the weekend: a booster bundle near $27, an ETB near $50, or a booster box near $162 is at MSRP — and for a current set, that's already a good price. Anything under those numbers is a genuine find.

Rockstar's patch didn't fix GTA 6's stuck weather for everyone — players found a cache-clear workaround that brings the storms back

By Matt

Leonida was supposed to have fog, thunderstorms, and hurricanes — but some players have had nothing but sunshine since launch, even after Rockstar's first patch. A cache-clear workaround players are sharing today is finally letting the weather change.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

One of the things Rockstar talked up most before GTA 6 launched was the weather. Thick rolling fog, violent thunderstorms, full-blown hurricanes — a system that could rain on one side of Leonida while the sun shone on the other, with wet roads, puddles, and clothes that stayed damp after a storm. A week into the game, a lot of players have seen none of it. Their Leonida has been stuck on sunny, day after day, and Rockstar's first patch didn't fix it for everyone. Now players have found their own fix, and it's a quick trip through the console's Safe Mode.

The patch that was supposed to fix it

The stuck weather was a known bug from launch week. Rockstar's first post-launch update, 1.002.002, rolled out on November 23 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and its patch notes included a line aimed squarely at the problem: "Fixed an issue that resulted in the weather not changing for extended periods." The same patch fixed the broken autosaves, crashes, and story-blocking phone calls.

For plenty of players, that was the end of it. But numerous players kept reporting the same problem after updating — endless sunshine, no rain, no storms, no change at all. One player at the center of today's workaround had gone 56 hours without experiencing dramatic weather before trying the fix.

The fix players are passing around

The workaround surfaced on November 26, when GameRoll shared it on X, crediting user @mauricioce85796 with originally finding it. The idea is simple: clear the console's system cache, which appears to let the game's weather system start cycling properly again. Several players have since reported that storms appeared after loading their save following the clear.

On PlayStation 5, the steps are:

1. Turn off the PS5 console completely.

2. Once it is fully powered down, press and hold the power button until you hear a second beep — about seven seconds — to enter Safe Mode.

3. Connect your controller with a USB cable and press the PS button.

4. Scroll down to Clear Cache and Rebuild Database.

5. Select Clear System Software Cache and let the console restart.

Then launch GTA 6 and resume playing. On Xbox Series X|S, the equivalent is a full shutdown, unplugging the power cable for two minutes, then plugging it back in and turning the console on.

What to expect — and what Rockstar hasn't said

A few things to know before trying it. First, don't expect a thunderstorm the second you load back in. The weather system is still dynamic, so it may take some time exploring Leonida before the next storm rolls through — the fix appears to unstick the cycle, not summon rain on demand. Second, clearing the system cache does not delete game saves, so there's no progress at risk. And third, Rockstar has not officially confirmed this workaround as a solution. It is player-reported, not studio-endorsed — but the number of players reporting success, including one outlet that tried it and noticed a change the same night, makes it worth trying if your Leonida has been stuck in permanent sunshine.

If neither method works and the patch hasn't helped, the honest answer is to wait for another update. But for players who have spent a week wondering where the weather went, a quick Safe Mode clear is a cheap thing to try.

One more thing not to confuse with the bug: hurricanes. They don't just show up in the normal weather rotation — they unlock through a secret bunker side mission up in North Leonard County, by Lake Leonida, and only start appearing randomly after that quest is done. If your weather is cycling but you've never seen a hurricane, that's the game working as designed, not the bug.

The best GTA 6 PC port just vanished — 25 FPS, then gone minutes after going public

By Matt

CGBJ was the furthest along of any unofficial GTA 6 PC port — reportedly running the game at 25 to 30 frames per second and nearly finished. Hours after it went public on GitHub, the repository was gone. Nobody has confirmed who removed it.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The unofficial race to play GTA 6 on PC just lost its leader. CGBJ, one of the furthest-along fan-made PC port projects, reportedly reached a playable 25 to 30 frames per second — and then its GitHub repository disappeared minutes after going public. As of Thursday evening, nobody has confirmed who removed it.

That uncertainty is the story. Take-Two's lawyers spent this week taking down the Leonida project and its 3,007 associated repositories, so the obvious suspect is Rockstar's parent company. But no DMCA notice against CGBJ has surfaced in GitHub's public record, and the team behind the project may have pulled it down themselves to avoid becoming the next takedown. Both explanations are live, and neither is confirmed.

How far it got

CGBJ was a fork of VIctory, the open-source compatibility layer that runs the leaked Xbox build's code directly on Windows, combining VIctory's runtime with XCL's shader translation technology. That is the same family of projects that spent this week climbing from one frame every two seconds to around 20 frames per second — but CGBJ had gone further than the rest.

XDA Developers reported on November 26 that CGBJ hit a playable 25 to 30 FPS just as its GitHub page vanished. GameGPU, citing the community tracker PortWatch, put the build at an average of 25 FPS on NVIDIA hardware and estimated the project was 91.5 percent complete overall, with the story campaign roughly 80 percent complete. Those are tracker estimates, not benchmarks, but they explain why this one mattered: of all the fan ports, CGBJ was the closest to something a person could actually play.

It was also, until Thursday, one of the more private efforts. XDA notes the project had previously been kept private before going public — and that public window lasted only minutes.

Who took it down

Nobody will say, because nobody can prove it yet. Fextralife, reporting Thursday evening, wrote that there is no publicly verified DMCA notice or official statement confirming that Rockstar or Take-Two targeted CGBJ, and that a missing repository does not necessarily mean a copyright takedown took place. XDA reached the same conclusion: it is unclear whether the team made the page private to avoid a potential takedown or whether Rockstar's legal department hit it. It usually takes a few days for GitHub DMCA notices to become public, so the paper trail may still appear.

GameGPU went further, reporting outright that Rockstar removed the repository minutes after it went public — but that reads as an inference from the timing, not a confirmed notice, and the other outlets covering the same disappearance would not go that far. Reddit users noted the speed of the removal suggests round-the-clock monitoring of the platform by Take-Two's lawyers, who had already secured the removal of Leonida and its forks earlier in the week.

What is confirmed is the 404: navigating to CGBJ's GitHub page now returns an error, and several forks of the project remain active, which means the code is already out in the wild whether the team pulled it or someone else did. In the short time the project was openly accessible, thousands of users copied the source code, and alternative mirrors have begun appearing on third-party hosting services, according to GameGPU.

The crackdown keeps working — and keeps not working

This is the third beat in the same week-long pattern, and it keeps cutting both ways. Take-Two's DMCA notice on November 24 took down the Leonida network — 3,007 repositories in one filing, the main project plus every fork, because GitHub processes a whole fork network when a complainant alleges most of it infringes. Leonida's 15-year-old creator quit the same day. Then the VIctory forks kept climbing anyway, hitting 20 FPS and sprouting a mod menu and a dedicated launcher.

CGBJ is the sharpest version of that contradiction yet: the most advanced build, the fastest disappearance, and a takedown — or a self-pull — that arrived after the code had already spread to forks and mirrors. The projects do not distribute the game's files; users are expected to supply their own, and the only source in circulation is the leak. The code can be taken down. The leak cannot be un-leaked.

And the warning from every previous post in this saga still stands: there is no official PC version of GTA 6, Rockstar has announced no PC release date, and there is no safe way to get one. Fake GTA 6 PC downloads are already spreading malware, and the port tracker is flagging fake repositories distributing malware under the guise of port tools. The builds get faster every few days. The takedowns keep landing. And 25 FPS on a project that no longer exists is still a long way from playable.

NFL · Nov 26, 2026 · 9:10 PM ET

Eagles rally from 21 down to stun Cowboys 39-38 on Thanksgiving

By Matt

Down 31-10 late in the third quarter, the Eagles stormed back behind Joe Milton's four touchdowns and DeVonta Smith's career-high 200 receiving yards, winning 39-38 on Jake Elliott's 59-yard field goal with two seconds left — the biggest comeback in NFL Thanksgiving history.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The Philadelphia Eagles trailed the Dallas Cowboys 31-10 late in the third quarter on Thanksgiving. They won 39-38.

Jake Elliott drilled a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left at AT&T Stadium to complete the biggest comeback in NFL Thanksgiving history, capping a fourth quarter in which Philadelphia outscored Dallas 22-7. It was also the Eagles' biggest comeback ever against the Cowboys, and their fourth-biggest against any opponent.

How the comeback unfolded

Dallas looked like it had the game wrapped up. The Cowboys led 28-10 at halftime behind three first-half touchdowns from Javonte Williams, and Brandon Aubrey's 59-yard field goal early in the third made it a three-score game.

Then the Eagles finally found the offense that had been missing all season. Philadelphia had not scored more than 24 points in any game this year and was averaging 16.7 points per game — then put up 22 in the fourth quarter alone, more than in any of their last eight games.

The rally started late in the third, when Joe Milton hit DeVonta Smith for a 45-yard touchdown to cut it to 31-17. Early in the fourth, Ty Robinson blocked a Dallas punt and Kenny Moore II recovered it in the end zone, making it a one-score game. Dallas answered on Dak Prescott's 14-yard touchdown run, but after a 55-yard Britain Covey kick return, Milton responded with a 15-yard touchdown run of his own to pull Philadelphia within 38-30.

Milton's third touchdown pass of the day — a 24-yarder to rookie Makai Lemon with 2:10 left — made it 38-36. The Eagles failed the two-point try for the second time, so they still needed the ball back. They got it in dramatic fashion: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer went for it on fourth-and-1 from the Philadelphia 39 with 55 seconds left, and Prescott was sacked. Milton drove the Eagles into range, Elliott split the uprights from 59, and Andrew Mukuba's toe-tap interception on the final play sealed it.

Milton beats his old team

The win belonged to Milton. In his third career start — and his first road start — the 26-year-old threw for 331 yards with three touchdown passes and a 15-yard scoring run, finishing with a 121.8 passer rating despite one interception.

The revenge angle was real. Milton spent more than a year with the Cowboys, learning behind Prescott, before Philadelphia signed him off Dallas' practice squad on October 16. He had played one game with Smith before Thursday. He threw him two touchdowns anyway.

All three of Milton's scoring passes came from outside the pocket. The first was the play of the game: flushed to his left, he waved Smith downfield and heaved the ball roughly 65 yards through the air from the Eagles' 42 for a 50-yard touchdown, with Smith boxing out cornerback Cobie Durant in the end zone.

Smith's career night

Smith finished with 11 catches for a career-high 200 yards and two touchdowns on 14 targets. The yardage total was the most by an Eagle since DeSean Jackson had 210 in Dallas in 2010, and the sixth-most in franchise history. He had just five touchdowns of at least 45 yards in his entire career before Thursday — he had two in one game.

He did it while banged up, leaving the field briefly with an apparent back injury after landing hard on an incompletion in the fourth quarter, then returning for a 5-yard catch on the final drive.

Elijah Moore added three catches for 57 yards, and Lemon's late touchdown was his latest big moment as a rookie.

What it means

Philadelphia improved to 4-7 with its second consecutive victory, avenging a 38-21 loss to Dallas in Week 7. The Eagles did it shorthanded: Jalen Hurts was out, Saquon Barkley left in the first quarter with a stinger, Dallas Goedert hurt his shoulder, and Cooper DeJean left with a concussion.

Dallas fell to 5-7, and the loss is a serious blow to its playoff hopes. The Cowboys came in averaging 30.6 points per game and led by three scores at home on Thanksgiving — and still found a way to lose.

Elliott, for his part, keeps building a case as one of the clutch kickers in the league. He is now 4-for-5 in his career on attempts of 59 yards or longer, and his four makes from that distance are tied for the fifth-most in NFL history.

Infinity Nikki Version 3.0 is live — two new cities, guns and magic, and 160 free draws

By Matt

Infinity Nikki's biggest update yet is live today: Version 3.0 'Of Yesterday and Tomorrow' takes Nikki and Momo to the Twin Cities of Art, Cicia and Ceremius, with nearly 10 hours of new story, four new exploration abilities, firearms and magic combat, and 160 free draws plus 19 outfit sets to celebrate the update and Nikki's birthday.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Infinity Nikki just got its biggest update yet. Version 3.0, "Of Yesterday and Tomorrow," is live today on PlayStation 5, and it is less a patch than a second launch: two new cities, nearly 10 hours of cinematic story, four new abilities, a combat system that now includes firearms and magic, and a pile of free rewards to mark the occasion.

The update takes Nikki and Momo to the Twin Cities of Art — Cicia and Ceremius, two cities that share a common origin and could hardly be more different. Cicia is the capital of art, where Nikki attends an academy, runs into strange anomalies on the streets, and gets pulled into an investigation of a group known as the Rogues. Ceremius sits behind a wall of mist, and the story there ties the city's past to a present-day crisis and the mystery of the Goddess des Arts.

Four new abilities, and combat grows teeth

Version 3.0 hands stylists four new tools for getting around and solving puzzles. Veiling lets Nikki throw a Shadow Beetle and teleport to it — or take over the view of certain objects it lands on. Alchemy turns gathered materials into brewed potions, with new recipes discovered through trial-crafting. Enhanced Floating adds a midair double jump and forward air dash. And Gemwork lets her appraise uncut gemstones out in the world, then work them into gems for outfit crafting and Alchemy.

Combat gets its biggest expansion since launch. Two new systems arrive: firearms, with a short musket for rapid fire and a long musket for aimed shots, and magic, with a staff that casts different Oracle Arts depending on the selected Nature's Breaths and chant tiers. A new build system sits on top of both, so players can tune their fighting style instead of relying on one fixed set of moves.

A living city, and a birthday haul

Cicia is built to feel like a working city. Nikki can drive a car from the in-game Brise Automobile brand to complete passenger commissions, run her own clothing store — the Warmhearted Boutique — and style outfits for customers, or try side activities like the Scoop & Smile Creamery ice cream shop and Fuse Bead Art. Ceremius leans into its mystery instead, with relic restoration, old photo restoration, and divination tied to local lore. Puzzle dungeons across both cities draw on the new exploration abilities, and the open world now has larger ambient NPC crowds, flowing traffic, and richer interactions — taxi passengers with stories, street musicians, NPCs dancing together.

The headline outfit is the first Star Crown Resonance set, "Where Stars Shine Again," which comes with both new weapons — musket and staff — and lets unused dashes be stored and released all at once. A new 5-Star set, "When Light Falls Upon," unlocks Air Jumps and Air Dashes, and two 4-Star sets, "Game for the Immortal" and "Beyond the Silence," summon chess pieces and a fairy-tale phantom for playful interactions.

New and returning players can also jump straight in: Version 3.0 lets stylists skip the standard beginner tutorial, try a new transitional tutorial, and use chapter select to start from any story chapter released so far.

And the free haul is generous. PlayStation Blog puts the total at 160 draws and 19 sets of clothes, all free, across Version 3.0 and Nikki's birthday celebrations — including a first top-up double bonus reset, a Black Friday sale, and two 5-Star outfits among the login rewards.

Max Verstappen played 40 hours of GTA 6 during the Las Vegas GP weekend — and still won the race

By Matt

Four-time F1 world champion Max Verstappen revealed he logged about 40 hours of GTA 6 across the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend — playing mornings and evenings around practice, qualifying and the race — then went out and won it anyway, his fourth victory of the 2026 season.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Max Verstappen spent the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend doing what most of the rest of the world was doing: playing GTA 6. The difference is that Verstappen squeezed it in around driving a Formula 1 car at 200 miles per hour — and still won the race.

The four-time world champion revealed on a livestream after the race that he logged about 40 hours on Grand Theft Auto VI across the weekend in Vegas, playing in the mornings and evenings between his track duties. "I played a lot in the evening and in the morning in Vegas," he said. "I mean, I can't go out anyways and walk around." He did not play on the flight home — that time was for sleep.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, November 19, the same week Formula 1 arrived in Las Vegas, so the timing was almost designed for it. Verstappen had talked before release about wanting to play the game, and once it unlocked, he went all in — by his own account, he is already about 80 percent through the story.

Pole, win, and a 40-hour side quest

The gaming marathon did not slow him down. Verstappen converted pole position into victory in the Las Vegas Grand Prix, his third win in Vegas and his fourth of the 2026 season, finishing ahead of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri in a 50-lap race that featured 35 lead changes.

It is the kind of stat that sounds made up until you remember who it is about. Verstappen is a keen gamer who streams on Twitch between races, mostly sim racing with his Team Redline outfit, and he dips in and out of other games too — including ARC Raiders. But he admits he cannot juggle too many at once. "I'm so bad when I play too many games at the same time. I can't, I just can't," he said on the stream. GTA 6, apparently, got the full focus.

He is not the only athlete who cleared the schedule for Vice City. Lewis Hamilton said before launch that he was hoping to take the day off to play it, and NBA center Steven Adams joked that sports leagues would "plummet" in quality while everyone was locked into Leonida. Verstappen just took the joke one step further: he played the game for the equivalent of a full work week and won a Grand Prix in the middle of it.

The next stop on the F1 calendar is Qatar, and Verstappen has a stream scheduled to play Minecraft ahead of it — though he admitted on the same livestream that after all that time in Vice City, he has "completely forgotten" how to play it.

Jeff Petry announces his retirement from the NHL

By Matt

Defenseman Jeff Petry announced his retirement on Wednesday's episode of the 'Never Offside' podcast, closing a career that ran from Edmonton to Minnesota by way of a Stanley Cup Final with Montreal.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

How he said it

Jeff Petry announced his retirement from the NHL on Wednesday's episode of the "Never Offside With Julie & Cat" podcast, the show co-hosted by his wife, Julie Petry, and Cat Toffoli. The National Hockey League Players' Association marked the moment with a congratulatory post of its own, confirming what Petry had just said himself: after a career that stretched across a decade and a half, he is hanging up his skates.

Petry had not played at all this season. He last suited up in 2025-26, splitting his final campaign between the Florida Panthers and the Minnesota Wild, and he went unsigned into the fall as a free agent. The announcement makes official what the empty season already suggested.

The career in numbers

Petry was a second-round pick, 45th overall, by the Edmonton Oilers in the 2006 draft, and he went on to skate in 1,048 NHL games over 16 seasons with six teams: Edmonton, Montreal, Pittsburgh, Detroit, Florida and Minnesota. He finished with 96 goals, 298 assists and 394 points, along with 428 penalty minutes.

For a defenseman who was never the flashiest name on a roster, that is a serious body of work. Year after year, coaches trusted him to eat hard minutes and not hurt them, and he kept answering the call.

The Montreal years

The longest chapter came in Montreal. The Oilers dealt Petry to the Canadiens at the trade deadline on March 2, 2015, and he spent just over eight seasons there — the heart of his career. His most productive stretch came in those years: four consecutive 40-point seasons from 2017-18 through 2020-21, when he was one of the steadiest two-way defensemen in the league.

The peak was the spring of 2021, when Petry helped the Canadiens reach the Stanley Cup Final — the run Canadiens fans will remember him for.

The last stop, and the international stage

After Montreal, Petry's career became a tour of the league's map: a trade to Pittsburgh in the summer of 2022, a move to his home-state Detroit Red Wings, then the one-year deal with Florida in July 2025 and the mid-season trade to Minnesota that closed out his final year.

He wore the USA jersey, too. Petry represented the United States four times at the IIHF World Championship, in 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2024, winning a bronze medal at the 2013 tournament in Sweden and Finland.

A defenseman who lasted a decade and a half in the league and kept getting the call for his country — that is a career worth the quiet announcement, and the respect that followed it.

Gaming · Nov 26, 2026 · 7:16 PM ET

GTA 6's unofficial PC port just hit 20 FPS — and modders already built a mod menu for it

By Matt

Three days ago the unofficial GTA 6 PC port needed one to two seconds to draw a single frame. Now community builds are running the open world at around 20 frames per second, holding a 41-minute session without a crash — and the first mod menu and dedicated PC launcher have already shown up.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Three days ago, the unofficial GTA 6 PC port needed one to two seconds to draw a single frame of the game world. Now community builds are running Leonida at around 20 frames per second, holding a session for 41 minutes without a crash — and the first mod menu and dedicated PC launcher for the game have already shown up.

It is still not playable in any real sense. But the pace of this is now the story: every day since the leaked Xbox executable surfaced on November 23, the port has jumped to a new milestone, and Take-Two's takedowns have not slowed it down.

From seconds per frame to 20 FPS

The numbers come from two separate forks of VIctory, the open-source compatibility layer that runs the leaked Xbox build's code directly on Windows. TweakTown reported on November 26 that footage posted to X by MrPoulpy shows the game running through VIctory with a live frame counter at 30 FPS in the menus and 19 to 23 FPS while riding a jet ski and driving along the coast. In town, it falls to about 12 FPS. The clip carries a watermark from another user, AzRage, and TweakTown's author wrote that he was unable to independently verify who made the build or what hardware it ran on — so treat that clip as a claim with video attached, not a benchmark.

The second report is easier to pin down. VGTimes covered a fork called VIctory-7900XTX, built by AvatarManz and tested on a Windows 11 PC with an Intel i9-12900K, 64 GB of RAM, and a Radeon RX 7900 XTX, running at 1440p on the Series X graphics profile. Its longest reported session stretched to 41 minutes without a crash. The prologue's indoor scenes reached 13 to 20 FPS, and the first boat mission ran at 19 to 22 FPS. A street chase full of cars and people dropped to 6 to 10 FPS — but the same scenes had taken 280 milliseconds per frame two days earlier, roughly 3 to 4 FPS. The fork used 40 to 46 GB of private memory, and its documentation recommends 64 GB of RAM.

A third data point comes from PC Games Hardware, cited by TweakTown: a public fork called VIctory-NVIDIA averages 20 to 22 FPS indoors on an RTX 5070 and a Ryzen 7 9800X3D. The catch is in the settings — that fork uses the Xbox Series S graphics profile, rendering internally at 960 by 540 before upscaling, with ray tracing largely switched off.

The main VIctory project's own README still lists the first mission intro at 1 to 2 seconds per frame. The forks are moving faster than the project documenting them.

The mod menu already exists

The port is not just getting faster — it is getting tooling. TweakTown reported on November 26 that community developers have demonstrated an in-game mod menu and a dedicated PC launcher, three days after the leaked executable surfaced.

Footage shared by X user cccurrenccc shows an in-game mod menu running on an unofficial PC build, with an interface resembling the mod menus previously built for GTA V. The current implementation was created primarily for debugging purposes, and it is unclear whether it has been made publicly available. Separately, Brazilian streamer Suco demonstrated a dedicated GTA VI launcher for PC, reporting an average of around 10 FPS on a system with a Radeon RX 7900 XTX and 64 GB of memory, with frame rates occasionally dropping to just 2 FPS.

That is the shape of this race now: the builds get faster every few days, the tooling shows up alongside them, and the takedowns keep landing. Take-Two's DMCA notice on November 24 took down the Leonida project's network of 3,007 GitHub repositories, and TweakTown noted several other port repositories have since vanished with no public takedown notice. VGTimes reported two more unofficial ports were taken down as the VIctory-7900XTX fork arrived.

Still not a game you can play

None of this is an official port, and Rockstar has announced no PC version of GTA 6. The visual bugs are not subtle: black holes sit where shoreline water should be, magenta streaks run along a road, and outdoor trees, plants, and distant buildings can flicker while textures arrive late. At 12 FPS in town on one build and 6 to 10 FPS in a street chase on another, this is a technical experiment, not a way to play the game.

And the warning from every previous post in this saga still stands: there is no playable PC version of GTA 6, and there is no safe way to get one. The leaked files have not been independently authenticated. Downloading them is piracy, and files circulating from strangers carry real malware risk — the port tracker is already flagging fake repositories distributing malware under the guise of GTA 6 port tools. The projects themselves do not distribute the game's files; users are expected to supply their own, and the only source in circulation right now is the leak.

The builds get faster every few days. The takedowns keep landing. And 20 FPS at 540p is still a long way from playable.

NBA · Nov 26, 2026 · 7:09 PM ET

LeBron's first Sixers triple-double cools off Heat

By Matt

LeBron James posted 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds for his first triple-double as a 76er, leading Philadelphia past Miami 111-104 in an NBA Cup game and snapping the Heat's seven-game winning streak.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

LeBron James recorded his first triple-double as a Philadelphia 76er on Wednesday night, and he did it in style — 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds to lead the Sixers past the Miami Heat 111-104 in an NBA Cup game at home. The win snapped Miami's seven-game winning streak and kept Philadelphia in contention in East Group B.

It was his best all-around game in his first season with the Sixers, and it came against a former franchise, in front of nearly 20,000 screaming fans.

The second-quarter takeover

The night turned in the second quarter, when James scored 14 consecutive Philadelphia points. It started simply enough with a three-point play. He buried a long three, then ripped an even longer one from the top of the arc. The third three was for show — a 35-footer off a dump-off from VJ Edgecombe just past midcourt, an old-fashioned swish. James ran back with his palms extended, bobbed his head and licked his lips as Miami called timeout and the arena blasted the "LeBron, LeBron, LeBron" remix. He powered down the lane for a layup to finish the run.

The burst gave Philadelphia a 47-39 lead and sent the crowd into a frenzy. James went into halftime with 16 points, 6 rebounds and 6 assists.

Closing it out

James kept the foot down after the break. His three early in the third quarter gave Philadelphia its first double-digit lead, and a layup shortly after stretched the advantage to 16. He capped the highlight reel with a ridiculous transition alley-oop pass from beyond halfcourt to VJ Edgecombe for a 98-84 lead, then grabbed the rebound he needed with 1:44 left to secure the triple-double — and the crowd stood for a rousing ovation.

Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers with 30 points, and his three with 2:31 left gave the hosts their largest lead at 111-95, essentially sealing the outcome.

The history

This was the 126th triple-double of James' career, the fifth-most in NBA history. For scale: that is more than Larry Bird, Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant and Scottie Pippen combined.

He also broke his own record for the oldest player with a triple-double in NBA history. He turns 42 on December 30, and he has now scored at least 20 points in each of his last four games, shooting at least 50 percent from the floor in all four.

Afterward, James put it simply: he can still "dust off the cape."

What it means

Philadelphia improved to 15-4, the best record in the Eastern Conference, and moved to 2-1 in NBA Cup group play. Miami's run is over, and the Sixers look every bit like the team to beat in the East right now — with a 41-year-old doing things no player his age has ever done.

NHL · Nov 26, 2026 · 5:47 PM ET

Cutter Gauthier is the first American ever with 21 goals in 14 games — and one goal from the NHL's monthly record

By Matt

Cutter Gauthier's power-play goal in the Ducks' 7-0 rout of the Sharks made him the first American in NHL history with 21 goals in a 14-game span — the first player from any country since Mario Lemieux in 1992-93 — and left him one goal shy of the calendar-month record with two games left in November.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Cutter Gauthier needed less than sixteen minutes of the first period to make history. With 4:43 left in the opening frame against the San Jose Sharks on Wednesday night, the Anaheim Ducks winger took a feed from Jackson LaCombe and Mikael Granlund and snapped a power-play shot home from just above the left face-off circle for a 3-0 lead — his 23rd goal of the season, pulling him level with Edmonton's Leon Draisaitl for the NHL lead.

The Ducks never looked back. Anaheim scored three goals in 100 seconds in the first period and rolled to a 7-0 win over the Sharks at a sold-out Honda Center, snapping a four-game losing streak in the most emphatic way possible. Laurent Brossoit, recalled from AHL San Diego that morning, made 22 saves for the first shutout by a Ducks goalie in 188 regular-season games — and 200 total games including the playoffs. The last one, coincidentally, also came against the Sharks, when Lukas Dostal blanked them 2-0 in the 2024-25 season opener. The 7-0 margin ties the franchise record for the largest shutout victory, set by the Mighty Ducks against Calgary on December 20, 1996.

Six different Ducks found the net. Judd Caulfield opened the scoring, Alex Killorn scored twice — including a mid-air rebound batted in for the 2-0 lead — and Ian Moore, Roger McQueen and Frank Vatrano added goals alongside Gauthier's. Granlund finished with three assists. Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 23 shots for San Jose, which has now lost two straight.

The record

The goal was Gauthier's 21st in his last 14 games — a pace no American has ever reached, and no player from any country has reached since Mario Lemieux in 1992-93. Since the start of the 1925-26 season, only five other players have scored 21 or more in a 14-game span: Lemieux (twice), Teemu Selanne, Alexander Mogilny, Bernie Nicholls and Wayne Gretzky, who did it three times.

The run started on October 29, when Gauthier scored twice against Buffalo, and it has included back-to-back hat tricks against Ottawa and Vancouver. He is the first player to hit the mark since Lemieux, more than three decades ago.

November is a second record chase running in parallel. The goal was his 19th of the month, making him just the eighth player in NHL history with 19 or more goals in a calendar month and the second American to do it, after Pat LaFontaine — and the first player since Pavel Bure in March 1994. One more ties the all-time calendar-month record of 20, shared by Selanne (March 1993) and Joe Malone (February 1921). It was also his eighth power-play goal of November, tying Paul Kariya (March 2001) and Selanne (February 1999) for the most in a single month in Ducks history.

What it means

This is the fourth Stat Line post on Gauthier's run in under a month, and each one has moved the goalposts — from a goal streak, to hat tricks, to a Ducks record. This one is different: it is not a franchise mark or a hot stretch. It is a league-wide first for an American player, in company that reads like a Hall of Fame ballot.

The Ducks needed the night, too. At 12-13-1 with 25 points, the win moved Anaheim back into the third and final playoff spot in the Pacific Division, over the Sharks, Flames and Kraken. A 7-0 rout with a shutout ends a four-game skid about as loudly as a skid can end.

What's next

Gauthier gets two more cracks at the monthly record this week, and both come against the same opponent. The Ducks open a Thanksgiving weekend home-and-home with the Los Angeles Kings on Friday, November 27, at home, then travel to Crypto.com Arena on Saturday, November 28. One goal ties Selanne and Malone at 20. Two makes him the first player in NHL history with 21 goals in a calendar month.

NFL · Nov 26, 2026 · 5:10 PM ET

Gibbs passes Barry Sanders for most rushing TDs before 25

By Matt

Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 205 yards and three touchdowns on Thanksgiving, and his first score passed Barry Sanders for the most rushing touchdowns by a player before turning 25 — in a 39-35 Lions loss to the Bears.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 205 yards and three touchdowns on 21 carries as the Detroit Lions fell 39-35 to the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving at Ford Field — and his first score of the day put him past Barry Sanders in the record book. The 1-yard run early in the second quarter was the 53rd rushing touchdown of Gibbs' career, passing Sanders for the most by a player before turning 25.

Gibbs also caught five passes for 47 yards, giving him 252 yards from scrimmage on the day. It was his first career 200-yard rushing game — and his second 250-yard game from scrimmage, after the 252 he put up earlier this month against New England.

The record

Gibbs came into Thanksgiving tied with Sanders at 52 career rushing touchdowns, after scoring twice the previous Sunday in Detroit's win over Tampa Bay. One yard was all he needed to move clear.

The path to the mark:

2023 (rookie): 10

2024: 16

2025: 13

2026 (through 10 games): 13

Thanksgiving vs. Chicago: 3

Career total: 55

This is the second Sanders mark Gibbs has taken this season. In the win at Arizona, he passed Sanders for the most total touchdowns — rushing and receiving combined — before age 25, when his 58th career score broke the old mark of 57. Sanders finished his 10-year Lions career with 99 rushing touchdowns.

Gibbs does not turn 25 until March 20, 2027, so he has the rest of the regular season — and any playoff games — to keep adding to the record. The milestone score was also his 16th touchdown of the season, and he finished the day with 18 total touchdowns through 11 games. Since 2000, he is just the third player to record 16 or more touchdowns in three consecutive seasons, joining LaDainian Tomlinson (2003–07) and Shaun Alexander (2001–05).

A Thanksgiving record, in a loss

Gibbs' 205 rushing yards also broke Bob Hoernschemeyer's Lions record of 198 rushing yards in a Thanksgiving game. He did most of the damage after halftime, with 148 of the yards and two of the scores coming in the final two quarters, including a 32-yard run where he reversed direction to escape tacklers.

His third touchdown — a 70-yard sprint midway through the fourth quarter — gave Detroit a 35-24 lead with 8:20 to play. It looked like the game was over. It wasn't.

Chicago answered in three plays, with Caleb Williams finding Rome Odunze for a 41-yard touchdown and then running in the two-point conversion. Williams then engineered the final drive, hitting Odunze for a 6-yard touchdown in the back corner of the end zone with three seconds left — the Bears' first lead of the entire game.

The loss snapped Detroit's six-game winning streak and dropped the Lions to 8-3. Chicago won its sixth straight, improved to 9-2, and took sole possession of first place in the NFC North.

The numbers

Jahmyr Gibbs (DET): 21 carries, 205 yards, 3 TD; 5 catches, 47 yards

Jared Goff (DET): 25/36, 313 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT

Amon-Ra St. Brown (DET): 7 catches, 146 yards

Caleb Williams (CHI): 30/44, 345 yards, 2 TD

Rome Odunze (CHI): 6 catches, 87 yards, 2 TD

What it means

Gibbs is on a historic pace. Through 11 games he has 1,754 yards from scrimmage, projecting out to 2,711 over a 17-game season — which would be a single-season record. He leads the NFL in rushing yards and touchdowns, and he is doing it in a season where Detroit's offense is built around him.

The record is his even in a loss, and it is the kind of number that sticks: passing Barry Sanders in anything, in a Lions uniform, on Thanksgiving, in front of the home crowd. The win went to Chicago, but the day belonged to Gibbs — and with seven weeks left before his 25th birthday, the number is only going up.

NHL · Nov 26, 2026 · 4:45 PM ET

Devils' Brenden Dillon suspended four games for the illegal check to the head that put Denton Mateychuk in concussion protocol

By Matt

The NHL's Department of Player Safety suspended Devils defenseman Brenden Dillon four games without pay for an illegal check to the head of Columbus defenseman Denton Mateychuk on Wednesday night. Mateychuk left the game and entered concussion protocol.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The league moved fast

The NHL's Department of Player Safety announced Thursday that New Jersey Devils defenseman Brenden Dillon has been suspended for four games, without pay, for an illegal check to the head of Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Denton Mateychuk.

The hit came early in the first period of Wednesday night's game in Columbus, with the Devils leading 1-0. Dillon was assessed a match penalty on the play, ending his night after just 3:23 of ice time, and the league scheduled a hearing for Thursday before handing down the four-game ban.

Under the collective bargaining agreement, Dillon will forfeit $82,474.24 in salary. The money goes to the Players' Emergency Assistance Fund.

What the league saw

The Department of Player Safety released its usual explainer video with the ruling, and it did not leave much room for debate. The hit satisfied both elements of the illegal check to the head rule: the head was the main point of contact, and the contact was avoidable.

"Once the puck was gone, Dillon finished a high, hard check, elevating upward and unnecessarily and making Mateychuk's head the main point of contact on a hit where such head contact was avoidable," the league said in the video.

Mateychuk had just moved the puck to a teammate near the blue line and continued into the Columbus zone when Dillon launched his right shoulder into the side of the 22-year-old's head. Mateychuk left the game and did not return, entering concussion protocol. He has been ruled out for the Blue Jackets' game Friday against the Detroit Red Wings.

This is not Dillon's first trip through the process. The 36-year-old veteran had previously been fined once and suspended twice by the league for infractions, which is part of why a four-game ban landed on a hit that, for a first-time offender, might have drawn less.

What it costs New Jersey

Dillon will miss Friday's home game against Calgary, Saturday's home game against Winnipeg, Tuesday's home game against San Jose, and Thursday's trip to Ottawa. He is eligible to return Saturday, Dec. 5, at Pittsburgh.

The timing stings for a Devils team in the middle of a four-games-in-seven-days stretch. New Jersey gutted out a 3-2 shootout win in Columbus on Wednesday despite losing Dillon minutes into the game, but the blue line now has to cover four games without one of its most physical defensemen — and do it while the schedule offers no breathing room.

Gaming · Nov 26, 2026 · 4:44 PM ET

GitHub celebrated a PS5-to-PC tool's GTA 6-fueled boom — then deleted the post

By Matt

GitHub's own X account toasted GTA 6's launch for pushing the AnyPS5 project past a big milestone, signed off 'Happy GTA VImas!' — and asked whether changing where games run crosses a legal line. Then the post vanished, two days after GitHub wiped thousands of unofficial GTA 6 PC-port repos for Take-Two.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

GitHub spent Thanksgiving morning celebrating the exact thing it had just spent the week deleting. The Microsoft-owned platform's official X account posted that GTA 6's launch had sparked "one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on GitHub," congratulating the AnyPS5 project on passing 58,000 stars since its August debut — and signed off with a festive "Happy GTA VImas!" Then, after the screenshots started circulating, the post disappeared.

The deleted post didn't just celebrate a star count. It posed a question to its developer audience that reads very differently coming from the company that hosts the code: "Does changing where games run cross a legal line?" The video attached to the post drove the point home, spotlighting a comment from an AnyPS5 contributor that read, "We have 3 days until GTA 6 everyone […] get your agents or deevs and work." One X user downloaded and re-uploaded the video before the deletion, so the whole thing is preserved anyway.

What AnyPS5 actually is

The headlines calling AnyPS5 a PlayStation 5 emulator are only half right, and the distinction matters. It isn't a traditional emulator that spins up a virtual PS5 operating system. It's an open-source C++ toolkit for static porting — converting PS5 executables into native Windows and Linux binaries. That doesn't make it a GTA 6 PC port on its own, and celebrating its star count isn't the same as endorsing an unauthorized port of the game. But the timing made the celebration land badly: the whole reason AnyPS5's community was sprinting was GTA 6, a game with no PC version, and GitHub's own video said so out loud.

The takedown two days earlier

The deletion looks even stranger against what happened just before it. Two days earlier, GitHub processed a DMCA notice from Take-Two covering the network of repositories behind Project Leonida, the unofficial GTA 6 PC port built from the leaked Xbox executable — removing 3,007 repositories in one sweep. So within the same week, GitHub took down thousands of repos for trying to bring GTA 6 to PC, then used GTA 6 to promote a tool whose community is trying to do the same thing from a different angle, then deleted the promotion.

GitHub and Microsoft have not publicly explained how the post cleared internal review or why it was pulled. IGN noted that GitHub had not responded to its request for comment at the time of publication. The likeliest reading is the simplest one: a social team saw a big open-source milestone tied to the biggest launch in gaming history and posted before anyone in legal had a look. The question it asked — whether changing where games run crosses a legal line — is one Take-Two has already answered for itself, with takedown notices. For now, the post lives on only in screenshots and re-uploads, which is usually how deleted posts end up reaching more people than the original ever would.
