Lenny Kravitz is HITMAN's new client — Bawma brings a voodoo-doll hit to Ambrose Island

By Matt

Lenny Kravitz lends his voice and likeness to Bawma, the Pirate King of Aleph from 007 First Light, in HITMAN's new Elusive Target The Mutiny — free from today through December 24, with a twist: this time, the celebrity is the client, not the target.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Agent 47 has a new client, and for once, the client is doing the briefing himself. Lenny Kravitz makes his World of Assassination debut as Bawma — the Pirate King of Aleph from IO Interactive's 007 First Light — in The Mutiny, a new Elusive Target mission live now in HITMAN World of Assassination through December 24. Kravitz lends both his likeness and his voice to the character, and the twist is the whole point: this time, the celebrity isn't the target. He's the one giving the orders.

Bawma is hiding out on Ambrose Island, and 47's job starts with finding him in the island's ruins and jungles and making contact. From there, Bawma directs the operation himself, staying in 47's ear throughout the mission — a first for the series, where Diana Burnwood normally runs the briefing. The targets are three of Bawma's own rogue lieutenants: Horace Stockton, Oswald Spoon, and Zui. They've turned on the Pirate King, and he wants them dealt with.

The voodoo doll

The signature way to take them down is pure HITMAN. Track down Madame Serafine on the island, gather the ritual ingredients, add them to her Ritual Bowl, and she'll hand you a Voodoo Doll. Then "kill" the doll — stab it, drown it, shoot it, blow it up, throw something sharp at it, set it on fire, or electrocute it — and the target goes down with it. It's one of the most creative elimination methods the series has ever offered, and it fits the mission's bright, upbeat, easygoing holiday tone — one of the most laid-back contracts in the World of Assassination, by IO's own description.

Bawma himself is a long way from a standard HITMAN target. The backstory IO lays out: a former child soldier who built Aleph, a sprawling black-market hub in the Western Hemisphere, into his personal kingdom. He commands fear and respect in equal measure — and he's paid the Agency generously, on one condition: he directs the operation himself.

Free, and what stays after December 24

The Mutiny is free for every HITMAN World of Assassination player, and newcomers can play it through the Free Demo — no full purchase needed. It's live globally on Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, ROG Xbox Ally, PC, and Switch, starting today through Thursday, December 24, 2026.

As with all Elusive Targets, the mission itself leaves the game when it expires. But players who own HITMAN World of Assassination or the Ambrose Island location keep permanent access to The Retaliator, the Arcade version of the mission, plus its Special Assignment, for free. And anyone who completes The Mutiny with an IOI Account while it's live unlocks the Rock Royalty Duck — a regal rubber duck in flashy sunglasses that detonates when it detects motion.

The mission arrives as part of the Season of Bawma, a new roadmap that also brings a fresh Escalation, new Arcade and Special Assignment contracts, Featured Contracts, a new Twitch Drop, returning Elusive Targets, and holiday events. Launching alongside it is the Rockstar Pack, a $5.99 collection of outfits, weapons, gear, and Freelancer Safehouse cosmetics inspired by rock 'n' roll icons — the World Tour Tee, the Rockabilly Suit, the Wildcard Suit, the Wild Rose Baller, the R0-AR Wildcat, a Drum Stick, a Guitar Pick, the Powerchord-A Guitar, and a Pyrotechnic Device.

It's a neat piece of cross-pollination from a studio that now owns both franchises: the breakout character from its James Bond game walks straight into its assassination sandbox, and for once, he's on 47's side. You've got until Christmas Eve to take the contract.

Rockstar explains why GTA 6 judges how you commit crimes — the Criminal Profile, from Professional to Irredeemable

By Matt

Rockstar's Rob Nelson says GTA 6's Criminal Profile grew out of Red Dead Redemption 2 — five tiers that track whether you're a clean professional or a permanent Irredeemable, and change how the cops and your Focus meter treat you.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

GTA 6 doesn't just count your crimes. It judges how you commit them. That's the Criminal Profile — a system that follows Jason and Lucia separately across Leonida, grading every robbery, every takedown, every body you leave behind, and sorting each of them into one of five tiers: Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable. Now Rockstar has explained why it's there, and the answer starts with Red Dead Redemption 2.

Rob Nelson, Rockstar North's co-studio head and head of development, told Eurogamer the studio wanted what players do in the open world to line up with how Jason and Lucia are portrayed in the story. The team was aiming to "build up the sophistication of the NPC population, and also allow for more player choice" — and to add "more options in terms of the way you interact with the world beyond just violence."

The five tiers

The profile is a long-term record of how you consistently approach crime, not a simple body count. A clean job — mask on, alarm disabled, hostages alive, clean getaway — pushes a character toward Professional. Using force that still spares lives lands around Hardened. Harming civilians, killing cops, and finishing off downed enemies slides toward Violent. Sustained, extreme violence earns Psycho. And if you stay there long enough, you hit Irredeemable — the point of no return. There is no natural way back from it; the only fix is reverting to an earlier save.

The tiers aren't just a label on a menu screen. They change how aggressively the police respond to you, and they change what refills your Focus meter — the slow-motion aim that matters in every gunfight. Professional and Hardened refill it through stealth and non-lethal takedowns. Violent and Psycho refill it through headshots. Irredeemable refills it with nothing.

One thing the system doesn't do: it doesn't punish you for the story. Violence inside main story missions doesn't count toward your profile, and neither does genuine self-defense. The profile is about what you choose to do when the game isn't telling you to do it.

Crime fights back now

Nelson also laid out the other half of the design: the world pushes back. In GTA 6, the person you're robbing might not just hand over the cash.

"It's still a world of violence, but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money," Nelson explained. "What if, instead of whipping an RPG out of nowhere, you have to call your car. You have to pop a car trunk and get it, and now I'm walking, and now people are noticing, but they're sort of sidling away, and it's more believable."

Try to hold somebody up and they might pull a gun of their own, or grab yours, and then you have to deal with that. It's the same philosophy that ran through Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor system, taken further: crime in Leonida is supposed to feel dangerous and unpredictable, not free.

The reception has been mixed — some players love that their choices carry weight, others just want to cause chaos without a permanent record of it. There's currently no way to turn the system off, and Rockstar hasn't said whether that option is coming. But the intent is clear now: in GTA 6, the game remembers not just what you did, but how you did it. Play clean and the world treats you like a professional. Go on a rampage long enough, and it decides you're something else entirely — permanently.

420 million hours: GTA 6 is the most-watched game launch in livestreaming history

By Matt

GTA 6 didn't just break sales records. In its first seven days, people watched 420 million hours of it — nearly triple the old record, and more than Valorant, Elden Ring, Diablo IV and Lost Ark drew in their opening weeks combined.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

GTA 6 didn't just sell. It got watched — at a scale livestreaming has never seen. Streams Charts closed the book on the game's first seven days on Tuesday, and the final tally is 420 million hours watched across Twitch, YouTube, Kick and the rest. That is nearly triple the previous first-week record, and it puts the launch in a category of its own.

The old record belonged to Valorant's closed beta in April 2020, at 150.48 million hours. GTA 6 cleared that mark in about two days and kept going. Its seven-day total also beat the combined opening weeks of Valorant, Elden Ring, Diablo IV and Lost Ark — four of the biggest launches of the last six years, added together, still came up short of one week of GTA 6.

The peak was just as absurd

At the busiest point in the first 24 hours, 7.91 million people were watching GTA 6 streams at the same time across platforms. Twitch alone peaked at 3.31 million simultaneous viewers, passing League of Legends' all-time peak for a game category on the platform. Twitch carried the largest share of total watch time, with YouTube and Kick finishing remarkably close to each other behind it.

The two-day checkpoint told the story early. After 48 hours, GTA 6 had already drawn 214.63 million hours watched — more than the combined opening weeks of Elden Ring, Hogwarts Legacy and Cyberpunk 2077, which totaled 186.98 million. The record wasn't close. It was over before the week was half done.

The streamers rode it too

TheBurntPeanut was the most-watched GTA 6 streamer of launch week, generating 11.43 million hours watched across his broadcasts, mostly on YouTube. IShowSpeed drew the most concurrent viewers on a single channel, near the end of a 52-hour marathon that ended with him finishing the story without sleeping, in tears on camera. Spanish streamer IlloJuan recorded the highest combined peak viewership across multiple platforms.

It wasn't just the big names. A total of 1,056 channels broke their all-time peak viewership records while playing GTA 6, and 193 of them pulled at least ten times their previous record audience. The launch didn't just set a record for the game — it reset the ceiling for more than a thousand streamers at once.

The context that makes it land

The viewing record sits alongside the sales records we already covered: GTA 6 cleared $4 billion in its first four days. But the streaming number measures something different. Sales say how many people bought it. Hours watched say how many people couldn't look away from someone else playing it — including millions who don't own a console that can run it yet.

Every launch-week record in the book now has the same name on it: biggest sales, biggest PlayStation launch, and now the most-watched game launch in livestreaming history. The week is over. The numbers are final. And the gap between GTA 6 and everything that came before it is not small.

Kai Cenat launches gaming channel after GTA VI marathon

By Matt

Fresh off a two-week GTA marathon, Kai Cenat opened @KaiCenatGaming — a separate channel for recorded play, horror games, and whatever his viewers ask for next.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Kai Cenat has a new home for his gaming. On November 25, he launched @KaiCenatGaming, a separate YouTube channel built for recorded play — not livestreams — and opened it with a video titled "Welcome To My Gaming Channel..."

The pitch is simple: offline gaming, horror games, and every other genre, with viewers asked to comment what they want to see him play next. Kai said he has plenty lined up but is keeping the specifics secret for now, and that the channel exists for the times he just wants to game and dive deeper into it.

Why now

The launch lands right after one of the biggest gaming events of his career. Kai spent November 5 to 11 playing all five earlier mainline GTA games back to back — GTA III, Vice City, San Andreas, GTA IV, and GTA V — finishing the run in just over 130 hours, ahead of GTA VI's release.

He then moved straight into GTA VI, streaming for roughly 67 hours before finishing the story. The back-to-back marathons turned his GTA run into one of his biggest gaming events yet, and the new channel is the natural next step: a place for the edited, recorded side of that same habit.

Gaming has always been a real share of his output, not a side quest. About 31% of his time streaming games on Twitch across his career has been spent playing video games, with the recent GTA marathons and Minecraft runs making up a large portion of that.

What to expect

Kai framed the channel as a consistency play. In the welcome video, he said he hopes to stay consistent, that he has a lot of fun stuff lined up, and that viewers should tell him what games to play — the channel's direction will follow what the audience asks for.

The first video sets the tone: horror games, fun games, and everything in between, recorded and edited rather than streamed live. The live marathons stay where they are; this channel is where the gaming lives after the stream ends.

Rockstar's UK staff vote against union recognition — 75% say no, a week after GTA 6 launched

By Matt

The ballot that could have made Rockstar's UK workforce the biggest union in British games is over: three in four staff voted against formal recognition, with 93% turnout across five studios.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Rockstar Games will not be recognizing a union. The UK staff at the studio behind Grand Theft Auto 6 voted overwhelmingly against a formal recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union, ending a ballot that ran through the biggest launch week in gaming history.

The result was decisive: 75.3% against, 24.7% in favor. Of the 1,544 employees who voted — a 93.2% turnout across Rockstar's offices in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee, and London — 1,163 voted no and 381 voted yes.

What was on the ballot

The vote was over formal recognition of the Rockstar Game Workers Union, part of the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB). Recognition would have forced Rockstar to collectively bargain with the union over pay and conditions. Had it passed, the union would have become the largest in the UK video game sector, covering more than 1,600 workers at a company of roughly 4,700 employees worldwide.

The ballot opened on November 12 and closed on November 26 — meaning it ran directly through the launch of GTA 6 on November 19, the week the game demolished sales records. The recognition bid itself was announced last month, and the vote was first reported by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, who broke the result on Thursday.

What both sides said

Rockstar's head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, said in a statement to IGN that the company was "extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI." Rockstar said it had worked with the union to facilitate a fair and transparent ballot.

The IWGB, for its part, said its Rockstar workers would keep organizing without formal recognition — the union's campaign doesn't end with the vote, even if the legal status it was seeking does.

Why it matters

This was the highest-profile union vote the games industry has seen. Rockstar is the studio behind the biggest entertainment launch ever, and the vote was watched as a test of whether unionization could take hold at a major AAA developer — especially one whose crunch culture was the subject of intense scrutiny during the Red Dead Redemption 2 era. The answer, from the workforce itself, was no, and by a wide margin.

There's also unfinished business hanging over the result: the ballot overlapped with the closing submissions of an employment tribunal, with judgment still pending. That case, not the vote, is the next thing to watch on the labor side of Rockstar.

One week after launch, GTA 6 is still breaking records. The studio that made it just voted, decisively, to stay as it is.

GTA 6 tops the Japan charts — and hands PS5 a rare win over Switch 2

By Matt

GTA 6 sold more than 200,000 physical copies in its first week in Japan — and the launch pushed PlayStation 5 past Nintendo's Switch 2 in hardware sales, something that almost never happens there.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Grand Theft Auto 6 didn't just conquer the US and UK at launch — it did it in Japan too, in a market where Western games and PlayStation hardware usually play second fiddle to Nintendo. Famitsu's charts for the week of November 16–22 tell the story: GTA 6 debuted at No. 1, and the PS5 outsold the Switch 2.

The game sold 200,759 physical copies in its first week in Japan, debuting at the top of the software chart and finishing more than five times ahead of the No. 2 game, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, at 35,295. It was the only new release to crack the top 10.

A rare hardware win

The bigger shock is on the hardware side. The PlayStation 5 family sold 41,472 units for the week, against 36,817 for the Switch 2 — a PS5 win in a market where Nintendo's machine dominates nearly every week. The PS5 Digital Edition did almost all of the damage on its own, moving 40,362 units, with the PS5 Pro adding 1,031 and the standard PS5 just 79.

For context, the week before, the Switch 2 sold 42,402 units while the PS5 Digital Edition managed only 10,448. GTA 6 flipped the chart in seven days — and, as Push Square put it, this is an incredibly rare scenario that likely won't be repeated again soon.

The Japan caveat

The number comes with a wrinkle: 200,759 physical copies is actually below the Japanese debuts of earlier GTA games — GTA 5 opened with 304,752 in 2013, Vice City with 223,933 in 2004, and San Andreas with 209,974 in 2007. But the comparison isn't clean. Buying habits have shifted hard toward digital in 13 years, and GTA 6's physical release is a code in a box, not a disc — which makes the retail number a floor, not the full picture.

The broader point stands: analysts had questioned before launch whether GTA 6 would land in Japan at all, with one telling Reuters the franchise was a niche pursuit there and the trends didn't fit. Instead it debuted at No. 1, moved the hardware chart, and did it in a week when the game was also lifting console sales in the US and topping the physical charts in the UK.

Launch week keeps finding new ways to be historic. This one just happened in the market everyone said it wouldn't.

NFL · Nov 26, 2026 · 1:09 PM ET

Aaron Rodgers' NFL options dwindling after Steelers divorce

By Matt

Dianna Russini asked around with multiple teams and found no taker for Aaron Rodgers — with the waiver clock running out at 4 p.m. ET today, his final season may already be over.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

No taker

Aaron Rodgers is on waivers, and so far nobody wants him.

NFL insider Dianna Russini checked with teams around the league on Wednesday and came back empty. "I've asked around about Aaron Rodgers with multiple teams," she wrote on X. "Right now, there's no taker. Injuries can change situations in an instant, but in what's supposed to be his final season, his options appear limited."

It is the quiet epilogue to the loudest 24 hours of the season. Rodgers was benched Tuesday night, torched head coach Mike McCarthy on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday morning, and was released by the Steelers about an hour later. Now the four-time MVP is waiting to see whether any team in the league will claim him — and the early answer is no.

The clock

The waiver window closes at 4 p.m. ET on Thursday, November 26. If no team claims him by then, Rodgers becomes a free agent and can sign anywhere.

That is a narrow window by design. With seven weeks left in the regular season and the trade deadline already passed, any team that picks him up is getting a rental for the stretch run — not a building block. And with most of the league either set at quarterback or already out of contention, the list of plausible landing spots is short.

Why nobody's biting

The Patriots and Ravens are the two names that keep surfacing — New England and Baltimore both have quarterback situations worth watching — but neither team has publicly shown interest, and Russini's reporting suggests the interest isn't there privately either.

Part of that is timing. The teams with the biggest holes under center, like the Giants and Vikings, addressed them before the trade deadline. Part of it is the player. Rodgers turns 43 next week and has said all year that 2026 is his final season, so a claim means inheriting the remainder of a one-year, $22.5 million deal for a quarterback who has already announced his exit.

And part of it is the exit itself. Any team that claims him is inviting in a quarterback who just publicly buried his head coach hours after being benched. The talent is not in question — he went 6-4 in 10 starts for Pittsburgh, throwing for 2,241 yards with 16 touchdowns and six interceptions — but the last 24 hours gave every front office a reason to pass.

Has he played his last game?

Clay Matthews, who spent 10 seasons alongside Rodgers in Green Bay, thinks the answer might be yes. Working as a Netflix analyst before the Packers-Rams game on Wednesday night, Matthews was asked whether fans had already seen Rodgers' last game.

"I think this is the last time we see him," Matthews said. "I don't think another team wants him as a QB right now."

That is not a report — it is one former teammate's read. But it lands the same way Russini's reporting does: the league has had a day to make a move on a four-time MVP, and nobody has.

The waiver deadline is the next inflection point. If the clock runs out at 4 p.m. and Rodgers clears, he becomes a free agent — still available to any team, still one injury away from a phone call. Russini's caveat is the only opening left: injuries change situations in an instant. Until one does, the most decorated quarterback of his generation is out of a job in the final weeks of his final season.

Gaming · Nov 26, 2026 · 12:46 PM ET

GTA 6 hides a ghost ship — and a cursed knife at the bottom of the sea

By Matt

A haunted lighthouse on the far edge of Leonida hides a century-old murder, a sunken wreck, and a Legendary melee weapon — and if you climb back up after 1 AM, the ghost ship itself sails past.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

GTA 6 has ghosts. Not the kind in your car — an actual ghost ship on the high seas, at the end of one of the most elaborate Easter eggs in the game. Players have mapped the whole thing now: a haunted lighthouse on the far northeastern edge of Leonida, two arguing specters, a century-old murder, and a Legendary melee weapon sitting on a skeleton at the bottom of the ocean.

It starts at the St. Lucia Lighthouse on Little Hardin Island, in Leonard County. Head there at night — after 10 PM — and you'll hear two men arguing somewhere above you. Climb to the top and you can watch them: two green ghosts scuffling in the lamp room until one of them is shoved off the edge.

The murder of Godfrey and Frank

The ghosts aren't random. Come back down and there's a photograph at the foot of the lighthouse stairs. Flip it over and it's dated 1909: Godfrey Asher, the assistant keeper, and Frank Pudney, the head keeper.

The rest of the story is in a ruined house on a small island northwest of the lighthouse. Break in, turn right, and a blue journal falls from the fireplace. The logbook tells of a storm, a strange chest that washed ashore, and Godfrey's growing obsession with it — the same obsession that ended with one keeper dead and the other haunted.

The Cursed Knife

The journal points east. Get in a boat with scuba gear and sail out from the lighthouse, and the sea turns on you: fog rolls in, a storm builds, and your engine cuts out. That's the spot. Dive down with your metal detector and you'll find a sunken boat on the ocean floor — and the Cursed Knife in the hands of a skeleton.

It's a Legendary melee weapon, and it's yours once you surface. But the egg isn't over.

The ghost ship

Climb back to the top of the lighthouse after 1 AM and look northeast with your binoculars. The ship is out there — a glowing green vessel sailing through the dark — and it disappears fast, so have the binoculars ready before you reach the top.

A few things to know before you go: you'll need a boat with scuba gear, or the Key Cloner to steal one from a dock on the island. The lighthouse is also a WAiNK Landmark, so scan it while you're there. And the guides note you may need to do the whole thing solo, as just Jason or just Lucia.

One week after launch, the Easter egg hunt is its own game inside the game. The Mario hats were the first prize everyone chased. A ghost ship and a cursed knife are the next one.

No disc, no problem: GTA 6 is the UK's biggest physical launch since 2019 — £32 million in three days

By Matt

The box holds a download code, not a disc — and it still outsold every physical launch in Britain since 2019. The no-disc gamble didn't slow GTA 6 down at the till. It barely registered.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Rockstar made the most controversial packaging decision in modern gaming history: Grand Theft Auto VI has no disc. The physical edition is a box with a download code inside. Fans argued about it for months — and then went out and bought it anyway. In its first three days on sale in the UK, GTA 6 took £32 million at retail, making it the biggest physical game launch in Britain since FIFA 20 in September 2019, according to NielsenIQ data reported by The Game Business.

That is a code in a box outselling every disc launch of the last seven years.

The all-time list tells the story

GTA 6 now ranks No. 17 for first-week boxed revenue in the UK since records began in 1995 — only 16 titles in three decades have taken more in their opening week, and the most recent of those was FIFA 19 in 2018. Its predecessors still sit ahead of it: GTA V is No. 1 all-time and GTA IV is No. 11. Launch day alone, Thursday, November 19, ranked as the 20th biggest day in UK games retail revenue since NielsenIQ's records began in 2000.

The concentration was extreme. GTA 6 accounted for around 74 percent of all physical software revenue in the UK that week, and 88 percent of its own first-week sales came on launch day. People did not trickle in over the weekend. They showed up on Thursday.

The whole shop came with it

The launch lifted everything around it. Total UK games retail revenue hit £142 million across the three-day launch period, up 99 percent week on week. Boxed software revenue reached £43 million — a 409 percent jump and the biggest week for physical games since Christmas 2018.

Hardware rode the same wave. Console sales rose 38 percent to their highest level since late 2025, with PlayStation 5 up 46 percent and Xbox Series up 75 percent week on week. Accessories generated £21 million, up 123 percent. Joypad volumes jumped 194 percent — PS5 pads alone were up 355 percent — headset volumes rose 94 percent, and external console SSDs had their biggest week of 2026 so far.

The context that makes it land

Here is the number that frames all of it: boxed software accounts for just 15 percent of UK games retail revenue so far in 2026, down from 50 percent in 2008. Physical is a shrinking slice of the market — and GTA 6 just posted one of the biggest physical weeks ever inside that shrinking slice. As NielsenIQ's Dorian Bloch put it, the performance shows the enduring retail power of one of gaming's biggest franchises, even as the market shifts toward digital downloads.

It was not just Britain, either. The Game Business reports more than a million boxed copies sold in France in three days, and the biggest physical launch in Spanish chart history. And the migration was visible on the other side of the industry too: VGC notes live-service games took a hit after launch, with players leaving Call of Duty, Fortnite and other online games to play through GTA 6. One game that benefited was GTA 5, which saw its own sales rise.

The digital numbers already told us GTA 6 was the biggest launch in entertainment history — the Alinea Analytics estimate we covered Monday put it at 44.9 million copies in four days. The UK retail data adds the part nobody was sure about: the box still matters. Rockstar bet that players would pay full price for a box with no disc in it, and the tills answered in three days.

GTA 6 patch fixes phone calls, but one softlock remains

By Matt

Update 01.002.002 fixes the phone calls that were blocking story progress in GTA 6 — but the Chapter 3 Missing Persons softlock is still live, and the only way out is an older manual save.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

GTA 6's latest patch fixed one of launch week's most annoying bugs — and left the worst one untouched. Update 01.002.002, released November 23, fixes several issues that kept phone calls from triggering correctly, including calls that progress the story or unlock mission content. But if you've hit the Chapter 3 Missing Persons softlock, the patch does nothing for you. Jason is still greyed out, and the only reliable way out players have found is an older manual save.

What the patch fixed — and what it didn't

The patch notes are clear about the phone-call fixes. What they don't mention is Missing Persons, or character switching at all. Rockstar has not commented on the softlock, and as of November 26 there is no newer patch — the company's Launch Updates page was still last updated November 23.

That leaves the Missing Persons lock as the game's most-reported blocker. On the community bug tracker GTA6Bugs, the Chapter 3 softlock is the most-viewed entry, and it's confirmed on both PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

How the softlock happens

Early in Chapter 3, the game locks you to Jason for a stretch while it sends you to meet Boobie in Vice City. You're free to roam and do side activities during that window — and that's the trap.

If you finish the Kelly County Missing Persons side case during that Jason-only stretch, the case's ending forces a switch to Lucia. The problem is the switch doesn't give Jason back. He stays greyed out on the character wheel, he won't answer the phone, and Lucia has no story mission to play. The story stalls completely.

Players have tried the obvious escapes — leaving the house, saving and reloading, asking Jason to meet up, sleeping — and none of them worked.

The way out

There is no official fix yet. The workaround players report working is to load a manual save made before the final Missing Persons meeting at the warehouse in Port Gellhorn. Your latest autosave won't help if it was made after the lock — it already carries the broken state.

The steps, as reported by Game Rant, Polygon, and the HUDWire guide:

1. Save the stuck game in a new slot first. Don't overwrite an older save — you may need the stuck save if Rockstar patches the bug.

2. Load a manual save from before you drove to the warehouse in Port Gellhorn for the final Missing Persons meeting.

3. Leave the warehouse marker alone. As Jason, play the Dealer's Choice mission upstairs at the Jack of Hearts until you can switch to Lucia freely, then make a manual save in a new slot.

4. Only then finish Missing Persons.

One unconfirmed trick — calling Lucia's contact Dunk — worked for some players, though others report no luck with it.

The simplest advice, if you haven't hit it yet: don't finish Missing Persons until you can freely switch between Jason and Lucia. And make a manual save in a new slot before every story mission — it's the best protection against this and the game's other remaining blockers until Rockstar ships a fix.

FaZe are out of the PGL Singapore Major at 1-3 — HEROIC end their season in Stage 1

By Matt

HEROIC beat FaZe 2-1 in the elimination series on Thursday, dumping one of Counter-Strike's biggest names out of the PGL Major Singapore at 1-3 — 28th to 30th in a 32-team field, and FaZe's worst Major finish since IEM Rio 2022.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

FaZe Clan are out of the PGL Major Singapore. HEROIC beat them 2-1 in a Stage 1 elimination series on Thursday — Mirage 13-3, Ancient 13-11 to FaZe, Nuke 13-3 — and the 1-3 record leaves FaZe 28th to 30th in a 32-team Major, their worst finish at a Major since IEM Rio 2022. PGL confirmed the exit on X at 08:42 UTC, minutes after HEROIC closed out the deciding map.

It is the end of a season that started with promise and fell apart. FaZe were not even at the IEM Cologne Major in June — they missed out through Valve's standings — and Singapore was their only Major of 2026. A year earlier they reached the grand final of the StarLadder Budapest Major, losing 3-1 to Team Vitality. This time they never left the first stage.

How HEROIC knocked them out

The series opened on FaZe's pick of Mirage, and it was over almost before it started. HEROIC won it 13-3, and FaZe were one map from elimination inside the first hour. FaZe answered on HEROIC's pick of Ancient, taking it 13-11, and the team account quickly posted that FaZe still had life.

Nuke, the map left over after both sides made their bans, ended the series in one direction. HEROIC won it 13-3, the same score as the opener, and FaZe managed only six rounds across the two maps they lost. HEROIC wasted little time on X, pointing FaZe toward the airport minutes after the win.

It is not the first time HEROIC have ended a FaZe Major either — they also beat FaZe 2-1 in the quarterfinals of the 2023 Paris Major.

A week that never got going

FaZe's Major began badly on November 24, when Wildcard beat them 13-9 on Nuke in the opening round. The first three rounds of Stage 1 are best-of-one matches, so a single bad map was enough to push FaZe straight into the 0-1 pool. They recovered later that day with a 13-3 win on Mirage over GOSH, the former BC.Game roster that includes s1mple, after s1mple's team had already lost to Team Liquid.

The second day brought another best-of-one defeat, this time 13-10 to PARIVISION on Anubis. That loss dropped FaZe into the 1-2 pool, and the Stage 1 Day 2 results paired them with HEROIC. Across six maps in Singapore, FaZe won 51 rounds and lost 66.

The numbers tell the same story as the scorelines. David "frozen" Čerňanský led FaZe with a 1.06 rating in the elimination series — top of the board for his team — but he went missing on the decider with a 0-9 start on the offense. Captain Russel "Twistzz" Van Dulken finished at 1.00, and AWPer Jason "JBOEN" Boe Nielsen at 0.76. On the other side, HEROIC's Linus "nilo" Bergman led all players at 1.24, with Tim "susp" Ångström and Ludvig "Brollan" Brolin both at 1.22.

Twistzz took the blame — and the roster's future is open

Twistzz did not hide after the loss. Speaking on the PGL broadcast, he said FaZe were "not a team that felt extremely competitive coming into this event" and that "throughout the season we regressed a lot as a team and maybe even individually." He took responsibility as captain and said he needed more out of a young lineup that features two Major rookies in JBOEN and Ryan "Neityu" Aubry.

"I'm not the most experienced captain, and I do my best work when I have a second voice to ping-pong with," he said. "I can tell people are pressured, nervous, I have to speak and I have to create ideas for them to move on the map."

He said the same thing on X after the match: "Said most of my thoughts in the post game. Disappointing to see where we are at and it's a shame to see the faze name far down in the ranks. See everyone next season."

frozen was shorter: "Shameful. Nothing else to say, see you next season."

The questions now are real ones. Twistzz's future as in-game leader is under scrutiny after a season in which he took over following Finn "karrigan" Andersen's surprise departure in April — karrigan went on to lift the Cologne trophy as a Falcons stand-in. JBOEN is only on loan from BIG, a loan that runs until the end of 2026, and he told Dust2.dk after the exit that his situation "has been uncertain in FaZe the whole time" and that he feels like he has "already got one and a half legs out of the camp, unfortunately." frozen, meanwhile, has reportedly been pursued by several organizations over the last year, and signed an extension only weeks before karrigan left.

The season that led here

The early exit ends what HLTV called another disappointing season for FaZe. It started in promising fashion despite karrigan's exit, with back-to-back top-four finishes in the team's first two outings in China and Malta with Twistzz taking over in-game leadership. Then it fell apart: FaZe could not make it past the top 16 in any of their top event outings, finishing 13th to 16th at the Esports World Cup, FISSURE Playground 3, and IEM Beijing at the start of November, where they lost both series 2-1 to FURIA and Falcons. On November 15 they lost to fnatic and HEROIC in the closed qualifier for PGL Cluj-Napoca 2027.

The early exit also cuts into FaZe's share of the Major Shop money. Valve's Singapore Major update says half of the proceeds from tournament items go to players, teams and the organiser, shared according to each team's initial seed and final placement — and a finish near the bottom of the field puts FaZe close to the bottom of that split, at a time when sticker money for teams is already under scrutiny.

HEROIC move to 2-2 and play again on November 27 for a place in Stage 2, alongside a Day 3 that also saw Team Liquid, Eternal Fire and PARIVISION through. Stage 1 finishes on November 27, and the Major moves to the Singapore Indoor Stadium for the playoffs from December 10 to 13. FaZe had not announced any roster changes by the time of writing.

GTA 6 didn't just sell copies — it sold consoles: PS5 sales ran 2.4x last year's pace the week before launch

By Matt

In the week ending November 14 — five days before Grand Theft Auto VI even launched — U.S. PlayStation 5 sales ran more than 2.4 times last year's pace and Xbox Series sales more than 2.3 times, according to Circana. And that happened after console prices jumped $100 to $150 in a year.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Grand Theft Auto VI sold 32.5 million copies by launch and roughly $4 billion on day one. That part we knew. The part that landed this week is what it did to the hardware sitting underneath it: in the week ending November 14 — five days before the game was even playable — U.S. PlayStation 5 unit sales ran more than 2.4 times the same week last year, and Xbox Series X|S sales ran more than 2.3 times, according to Circana retail data shared by analyst Mat Piscatella.

People bought the machine before they could buy the game. The launch-week surge was a pre-launch surge.

The prices went up. The buyers came anyway.

This is the detail that makes the numbers land. A year ago, a standard PS5 cost $550. Today it costs $650. The PS5 Pro went from $750 to $900. Xbox Series X jumped from $650 to $800, and the Series S from $400 to $500. That is $100 to $150 more per box, across the board — and hardware still more than doubled its year-ago pace.

Piscatella himself had predicted before launch that GTA 6 would lift console sales, but maybe not dramatically, precisely because of those prices. The market disagreed. For the biggest release in entertainment history, the price tag was not the obstacle — not having a machine to play it on was.

The PS5 Pro, notably, was not the driver: it made up less than 10 percent of PlayStation unit sales that week. This was the standard PS5 doing the work — the $650 box, bought by people who needed somewhere to play Vice City.

Even the Switch 2 got a lift — without the game

The one console that cannot play GTA 6 also surged. Nintendo Switch 2 hardware sales rose more than 40 percent over the same week last year, per the same Circana data. Eurogamer credits that to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and a special-edition Zelda Switch 2 console landing in the same window — a reminder that the week before GTA 6 was a big hardware week across the board, not just a two-console story.

Two straight weeks of doubling

The week ending November 14 was not a one-off. Circana data reported the prior week showed the same shape — PS5 sales more than 2.4 times the year-ago week, Xbox more than 2.3 times — for the week ending November 7, as buyers started preparing for the November 19 launch. Two consecutive weeks of hardware running at more than double last year's pace, both of them before the game was out.

The full picture arrives with Circana's November U.S. report in December, which will show whether the lift held through launch week itself and how much of the market moved beyond the one game. But the pre-launch evidence already answers the question the industry was asking all year: whether a single game could still move hardware at these prices. It did — by more than double.

Esports World Cup 2027 names its first five games — League of Legends, Valorant, Fatal Fury, Chess and Dota 2

By Matt

The Esports Foundation has unveiled the first five titles for the 2027 Esports World Cup: League of Legends, Valorant, Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves, Chess and Dota 2 return for the summer event, with more titles, qualifiers and Club Championship details still to come.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The 2027 Esports World Cup is starting to take shape. The Esports Foundation announced on November 25 the first five titles for next summer's tournament: League of Legends, Valorant, Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves, Chess and Dota 2. The event runs in July and August 2027, with more titles, qualification pathways, tournament schedules and Club Championship details to be revealed in the coming weeks.

All five are returning titles, not debuts — and each one carries a storyline into next summer.

League of Legends: can anyone break the Korean streak?

League of Legends returns for a fourth consecutive year, and South Korea has owned it from the start. Three different Korean teams have lifted the trophy in three editions — T1, Gen.G, and most recently Dplus KIA, who won the 2026 edition in Paris. All three also reached the quarterfinals at the recent League of Legends World Championship, which Bilibili Gaming won. The big question for 2027 is whether BLG, the reigning world champions, can become the first Chinese team to win the League of Legends title at the Esports World Cup.

Valorant: 100 Thieves defend an undefeated run

Valorant is back after a 2026 edition won by 100 Thieves, who finished the tournament undefeated and beat world champions NRG in the final. The Foundation expects 100 Thieves, NRG, LOUD, Paper Rex, Team Vitality, Team Liquid and 2026 Club Champion AG.AL among the field again in 2027.

Fatal Fury and Chess: the three-timers

Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves and Chess have both been included as official titles for three consecutive years. NAVI's Luis Guadalupe "DarkAngel" Castillo Gomez won the Fatal Fury title at the 2026 event. In Chess, Magnus Carlsen has won two straight — defending his title undefeated at the 2026 tournament, with AG.AL's Denis Lazavik finishing runner-up.

Dota 2: no repeat winner yet

Dota 2 returns for a fourth consecutive year, and it remains the most wide-open title on the slate. Three different clubs with three completely different rosters have lifted the trophy over the past three iterations, and no club or player has ever won it twice. PVISION claimed the championship at the 2026 event after a semifinal defeat the year before.

What else is confirmed

Two more titles have already been confirmed separately for 2027 through the Esports World Cup's own press room: Counter-Strike 2, which returns for 2027 and 2028, and Street Fighter 6, back for a fourth consecutive year. The Foundation says it will reveal additional titles, qualification routes and the Club Championship structure over the coming weeks. AG.AL claimed the 2026 Club Championship in Paris, a seven-week event featuring more than 2,000 players, 200 clubs and 25 tournaments.

The first five are the spine of the 2027 event. The rest of the lineup — and whether anyone can finally take a title off Korea in League of Legends — comes next.

Rockstar reveals what GTA 6 cut: tennis, cinema trips, home decorating, crafting — and why each one went

By Matt

A week after launch, Rockstar North's Rob Nelson and Scott Mitchell told PC Games what GTA 6 left on the cutting-room floor: tennis that didn't meet the bar, cinema trips that weren't interactive enough, and a home life that didn't fit the story.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, and Rockstar is already telling players what is not in it. In an interview published November 25 with the German outlet PC Games, Rockstar North development manager Rob Nelson and design producer Scott Mitchell laid out the features that were planned or prototyped and then dropped before launch — and none of them were cut for time alone. Each one failed a different test.

The list, as the two developers laid it out: tennis, cinema and theatre visits, crawling, home decorating, and crafting.

Tennis is the cut that stings most

Tennis is the one players have actually played before. The sport was in GTA 5, and Rockstar built a version for GTA 6. Then the studio looked at it and decided it was not good enough to ship, so the minigame went entirely. Mini golf, the other country-club pastime, survived and is in the finished game — which makes the tennis decision feel deliberate instead of careless. Rockstar would rather have one good minigame than two where one is a disappointment.

Cinema trips weren't interactive enough

The cinema and theatre visits went for the opposite reason. GTA 5 let players sit down and watch short films in Los Santos, but the developers felt that kind of activity was not interactive enough to earn a place in GTA 6. Rockstar has steered this game toward things players actively do with Jason and Lucia instead — dates at the gym or a bar, missions built around the couple.

There is an irony here, because GTA 6 already has televisions playing cartoons and reality shows in Jason's house, and players can sit down and play entire games on the JoySystem. Rockstar drew a line between watching something on a couch at home, which fits the fantasy of two people living together, and buying a ticket to watch something in a dark room, which does not.

The home life that didn't fit

The home-life ideas are the most revealing cuts of all. At various points Jason and Lucia could crawl across the floor, furnish their safehouse, and craft items. The team also specced out a system where the couple restocked their own fridge with grocery runs, then pulled it to keep daily life simple. None of it fit the story Rockstar wanted to tell or the way the game actually plays, so all of it went.

The developers said they are proudest of the relationship between the two leads, and that Red Dead Redemption 2's slower pacing inspired GTA 6 to make room for quiet moments between the chaos. The cuts were not about removing life from the game. They were about protecting the parts of that life that matter to the story.

What wasn't cut — and what to ignore

One thing to be careful about: several posts on social media added darts to the list of cut activities overnight. The PC Games interview does not mention darts at all, and the claim could not be traced to anything a Rockstar developer has said on the record. Treat it as unconfirmed until Rockstar addresses it directly.

It is the same instinct behind the no-mission-replay call Rockstar explained the same week: if a feature clashed with the story the game is telling, it went, even if players expected it. Cut features do not always stay cut, but Rockstar has made no promises about any of these returning — not in single-player updates, and not in GTA 6's online mode, which still has no official release date.

Until Rockstar says more, the PC Games interview is the clearest official account of what was left out — and the clearest window yet into what Rockstar thinks this game is supposed to be.

Wizards Seeks Up to $28.65M Over Fake Magic Cards

By Matt

Wizards of the Coast filed a 97-page federal lawsuit against a Utah printing operation it says sold counterfeit Magic: The Gathering cards disguised as proxies, seeking up to $28.65 million in statutory damages.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Wizards of the Coast is going to war over fake Magic cards — and the number attached to the fight is massive.

The company filed a 97-page federal lawsuit on November 23, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington, accusing a Utah printing operation called PrintMTG Enterprise of running a counterfeit-card ring disguised as a proxy business. Wizards is seeking up to $28.65 million in statutory copyright damages.

What Wizards alleges

The complaint names Ryan James Dunn and other defendants, who Wizards says run a print shop in Springville, Utah behind a network of differently named websites. The cards were sold as "proxies" — stand-in cards players print to test decks or play casually — but Wizards says they were made to be mistaken for the real thing.

That distinction is the whole case. Proxies are a normal, widely accepted part of Magic: a clearly marked stand-in for a card you don't own yet. A counterfeit, in Wizards' definition, is made to be mistaken for a real card and to take its place as something owned, traded, or sold. The suit quotes PrintMTG's own ProxyKing.biz site against it: "At Proxy King we try to make our proxies as realistic as possible. This lets you join games and play without people noticing you are running proxy cards in your Magic deck."

The complaint's own language is blunt: "They intend that the people who encounter their product after the sale, including opponents, judges, retailers, and later purchasers, will mistake it for Wizards' genuine product."

How far the copying allegedly went

The filing covers 191 Magic sets, including 46 designs from Limited Edition Beta (1993), 20 from the original Zendikar, and 68 from Modern Horizons 2. Wizards says the operation copied card backs as well as faces — and on rares and mythic rares, reproduced the security hologram, right down to the trademark printed inside it.

The alleged operation went beyond cards. The suit says the same network sold fake Pokémon cards and Lego minifigures, ran an Etsy storefront offering Pokémon proxies, and operated sticker-selling sites — YouStickers.com and CustomStickers.com — that Wizards alleges were used to launder money from the card sales. It also accuses the group of hijacking website domains: one site, KrakenOpus.com, was a luxury publishing operation whose domain was turned into an MTG news site with links directing visitors to a proxy-printing site.

The charges

The complaint brings claims including copyright infringement, trademark counterfeiting and trademark infringement, a civil RICO claim alleging mail fraud, wire fraud, and money laundering, and a violation of the Washington Consumer Protection Act. Beyond the damages figure, Wizards is asking the court to shut the operation down, seize the printing equipment, and order the defendants to stop.

The statutory math behind the headline figure: on the copyright claims alone, Wizards says it could recover up to $150,000 per work for willful infringement. Across 191 works, that is where the maximum comes from. It is a ceiling, not a guaranteed payout — and the defendants had not publicly responded to the allegations as of this writing.

Why this one matters

Wizards has sued over counterfeits before, but this case is different in scope: a whole alleged enterprise, not a single seller, with its own storefronts, domains, and laundering infrastructure. And the timing matters for players. Realistic fakes have been circulating on eBay, Temu, and other marketplaces for years, largely unchecked — and every fake that enters the singles market undercuts both retailers selling real sealed product and players who might pay real-card prices for a forgery.

If Wizards prevails, the case could become the template for future litigation against other proxy printers who cross the line from stand-in to forgery. The message to the proxy community is narrow but clear: Wizards is not suing over proxies themselves. It is suing over cards designed to pass as real.

TSL Bets: The Thanksgiving night parlay (~+248) — Cook anytime TD, Rice OVER 46.5 receiving yards

By Matt

James Cook has scored in five straight games and Rashee Rice has gone over 46.5 receiving yards in 8 of his last 10 — including all three meetings with Buffalo. Two legs, about +248, under the lights in Orchard Park.

The game

Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) at Buffalo Bills (9-1) — 8:20 PM ET, Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park, NY (NBC/Peacock)

Bills -3 (-102), total 46.5 (Over -108 / Under -110), moneyline Bills -150 / Chiefs +125 (BetMGM via USA Today Sportsbook Wire, November 25). Forecast: rain, mid-30s, wind gusts up to 24 mph.

Injuries — Kansas City: RB Kenneth Walker III OUT (groin — third straight game missed). OT Jaylon Moore OUT (ankle). DT Omarr Norman-Lott OUT (knee). FB Ben VanSumeren OUT (knee). TE Noah Gray QUESTIONABLE (rib). DT Peter Woods QUESTIONABLE (neck). QB Patrick Mahomes CLEARED (knee/right elbow — full practice). WR Rashee Rice CLEARED (knee — full practice). G Trey Smith CLEARED (concussion — full practice).

Injuries — Buffalo: CB Christian Benford QUESTIONABLE (groin — missed Week 11). TE Dalton Kincaid QUESTIONABLE (thumb/ankle). DL T.J. Sanders QUESTIONABLE (shoulder). G O'Cyrus Torrence QUESTIONABLE (ankle). LB Dorian Williams QUESTIONABLE (calf).

Storylines: This is the first home Thanksgiving game in Bills franchise history, and the AFC's top seed is on the line — Buffalo is 9-1, Kansas City 8-2, the third-highest combined winning percentage (.850) in a Thanksgiving game since 1950. Buffalo has won the last five regular-season meetings; Kansas City owns the postseason, with four straight playoff wins over Josh Allen's Bills. Mahomes has been surgical since Week 8: 1,235 passing yards, 13 touchdowns, zero interceptions, with 300-plus yards, three touchdowns and no picks in four separate games this season. Allen threw for 304 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions against Miami last week, and the Bills have won six straight. With Walker out again, rookie Emmett Johnson starts at running back for Kansas City for the third straight game.

Leg 1 — James Cook anytime touchdown

Cook has a rushing touchdown in each of his last five games — one apiece against Miami, the Jets, Minnesota, Baltimore and Las Vegas — and 10 rushing touchdowns this season. He has scored in 9 of his last 10, and in 3 of 6 against this opponent. He ran for 89 yards and a touchdown against Miami last week. Odds Index's model puts his touchdown chance at 56.0% against 52.6% implied by the price, and rates this one HIGH. Line: anytime touchdown (-111, Odds Index; -110, DraftKings via SI Betting).

Leg 2 — Rashee Rice OVER 46.5 receiving yards

Rice has 40-plus receiving yards in five straight games (53, 82, 49, 53, 88) and has gone over this line in 8 of his last 10 — and in all three meetings with Buffalo, including a career-best 80 yards against them. His target share is 24%, and Buffalo's top corner, Christian Benford, is questionable with a groin injury after missing Week 11. Mahomes has thrown 13 touchdowns without an interception since Week 8, and Rice is his first read. Line: OVER 46.5 receiving yards (-120, Odds Index).

The bet

James Cook anytime touchdown (-111, Odds Index) + Rashee Rice OVER 46.5 receiving yards (-120, Odds Index) — about +248. A $10 ticket returns about $34.85.

Why these legs

Both legs clear on their own. Cook is a near-even-money touchdown scorer on a five-game scoring streak, and Rice is a yardage prop with a five-game floor, a 3-for-3 record against this opponent, and a banged-up corner across from him. Neither leg depends on the other — different players, different sides of the ball, different markets. That is the juice rule working as intended: two props with real trend edges, about +248 instead of the chalky +150 you get from stacking favorites.

The honest caveats

The weather is the shared risk — rain, mid-30s, wind gusts to 24 mph in Orchard Park can suppress the passing game, and Rice's leg is the exposed one. Both legs live in the same game, so one bad night in Buffalo sinks both. Cook's touchdown depends on red-zone touches in a game Buffalo could win through the air, and Rice's knee was on the injury report this week even though he practiced in full and is cleared. And a parlay needs both legs — either one can sink it alone. The edge is real, but it is an edge, not a lock.

The record

By Matt

The game slip

Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) at Dallas Cowboys (5-6)

Thursday, 4:30 PM ET — AT&T Stadium, Arlington, TX (FOX)

• Spread: Cowboys -8.5 (-110)

Injury report — Cowboys: TE Jake Ferguson OUT (knee/ankle). RG Tyler Booker OUT (ankle). WR Jonathan Mingo OUT (ankle). S P.J. Locke OUT (concussion). CB Devin Moore QUESTIONABLE (hip). S Jalen Thompson QUESTIONABLE (hamstring).

Dak Prescott OVER 249.5 passing yards (-196, Odds Index)

Why this prop

The trend and the matchup point the same way. Philadelphia's offense cannot keep up — Milton averages 155 yards a game — so Dallas should have the ball plenty, and the Eagles' defense is 18th in scoring defense (23.7 points a game) and 21st in total defense. And Dallas is an 8.5-point favorite: if the Cowboys pull away early the way they did against Tennessee, the fourth quarter belongs to the backups and the clock. Bears-Lions for First Place Opens Thanksgiving Tripleheader

By Matt

The 8-2 Bears visit the 8-2 Lions at 1 PM ET on CBS with first place in the NFC North on the line, opening a Thanksgiving tripleheader that runs through Eagles-Cowboys and Chiefs-Bills.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Thanksgiving football opens with a game that actually decides something. The 8-2 Chicago Bears visit the 8-2 Detroit Lions at 1 PM ET on CBS, and the winner walks out of Ford Field in sole possession of first place in the NFC North.

Both teams arrive on the two longest active winning streaks in the NFC — five straight for Chicago, six for Detroit — and this is just the fourth time in 193 all-time meetings that both clubs have entered at least six games over .500.

The stakes

The division lead is the headline, but the seeding underneath it matters too. The winner takes the inside track in the NFC North with the stretch run ahead; the loser drops to second, a game back, and hands its rival the head-to-head tiebreaker. Chicago hasn't started a season this well in 20 years, and Detroit is 6-0 at home this season.

The rest of the tripleheader

The holiday slate keeps going after the opener:

Bears at Lions: 1:00 PM; CBS

Eagles at Cowboys: 4:30 PM; Fox

Chiefs at Bills: 8:20 PM; NBC

Three games, three networks, one full day of football.

Why this one stands out

Thanksgiving in Detroit is a tradition, but a first-place showdown this late in November is not the usual holiday fare. The Bears have won five straight behind a defense that has thrived since the Jeffery Simmons trade, while the Lions have won six in a row with one of the league's most explosive offenses. Both teams are playing their best football of the season at the same time — and only one of them leaves Thursday in first.

NHL · Nov 26, 2026 · 5:08 AM ET

Marchand, Barkov return as Panthers beat Senators 5-3

By Matt

Brad Marchand had three assists and Aleksander Barkov scored into an empty net as both returned from knee injuries to lift the Florida Panthers past the Ottawa Senators 5-3.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Brad Marchand had three assists and Aleksander Barkov scored into an empty net as both returned from knee injuries to lift the Florida Panthers past the Ottawa Senators 5-3 at Amerant Bank Arena on Wednesday night.

The returns

Marchand had missed 20 games since sustaining a knee injury in a 2-1 win at the Los Angeles Kings on Oct. 6. Barkov, the Panthers captain, had been out 22 games after a knee injury of his own, sustained in a 4-3 overtime loss at the San Jose Sharks on Oct. 1.

Barkov's road back was the longer one. He missed the entire 2025-26 season with a right knee injury, then hurt his left knee in the second game of this season. Wednesday was just the sixth regular-season game with both him and Marchand in the lineup — and the first since the 2024-25 season. It was the first time the two have dressed together since Florida's Stanley Cup-clinching win in 2025, and the first regular-season game with Barkov, Marchand, Seth Jones, Matthew Tkachuk and Brady Tkachuk all in the lineup at once.

Marchand wasted no time making his presence felt. When his name was announced for the assist on the opening goal, the crowd got to its feet.

How it went down

Marchand set up Eetu Luostarinen at 16:16 of the first, getting to a puck behind the net and sending a backhanded feed through the goal mouth. Ottawa answered with two goals 41 seconds apart early in the second — Dylan Cozens at 1:12, then Philip Tomasino splitting two Florida defenders on a rush at 1:53 — to take a 2-1 lead.

Niko Mikkola tied it midway through the second, fighting to the front of the net to deflect a Matthew Tkachuk point shot past Linus Ullmark. Then Marchand drove up the ice and fed Anton Lundell charging the goal at 18:55, and Lundell buried his own rebound for the lead going into the third.

Sam Bennett made it 4-2 on the power play at 9:17 of the third, and Barkov sealed it with the empty-netter at 16:08 — his first goal of the season. Michael Amadio pulled one back for Ottawa at 19:09 with Ullmark pulled for the extra attacker, and Sam Reinhart hit the crossbar with fourteen seconds left, but Florida closed it out.

The night's scoring

Brad Marchand (FLA): 3 assists

Aleksander Barkov (FLA): 1 goal (empty net)

Anton Lundell (FLA): 1 goal, 1 assist

Niko Mikkola (FLA): 1 goal, 1 assist

Sam Bennett (FLA): 1 goal

Eetu Luostarinen (FLA): 1 goal

Jacob Markstrom (FLA): 25 saves

Philip Tomasino (OTT): 1 goal

Dylan Cozens (OTT): 1 goal

Michael Amadio (OTT): 1 goal

What it means

Ottawa came into the night with wins in five of its past six and a five-point lead on the Panthers in the Atlantic — and left with its nine-game point streak (7-0-2) over. The win pulled Florida within one point of second in the division and wrapped up the homestand with two straight wins.

More than the standings, this was the first look at the team Florida envisioned in the offseason: the captain and Marchand back together, the Tkachuk brothers on the same side, and the full group healthy at the same time. If both stay in the lineup, the Panthers look a lot more like the team that lifted the Cup.

Sengun's Triple-Double Passes Olajuwon as Rockets Beat Suns 116-104

By Matt

Alperen Sengun posted 23 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists to pass Hakeem Olajuwon for second-most triple-doubles in Rockets history — on the same night Kevin Durant joined the 33,000-point club.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Alperen Sengun didn't just complete a triple-double on Wednesday night. He passed a Rockets legend to do it.

Sengun finished with 23 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists as Houston beat the Phoenix Suns 116-104 in an NBA Cup group-stage game at Toyota Center, locking up the win with a late run after Phoenix had clawed back within two.

The line

Points: 23

Rebounds: 11

Assists: 11

Field goals: 9-of-17

Three-pointers: 3-of-5

Minutes: 32

Seven of his 11 rebounds came on the offensive glass, and Houston won the rebounding battle 51-38.

Passing The Dream

The triple-double was Sengun's third of the season — and the 15th of his Rockets career, moving him past Hakeem Olajuwon into second place on the franchise's all-time triple-double list. He'd recorded his previous one just two games earlier, on November 20 in Denver.

He clinched this one with an assist at the 3:49 mark of the fourth quarter, then kept making plays after it: a second-chance basket off his own offensive rebound pushed the lead to 109-100, and a mean dunk with 5:30 left — driving past Khaman Maluach after taking the ball at the top of the key — had put Houston up 101-97 and cooled Phoenix's rally.

How the finish played out

Phoenix refused to go away. The Suns cut the deficit to 99-97 in the fourth before Houston closed on a 17-7 run. Fred VanVleet supplied the daggers, drilling a three with 4:32 left to make it 104-98 and another at the 1:45 mark for a 112-102 lead. He finished with 13 points and six assists.

Devin Booker led Phoenix with 25 points in the loss.

A second milestone in the same game

Sengun wasn't the only Rocket making history. Kevin Durant scored 20 points with 10 rebounds and became the fifth player in NBA history to reach 33,000 career points. Two franchise milestones, one night, one win.

What it means

Houston improved to 14-5, including 9-1 at home, and won their NBA Cup West Group A matchup — though the Rockets had already been eliminated from quarterfinal contention, and the loss ended the Suns' hopes of advancing. Sengun is now averaging near 22 points, 9.3 rebounds and 7.2 assists on the season — and at 24 years old, he's already second in franchise history in triple-doubles.

NFL · Nov 26, 2026 · 1:09 AM ET

Rams shut down Packers in second half for 26-13 win

By Matt

Blake Corum ran for a career-high 184 yards on his 26th birthday as the Rams shut out Green Bay after halftime, winning 26-13 in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game for their fifth straight victory.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Blake Corum ran for a career-high 184 yards and a touchdown as the Los Angeles Rams beat the Green Bay Packers 26-13 on Wednesday night at SoFi Stadium, shutting Green Bay out after halftime in the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game.

The win was the Rams' fifth in a row, lifting them to 7-4 and ahead of the Packers in the NFC wild-card race. Green Bay fell to 6-5 with its second straight loss and now sits outside the playoff picture with six games to play.

A tie at halftime, then all Rams

The first half was even. Brandon McManus kicked two first-quarter field goals for a 6-0 Rams lead, and after Trey Smack answered from 54 yards, Kyren Williams' 7-yard touchdown run made it 13-3 midway through the second. Green Bay fought back to 13-13 by halftime on Christian Watson's 6-yard touchdown catch and another Smack field goal.

The second half belonged entirely to Los Angeles. The Rams opened the third quarter with a 15-play, 68-yard drive, capped by Corum's 1-yard touchdown run, and the Packers never scored again. McManus added field goals of 40 and 30 yards in the fourth to close it out.

Corum's career night

Corum carried 32 times — the most by a Rams running back in the Sean McVay era and the most by any player in the NFL this season. He did most of the damage after the break, with 25 carries for 161 yards in the second half alone, and added two catches for 21 yards.

The touchdown was his seventh straight game with a score. It also came on his 26th birthday, and his yardage total was the second-most ever by a player on his birthday in NFL history.

The ground game as a whole was overwhelming: the Rams ran 47 times for 241 yards and held the ball for 40:40, more than double Green Bay's 19:20. The Packers managed just 244 yards of total offense.

The playoff picture

The win was also McVay's first over his former assistant Matt LaFleur in six meetings, and it vaulted the Rams ahead of Green Bay in the race for the NFC's final wild-card spot. Thursday's Lions-Bears game will shape the race further for all four teams involved.

Green Bay did get star edge rusher Micah Parsons back — he recorded a sack in his first game of the season — but the Rams made sure he wasn't much of a factor, and Jordan Love's late interception to Emmanuel Forbes with 3:39 left ended any comeback hopes. Love finished 17 of 29 for 198 yards with one touchdown and two picks, while Matthew Stafford went 16 of 23 for 140 yards with one interception.

The Packers also lost Watson to a concussion late in the second quarter, on a hit that got Rams safety Kamren Kinchens ejected. They now get extended time off before visiting New Orleans on December 6, while the Rams turn around quickly for a Thursday night home game against the Chiefs in Week 13.

Gaming · Nov 25, 2026 · 9:47 PM ET

Rockstar made 100 custom GTA 6 PS5 Pros — and you can't buy one

By Matt

Rockstar built a run of custom GTA 6 PS5 Pro consoles — dark plates, etched palms, neon Vice City stripes, each one numbered. They went to Heat players and streamers. They will never be sold.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Rockstar made the most desirable PlayStation on the planet this week, and then made sure almost nobody can have it. At least 100 custom Grand Theft Auto 6 PS5 Pro consoles exist — dark plates, etched palm trees, neon Vice City stripes, each one carrying its own serial number — and every single one is a gift. They are not for sale, and Rockstar has no plans to sell them.

The first wave went to Miami Heat players just before the November 19 launch, part of the team's Vice City-themed collaboration. Davion Mitchell, Nikola Jovic, Myron Gardner, and Keshad Johnson all posted their care packages to Instagram Stories, and the packages were serious: fitted hard flight cases holding the console, matching DualSense controllers, and a physical copy of the game.

The creators' batch

The second batch is going out now, to streamers and influencers. Streamer Davy Jones unboxed his live on YouTube, holding up the console for the camera — the etched palms across the dark gray plates, the teal-to-magenta stripes down the middle, the numbered Rockstar badge in the corner. His unit is number 96. Images from the unboxing were shared by the videotech account on X, which reported the size of the run, and the styling matches the Heat players' units exactly, confirming Rockstar produced a deliberate small run rather than a handful of one-off customs.

That matching design is the tell. This was planned as a single prestige object: one console, one look, a numbered badge under the Rockstar symbol, handed to athletes first and creators second. What remains unconfirmed is whether the creator batch is the same production run as the Heat batch or a second allocation on top of it — the reporting so far doesn't settle that, and neither Rockstar nor Sony has commented.

The part you can actually buy

The console is strictly promotional, and Rockstar and Sony have said nothing about a retail version despite years of fan requests for a proper GTA bundle or even just official faceplates. The limited-edition DualSense controllers are a different story: Sony and Rockstar released black and white versions for retail sale, and those have been available at major stores and PlayStation Direct.

So the split is deliberate. The controllers are the souvenir anyone can buy. The console is the status object — a thank-you to the people who made launch week the biggest the industry has ever seen.

Why now

The timing is the reward. Streams Charts called GTA 6 the largest game launch in livestreaming history, with Twitch peaking at 3,313,371 simultaneous viewers. PlayStation said the launch drove a record number of new systems coming online for the game's debut. Rockstar didn't need a special console to sell hardware — the game did that on its own. The custom Pros are a victory lap in physical form, handed to the athletes and creators who carried the launch, and a reminder to everyone else that the closest they'll get is the controller.

Gaming · Nov 25, 2026 · 8:17 PM ET

GTA 6 hid working QR codes in the world — scan one with your real phone and the FIB 'seizes' the website

By Matt

Rockstar hid real QR codes on posters and cars all over Leonida. Scan one with your actual phone and you land on a spoof federal seizure notice — a joke Rubius walked straight into live, in front of millions.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Rockstar didn't just fill Leonida with detail — it wired the world to the real internet. Hidden QR codes are plastered on posters, bathroom walls, and cars all over GTA 6, and they're not decoration. Point your real phone at one and it opens a page on Rockstar's own website: a parody seizure notice from the Federal Investigation Bureau, the game's fictional FBI, declaring the site seized under warrant.

Spanish streamer Rubius found that out the hard way, live. Standing in a bathroom in front of a poster with a QR code, he tried scanning it with his in-game phone first. Nothing happened. So he pulled out his real phone and tried again — and the spoof seizure notice popped up on screen. The clip, shared by Movistar eSports, has passed 21.8 million views on X. He wasn't the only one caught out: streamer ohnePixel and other players have reported falling for the same gag.

What the codes actually do

The codes route through Rockstar's rsg.ms/qr1 short link to a page on rockstargames.com that pretends the FIB seized the site, citing a warrant under "47 U.S.C. § 11.25(A)." The joke keeps going once you're there: the page claims that, due to a lack of federal funding, the FIB is selling ad space on seized IP addresses. The rotating joke ads change between visits.

The pages tie into Peekhole, GTA 6's parody of creator subscription sites — QR stickers for it show up on cars around Leonida, and fan tracking site Peekhole.de has been cataloguing the codes' destinations. Players have also confirmed the same seized-page gag from a code at Dynamix Fitness, the in-game gym, and from a QR code in a shower during HasanAbi's charity stream on November 22.

QR codes are a real mechanic, not a one-off gag

This isn't a single hidden joke. Scanning QR codes is built into how the game works: the side mission "The Final Flush" starts by scanning a QR code on a handwritten poster by a toilet — with the in-game WaiNK IT app — which kicks off a conspiracy-theorist questline about Big Sewage. Rockstar just made some of the codes in the world point somewhere real, too, and let players discover the difference for themselves.

The in-game codes are safe to scan. The usual caution applies to codes anywhere else, but inside Leonida, the worst a QR code can do is get you fake-arrested by a fake federal agency.

Leonida keeps rewarding the curious

A week after launch, the discoveries haven't slowed down. The QR gag sits alongside the Mario and Luigi hats hidden in the Lummox County woods and the time-travel trip back to PS2-era Vice City — a game that keeps hiding jokes in places only the players who stop and look will ever find. The FIB seizure page is the funniest kind of Rockstar punchline: the game reaches out of the screen, grabs your real phone, and arrests you for it.

NHL · Nov 25, 2026 · 8:16 PM ET

Patrik Laine just had knee surgery — and his road back to the NHL got a whole lot longer

By Matt

Patrik Laine announced Wednesday that he recently underwent knee surgery after a setback in training, and faces a lengthy recovery. The 28-year-old winger is unsigned, hasn't played an NHL game since October 2025, and gave no timeline for a return.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The announcement

Patrik Laine announced on Wednesday, November 25, that he recently underwent knee surgery and is facing a lengthy recovery.

The 28-year-old winger shared the news himself on Instagram, saying the operation followed a setback in his training. "I recently underwent knee surgery following a setback in my training," Laine wrote. "I have a lengthy recovery ahead, and my focus right now is on rehabilitation, putting in the work and taking things one day at a time."

He thanked his family, friends, and medical team for their support, and everyone who has reached out with messages of encouragement.

Laine gave no timeline for a return. He did not say which knee was operated on.

A season that never got going

The surgery is the latest blow in a stretch of hockey that has mostly been defined by absence.

Laine appeared in only five games for the Montreal Canadiens last season, recording a single assist, before core muscle surgery in October ended his campaign. He eventually returned to practice and was cleared by the team's medical staff, but he never drew back into the lineup for the remainder of the season.

It was not his first extended spell on the shelf in Montreal. He missed 24 games with a left knee sprain during the 2024-25 season, his first with the Canadiens.

At the team's locker-room cleanout on June 1, Laine sounded certain his NHL career was far from over. "I know I'll be playing in this league for a long time," he said. "That's not a question. Never something I've doubted. Just going to need an opportunity."

That opportunity never came. His four-year, $34.8 million contract — a deal carrying an $8.7 million cap hit — expired, and the Canadiens elected not to bring him back. Laine has been an unrestricted free agent ever since, and he has not played an NHL game since October 2025.

What Laine has been

This is not a fringe player trying to hang on. Laine was drafted second overall by the Winnipeg Jets in 2016, and his shot made him one of the most feared young scorers in the league — a 44-goal season at 19 years old, and a hat-trick record in a calendar month that Cutter Gauthier only just matched this November.

Across his career with the Jets, Columbus Blue Jackets, and Canadiens, Laine has 224 goals and 422 points in 537 games. Montreal acquired him before the 2024-25 season from Columbus in exchange for defenceman Jordan Harris and a draft pick.

He also represented Finland at the 4 Nations Face-Off last season, recording three assists in a fourth-place finish.

What comes next

There is no return date, and no team waiting. With the season well underway and a lengthy recovery ahead, a return to NHL ice in 2026-27 looks unlikely.

For now, the comeback Laine was sure of in June is on hold — again — and the only work in front of him is the rehab he described in his announcement: one day at a time.
