The NBA just put $11 billion behind its European league — new arenas, new districts, and a launch next fall

By Matt

The NBA unveiled a €10 billion arena initiative on Wednesday to back the launch of its new European league — a fund for building and renovating venues across the continent, backed by some of the biggest investment firms in the world.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The announcement

The NBA's European league took its biggest step yet toward becoming real on Wednesday — with money attached.

The league announced a plan to raise at least €10 billion, nearly $11 billion, to develop and renovate basketball arenas across Europe, plus the sports and entertainment districts around them. A group of global investment firms is backing the initiative, including Apollo Sports Capital, Ares Management, Arctos, Blackstone, HPS Investment Partners, J.P. Morgan, Sixth Street and Stonepeak.

The money is aimed at the new league the NBA is building with FIBA, which the two sides have said will begin play next fall.

"We've seen firsthand how state-of-the-art arenas and the related developments around them can transform basketball teams and their surrounding communities," NBA Commissioner Adam Silver said in a statement announcing the initiative. "As we prepare to launch a new league in Europe alongside FIBA, we see a significant opportunity to help clubs develop facilities which both build on the unique traditions that define European basketball while also elevating the fan experience and attracting many more live events."

What the fund actually does

This is not the NBA writing a check for its own teams. The investors will partner with participating clubs, ownership groups, local developers and other service providers to build new arenas and renovate existing ones — and, where it makes sense, the mixed-use districts around them, with housing, workplaces, restaurants, retail and public spaces.

The initiative is entirely separate from the team investment process — the separate track where the league is picking owners and franchises for NBA Europe. The arena fund is meant to hand prospective clubs long-term capital and venue expertise, so the buildings are ready when the league is.

The plan calls for 16 teams: 12 permanent franchises and four that qualify each year through FIBA's Basketball Champions League or a qualifying tournament. Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum has said the initial franchises are expected to be formalized by the first quarter of 2027.

Where the league is headed

The target cities are no secret, even if none has been formally confirmed as a selection. The list the league has been working from includes London and Manchester in Britain, Paris and Lyon in France, Madrid and Barcelona in Spain, Rome and Milan in Italy, Munich and Berlin in Germany, Athens in Greece and Istanbul in Turkey.

The NBA and FIBA have been talking about this league for years — the plan to officially move forward was announced in March 2025 — and the pitch is that European basketball's commercial and competitive potential is nowhere near realized. The league's argument is that the arena infrastructure is the bottleneck: Europe does not have many venues like the ones NBA teams play in, and the league believes clubs are leaving money on the table.

Not everyone is sold. Some investors have raised concerns about franchise fees that could reach up to $1 billion, and a majority of the 12 licensed EuroLeague clubs rejected an NBA proposal in October. The EuroLeague remains the elephant in the room — the established competition whose clubs the NBA needs, or needs to work around, to make its league credible.

Why arenas, why now

Silver has made the arena argument before: new world-class venues drive economic growth in the cities where they sit, through ticket sales, jobs, and the revitalization of the surrounding area. Critics of that claim note that multiple studies suggest it is more a redistribution of spending from other parts of a city than new spending altogether.

Either way, the timing is deliberate. With a launch targeted for next October, the buildings are the long pole — you cannot announce franchises without somewhere for them to play. The arena fund answers that question before the franchise announcements arrive.

A league that was a press release in March now has a funding plan, a roster of the world's biggest investment firms, and a deadline. The next step is naming the cities.

Tigers land Kevin Gausman on a one-year, $25 million deal — the latest strike in Detroit's pre-lockout spending spree

By Matt

Detroit agreed to a one-year, $25 million deal with veteran right-hander Kevin Gausman on Wednesday — the fifth significant move of a Tigers offseason that refuses to wait for the lockout.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The deal

The Detroit Tigers are not waiting for the lockout. On Wednesday, they agreed to a one-year, $25 million contract with veteran right-hander Kevin Gausman, first reported by ESPN's Jeff Passan and confirmed by the Detroit Free Press, theScore, MLB Trade Rumors and TSN. The deal is pending a physical.

It is the fifth significant move of a Tigers offseason that has been all gas since the World Series ended: a six-year extension for Troy Melton, a one-year deal for former AL Rookie of the Year Luis Gil, a one-year deal for infielder Ha-Seong Kim, a deal for reliever Emilio Pagán — and now a $25 million bet on a 35-year-old workhorse starter.

The 2026 season

Gausman split last season between two teams. He opened the year in Toronto, going 5-10 with a 4.38 ERA in 23 starts, before the Blue Jays traded him to the Chicago Cubs at the August 2 deadline for prospects Brett Bateman and Ty Southisene. In nine starts for Chicago he went 4-2 with a 4.83 ERA.

Put it together and the line reads 9-12 with a 4.51 ERA, a 1.27 WHIP and 184 strikeouts across 177⅔ innings in 32 starts. The ERA was his worst since 2019, and the 26 home runs he allowed were a career high. But the underlying numbers tell a kinder story: his 3.74 FIP sat nearly eight-tenths of a run below his ERA, and his strikeout rate held steady at roughly 24.5 percent — the splitter is still missing bats.

Why Detroit is buying

The Tigers are buying the one thing Gausman has never stopped providing: innings. He has made at least 30 starts in every season from 2016 through 2026, except for the COVID-shortened 2020 campaign, when he made all 12 of his scheduled starts. He turns 36 in January, and Detroit is paying him like a pitcher it expects to take the ball every fifth day.

The résumé backs up the price. Gausman was the No. 4 overall pick in the 2012 draft out of LSU, is a two-time All-Star, and owns a 121-125 career record with a 3.87 ERA and 2,138 strikeouts in 354 starts. He just finished a five-year, $110 million contract with Toronto and pitched in the 2025 World Series with the Blue Jays. The $25 million is a raise on his old deal's average annual value — and a one-year commitment, so Detroit carries no long-term risk if the age-35 season turns out to be the start of a decline rather than a blip.

The lockout clock

The timing is the story as much as the player. Major League Baseball's collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on December 1, and the owners are expected to lock the players out the moment it does — a fight that reached federal court on Wednesday, when MLB sued the players' association. Once the lockout starts, trades and free-agent signings freeze.

Detroit is racing that clock like everyone else. MLB Trade Rumors notes the Tigers have a full 40-man roster and still need to make the Gil and Kim deals official alongside Gausman's, meaning three roster spots have to open before any of the three can be announced. The Gausman agreement lands with six days to spare — and the Tigers' rotation, fronted by Melton and Jackson Jobe, now has a veteran anchor who has done this for a decade.

Gaming · Nov 25, 2026 · 5:45 PM ET

Rockstar explains why GTA 6 has no mission replay — replaying 'diminished the choices you had made'

By Matt

GTA 6 has no way to replay a finished story mission, and Rockstar says that is a deliberate choice, not an oversight. Senior design director Scott Butchard told Kotaku the feature 'felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell' — because in Leonida, your choices stick.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

If you have finished a story mission in Grand Theft Auto 6 and gone looking for the replay button, you already know the answer: there isn't one. Rockstar has now explained why — and the reason is baked into how the game is built.

Senior design director Scott Butchard told Kotaku that mission replay "was certainly something we looked at early on in development, and we do not currently support it." The problem, as he put it, was that replaying missions outside the story "felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected."

"Sitting outside of the game as it were and replaying missions really diminished the choices you had made," Butchard said.

A break with 17 years of GTA tradition

Mission replay has been part of the series since The Ballad of Gay Tony, the GTA 4 expansion, introduced it. GTA 5 brought it back with a medal system that graded how well you completed each mission's secondary objectives — and plenty of players went back again and again chasing the highest rating.

GTA 6 drops both. There is no replay menu and no gold medal objectives at all. Challenges still exist, but they live in their own section of the progress menu rather than being attached to individual missions.

Why your choices stick this time

The design makes more sense once you know how GTA 6's story works. Missions are not self-contained episodes that reset when they end. They change the world around you, and the outcomes can be permanent — relationships shift, open-world events get set in motion, and a decision you made hours ago can still be echoing through Leonida.

Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson made the same point to IGN during the review period: because story missions affect the world and its open-world events, you cannot simply replay a mission and choose a different outcome once those events are in motion.

It is a different philosophy from GTA 5, and it has more in common with Red Dead Redemption 2 — a game where the story is the point, and where getting a perfect outcome matters less than living with the one you got. Kotaku's piece makes the comparison explicit, likening GTA 6's missions to quests in an RPG like The Witcher 3, where the outcome you do get is what tells the story of your time in the world.

The one way back in

There is a workaround, and it is the old-fashioned one: manual saves. GTA 6 gives you 15 manual save slots, and if you save before a story mission, you can load that save to play it again. The catch is that you have to plan ahead — a save made after the mission does not help, and the autosave will overwrite itself as you keep playing.

The practical advice is simple: rotate manual saves before the big turning points. If a mission looks like it might matter, bank a save first.

What is repeatable, without any of that, is most of the rest of the game. Races, stunts, pool and other minigames can be played again, and shop robberies and bank jobs reset after a cooldown once the story unlocks them. It is only the story itself that is one and done.

Don't expect it in a patch

Rockstar has not said the feature is coming later, and Kotaku's reporting suggests not to hold your breath. The omission is a creative decision, not a missing feature waiting on an update — the studio looked at replay, tried it, and decided it clashed with the game it was making.

The one exception might be PC. GTA 6 has no PC version yet, and whenever it arrives, modders will almost certainly build a mission replay of their own. Until then, Leonida is a one-way street: every mission happens once, and the choices you make are the story you get.

Gaming · Nov 25, 2026 · 5:17 PM ET

Epic is banning Fortnite players who cheated their way to the Pirate Shop token — and their teammates are losing everything too

By Matt

Epic Games announced November 25 that it is banning Fortnite players who used cheats to win the Pirate Shop Access token — and anyone who partied up with a cheater loses the token and every cosmetic they claimed through it, even if they had no idea. Random Squad Fill matches are the only exception.

Epic Games has had enough of the Pirate Shop token hunt. The company announced November 25, through its Fortnite Status channel, that it is banning players who used cheats to obtain Pirate Shop Access in the Treasure Hunters mini season — and revoking the access and every cosmetic claimed through it. The crackdown lands with just over a week left in the season, and it comes with a warning that reaches further than the cheaters themselves.

Your squadmates pay for it too

The part players need to hear is the second half of the announcement. Anyone who won the token by teaming up with a cheater loses the token and all the Item Shop goodies they claimed while it was active — even if they had no idea someone in their party was cheating. They will not be banned themselves, but the rewards are gone. The one exception is random matches: players who were paired with a cheater through Squad Fill are exempt, since they never chose the party.

Epic's target is clear from the design of the punishment. A player who builds a throwaway smurf account, cheats their way to the token, and funnels the free cosmetics to their main account through a party gains nothing now — the whole party's haul gets wiped. The message is aimed at the grey market that has grown up around the token all season, from paid carries to accounts listed for sale.

Why everyone is this desperate

The token is the most coveted item in Fortnite history, and the numbers explain the frenzy. It grants up to 28 days of free Item Shop cosmetics, and it drops from treasure chests at odds of roughly one in 137,500. Some players have opened more than 150,000 chests without ever seeing one, which is why the hunt has driven people to cheats, exploits, and fake tools all month.

This is not the first time Epic has had to shut a shortcut down. On November 21 the company switched off geysers across the Battle Royale map after players used them with SUVs to glide endlessly and farm chests, and earlier in the month it patched a glitch that let players break open chests inside locked vaults without a key. Epic has said throughout the season that there is no special way to get the token and that buying accounts or using fake tools is a scam that can get you banned.

The Squad Fill exemption has already been tested once. A player who won the token in a random fill match posted that he had been banned days later; Epic replied that his account had not been banned at all — it had been locked because it was hacked, a different problem entirely. The company has repeated since that it does not ban players just for being matched with a cheater in fills.

What happens next

Epic has not said how many accounts have been hit in this wave, or whether the bans are permanent. The clock is the real pressure now: Golden Week starts November 28 with better odds on the season's gold rewards, the final Treasure Hours windows run that Saturday with the token's odds boosted, and Treasure Hunters ends December 5 with the "Out of Time" live event. After that the token is vaulted for good — which is exactly why the cheating got this desperate, and why Epic is drawing the line before the final week.

Gaming · Nov 25, 2026 · 3:49 PM ET

GTA 6 writer Alexa D'Agostino deletes her X account after harassment campaign over Lucia

By Matt

Alexa D'Agostino, one of the writers behind GTA 6, deleted her X account after a wave of harassment targeting her over Lucia — including a claim about an old blog post that falls apart on a second look. The abuse has since spilled onto a different woman who shares her name.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

One of the writers behind Grand Theft Auto 6 has deleted her X account after a wave of online harassment and misinformation, targeted at her over Lucia Caminos — the game's co-lead and the franchise's first female protagonist.

Alexa D'Agostino, who has thank-you credits on GTA 5, Red Dead Online and GTA Online, was one of the writers who worked on GTA 6. She had previously spoken publicly about the writing inspirations behind Lucia. After the game's launch on November 19, she was active on X, sharing videos of GTA 6 gameplay. Now the account is gone — and her old handle appears to have been taken over by a crypto enthusiast.

What the harassment is about

The people targeting D'Agostino dislike the inclusion of Lucia as a playable character, and blame her for the parts of GTA 6 they don't like. The posts being circulated criticise her for wanting Lucia to be a strong character — one who could stand alongside Arthur Morgan and Rockstar's other protagonists.

An X thread laying out why she was targeted cites her support of LGBTQ+ pride and posts that are critical of US President Donald Trump. It also claims she ran a blog that encouraged women to "manipulate and take advantage of men."

That claim is the part that falls apart. The blog post the thread points to gave women advice on how to handle meeting their boyfriend's friends: be themselves, let the friends lead the conversation, and ask their boyfriend what his friends are like before they meet them. That is the evidence. Video Games Chronicle, which reported the story, notes that many of the posts about D'Agostino are misogynistic and racist in nature.

The woman behind Lucia

D'Agostino spoke about writing Lucia before the game launched, and the character came from somewhere personal. She told Love Magazine she thought of the women she knows — her mother was an immigrant who grew up in Newark, New Jersey, close to Lucia's hometown of Liberty City.

"When it came to writing Lucia, I thought of the women I know," she said. "My mother was an immigrant who grew up in Newark, New Jersey, close to Lucia's hometown of Liberty City. I thought about the way she raised me: rowdy, kind, but not to take any shit. I related a lot to Lucia, and writing her came very naturally to me."

"When you are focusing on writing a fully realised person with their own wants, you're going to get something perfectly imperfect — with clichés, but also undeniably real. That's how you get a woman that can stand tall next to the likes of Arthur Morgan and Niko Bellic."

That quote is now being used to disparage her. It is, on its face, a writer explaining why a character works.

The abuse found a second target

After D'Agostino deleted her X account, much of the vitriol was instead sent to another woman who shares her name — someone with no connection to the game at all. That is what a harassment campaign does when its target logs off: it keeps going and finds the nearest name that matches.

This is not new, and the industry knows it

Incidents like this are nothing new in gaming. Tati Gabrielle, the star of Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, faced online harassment as soon as the game was revealed — and has since said Naughty Dog gave her training to prepare for it. Laura Bailey was harassed for playing Abby in The Last of Us Part 2.

The pattern is the same every time: a game gets big, a woman attached to it becomes a target, and the people doing it dress up a pile of misinformation as a critique of the game. GTA 6 is the biggest launch in entertainment history. Lucia is half of it. The writer who helped make her real had to leave social media a week after launch — and the claim used to justify it doesn't survive a single click.

NFL · Nov 25, 2026 · 3:46 PM ET

Steelers release Aaron Rodgers hours after his scorched-earth Pat McAfee interview

By Matt

About an hour after Aaron Rodgers went on the Pat McAfee Show and torched Mike McCarthy, the Steelers released him — ending a two-year tenure in Pittsburgh and sending the four-time MVP to waivers.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The release

Aaron Rodgers is a free man — or about to be one. The Pittsburgh Steelers released the four-time NFL MVP on Wednesday afternoon, about an hour after Rodgers went on ESPN's "Pat McAfee Show" and publicly torched head coach Mike McCarthy, according to multiple reports.

The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac first reported the release, and ESPN's Adam Schefter amplified it within the hour. USA Today, the New York Post, Fox Sports and Bleacher Report all confirmed it shortly after.

It ends a two-year tenure in Pittsburgh that was supposed to be a storybook finish. Rodgers joined the Steelers in June 2025, reuniting with the coach he won a Super Bowl with in Green Bay, and said all year that the 2026 season would be his last in the NFL. Instead, his final act in black and gold was a benching, a tell-all interview, and a pink slip — in that order, inside about 18 hours.

The about-face

The speed of the decision is the tell. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that the Steelers had initially planned to keep Rodgers after benching him — inactive, fourth string, but still on the roster — and changed course after the bombshell interview.

That matches what our earlier post on the interview reported: as of Wednesday morning, there were no immediate plans to release him. The interview changed that. Rodgers used the appearance to accuse McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings, skipping walk-throughs, and failing to prepare — and to say he would never play another snap for Pittsburgh. The team answered by making that permanent.

What happens now

Rodgers goes on waivers. Any team can claim him until 4 p.m. ET on Thursday, and if no team does, he becomes a free agent who can sign anywhere.

Whether anyone will is an open question. The New York Post floated the Patriots and Ravens as teams that could use a quarterback, and NFL insider Dianna Russini reported that Rodgers likely won't draw much interest if he hits the open market. He turns 43 next week and has said this is his final season — so any team that claims him is getting a bridge, not a building block.

Friday's game goes on without him either way. Mason Rudolph starts against the Denver Broncos on Black Friday, with Rodgers inactive — the same arrangement the Steelers announced late Tuesday night, before any of this exploded.

How it ended

The collapse took less than a day. McCarthy publicly backed Rodgers as his QB1 on Monday. On Tuesday night, the Steelers announced Rudolph would start and Rodgers would be inactive. Rodgers learned of the decision from tight end Pat Freiermuth, not from the team, and on Wednesday morning he went on McAfee and said everything he had been sitting on for a decade — the snoring in meetings, the missed walk-throughs, the "1-2-3 Packers" huddle break at halftime of Sunday's loss in Philadelphia.

"At this point, I'm not going back to Pittsburgh," he said. "That ship has definitely sailed."

He was right. The Steelers just made sure of it.

The Pittsburgh numbers

Rodgers started 10 games for Pittsburgh and led the Steelers to a 6-4 record, completing 60.9% of his passes for 2,241 yards with 16 touchdowns and six interceptions. The team sits in an AFC wild-card spot with seven weeks left, and its season now belongs to Rudolph.

The reunion was the whole point of the signing. Rodgers and McCarthy spent 13 seasons together in Green Bay, winning the Super Bowl at the end of the 2010 season — against the Steelers. Rodgers vouched for McCarthy to get the Pittsburgh job after Mike Tomlin stepped down last January, hoping it would be different in McCarthy's hometown, in his dream job, in Rodgers' final year.

It wasn't. And now the most decorated quarterback of his generation is on waivers in the final weeks of his final season, waiting to see if anyone wants the ending to happen somewhere else.

NFL · Nov 25, 2026 · 3:15 PM ET

Aaron Rodgers says he's done in Pittsburgh — 'that ship has sailed' — and torches Mike McCarthy on Pat McAfee

By Matt

Aaron Rodgers went on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday and said he will not return to the Steelers — then accused Mike McCarthy of sleeping through meetings, skipping walk-throughs, and calling '1-2-3 Packers' at halftime in Philadelphia.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The quote

Aaron Rodgers is done with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and he said so himself on Wednesday.

Appearing on ESPN's "Pat McAfee Show" in his first public comments since the Steelers benched him late Tuesday night, Rodgers dismissed any possibility of a return after Mason Rudolph was named the starter for Friday's Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos.

"At this point, I'm not going back to Pittsburgh," Rodgers said. "That ship has definitely sailed."

USA Today, Sports Illustrated, the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel and the New York Post all carried the quote within the hour. Rodgers added that he did not see this ending coming, and did not want it to end this way — but that the team has chosen to back McCarthy, and the players' position is clear.

The ultimatum

Rodgers said the break came down to a conversation on Monday, when he told McCarthy that the offense needed a change for the betterment of the team. In Rodgers' telling, he gave the coach a choice: stop calling plays, or release him.

"I think there's got to be a change," Rodgers said he told McCarthy. "You don't want me to call it because you don't think I'm going to call enough runs? Fine, let somebody else call it, that's what's in the best interest of the team."

McCarthy did neither. The Steelers instead announced Tuesday night that Rudolph would start and Rodgers would be inactive — fourth string, behind 2025 draft pick Will Howard and 2026 third-rounder Drew Allar. Rodgers said he never heard the word "benching" from McCarthy at all, and did not learn of the decision from the team. He found out in a phone call with tight end Pat Freiermuth after a contentious meeting with McCarthy on Tuesday night, and said he has not heard from McCarthy since their last conversation in the 6 p.m. window that evening.

He also said the issue was not a secret inside the building. Rodgers claimed he told general manager Omar Khan about McCarthy's alleged sleeping issues, and he criticized Khan and owner Art Rooney II for permitting what he described as unprofessional behavior while knowing how McCarthy conducted himself. He called it "comedy" that Khan would defend McCarthy while knowing about it.

The accusations

The heart of the interview was a series of specific claims about McCarthy's preparation and presence — claims Rodgers said go back to training camp, not just the last week.

He alleged that McCarthy frequently fell asleep in meetings or did not show up to them at all. He described one quarterbacks meeting last Wednesday where McCarthy came in late and began snoring within 10 minutes: "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers, we all looked around, five minutes later, you hear the snoring again," Rodgers said. "Less than five minutes after that, he walked out of the room like nothing happened."

Rodgers further claimed that McCarthy missed an offensive meeting and a protective assignments walk-through on Thursday, skipped Friday's team walk-through, and missed Saturday's morning meeting before the Eagles game — a meeting that mattered more because the team did not meet Saturday night in Philadelphia.

"I don't think he knows the plan," Rodgers said. "I think he learns the plan during the week. ... That part is disrespectful to the game itself."

He also alleged that McCarthy has made little effort to spend time with the defensive players, and quoted the coach's response when Rodgers encouraged him to do so: "I don't think I need to." Rodgers said McCarthy had "kind of lost a lot of those guys," and contrasted him with former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin: "You don't have to be Mike T, but you have to connect with the guys."

Rodgers said McCarthy denied the allegations and would get "super angry" if others mentioned them, and said multiple other players in the locker room would vouch for having witnessed the behavior. He framed his own willingness to speak as a function of having nothing to lose: the coaching staff worries about job security, the players worry about their money and job security, and he does not.

McAfee, listening to it all, replied that he was worried about McCarthy after hearing what Rodgers said.

"1-2-3 Packers"

The moment Rodgers called the breaking point for the locker room came at halftime of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles — a defeat to a team that had lost seven straight, and Pittsburgh's second loss in a row.

According to Rodgers, McCarthy went to break down the team and instead of saying "1-2-3 Steelers," said "1-2-3 Packers."

"That was one of those things where nobody was even like saying Steelers because it was so in the moment and it was like this weird rambling something," Rodgers said, "that it was odd enough everyone across the entire locker room heard it and I think we all looked around going, 'What the f–k? What is going on? Where's his head at at this point?'"

McCarthy coached Green Bay from 2006 until a midseason firing in 2018, and Rodgers alleged the coach still holds that firing against him. "In Mike's mind, I got him fired in 2018. I'm the reason. He told a staff member that," Rodgers said. "That he still doesn't forgive me for getting him fired in 2018."

Ten years in the making

Rodgers said he has been sitting on this for a decade — that the same behavior was happening in Green Bay, and that he covered for McCarthy there for years.

"I sat on this for a long time. I sat on it for 10 years. 10 years in Green Bay with this stuff going on," he said. "But we worked around it, we won division championships, went to the playoff for eight straight years. ... I covered for him for a lot of years. The people in Green Bay knew what was going on. The people in Dallas knew what was going on."

He said he looked into McCarthy's tenure with the Cowboys from 2020-24 and found the same things happening there. He also contrasted McCarthy's process with that of his former Packers coach Matt LaFleur and Rams coach Sean McVay, saying LaFleur was not missing those types of meetings.

The irony, which Rodgers owned on the show, is that he helped bring McCarthy to Pittsburgh. After Mike Tomlin stepped down last January, Rodgers said he advised Khan to give McCarthy an interview — and vouched for him in his exit interview after the 2025 season, hoping it would be different in McCarthy's hometown, in his dream job, with Rodgers in his final year.

"It's on me. Because I vouched for him and I had the hope that it was going to be different," Rodgers said. "It's insanity. It's on me. I bought into the insanity. I knew this was a possibility."

He signed a one-year deal to return to Pittsburgh in May, citing the relationship with McCarthy — his coach for the Packers' Super Bowl win at the end of the 2010 season and two of his four MVP awards — as an enticing reason to come back for a 22nd season. He also said on his return that this season would be his last in the NFL.

What happens now

The Steelers excused Rodgers from Wednesday's practice, and he took them up on the offer. The team has not released him — he remains on the roster, inactive as the fourth-stringer — and there were no immediate plans to release him, per NFL Network's reporting earlier Wednesday.

Rudolph starts Friday against the Broncos. Rodgers, who turns 43 next week, has started 10 games for Pittsburgh, completing 60.9% of his passes for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions, and has been sacked 31 times. The Steelers sit at 6-4, holding an AFC wild-card spot, with their season now in Rudolph's hands.

Rodgers said he regrets that he will not get to move forward with teammates he respected, who he insisted "felt the exact same way." Whether he has played his final NFL game is now an open question — he has said this is his last season, and he has now said he will not play another snap for Pittsburgh. A release would let another team sign him. Until then, the most decorated quarterback of his generation is a healthy scratch who just told the world exactly why.

Avengers: Doomsday confirms Kate Bishop's return

By Matt

Hailee Steinfeld is officially back as Kate Bishop in Avengers: Doomsday, confirmed alongside the final trailer — in theaters December 18.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Hailee Steinfeld is officially returning as Kate Bishop in Avengers: Doomsday, confirmed in a Disney and Marvel Instagram post. The announcement lands with the film's final trailer, released November 23, and the movie opens in theaters December 18, 2026.

What the final trailer shows

The trailer centers on Steve Rogers living with Peggy Carter and their son — the life he chose at the end of Avengers: Endgame — before he leaves them to go off with the Fantastic Four. NFL · Nov 25, 2026 · 2:44 PM ET

Brandon Aiyuk has a new team — the Commanders sign him to the practice squad, two days after the 49ers cut him

By Matt

Two days after San Francisco released him, Brandon Aiyuk agreed to join the Washington Commanders' practice squad — reuniting with Jayden Daniels and giving a receiver-starved team a nearly free flier on a 28-year-old who was an All-Pro two seasons ago.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

Brandon Aiyuk has a new team. The free-agent wide receiver is signing with the Washington Commanders' practice squad, his agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Wednesday — hours after Aiyuk visited the team in Ashburn and two days after the 49ers released him.

It is a one-year deal for the rest of the regular season, and it came together fast. Rosenhaus had said earlier Wednesday that a decision was unlikely to happen today. By the afternoon, the two sides had an agreement.

One wrinkle: the signing is not expected to be officially completed today. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported it should be official next week — but the agreement is done, and Aiyuk is a Commander.

The reunion

The landing spot was never much of a mystery. Aiyuk reached out to Jayden Daniels about a month ago — the two were teammates at Arizona State in 2019 — and the two have reconciled after a summer rift. Daniels is now his quarterback again.

Washington's general manager Adam Peters knows him, too. Peters spent seven seasons in the 49ers' front office and was the team's vice president of player personnel when San Francisco drafted Aiyuk in the first round in 2020.

And the Commanders need receivers badly. Terry McLaurin is out with a torn patellar tendon suffered in Week 6, and Dyami Brown and Jaylin Lane are on injured reserve. Stefon Diggs is on a one-year deal, and rookie fourth-rounder Antonio Williams has flashed — nine catches for 122 yards against Cincinnati on Monday Night Football — but Washington has been working out receivers for weeks. Aiyuk is the biggest name it has brought in.

The player

Nobody needs a reminder of what Aiyuk was two seasons ago. In 2023 he posted a career-high 1,342 receiving yards and was named a second-team All-Pro during the 49ers' run to the Super Bowl. Across six seasons in San Francisco he caught 294 passes for 4,305 yards and 25 touchdowns in 69 games, averaging 14.6 yards per reception.

Then came the knee injury — a torn ACL and MCL in his right knee seven games into 2024 — and he has not played since October of that year. The recovery never became a comeback in San Francisco. He stopped attending team-directed rehab and meetings, communication with the team broke down, he was placed on the reserve/left squad list last December, and after hiring Rosenhaus and winning reinstatement on November 9, the 49ers released him Monday when their two-week roster exemption expired.

Rosenhaus says Aiyuk is 100 percent healthy, with clean MRIs and X-rays. The Commanders are about to find out.

The cost

The flier costs Washington almost nothing. The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala noted that if the Commanders signed Aiyuk to the practice squad at the maximum rate for a player of his experience and elevated him for three games, it would owe him roughly $305,000 for the rest of the regular season.

Practice-squad rules mean he can be elevated for Sunday's game against the Cardinals if Washington wants him that fast. If he plays anything like the receiver he was in 2023, the Commanders get a steal for the price of a rounding error. If he does not, they can move on without losing much.

Two days after the ugliest exit in the league this season, Aiyuk has a locker again — and a quarterback he already trusts throwing him the ball.

Gaming · Nov 25, 2026 · 1:49 PM ET

The Blood of Dawnwalker just beat GTA 6 for the AP's game of the year

By Matt

The Associated Press put The Blood of Dawnwalker at No. 1 on its top 10 games of 2026 — ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI, the biggest entertainment launch in history. The year's best-selling game didn't win the year's best-game argument.

---

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Grand Theft Auto VI has spent the last week breaking every record in the book. It did not win the Associated Press's game of the year.

The AP's top 10 games of 2026, published Monday by critic Lou Kesten, puts The Blood of Dawnwalker — the medieval vampire RPG from Rebel Wolves — at No. 1, with GTA VI second. It is the clearest split yet between the year's commercial story and its critical one: the game that sold more than anything ever made sits behind a dark fantasy RPG that most of the mainstream audience only discovered this fall.

The list

Here is the AP's full top 10:

1. The Blood of Dawnwalker

2. Grand Theft Auto VI

3. Star Wars Zero Company

4. Mina the Hollower

5. Resident Evil Requiem

6. Pragmata

7. Crimson Desert

8. Zero Parades: For Dead Spies

9. Control Resonant

10. Pokémon Pokopia

The list mixes blockbusters with smaller swings. Star Wars Zero Company, a tactical strategy game, takes third; Mina the Hollower, the retro-inspired indie, is fourth; and Resident Evil Requiem — the horror entry that lost out to Hellraiser: Revival at the Horror Game Awards — rounds out the top five.

Why Dawnwalker won

Dawnwalker is Rebel Wolves' first game, published by Bandai Namco, and it launched September 2 on PC and consoles. You play Coen, a young man turned into a Dawnwalker — human by day, vampire after dark — in 14th-century Europe, with a ticking clock: every quest you accept advances time and eats into the days your family has left.

The AP praised it as a cleverly constructed role-playing epic, and the awards season has agreed so far: the game is nominated for Best Narrative and Best Role Playing Game at The Game Awards, which hand out their prizes December 10 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. GTA VI leads that show with eight nominations, including Game of the Year — so the rematch is two weeks away.

If the ranking sends you to the store, the timing is kind: Dawnwalker is 20 percent off on Steam for the first time, down to $55.99 from its $69.99 list price, with the sale running until December 7.

What second place says about GTA 6

The AP was not down on GTA VI — it called the game a landmark in interactive storytelling, praised its central romance between Jason and Lucia, and noted that other publishers spent the year steering clear of its launch window entirely. Second place on a top-10 list is not a snub.

But the gap between the two lenses is the story. Take-Two announced day-one retail sales of $3.79 billion for GTA VI, a record for any entertainment product, with 32.5 million copies sold before release. No game has ever been bigger. The AP's list says biggest and best are different questions — and this year, a vampire RPG from a first-time studio answered the second one better.

227 new issues land today

By Matt

It's the last New Comic Book Day of November: 227 new issues hit shops today, led by Amazing Spider-Man #1004 — and Jean Grey #1 starts a new five-issue series as the Phoenix comes back to Earth.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

It's the last New Comic Book Day of November, and it's a big one: 227 new issues land in shops today, with 591 new variants across them. The Christmas comics are starting to arrive, and the week's haul is led by a familiar name at the top of the list.

The week's headliner: Amazing Spider-Man #1004

The Amazing Spider-Man #1004 takes the number one spot on the week's list again. The series is still going strong after its big #1000 milestone, and the demand hasn't let up.

This week's issue comes from Joe Kelly, Francesco Manna, and Luca Maresca. Itsy Bitsy has some feedback for J. Jonah Jameson — shut up and shove off this mortal coil — and while Spidey leaps into action to save JJJ, another friend flips and puts the wall-crawler between him and his revenge. Cover A is by Ed McGuinness, with variants from Peach Momoko, Mark Spears, Sara Pichelli, and Ron Lim, among others. Cover price is $4.99.

Elsewhere in the Spider-corner of the Marvel list, Dan Slott and Stefano Caselli's Spectacular Spider-Man #6 also hits shelves today.

The big debut: Jean Grey #1

The week's biggest launch is Jean Grey #1, the start of a new five-issue series from Jed MacKay and Rogê Antônio. It's the first of eight variants for the issue, and the timing is no accident — with the X-Men heading back to the big screen in Avengers: Doomsday, it's a good moment to make room for Marvel's mutants on the reading pile.

The setup: after DNX, the Phoenix is coming home — and Jean Grey is burning with it. The question hanging over the issue is whether she can hold onto a power that gives life and takes it in the same breath, or whether it burns through everything she touches when she lands. It's a new chapter for Jean and the X-Men, and the early word is strong: ComicBook.com gave the debut 4 out of 5, calling it a character study that bridges her cosmic era as Phoenix with her return to Earth.

The full creative team is MacKay on writing, Antônio on art, Edgar Delgado on colors, and Arianna Maher on letters. Cover A is by Joëlle Jones, with variants from Ito, Nogi San, Peach Momoko, and Miguel Mercado. It's 32 pages for $4.99.

The rest of the stack

Jean Grey isn't the only new series launching today. The week's debutants also include Robin Hood #1, Leaded Gasoline #1, Rampant Swine #1, and DC's Naughty List #1, plus the Batman 2026 Annual.

The rest of Marvel's list includes Alien vs. X-Men #3, Amazing Venom #3, Gambit Gone #3, Marvel Zombies: War Zone #3, Predator vs. Planet of the Apes #5, and Spider-Man / Hulk: Fire and Brimstone #4. All told, Comics Bulletin counts 83 new releases for the week — and once every variant edition is tallied, CLZ's count runs to 227 new issues.

If you're heading to the shop before the holiday, Jean Grey #1 is the one to grab first. Spider-Man #1004 is the one to grab second. Everything after that is gravy.

MLB · Nov 25, 2026 · 12:44 PM ET

MLB sues its own players' union before the lockout even starts — the labor fight is now in federal court

By Matt

Six days before the collective bargaining agreement expires, Major League Baseball sued the players' association in federal court — asking a judge to declare the coming lockout legal before the union can challenge it. The union called the suit 'completely frivolous.'

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The filing

Major League Baseball took its labor fight to federal court on Wednesday — before the lockout has even begun.

The league sued the Major League Baseball Players Association in the Southern District of New York, in a pre-emptive strike aimed at the union's most powerful legal weapon. The complaint asks a judge to declare that the impending lockout is legal under antitrust law and cannot be enjoined by a court — even if the players give up their union status, as the league anticipates they will.

The suit is a class action, and it names as defendants the eight members of the union's executive subcommittee — including star pitchers Tarik Skubal and Paul Skenes.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the filing. The union answered within hours.

What MLB wants

The league is not seeking damages. It wants a declaratory judgment: a court ruling, in advance, that the lockout is permissible should the union consider disclaiming.

The move is aimed squarely at a maneuver known as a disclaimer of interest. If the players dissolved their union and reconstituted as a trade association, they could argue the lockout is an illegal group boycott and sue MLB on antitrust grounds — the same path NFL players took in 2011, when a court enjoined that league's lockout. The risk for owners is severe: losing an antitrust case could mean treble damages, three times the players' proven losses.

MLB's filing tries to take that option off the table before it is ever used. The league also wants any future litigation kept in the Southern District of New York, where both parties are based, and not "in some unrelated location cherry-picked by the union to litigate their meritless claims."

League spokesman Glen Caplin framed the suit as an attempt to have a judge "proactively disarm the union's nuclear option of disclaiming."

The complaint also alleges the union has failed to negotiate in good faith, and the league said it is imminently filing an unfair labor practice charge with the National Labor Relations Board — arguing the dispute belongs before the NLRB, not a federal court.

The union's answer

The players' association did not wait long to respond, and it did not mince words.

"The lawsuit filed today by MLB is completely frivolous. We will respond appropriately, but MLB's decision to run to court in the middle of negotiations rather than bargain in good faith is incredibly disappointing," the MLBPA said in a statement, reported by The Athletic's Evan Drellich.

The union's position has not moved in months: no salary cap, under any circumstances. Owners have been equally firm — Commissioner Rob Manfred said last week they will not agree to a deal without one.

Why the league moved first

The calendar explains the timing. The current five-year collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1 at 11:59 p.m. ET, and owners are expected to lock the players out the moment it does — the sport's 10th work stoppage since 1972, halting signings and trades.

The two sides traded proposals again on Monday, and neither budged on the cap. The owners' standing offer is a $258.2 million ceiling and a $180.2 million payroll floor beginning in 2028, with the current system kept for 2027. The union countered by agreeing to split all local media revenue evenly among the 30 teams — a first for the sport — but without a cap attached.

MLB tweaked its proposal on Tuesday, pledging that all contracts will remain fully guaranteed and no money will be put in escrow if the union accepts a cap and floor. Union head Bruce Meyer immediately condemned it as providing "no real substance."

With talks stalled and the deadline six days away, the league decided to fight the next battle — the courtroom one — before the lockout even starts.

What happens next

The free-agent market has been sprinting to beat the freeze. Skubal got his nine-year, $450 million deal from the Mets done ten days before the shutdown — the richest contract ever for a pitcher, with a $45 million signing bonus paid right away so the lockout cannot touch it. Everyone else in the market has a week to get deals done, or spend the winter wondering.

Negotiations are expected to resume Sunday or Monday in Phoenix, where the union holds its annual executive subcommittee meetings in Scottsdale. The last full lockout, in 2021-22, lasted 99 days and still started the season on time. This one has a salary cap on the table, a federal lawsuit already filed, and a union that has a legal nuclear option of its own.

The fight is no longer just at the bargaining table. It is in court now, too — and opening day is the clock both sides are racing.

Royals land Alec Bohm — two years, $20 million, and a new third baseman for Kansas City

By Matt

Kansas City agreed to a two-year, $20 million deal with All-Star third baseman Alec Bohm on Wednesday, filling the hole at third base left by last week's Maikel Garcia trade — pending a physical.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The Royals have their third baseman.

Kansas City agreed to a two-year, $20 million contract with Alec Bohm on Wednesday, multiple outlets reported, with MLB Network's Jon Morosi first reporting the agreement and The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal confirming the terms. The deal is pending a physical. Reuters, the New York Post and USA Today all corroborated the agreement within the hour.

Bohm hits free agency this fall after seven seasons with the Philadelphia Phillies, who drafted him third overall in 2018. He leaves the only organization he has ever known — and he does it for a Royals team that suddenly had a glaring hole at the hot corner.

The player

Bohm is a 2024 National League All-Star, and he has been an everyday player in Philadelphia for years. He batted .249 with 15 home runs and 88 RBIs across 155 games for the Phillies in 2026, and for his career he is a .273 hitter in 874 games with 85 home runs and 483 RBIs.

He is not a star who carries a lineup — the power is modest for a corner infielder, and the 2026 average was down from his .287 mark in 2025 — but he is a durable, professional bat who plays every day and drives in runs. In Kansas City, that profile fits: the Royals need a steady third baseman, not a savior.

The hole he fills

The timing is no accident. Last week the Royals traded Maikel Garcia to the Seattle Mariners, and Garcia had manned third base in 440 of his 531 career games in Kansas City — winning a Gold Glove and making the American League All-Star team in 2025. Trading him left the position empty, and Bohm walks straight into it.

The Phillies, for their part, were never really in the mix to bring him back. The New York Post reported the Yankees had interest in Bohm before Kansas City closed the deal, and the Royals moved first.

What it means

This is the kind of signing that tells you where the Royals think they are. A two-year, $20 million deal for a 30-year-old former All-Star is not a rebuild move — it is a win-now move at a position of need, made in the final days before the current collective bargaining agreement expires on December 1 and a widely anticipated owners' lockout shuts down baseball business.

Bohm gets a fresh start in the American League for the first time in his career. The Royals get their third baseman. And with the lockout clock ticking, the hot stove is not slowing down.

Eddie Cha dies at 53 — the striking coach behind Cejudo, Korean Zombie and a generation of UFC fighters

By Matt

Renowned striking coach Eddie Cha, the head striking coach at Fight Ready MMA who helped turn Henry Cejudo into a two-division champion, died Tuesday at 53. No cause of death has been publicly revealed.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The news

The MMA world lost one of its most respected teachers on Tuesday.

Eddie Cha, the renowned striking coach and head striking coach at Fight Ready MMA in Glendale, Arizona, died at 53. The news first circulated Tuesday through tribute posts from fighters and friends, including former UFC fighter Michael Chiesa and one of Cha's first UFC fighters, Francisco Rivera. Iridium Sports Agency confirmed the news in a public statement, and people connected to Fight Ready confirmed it directly to MMA Junkie. No cause of death has been publicly revealed.

The coach

Cha was not a household name to casual fans, but inside the sport he was one of the most trusted striking minds in the game. He spent years as a striking coach and mitt holder at Fight Ready, working with dozens of UFC fighters — and his fingerprints are on some of the biggest careers of the last decade.

His most famous project was Henry Cejudo. Cha played a major role in transforming Cejudo from an elite wrestler into a two-division UFC champion, building the striking game that carried "Triple C" to titles at flyweight and bantamweight. He also worked closely with Chan Sung Jung — "The Korean Zombie" — along with former heavyweight champion Jon Jones, strawweight champion Zhang Weili, Deiveson Figueiredo, Benson Henderson, Kelvin Gastelum, Tracy Cortez, Mackenzie Dern and Casey O'Neill.

The road to Fight Ready

Cha's path to the corner was an unusual one. He became a full-time coach after a career as a professional poker player, opening his own All In MMA gym in Buena Park, California. He moved to Arizona in 2016, began training at MMA Lab in Phoenix, and eventually found his home at Fight Ready, where he coached alongside Santino Defranco and Brady Fink and became one of the gym's most recognizable figures.

He was, by every account from the people who knew him, a coach who gave everything to his fighters. Iridium Sports Agency's statement called him "one of the most successful, passionate and selfless coaches in MMA."

What it means

Fifty-three is far too young, and the tributes that poured in on Tuesday made clear how wide Cha's reach was — from champions he built to the dozens of fighters he held mitts for every day in Glendale. The sport does not have many coaches who shape a generation the way he did, quietly, from the corner.

No memorial arrangements have been announced. The cause of his death has not been disclosed.

A Japanese VTuber just escaped GTA 6's 'impossible' six-star wanted level — through a portal to 2002 Vice City

By Matt

Japanese VTuber Haigure Tamao has done what GTA 6 says can't be done: escaped a six-star wanted level. His way out was the game's secret Tommy Vercetti portal — step through to 2002 Vice City, come back to Leonida with zero stars.

Grand Theft Auto VI says a six-star wanted level is impossible to escape. The game tells you so on screen — the whole map goes under search, the usual tricks stop working, and even trying to flee by jet draws missile fire. A Japanese VTuber just proved the game wrong, and his escape route runs through 2002.

Haigure Tamao, streaming with a VTuber avatar, set out to test whether the secret portal hidden in GTA 6's Tommy Vercetti Easter egg could wipe a six-star wanted level. It did. He went in with the full force of Leonida on him and came back clean.

The escape

The portal is the payoff of one of the game's deepest secrets. Players have to solve a puzzle spanning a dozen electrical substations across Leonida, visited in a specific order — the letters painted on their walls spell out "LIFEISPASSINGMEBY," a cheat code from the original Vice City that sped up in-game time. Finish it and a text message points to Reactor 2 at the Turtle Head Power Station, where a portal opens between 7 PM and 6 AM on the in-game clock. Step through and Jason lands in a recreation of the original Malibu Club, rendered in PS2-era graphics, with returning character Kent Paul — once again voiced by Danny Dyer. The portal itself was first found by YouTuber Memeio, who spent three days following the clues across the map.

Tamao's first attempt failed — he couldn't survive the chase long enough to reach the portal. So he solved a second secret first: the president's hidden bunkers, which hand over a tank. With the tank he caused chaos near the power station, hit six stars with only minutes to spare before the portal closed, and drove through. On the other side, in retro Vice City, his wanted level was gone instantly. The real question was whether it would come back with him. It didn't.

"I finally did it! I went from a Wanted level of six to zero!" he celebrated, in Dexerto's translation.

A second way out — and one that doesn't work

Tamao isn't the only one who cracked it. A second creator, Fear, found a shorter route: simply walking into the hidden tank bunker clears six-star heat too. Why that works is unclear — the bunker keeps the player inside Leonida, so the portal's logic about leaving the map shouldn't apply. The working theory is that the police can't track a player inside the bunker.

There is also a control case that proves this isn't just about hiding underground: the underwater facility does not clear six-star heat. So the bunker result reads as a quirk of the game, not a general rule.

Is it supposed to work?

Rockstar hasn't commented, and nobody can say yet whether the escape is intentional or just a side effect of the wanted level not carrying over between two worlds. The portal route has only been shown working once, so whether it repeats every time is unconfirmed — but two separate escape routes in the same week, after five days of players insisting six stars was a death sentence, is the kind of discovery that rewrites how the game's hardest chase is understood.

Five days after launch, the "impossible" wanted level has an exit. It just happens to run through a nightclub from 2002.

Riot banned an entire Valorant team for four years — every player and the coach, for cheating in a qualifier

By Matt

Riot Games has banned all five players of Team BONK and their head coach from all Riot-sanctioned competition after its Anti-Cheat team confirmed unauthorized software was running during the VCT EMEA Kickoff Open Qualifier — and Riot says every player knowingly took part.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Riot Games has handed down one of the harshest punishments in Valorant history. All five players of Team BONK and their head coach have been banned from competition for 48 months after Riot's Anti-Cheat team confirmed unauthorized software was running during official matches in the VCT EMEA Kickoff Open Qualifier. The ban is effective immediately, covers every Riot-sanctioned esports competition, and applies equally to the coach who ran the software and the five players Riot says knowingly took part in the scheme.

The ruling, published by Riot's Competitive Operations team on Tuesday, closes a case that started with an upset nobody expected. BONK played in the VCT EMEA Kickoff Open Qualifier #1 on November 6 and 7, and stunned Turkish organization Aurora Gaming — a result that immediately drew suspicion. Reports of possible cheating prompted Riot's Anti-Cheat team to investigate, and the findings were damning: unauthorized software was actively running on a computer linked to BONK's head coach, Massimo#365, during official matches, feeding him live information about the opposing players' positions.

How the case unfolded

Riot moved fast once the investigation confirmed what happened. BONK was disqualified from the qualifier on November 8, and the affected matches were replayed. Formal disciplinary proceedings opened on November 10, with each of the six individuals given a chance to respond before the ruling landed. The ruling does not name the specific software that was used, or detail how the information was shared with the players — but it is explicit that the arrangement was deliberate, and that the deliberate nature of the misconduct shaped the length of the punishment.

The six banned individuals are head coach Massimo#365 and players WaddlesThePig, kubfu, Yaquob "Corsa" Hanif, Aleks "Kaaru" Grudniewski, and Max "deqadz" Vinall. All six were found to have breached Article 4.3 of Riot's Esports Global Code of Conduct, which prohibits cheating with unauthorized methods or technology — and also prohibits knowingly participating in, enabling, or assisting cheating. That second half is why the players received the same punishment as the coach. Riot did not need to prove that each player had cheating software installed on their own computer to find them in breach.

Why the ban reaches so far

The suspensions are separate from the disqualification, and their scope is what makes this a career-altering ruling. Because the bans cover all Riot-sanctioned esports competitions, the six cannot regain eligibility by joining another Valorant organization or switching to a different Riot title. With the suspensions taking effect in November 2026, they are out of official competition until late 2030 — effectively the rest of the VCT 2027 season and three more after it.

The other side of the ruling is Aurora Gaming, the team BONK beat to trigger the investigation. Aurora was reinstated after the disqualification, with the affected matches replayed, and qualified for the EMEA Qualifier playoffs starting November 25. The team that lost to a cheater gets its shot; the team that cheated loses four years.

What this says about the VCT's open qualifiers

The case is a warning shot at the exact point where the VCT is most vulnerable. Open qualifiers are the on-ramp for unknown teams — anyone can enter, and a deep run can launch a career. That openness is also the risk: a team nobody has heard of beating an established organization is exactly the kind of result that invites suspicion, and here the suspicion was right. Riot's answer is a punishment with no ambiguity in it: cheat in a qualifier and the whole roster goes down, coach included, for four years.

It also shows how much Riot is willing to invest in policing the lower rungs of its own system. This was not a Champions final or a Masters event — it was an open qualifier in early November, and Riot still ran a full Anti-Cheat investigation, a formal disciplinary process, and a public ruling. For every other team grinding through the open bracket this season, the message is now written down in the rulebook and in the record: knowing about it counts the same as doing it.

Two streamers' PS5s died playing GTA 6 — and now players are checking their vents

By Matt

A Twitch streamer's PS5 froze mid-game with green artifacts across the screen, then refused to boot at all. Days earlier, another streamer's console started smoking while GTA 6 was paused. Nobody has proven the game is to blame — but a repair tech measured it pulling more power than a typical game ever does.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

GTA 6 is the biggest game ever made, and it might also be the hardest a PlayStation 5 has ever had to work. Two Twitch streamers have now lost their consoles mid-session while playing it — one to a dead GPU, one to smoke — and players across Reddit are suddenly very interested in the state of their vents.

Nobody has proven the game is killing consoles. That matters, and it is the first thing to say. But the two cases are real, they happened on camera, and the power numbers behind them explain why people are worried.

The two consoles

The most dramatic case is Twitch streamer shivjam, whose PS5 died live on stream on November 24. The game froze as Jason got on a bike with Lucia, the screen went pixelated and green — the classic look of failing graphics hardware — and then the console failed outright. "GTA6 tonight fried my PS5," she posted on X. "The GPU is done and the console is gone."

It was not the first warning sign in that same broadcast: the PS5 had already crashed once earlier in the stream, and she thought the issue had resolved itself until the console fully died. When people blamed dust, she showed the inside of her console in a follow-up post — very minimal coating on the fans, kept in open space and good condition.

Days earlier, shortly after launch, streamer JoJoJosiah_ had the scarier version. He paused the game, left the room, and came back to find his PS5 smoking. "Was playing GTA VI on stream but had to go poop," he posted. "Paused it and put on a sensory vid for my chat. PS5 started just smoking out its a** and now I need to get a replacement." The smoke set off alarms, and he had to disconnect the machine to stop further damage.

The power numbers explain the worry

Console repair technician modyfikatorcasper put a meter on a PS5 running GTA 6 to find out what the game is actually demanding. Standing next to a car with little happening on screen, the console pulled 220 watts. Under maximum load, the meter recorded 274.2 watts at the wall.

A typical game peaks at 180 to 220 watts. Sony designed the PS5 to draw up to 340 to 350 watts, so GTA 6 is still inside the console's power budget — but it sits at the high end of it, well above what most games ask for. The technician called the game "the toughest real-world PS5 stress test I've seen," and suspects the heavy load is exposing weak cooling in older base PS5 models, where the liquid metal between the processor and heatsink can shift over time. Sony modified newer base models and the PS5 Pro to mitigate exactly that.

That is the most plausible explanation anyone has offered: not that GTA 6 breaks healthy consoles, but that it is the first game demanding enough to expose cooling problems in aging ones. With only a handful of public cases so far, it is too early to say whether the game is to blame or simply pushing consoles that were already on their way out.

The crashes are the bigger story

Dead hardware is rare. Crashes are not. Players are reporting frequent crashes and sudden shutdowns while playing GTA 6, with error code CE-108255-1 the most common — and reports say Rockstar's first patch did not fix it. That is the part affecting far more people than two streamers, and the part with no answer yet.

Neither Sony nor Rockstar has commented on the hardware failures. Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S consoles have not had similar issues reported, which lines up with the console comparison from earlier this week: the Series X is handling the game more smoothly than the base PS5, with steadier frame pacing and 120Hz VRR support the base PS5 lacks.

If you are playing on an older base PS5, the practical advice from all of this is unglamorous: make sure the console can breathe, clean the vents, and do not bury it in a cabinet. A game this demanding will find whatever weakness your cooling already had.

Zeus is back with T1 — the two-time world champion returns on a deal through 2029

By Matt

T1 officially announced the return of Choi 'Zeus' Woo-je on Tuesday, bringing the two-time world champion back to the organization he left two years ago — and reuniting most of the roster that won back-to-back Worlds titles.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The worst-kept secret of the League of Legends offseason is finally official. T1 announced on Tuesday that Choi "Zeus" Woo-je is returning to the organization, signing a three-year deal that runs through 2029 and putting the two-time world champion back in the top lane where he won back-to-back Summoner's Cups.

The announcement came at T1's "2027 T1 Announcement" event at the team's Basecamp in Gangnam, Seoul, where Zeus appeared on stage in front of fans to confirm the move himself. T1's own post said it plainly: "The God of Thunder returns! 'Zeus' is back with T1 through 2029."

The reunion two years in the making

Zeus came up through T1's academy and formed the core of the most decorated roster in modern League of Legends. Alongside Lee "Faker" Sang-hyeok, Mun "Oner" Hyeon-jun, Lee "Gumayusi" Min-hyeong and Ryu "Keria" Min-seok — the ZOFGK lineup — he won the World Championship in 2023 and again in 2024, the first back-to-back titles since SK Telecom T1's run a decade earlier.

Then it fell apart. Contract talks between Zeus and T1 broke down at the end of 2024, and he left for Hanwha Life Esports while Choi "Doran" Hyeon-jun went the other way. The split turned into a public dispute over how the negotiations were handled, and it only ended in July 2025, when T1 COO Josh Ahn publicly apologized to Zeus, his family and his agency.

The two years away were not wasted. At HLE, Zeus won the 2025 LCK Cup, the inaugural First Stand tournament and the 2026 Mid-Season Invitational — the first player to win First Stand, MSI, Worlds, the Asian Games and the Esports World Cup. The one thing missing was another Worlds title: HLE exited Worlds 2026 in the Swiss stage after losses to Gen.G, Invictus Gaming and eventual champions Bilibili Gaming.

How the deal came together

The move had been an open secret for a week. Zeus's contract with HLE expired on November 16, and the club officially said goodbye on November 19. Korean outlet Xportsnews first reported the T1 agreement, with Sheep Esports confirming that T1 executives Becker and Joe Marsh reached terms on November 18 — a straight three-year contract, not the two-plus-one structure earlier rumors had suggested.

Speaking at the announcement event, Zeus was candid about why he wanted a long deal wherever he landed. "After becoming a free agent, I had many thoughts," he said. "I felt it was time for a change. T1 presented a great value and vision, and I decided to return." He added that going through the transfer window is "mentally draining," and that he wanted a multi-year contract at his next team. His message to the fans was shorter: "I'm back to take T1's top-lane spot."

A new-look T1 for 2027

Zeus is the only change to the starting five, but the roster around him has shifted. The 2027 lineup is Zeus in the top lane, Oner in the jungle, Faker in mid, Kim "Peyz" Su-hwan at ADC and Keria on support — Peyz replacing Gumayusi, who is out after years as T1's bot-lane cornerstone. The coaching staff has been overhauled too: Kim "Roach" Kang-hee is the new head coach, with former pro jungler Eom "UmTi" Seong-hyeon and Lee "Easyhoon" Ji-hoon alongside him. T1 parted ways with head coach Kim "kkOma" Jeong-gyun and his staff on November 21.

Doran, the man Zeus replaces, has already landed: Dplus KIA signed him on November 20. He leaves T1 as a world champion himself, having helped the team to its third straight Worlds title in 2025.

The reunion rebuilds most of the core that dominated the last two years, with a new ADC and a new coaching staff around it. Zeus's first official match back in T1 colors comes when the 2027 LCK season begins — and the target is obvious. BLG hold the Summoner's Cup after beating Gen.G 3-1 in the Worlds 2026 final, and T1 just brought back the top laner who knows exactly what it takes to take it from them.

NHL · Nov 25, 2026 · 9:07 AM ET

Eichel scores twice as Golden Knights hand Oilers fourth straight loss

By Matt

Jack Eichel and Trevor Connelly each scored twice as Vegas beat Edmonton 5-3 at Rogers Place, pulling within three points of the Pacific lead.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Jack Eichel and Trevor Connelly each scored twice as the Vegas Golden Knights beat the Edmonton Oilers 5-3 at Rogers Place on Tuesday night, handing Edmonton its fourth straight loss and tightening the race at the top of the Pacific Division.

It was the first meeting of the season between the division's top two teams, and it lived up to the billing. Vegas pulled within three points of Edmonton for first place with the win.

How it went down

Vegas came out flying and had a two-goal lead before the first period was ten minutes old.

Eichel opened the scoring on the power play at 6:13 of the first, taking a cross-ice feed from Mitch Marner and beating Devon Levi far side with a wrist shot from the left dot. Less than three minutes later, Connelly doubled the lead, stripping the puck from Shakir Mukhamadullin in front of the Edmonton crease and lifting a quick backhand past Levi's glove.

Edmonton answered in the second. Colton Dach got the Oilers on the board, and Connor McDavid tied it 2-2 at 19:41 of the period on a give-and-go.

The Knights had the sharper response after the intermission. Nic Dowd restored the lead from in front at 2:08 of the third, and Eichel finished a 2-on-1 rush with a wrist shot five-hole at 5:29 to make it 4-2. Vasily Podkolzin pulled one back just 16 seconds later, but Connelly sealed it with an empty-net goal at 17:28.

The night's big performances

Trevor Connelly (VGK): 2 goals, 1 assist

Jack Eichel (VGK): 2 goals

Mitch Marner (VGK): 2 assists

Connor McDavid (EDM): 1 goal

Carter Hart (VGK): 21 saves

Devon Levi (EDM): 22 saves

For Connelly, it was a first on two fronts: his first career three-point game and his first career multi-goal game. The rookie's two goals were his eighth and ninth of the season, moving him into the rookie scoring lead with 19 points. He has seven points in his last four games.

Eichel's second goal was the game-winner, and he has seven points in his last five games.

Where the Pacific race stands

The win was Vegas's second in a row after a four-game skid, lifting the Knights to 15-6-5. Edmonton fell to 17-6-4 and is 0-3-1 during its season-long losing streak — the longest skid of the year for a team that has spent most of the season setting the pace in the West.

Vegas now sits three points back of Edmonton with the division lead in sight. The two teams won't have to wait long for the next chapter — and with the gap this tight, every meeting between them carries real weight in the standings.

TSL Bets: The Thanksgiving Eve parlay (~+382) — Williams anytime TD, Adebayo OVER 1.5 steals

By Matt

Kyren Williams is the Rams' goal-line back with both top receivers out, and Bam Adebayo is averaging 2.1 steals a game and just posted a triple-double. Two legs, about +382.

The games

Miami Heat (10-6) at Philadelphia 76ers (14-4) — 5:00 PM ET, Xfinity Mobile Arena, Philadelphia, PA (ESPN, NBA Cup)

76ers -1.5, total 238.5, moneyline 76ers -115 / Heat -105 (USA Today Sportsbook Wire).

Injuries — Miami: F Giannis Antetokounmpo QUESTIONABLE (right groin tendinitis — sat out Sunday, told reporters "I'm good").

Injuries — Philadelphia: C Joel Embiid DOUBTFUL (illness — missed Monday's loss to Portland). C Ariel Hukporti OUT (Achilles, season-ending).

Green Bay Packers (6-4) at Los Angeles Rams (6-4) — 8:00 PM ET, SoFi Stadium, Inglewood, CA (Netflix)

Rams -2.5, total 44.5, moneyline Rams -137 / Packers +120 (DraftKings via NBC Sports).

Injuries — Green Bay: RB Josh Jacobs QUESTIONABLE (finger — unlikely to play). EDGE Micah Parsons QUESTIONABLE (knee — activated off PUP, expected to make his season debut). LB Zaire Franklin QUESTIONABLE (shin). G Kevin Zeitler QUESTIONABLE (triceps). C Sean Rhyan QUESTIONABLE (ankle).

Injuries — Los Angeles: WR Puka Nacua OUT (IR, knee — season over). WR Davante Adams OUT (IR, hamstring). G Steve Avila OUT (hamstring). C Coleman Shelton OUT (hamstring). TE Terrance Ferguson OUT (hamstring/ankle). RB Kyren Williams PROBABLE (toe).

Storylines: With Nacua and Adams both on injured reserve, the Rams' passing game has struggled and the ground game has become the focal point — and the goal line runs through Williams. He leads the Rams with seven touchdowns this season and has scored in 6 of his last 10, with 14 red-zone targets and 84 red-zone carries. On the other side, Bam Adebayo just posted a triple-double against Oklahoma City on Sunday (24 points, 15 rebounds, 12 assists) and averages 2.1 steals a game. With Giannis questionable and Embiid doubtful, Bam shoulders more of everything for Miami — scoring, playmaking, and defense — against a Sixers team that would be playing smaller and faster without its center.

Leg 1 — Kyren Williams anytime touchdown

Williams is the Rams' goal-line back in a game where Los Angeles has no choice but to run it near the end zone: both starting receivers are out, the offensive line is banged up, and the passing game has thrown an interception in four straight games. He has 7 touchdowns this season, has scored in 6 of his last 10, and carries the ball 14.2 times a game with top-10% red-zone usage. His toe injury is listed probable after a full Monday practice. Line: anytime touchdown (+115, FanDuel). Odds Index's model gives him a 49.1% chance to score; +115 implies 46.5%.

Leg 2 — Bam Adebayo OVER 1.5 steals

Adebayo averages 2.1 steals a game and has cleared 1.5 in 12 of 16 games this season and 7 of his last 10. He is coming off a triple-double and plays 32-plus minutes a night as Miami's defensive anchor, jumping passing lanes and cleaning up in help. With Giannis questionable, his defensive load only grows, and if Embiid sits, Philadelphia plays smaller and faster — more perimeter touches for Bam to disrupt. Line: OVER 1.5 steals (+124, Odds Index). The +124 price implies 44.6%, well below his hit rate.

The bet

Kyren Williams anytime touchdown (+115, FanDuel) + Bam Adebayo OVER 1.5 steals (+124, Odds Index) — about +382. A $10 ticket returns about $48.16.

Why these legs

Both legs clear on their own. Williams is a plus-money goal-line back in a game script built for him, and Bam is a 2.1-steals-a-game defender at a line he clears in 7 of his last 10. Neither leg depends on the other — different players, different sports, different games. That is the juice rule working as intended: two plus-money legs, about +382 instead of the chalky +150 you get from stacking favorites.

The honest caveats

Williams shares goal-line work with Blake Corum, who has scored in six straight games — the Rams have two backs who can vulture the touchdown. Micah Parsons is expected to make his season debut for Green Bay, and his biggest impact in this game may be as a run defender. Bam's steals are a high-variance market, and OPTIMAL projects him for 1.4 steals tonight — under the line — even though he has hit in 7 of his last 10. If Giannis sits, Miami's game script changes, and if Embiid plays, Philadelphia slows down and posts him up instead of living on the perimeter. And a parlay needs both legs — either one can sink it alone. The edge is real, but it is an edge, not a lock.

The record

TSL Bets is 22-42 in November, 26-63 all-time.
