Gaming · Nov 24, 2026 · 10:21 AM ET

Fortnite's Treasure Hunters ends December 5 with the 'Out of Time' live event — and Treasure Week is your last shot at the gold

By Matt

Fortnite's Treasure Hunters mini season ends Saturday, December 5 with the newly announced 'Out of Time' live event at 2 p.m. ET — and Epic is giving players one final push first, with Treasure Week starting November 28 and tripled treasure odds in every chest.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Fortnite's Treasure Hunters season has an end date now, and a finale to match. Epic Games has confirmed the mini season wraps up on Saturday, December 5 with a live event called "Out of Time," kicking off at 2 p.m. ET / 7 p.m. UTC. Downtime follows the event, and Chapter 8 begins sometime after that. Before the curtain falls, Epic is running one last promotion to help players finish their collections: Treasure Week — also called Golden Week — starts Saturday, November 28 at 9 a.m. ET and runs right up to the event.

Treasure Hunters launched November 1 as a short Chapter 7 bridge season built around an 80-player island, Devil Fruit Mythics, and the One Piece crossover. It was always going to be a quick one, and the last real content drop already landed: Oscar's Captain's Day went live November 22 with a new boss, a Map Fragment, 17 sprites, and the Frenzy Auto Shotgun. Everything since has been staging for the finale, and today's update — v43.11, which went live this morning after downtime starting at 4 a.m. ET — is exactly that: a small patch that adds the files for the December 5 event and Golden Week, with no new weapons, no new sprites, and no map changes. The viral patch notes that circulated earlier in November, claiming Pirate Tokens were being removed from storm chests and the whole economy rebalanced, were fake. The real update is plumbing, and that is the point.

Treasure Week: triple the treasure, every gold reward back

Treasure Week works like the season's Treasure Hours, only stretched across the whole final week. The headline change is the treasure spawn rate in loot chests, which jumps from 1 in 62 to 1 in 21 — roughly three times as likely to unearth a treasure. Every gold reward from the season returns to the loot pool at the same time, so any gold skin variant, gold back bling, pickaxe, vehicle, jam track, or loading screen from the season can drop again. A bonus gold skin joins the pool too: gold Captain X becomes findable from November 28, alongside the returning gold A$AP Rocky, Lil Uzi Vert, Miku, and Kasane Teto skins.

The item-specific boosts are smaller than the headline number. Gold vehicles improve from 1 in 7,813 to 1 in 1,563, a fivefold jump, while gold skins move from 1 in 1,562,500 to 1 in 781,250. Pickaxe, back bling, jam track, loading screen, and gizmo odds stay where they were. Treasure Week also doubles Sprite Dust and Sprite XP all week, so the grind itself pays better even when the chest does not.

The update also added three free Solid Gold skins for players who do not want to chase chests at all. Battle Pass owners get the Gilded Charlotte-Sensei skin the next time they log in, anyone who buys the 2,400 V-Bucks bundle this season gets the Gilded Hunter Hope skin, and the Gilded Buccaneer Jones skin was available through Twitch Drops.

The Pirate Shop token still needs Treasure Hours

There is one catch, and it is the item most players actually want. The Pirate Shop Access token — the one that grants up to four weeks of free Item Shop goodies — does not get a week-long odds boost. Its drop rate only improves during Treasure Week's two Treasure Hours windows: Saturday, November 28 from 2 to 4 p.m. EST, and Saturday night from 9 to 11 p.m. EST.

Those two windows are the best shot anyone will get. During Treasure Hours the token's odds rise 1.5 times, from 1 in 137,500 to 1 in 91,667, while gold skin odds jump fifteenfold, from 1 in 1,562,500 to 1 in 104,167, and gold vehicles tenfold, from 1 in 7,813 to 1 in 781. After that, the season's treasure — token included — gets vaulted on December 5. The final Treasure Hunt Chest rewards land November 26, including the Solid Gold Captain X outfit, a Gold G-Wagon vehicle, and another round of Pirate Shop Access tokens, including a free 14-day token for 2027.

What happens December 5

The "Out of Time" event is the season's send-off and the bridge into Chapter 8. Epic has not said what the event itself contains — only the date and start time, and that downtime and Chapter 8 follow. Treasure Hunters kept Fortnite's player base active through the biggest launch week in gaming history, with GTA 6 dominating everything else, and the season's pirate-treasure loop clearly worked well enough to get a golden send-off. Whether Chapter 8 can match it is the open question; the treasure era ends in eleven days either way.

NHL · Nov 24, 2026 · 10:18 AM ET

Connor Bedard out four months after shoulder surgery — the Blackhawks lose their captain until the season's final weeks

By Matt

Connor Bedard's right shoulder surgery is done, and the timeline is now firm: about four months out. The Blackhawks' captain — and their leading scorer — won't be back until late March at the earliest, with the regular season nearly over.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The surgery is done, and the timeline is firm

Connor Bedard had surgery on his right shoulder on Monday, November 23, and the Chicago Blackhawks now have the answer they were waiting for since the decision was made on Saturday: their captain will be out for approximately four months.

Blackhawks team physician Dr. Michael Terry released the update after the procedure. "This afternoon, captain Connor Bedard underwent successful surgery to repair his right shoulder," Terry said. "We expect him to make a full recovery in an approximate timeline of four months."

That is the number Chicago was hoping to avoid hearing, and the one that changes the shape of the rest of the season. Bedard chose the surgical route rather than attempting rehabilitation, a decision made to avoid potentially delaying the procedure until the offseason. Dr. Peter Millett — the surgeon who operated on Bedard's left shoulder in July — performed this operation as well.

What the timeline means

If the recovery goes as planned, Bedard could return to the ice in late March or early April 2027. Chicago's final game of the regular season is scheduled for April 10 against the Seattle Kraken, so the timeline puts his return in the season's final weeks — with barely any runway left.

Whether he would be ready for a potential playoff run is a separate question, and one the team did not answer on Monday. The Blackhawks were placed in a difficult spot the moment the decision was made: at 8-14-2, they have won two in a row but sit well outside the playoff picture, and they will now spend the next four months finding out what the rebuild looks like without its centerpiece.

Bedard was placed on injured reserve on Sunday, freeing up a roster spot ahead of the procedure.

How it happened

The injury came on Tuesday, November 17, in Chicago's 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs. Bedard was set to take a faceoff against Maple Leafs forward Nick Paul 54 seconds into the third period when, as he put his stick on the ice, Paul's stick made contact with Bedard's right hand. The Blackhawks captain yelled out in pain and immediately went to the locker room. He did not return.

He had scored his seventh goal of the season at 18:51 of the second period, giving Chicago a 3-2 lead at the time.

For a few days, the Blackhawks held out hope that rehab might be enough. On Thursday, coach Jeff Blashill ruled Bedard out of that night's game against Columbus and the three-game road trip that followed, saying the medical staff was still weighing rehab against surgery. On Saturday, after a 4-3 overtime win in Calgary, general manager Kyle Davidson announced the decision: surgery, this week, with no timeline until after the procedure.

The third shoulder injury in less than a year

This is the third shoulder injury for Bedard in less than a year, and the pattern is what makes it sting.

His first right-shoulder injury happened much like this one — setting up for a last-second faceoff, against the St. Louis Blues on December 12, 2025. He came back from that one against the Washington Capitals on January 9, but he did not take a faceoff in a game until February 26 against Nashville, when he went 8-for-16.

The left shoulder went under the knife this past summer. Bedard injured it during an offseason training session in Vancouver in early July and had surgery a few days later. He was originally expected to be out until November. He beat it — returning for the season opener on October 13.

Now the right shoulder needs the same operation, and the same surgeon. The difference this time is the calendar: there is no summer to recover in. The four-month window runs straight through the heart of the season.

The faceoff question

Blashill was asked on Wednesday whether there is a concern about Bedard taking faceoffs moving forward, and he did not dodge it.

"I haven't looked at the video back-to-back yet, but I think in both instances, when he went to the face-off he actually hit the opponent's stick on the way down," Blashill said. "It's like you're not expecting that and it jerks yourself a little bit. It was the exact same thing in a lot of ways."

The coach added that the team knew the risk was there. "We knew there was high risk of it coming back out, not just [on] face-offs, just high risk. He knew the odds. That's the reality of it. So, whatever. We'll have to kind of move forward but part of what he is as a centerman is taking face-offs. I do think there are ways to take them without picking your stick up and coming down. So that's also something we'll explore."

Patrick Kane, speaking on Thursday before the timeline was known, put the loss in plain terms. "Obviously we're thinking about him," Kane said. "I think he knows how big of a piece he is to this team, what he means to the organization. Entertainment value, right, for fans and for the League and what he's able to provide to the game. So, obviously it's tough when you're missing a player like that."

What Chicago loses

Bedard leads the Blackhawks with 18 points in 15 games this season, tied with forward Roman Kantserov. He is the 2023 No. 1 overall pick, the face of the rebuild, and the player Chicago signed to a five-year, $75 million contract extension in July before naming him captain in September. Across his career, he has 221 points in 234 games with the Blackhawks.

The Blackhawks conclude their three-game road trip against the Seattle Kraken on Wednesday night. They will do it without their captain, and they will do the next four months the same way — waiting on a timeline that, for the first time since the injury, finally has a number on it.

Kaprizov sets the Wild's record — 15 straight games with a point, and Minnesota just won't lose

By Matt

Kirill Kaprizov broke his own franchise record with a point in his 15th straight game, and the Wild stretched their own record point streak to 15 with a 5-2 win in San Jose — 12-0-3 in that span, and alone at the top of the NHL.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Kirill Kaprizov keeps rewriting the Minnesota record book — and this time he broke his own record to do it.

Kaprizov scored a goal and added three assists in the Wild's 5-2 win over the San Jose Sharks on Monday night at SAP Center, extending his point streak to 15 games. That passes the 14-game mark he set himself in November and December of 2022, and it is the longest point streak in Wild franchise history.

The team streak matched it. Minnesota has points in 15 straight games — 12 wins, no regulation losses, three overtime defeats — the longest point streak in franchise history, passing the 14-game run from the 2022-23 season. The Wild have not lost in regulation since October 22.

The numbers

The production inside the streak is absurd. Kaprizov has 32 points across the 15 games — eight goals and 24 assists — and he opened the scoring Monday on the power play 7:37 into the first period, his 19th goal of the season.

He was not alone. Joel Eriksson Ek scored twice and added an assist, Matt Boldy had three assists of his own, and Filip Gustavsson made 22 saves in his season debut after offseason hip surgery.

The run has carried Minnesota to the top of the entire league. The Wild are 18-3-5 with a league-best 41 points.

The other record

One more piece of franchise history got rewritten Monday, quietly. Defenseman Jared Spurgeon played his 1,029th game as a member of the Wild, passing Mikko Koivu for the most games played in franchise history.

What it means

Fifteen games is a long time to never leave the rink empty-handed, and the Wild are doing it with the whole roster contributing — Kaprizov driving it, Eriksson Ek and Boldy piling up points behind him, and a goalie coming off hip surgery winning his season debut.

The record Kaprizov broke was his own. The next names on the all-time list belong to the league's greats — and at this pace, it is a matter of when, not if, that conversation starts.

Bills host Chiefs in Thanksgiving night showdown

By Matt

The 9-1 Bills host the 8-2 Chiefs at Highmark Stadium on Thanksgiving night at 8:20 p.m. — a first-place AFC clash between Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, with Kenneth Walker III's availability still uncertain after a groin injury kept him out of Kansas City's win over Arizona.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Thanksgiving night closes with the best game on the holiday slate. The Bills host the Chiefs at Highmark Stadium on Thursday at 8:20 p.m., and the AFC's top seed is very much in play.

The stakes

Buffalo comes in at 9-1, Kansas City at 8-2. A Bills win strengthens their grip on home-field advantage and the first-round bye; a Chiefs win pulls them level in the race and shakes up the No. 1 seed picture. It's a Week 12 meeting between the conference's two best records, under the lights, on NBC.

Record: 9-1; 8-2

Kickoff: Thursday, 8:20 p.m. ET

Venue: Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park, NY

TV: NBC / Peacock

The rivalry, in one paragraph

This is the tenth meeting between Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, and the series is dead even at five wins apiece. The split flips depending on the stage: Allen holds a 5-1 edge in the regular season, while Mahomes has won all four playoff meetings between the two, including a pair of AFC championship games. Thursday is a regular-season game — Allen's half of the ledger — but the seeding stakes give it a postseason feel.

The one availability watch is in Kansas City's backfield. Kenneth Walker III missed the Chiefs' 34-7 win over Arizona with a groin injury, leaving his status for Thursday uncertain. The Chiefs have managed without him — that Arizona win was their third straight by 20-plus points — but Buffalo's defense is a different test, and Walker's return would change how the Chiefs attack on the ground.

TSL Bets: The Tuesday parlay (~+283) — Flagg OVER 23.5 points, Wagner OVER 22.5 points

By Matt

Cooper Flagg is the Mavericks' lead scorer against a soft Denver defense at plus money, and Franz Wagner is averaging 27.4 a game with Paolo Banchero out. Two legs, about +283.

The games

Detroit Pistons (10-6) at Orlando Magic (7-9) — 7:00 PM ET, Kia Center, Orlando, FL

Pistons -2.5, total 213.5, moneyline -135 / +114 (ESPN).

Injuries — Detroit: C Jalen Duren OUT (hamstring). G/F Duncan Robinson OUT (quadriceps). F Taurean Prince OUT (knee). G Cade Cunningham day-to-day (knee). F Ebuka Okorie OUT (oblique).

Injuries — Orlando: F Paolo Banchero OUT (ankle). F Jonathan Isaac OUT (knee). F Noah Penda OUT (hamstring). F Izaiyah Nelson OUT (ankle).

Dallas Mavericks (10-7) at Denver Nuggets (10-5) — 10:00 PM ET, Ball Arena, Denver, CO

Nuggets -7.5, total 233.5, moneyline -310 / +251 (ESPN).

Injuries — Denver: No players listed on the injury report.

Injuries — Dallas: C Dereck Lively II OUT (foot). F P.J. Washington day-to-day (illness). F Tobi Lawal OUT (groin). G Sergio de Larrea OUT (knee). F Tarik Biberovic OUT (heel).

Storylines: With Banchero out, Wagner has become Orlando's offense — 27.4 points a game over his last 10, including 35 against Brooklyn on Nov 20 and a 35-point night against Milwaukee. Detroit is without its starting center in Duren, and Cunningham is day-to-day with a knee issue, so the Pistons' defense is thinner than the -2.5 spread suggests. In Denver, Flagg is the Mavericks' lead scorer at 24.3 a game with a 28.7% usage rate, coming off 28 points at Utah, and he faces a Nuggets defense ranked 21st in the league (115.6 defensive rating) with no Lively to protect the rim.

Leg 1 — Cooper Flagg OVER 23.5 points

Flagg averages 24.3 points a game and drives 16.4 times a night, scoring 9.4 points a game on those drives alone. He just put up 28 at Utah and 33 against Golden State, and Dallas staggers him with Irving so he gets plenty of possessions as the lead scorer. Denver's defense is 21st in the league and short on rim protection. Line: OVER 23.5 points (+100, Splash Sports).

Leg 2 — Franz Wagner OVER 22.5 points

Wagner is scoring 27.4 points over his last 10, up from 24.5 for the season, and has cleared 22.5 in 7 of those 10 games. His usage is 29.7%, he attacks the rim 21.9 times a game, and with Banchero out he carries even more of the shot creation. He is averaging 29.3 points, 7.6 rebounds and 7.6 assists over his last seven games. Line: OVER 22.5 points (-109, Bally Bet).

The bet

Cooper Flagg OVER 23.5 points (+100, Splash Sports) + Franz Wagner OVER 22.5 points (-109, Bally Bet) — about +283. A $10 ticket returns about $48.30.

Why these legs

Both legs clear on their own. Wagner is a 27.4-points-a-game scorer over his last 10 at a line nearly five points below that, with the volume and usage to back it, and Flagg is a plus-money lead scorer against a soft defense who just dropped 28. Neither leg depends on the other — different players, different games, different conferences. That is the juice rule working as intended: a plus-money leg plus a near-even leg, about +283 instead of the chalky +150 you get from stacking favorites.

The honest caveats

Flagg is the volatile leg: he has cleared 23.5 in only 4 of his last 10, with 12- and 17-point nights in that stretch — the plus money is the market telling you this is close to a coin flip. Wagner just scored 16 at Washington on Sunday, so the hot streak is not a straight line. And a parlay needs both legs — either one can sink it alone. The edge is real, but it is an edge, not a lock.

NBA · Nov 24, 2026 · 3:08 AM ET

Herro's 32 ends Bucks' 13-game losing streak

By Matt

Tyler Herro scored 32 as the Bucks beat the Raptors 116-111 in Toronto, snapping a 13-game skid — the second-longest in franchise history — for their first win since October 26.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Thirteen games later, the Milwaukee Bucks finally won one. Tyler Herro scored 32 points and Myles Turner added a season-high 27 as Milwaukee beat the Toronto Raptors 116-111 on Monday night at Scotiabank Arena, ending a skid that had stretched nearly a month and stood as the second-longest in franchise history.

The win moved Milwaukee to 2-16. It was the Bucks' first victory since beating Indiana on October 26.

How the night unfolded

It did not start like a breakout. Herro, two nights removed from a career-high 50 in a loss at Philadelphia, managed only three points in the first half as Toronto's physical defense keyed on him. Milwaukee stayed in it anyway: Turner scored 18 before the break and Kyle Kuzma added 11, and the Bucks trailed by just four at halftime despite getting almost nothing from their hottest scorer.

The third quarter is where the game turned. Herro made six of seven shots in the period for 15 points, finding his rhythm after a quiet opening two quarters and giving Milwaukee the lift it had been waiting a month for.

He finished the job in the fourth, scoring 14 more as the Bucks pulled away late and built a 10-point lead with a minute to play. With 1:51 left, Toronto's Jamal Shead missed two free throws; Herro answered at the other end to push the lead to 113-104 with 1:33 remaining, then splashed a three to make it 116-106 with 1:03 left. Toronto never got closer than the final five-point margin.

Tyler Herro: 32; 6; 8; 10-16 FG, 4-5 3PT, 8-8 FT

Myles Turner: 27; 11; —; 5 threes made

Turner fouled out after his season-best scoring night, which included five three-pointers. His first-half scoring was the reason Milwaukee was still in the game when Herro heated up.

Where the skid sits in history

Only one losing streak in Bucks history runs longer than this one: 15 straight games in March 1996, by a team that finished 25-57. The 13-game run was tied for the second-longest in franchise history, last matched in Giannis Antetokounmpo's rookie season of 2013-14 — the year that team went 15-67, the worst record in franchise history.

The drought had also produced the worst start in the franchise's 59-year history. Milwaukee dropped to 1-14 during the run, and at 2-16 it still owns the league's worst mark by winning percentage. The win in Toronto doesn't fix any of that. It just stops the bleeding — and for a team that had found a new way to lose nearly every night for a month, that counts for plenty.

Herro's week

The context makes the two nights even stranger. On Saturday in Philadelphia, Herro dropped a career-high 50 — and the Bucks lost anyway. On Monday, he scored three points in a half and still finished with a game-high 32 in a win. The scoring hasn't been the problem. The rest of the roster catching up has been, and on this night Turner and Kuzma did exactly that in the first half, holding the line until their star found his shot.

MLB · Nov 23, 2026 · 11:44 PM ET

Cubs land Trevor Rogers on five years, $120 million — the pivot after losing Skubal

By Matt

The Cubs missed on Tarik Skubal, then moved fast: left-hander Trevor Rogers is headed to Chicago on the winter's second-biggest pitching deal, pending a physical.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The Cubs did not sulk after losing Tarik Skubal. They pivoted — fast.

Chicago agreed to a deal with free agent left-hander Trevor Rogers on Monday night, MLB Network's Jon Morosi first reported. Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic reported the terms, and Jeff Passan of ESPN confirmed the guarantee: five years, with deferrals that bring down the net present value. The agreement is pending a physical.

Rogers rejected a $23.15 million qualifying offer from the Orioles earlier this month, so the signing costs Chicago draft capital on top of the contract: the Cubs forfeit their second- and fifth-highest picks in the 2027 draft, plus $1 million in international signing pool money.

The player

Rogers is 29 and coming off a full season as a rotation anchor. He made 30 starts for Baltimore in 2026, going 10-11 with a 4.03 ERA over 169⅔ innings — but the peripherals were better than the ERA: a 3.45 FIP, a 5.6% walk rate and a 22.5% strikeout rate. He leans on a five-pitch mix led by a low-to-mid-90s four-seamer, with a changeup, sweeper, sinker and cutter behind it.

The year before was the breakout. Rogers went 9-3 with a 1.81 ERA in 2025 and was voted the Orioles' most valuable player — a stunning turnaround for a pitcher Baltimore acquired from Miami in a 2024 trade that was panned at the time. Since returning to the majors for good last June, he has thrown 273 innings of 3.23 ERA ball.

MLB Trade Rumors called him arguably the second-best pitcher available this offseason, and the market agreed: with Skubal off the board, Rogers was the next arm every contender wanted.

The fit

Chicago needed this. The Cubs watched Skubal sign with the Mets on Sunday for nine years and $450 million — the richest pitcher contract in baseball history — and the rotation had a hole at the top that was not going to fill itself. Rogers slots in as a mid-rotation starter with top-of-the-rotation upside if the 2025 version is real, and at 29, the five-year commitment buys his age-30 through age-34 seasons.

The timing matters too. The collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, with a lockout expected to follow, so teams are racing to get business done before the market freezes. The Cubs got their starter with eight days to spare.

What it means

This is the winter's second-biggest pitching deal, and it tells you where the market is: even the runner-up prize costs nine figures now. Rogers is not Skubal — nobody is — but he is durable, he misses bats without walking anybody, and his last two seasons say the 2025 breakout was not a fluke.

For the Cubs, it is a statement that losing the Skubal sweepstakes did not end their offseason. For the Orioles, it is a hole in the rotation and a reminder that the qualifying offer only buys you draft picks, not the player. And for Rogers, it is life-changing money for a pitcher who, two summers ago, looked like a change-of-scenery reclamation project.

Sports · Nov 23, 2026 · 8:50 PM ET

The SEC will vote December 3 on whether to kick LSU out of the conference

By Matt

The SEC filed an amended federal complaint Monday and set a December 3 vote of league presidents on terminating LSU's membership — the second time this fall the league has put expulsion on the table, and a step the conference has never taken against a member.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The vote

The Southeastern Conference will vote on whether to kick LSU out of the league.

The SEC announced Monday that it filed an amended complaint and a motion for a temporary restraining order in its federal lawsuit against Louisiana State University, and that the conference's presidents and chancellors will meet Thursday, December 3, to deliberate LSU's ongoing membership in the conference. The court filing goes further than the public statement: the league's CEOs, it says, intend to hold the December 3 special meeting and "consider termination of LSU's membership in the SEC."

Commissioner Greg Sankey made clear in a signed affidavit that the vote is happening regardless of what LSU does next. Termination of LSU's membership, he wrote, "will be considered whether or not LSU continues to exclude Mr. Luis from participating in basketball games as a player on the LSU team."

That is the sentence that turns a legal fight into an existential one. LSU has already done what the league asked on the player at the center of it. The SEC is voting anyway.

How we got here

The flashpoint is men's basketball guard RJ Luis Jr., whom the SEC deemed ineligible. LSU played him anyway last week against Louisiana-Monroe, after a Louisiana court barred the conference from penalizing the school for rostering him. LSU president Wade Rousse then instructed head coach Will Wade not to play Luis, and Luis has since been removed from the roster.

But the Luis case is the second act, not the first. The feud started in September, when LSU football — under first-year head coach Lane Kiffin — tried to add two former NFL players, tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris, to its roster. The SEC threatened expulsion then, too, and convened the other conference schools on September 10 to discuss it. No vote was taken, LSU backed down and declined to roster either player, and the league said discussions would continue toward an "appropriate resolution."

They continued, all right. The SEC's amended complaint now accuses LSU of conduct that confirms "the lack of institutional control over the athletics program at LSU that is required by Article 6 of the SEC Constitution." The league's legal theory, laid out in its filing, is a First Amendment freedom-of-association argument: like a private association, it says it has the right to expel a member whose conduct contradicts its message. The SEC is also asking a federal judge in Alabama to keep anyone from going to court to block the December 3 meeting.

The bar — and the history

Removing LSU would take a two-thirds vote of the conference's members, with LSU presumably not voting to expel itself.

It would also be something the SEC has never done. No member has ever been voted out of the conference. The three schools that left — Sewanee in 1940, Georgia Tech in 1964, Tulane in 1966 — all walked away voluntarily. LSU is a founding member, and one of the league's most valuable and successful on-field brands.

That is why the threat lands the way it does even if the votes are not there. When the idea first surfaced in September, Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana called it "bone deep down to the marrow stupid." The skepticism has not gone away — but the vote is now scheduled, with a date, after the league went to federal court to protect its right to hold it.

What's at stake

Expulsion would end LSU's membership in every sport, not just the one that started the fight. Football, basketball, baseball, all of it — out of the conference LSU helped build, with no obvious landing spot that replaces the money, the schedule, or the recruiting footprint of the SEC.

And the stakes run past Baton Rouge. The SEC is suing one of its own members in federal court to establish that it can enforce its eligibility rules after years of court rulings that have cut the other way. If the league wins that argument, every conference in the country gains a precedent. If it loses — or if its own presidents blink on December 3 — the message is that a member can defy the league in court and survive.

What's next

The December 3 meeting will be held by videoconference. The federal court still has to rule on the SEC's request for a temporary restraining order, and no hearing date has been made public. Between now and then, expect Louisiana politicians, LSU leadership, and the other 15 SEC schools to spend ten days counting votes in public and in private.

The vote itself is the story. Whatever the presidents decide on December 3, a conference putting a founding member's existence to a vote is the kind of thing that only happens once — and college sports will be living with the answer for a long time.

Florida State hires Georgia's Glenn Schumann — the 36-year-old first-timer tasked with bringing the Seminoles back

By Matt

Florida State has its next head coach: Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann, 36, on a five-year deal. He stays with the Bulldogs through the postseason, then takes over a program that fired Mike Norvell three weeks ago.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The hire

Florida State has its next head coach. The Seminoles announced Monday evening that Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann will take over the program, ending a three-week search that began when Mike Norvell was fired on November 1.

ESPN's Pete Thamel and Andrea Adelson first reported the agreement, and the Tallahassee Democrat confirmed it. Schumann, 36, has agreed to a five-year deal, per ESPN, and he will remain with Georgia through the Bulldogs' postseason run before taking over in Tallahassee full time.

He is a first-time head coach. That is the gamble, and Florida State knows it — the Seminoles reportedly preferred a candidate with head-coaching experience, and hired the one without it anyway. What Schumann lacks in that column, he makes up for in the only currency that matters in this sport: he has spent his entire adult coaching life inside the two programs that have defined the last decade of college football.

The pedigree

Schumann enrolled at Alabama in 2008 to work under Nick Saban and spent seven seasons on the Crimson Tide's defensive staff. He followed Kirby Smart to Georgia in 2016, coached inside linebackers for all 11 seasons there, became co-defensive coordinator in 2019, and has run the defense as its coordinator since 2022.

The résumé from those stops is hard to argue with. He has been on staff for six national championships between Alabama and Georgia, including Georgia's back-to-back titles in 2021 and 2022 — he was co-defensive coordinator for the first and the defensive coordinator and primary play caller for the second. As a position coach, he produced three Butkus Award winners, making him the only primary position coach of multiple winners from 2016 through 2025.

The defense he is leaving behind is still elite. Through 11 games this season, Georgia ranks sixth nationally in total defense and scoring defense, eighth in sacks and ninth in rushing defense. He also becomes the seventh former Smart assistant to land a college head-coaching job, joining Dan Lanning, Shane Beamer, Fran Brown, Sam Pittman, Mel Tucker and Dell McGee.

The job he inherits

Norvell's firing came after a 3-5 start in his seventh season, and the numbers explain why the leash ran out: 41-39 overall in six-plus seasons, and a $50 million buyout Florida State is paying anyway. Interim head coach Rick Stockstill has steadied things at 2-1 since taking over, but this is a rebuild, not a tune-up.

The calendar gives Schumann no runway. Signing Day is one week away, and the transfer portal opens January 4 and runs through January 13. His first major decision — and the one that will define the hire as much as anything he does on defense — is who he picks as offensive coordinator. He is a defensive coach taking over a program whose problems have mostly been on the other side of the ball.

There is a personal thread here, too. Schumann is a Valdosta, Georgia, native whose grandfather, Jack Haskin, founded Florida State's Flying High Circus and was an assistant coach for the Seminoles' inaugural football season in 1947. And the hire carries a sting for anyone in Tallahassee who remembers December 30, 2023: Schumann's Georgia defense beat Florida State 63-3 in the Orange Bowl, a result that helped accelerate Norvell's downfall. The man who helped end the last era is now in charge of the next one.

What's next

Schumann finishes the season with Georgia first, so Florida State's new era starts in earnest once the Bulldogs' postseason ends. The Seminoles will not have to wait long to measure him against his old program, either — Florida State and Georgia are scheduled to meet in Nashville's Nissan Stadium in 2028, his second season on the job.

Astros part ways with pitching coach Josh Miller after 16 years — the Ausmus overhaul rolls on

By Matt

Houston told Josh Miller in October that he'd be back for 2027. Then Brad Ausmus arrived as manager, and the 16-year Astro is out — the latest piece of a full teardown in Houston.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The Houston Astros will have a new pitching coach in 2027. Josh Miller will not return to the staff under new manager Brad Ausmus, MLB.com's Brian McTaggart first reported on Monday, with The Athletic confirming the same through team sources.

It ends a 16-year run with the organization for Miller, who joined the Astros in 2010 and worked his way up from scout and minor league coach to bullpen coach and, since 2022, major league pitching coach. He was in the organization for both World Series titles.

The reversal

This one caught people off guard because Houston had already said the opposite. Last month, the club announced Miller was among the coaches who would return for the 2027 season, alongside first-base coach Dave Clark, field coordinator Jason Bell, hitting coach Victor Rodriguez and bullpen catcher Javier Bracamonte.

That announcement came before Ausmus was hired as manager on November 13. Once the new skipper arrived, the plan changed. Miller is now the second coach from that supposedly returning group to leave, after Bell took a job on the Boston Red Sox staff.

Whether Ausmus drove the decision or Miller had a change of heart himself is unclear. Either way, the message is the same: the new manager gets his own staff.

The backstory

Miller, who turns 48 in February, was a minor league pitcher who also pitched professionally in Taiwan before moving into coaching. He spent two years as Houston's bullpen coach under Brent Strom, then took over the pitching coach job when Strom left after the 2021 season. Strom, notably, returned to the organization as a pitching consultant a few months ago — but that relationship did not keep Miller on Ausmus' staff.

The results in 2026 did Miller no favors. Houston finished 81-81, and the pitching staff posted a 4.45 ERA, 24th in baseball, while issuing 650 walks. A staff that used to be the organization's calling card spent the season leaking runs and free passes.

The overhaul

Miller's exit is one piece of a teardown that now touches every level of the organization. Owner Jim Crane fired general manager Dana Brown in August and announced after the season that manager Joe Espada would not return. Randy Flores, hired away from the Cardinals, is the new general manager after the Astros' first choice, Brewers assistant GM Matt Kleine, turned down the job.

On the coaching staff, the vacancies are piling up. Beyond pitching coach, Houston still needs a third base coach, a bullpen coach, and assistant hitting and pitching coaches. The club announced last week that longtime big league catcher Bobby Wilson, who had been the Nationals' catching and game-planning coach, will be the new bench coach. Rodriguez and Clark are still expected back, though that was also true of Miller until Monday.

What's next

Houston now has to find a pitching coach who fits Ausmus' vision and can rebuild a staff that lost its way in 2026 — and do it before a December 1 lockout freezes the sport. Miller, meanwhile, becomes one of the more experienced pitching coaches on the market, with a World Series ring on his resume and sixteen years inside one of baseball's model organizations.

The Astros spent a decade as the standard. This offseason, they are starting over.

NFL · Nov 23, 2026 · 4:13 PM ET

Cardinals fire DC Nick Rallis — the defense finally costs someone his job

By Matt

Arizona fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis on Monday, a day after a 34-7 loss to the Chiefs dropped the Cardinals to 3-8 with the league's second-worst scoring defense. Teryl Austin takes over for the final six games.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The Arizona Cardinals fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis on Monday, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport first reported, with ESPN's Adam Schefter confirming the same. Senior defensive assistant Teryl Austin will serve as interim defensive coordinator for the final six games of the season.

It is the second coordinator firing of the NFL season. The Carolina Panthers dismissed defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero on October 30.

The breaking point

The timing was not hard to read. Arizona lost 34-7 to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, a game in which the Chiefs sat most of their starters for much of the fourth quarter and still won by 27. The Cardinals dropped to 3-8, and the defense now ranks 31st in scoring defense, allowing 29.4 points per game — the second-highest average in the league behind only the Las Vegas Raiders.

That number is not a one-week blip. Rallis' 2025 defense allowed 28.7 points per game, 29th in the league, and Arizona has now given up 323 points through 11 games this season. The unit has been bottom-five in scoring defense in back-to-back seasons.

The backstory

Rallis, 33, had run the Cardinals defense since 2023, hired under former head coach Jonathan Gannon. When first-year head coach Mike LaFleur took over this season, he kept Rallis on staff despite interviewing other candidates for the job — a hesitant retention, and one that lasted eleven games.

LaFleur had already hinted at the frustration publicly. Three days after telling reporters "it ain't working right now," his defense held the Rams to 16 points in an 18-16 win at SoFi Stadium. It was the exception, not the turn. The Chiefs loss was the second straight game in which Arizona gave up 34 points.

Rallis still had one more season left on his contract.

The replacement

Austin is a familiar name with a long coordinator resume. He ran defenses in Detroit from 2014 to 2017, Cincinnati in 2018, and Pittsburgh from 2022 to 2025. The Bengals fired him nine games into 2018, a day after a 51-14 loss to the New Orleans Saints — the same kind of Monday-after exit Rallis got this week.

Whether Austin is a candidate for the full-time job beyond these six games is an open question. LaFleur has not said.

What's next

Austin inherits a defense that has been one of the league's worst for two straight years and a team playing out the string at 3-8. The firing does not fix the roster, and it does not answer the bigger question in Arizona — whether LaFleur himself is safe after a first season that has gone sideways. But somebody had to pay for a defense giving up nearly 30 points a game, and on Monday, it was Rallis.

MLB offers a $1 million minimum salary and earlier free agency — but only if players accept a salary cap

By Matt

With eight days left before the collective bargaining agreement expires, MLB offered a $1 million minimum salary, earlier free agency and a bigger pre-arbitration pool on Monday — all conditioned on a salary cap the union has vowed never to accept.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The offer

Major League Baseball put its most player-friendly proposal of the labor fight on the table Monday — and tied every dollar of it to a salary cap.

The league agreed to raise the minimum salary to $1 million for all players beginning next season, up from $780,000. It would be the largest minimum-salary increase in baseball history, eclipsing the previous record jump of $129,500.

Free agency would come sooner, too. MLB formally accepted the union's proposal to cut the service-time requirement from six years to five for players who turn 30, with the team keeping the right to sign the player to the average salary of the 125 highest-paid players. According to MLB's research, the change would affect 512 players on 40-man rosters.

The pre-arbitration bonus pool would grow 30 percent, from $50 million to $65 million, rising to $75 million before the end of the next collective bargaining agreement. Players who spent at least one full season in the major leagues would receive at least $1.1 million through the pre-arbitration bonus program. MLB claims 57 percent of all players on 40-man rosters would benefit from the increase beginning next season.

Two more sweeteners came with it: an automatic 5 percent signing bonus for arbitration-eligible players who sign without going through the arbitration process, and a yearly, centrally funded $500,000 bonus for one veteran per team with at least six years of major-league service who signs a one-year contract for $10 million or less. MLB also proposed eliminating the qualifying offer and draft-pick compensation in free agency.

The catch

None of it happens unless the players accept a salary cap and a payroll floor.

Commissioner Rob Manfred has said owners will agree to a deal only if it includes one, and the league's standing proposal sets the cap at $258.2 million and the floor at $180.2 million, starting in 2028. The union has vowed never to accept a cap.

MLB spokesman Glen Caplin framed the offer as meeting the players' objectives: "Every other major U.S. sport has a salary cap and floor system to limit payroll disparity, and the fact remains that growth in player compensation has been slower in baseball than every one of those leagues. MLB is trying to reach an agreement with the players by meeting their objectives on a number of important issues, including earlier access to free agency and increased compensation for players earlier in their careers."

The union's interim executive director, Bruce Meyer, did not buy it: "The league's proposals today don't add a single dollar in overall player compensation as compared to prior proposals, and once again are expressly conditioned on accepting their salary cap and other anti-player restrictions. Any supposed benefits to certain classes of players are simply taken out of the pockets of other players."

The union's counter

The players answered Monday with a proposal of their own: share all media revenue equally among the 30 clubs — without a cap attached.

That is a real concession in one direction. The union formally agreed to the owners' proposal to equally share all MLB media revenues, a first for the sport. Local media revenue has fallen to $1.8 billion this year, down $575 million from a high of about $2.4 billion annually from 2021 to 2024, as cable networks have declined.

The union is also proposing that low-revenue teams receive more than $950 million beginning in 2027, up from about $700 million this past season, with rewards designed to discourage tanking: $20 million for revenue-sharing recipients that qualify for the postseason or finish with a better record than the worst postseason qualifier, and $10 million for finishing above .500.

What happens next

The clock is the story now. The current five-year labor contract expires Dec. 1 at 11:59 p.m. EST, and management is expected to lock out the players — the sport's 10th work stoppage since 1972, bringing signings and trades to a halt.

The two sides are expected to resume negotiations Tuesday in New York, take a break through the Thanksgiving holidays, and perhaps pick up again during the weekend in Phoenix, when the union holds its annual meeting with its executive sub-committee.

The talks resumed one day after Tarik Skubal agreed to a $450 million, nine-year contract with the Mets, the richest pitcher deal in baseball history — and the market has been sprinting ever since, with Paul Goldschmidt signing with the Mets on Monday as well. Everyone in the game knows what Dec. 1 means. The question is whether eight days is enough to bridge a gap that has not moved in months.

49ers release Brandon Aiyuk — the two-year standoff ends, and Washington is waiting

By Matt

San Francisco released Brandon Aiyuk on Monday, closing a two-year standoff that outlasted a $120 million extension and a devastating knee injury. The Commanders, short on receivers and long linked to him, are the likely landing spot.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The 49ers are done waiting on Brandon Aiyuk. San Francisco released the wide receiver on Monday, ESPN sources told Adam Schefter, and Ian Rapoport reported the same — with Aiyuk likely to join the Washington Commanders practice squad.

It is the end of a standoff that has stretched across two seasons, a contract fight, a serious knee injury, and a complete breakdown in the relationship between the player and the team. Nobody in Santa Clara pretended this was a football decision anymore. Head coach Kyle Shanahan had already said Aiyuk would not be an option for the team at any point in the future.

The fall

Aiyuk arrived in San Francisco as a 2020 first-round pick and, two years ago, looked like a foundational piece. The 49ers signed him to a four-year extension before the 2024 season, and he was playing well before the year came apart — seven games in, he tore the ACL and MCL in his right knee, an injury that ended his season and kept him off the field for all of 2025. He has not played since October 2024.

The recovery never became a comeback. Aiyuk reportedly stopped attending team-directed rehabilitation sessions and meetings, communication with the team broke down, and the 49ers placed him on the reserve/left squad list after he stopped reporting to the facility last December.

The last act played out over the past three weeks. Aiyuk hired agent Drew Rosenhaus, filed paperwork to be reinstated, and reported to the team facility. He was reinstated on November 9, passed the 49ers' physical — Rosenhaus says he is 100 percent healthy, with clean MRIs and X-rays — and the clock started on a two-week roster exemption that expired Monday. The 49ers had to make a call by the deadline. They made it.

The money

The divorce is not cheap for either side, and it is not finished. The 49ers say Aiyuk owes about $13 million of a roughly $23 million signing bonus and are negotiating forfeiture, and his 2026 salary was voided. He also lost $27 million in 2026 guarantees over his absences from team meetings and activities.

What's next

Because the trade deadline has passed, Aiyuk goes through waivers first. He is widely expected to clear, and then he becomes a free agent. Rosenhaus told Dianna Russini that Aiyuk plans to hold workouts for interested teams.

Washington is the obvious fit, and it has been for a long time. Aiyuk reached out to Jayden Daniels about a month ago — the two were teammates at Arizona State — and the two have reconciled. The Commanders are also desperate for receiver help: Terry McLaurin is out with a torn patellar tendon suffered in Week 6, and Dyami Brown and Jaylin Lane are on injured reserve. Washington has already worked out receivers and signed Malik Heath to the practice squad.

The cost of a flier is almost nothing. The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala noted that if Washington signed Aiyuk to the practice squad at the maximum rate for a player of his experience and elevated him for three games, it would owe him roughly $305,000 for the rest of the regular season. And the upside is a receiver who, in 2023, posted a career-high 1,342 receiving yards during the 49ers' run to the Super Bowl.

If he plays anything like that again, Washington gets a steal. If he does not, the Commanders can move on without losing much. Either way, the Aiyuk era in San Francisco is over.

49ers lock up GM John Lynch with a contract extension — the Shanahan-Lynch braintrust stays together

By Matt

Hours before the 49ers rolled the Vikings in Mexico City, San Francisco finalized a contract extension with general manager John Lynch — keeping the architect of one of the NFL's best teams in place for the foreseeable future.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The 49ers are not letting their general manager get away.

San Francisco finalized a contract extension with John Lynch shortly before Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City, Fox Sports' Jay Glazer reported. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport also reported the agreement. Lynch will remain the team's president of football operations and general manager for the foreseeable future.

No terms were announced, and no length was disclosed — just that the deal is done and the braintrust stays intact.

The timing said plenty. Hours after the extension was finalized, the 49ers went out and dismantled Minnesota 35-10 in Mexico City to improve to 9-1, tied for the best record in the NFL.

The partnership

Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan arrived in San Francisco together in 2017, and they have been extended in lockstep ever since — joint extensions in 2020 and again in 2023, and now a third round. Shanahan quietly signed his own extension in September, believed to run through 2027.

Lynch needed this one. His contract was set to expire after this season, and owner Jed York had said at the league meetings in March that he wanted both men around for a "very long time." Now both are under contract going forward.

The record

The results make the case for the extension on their own. Under Lynch, the 49ers are 91-68, with five playoff berths and two Super Bowl appearances.

Lynch came to the job from an unusual place — the Fox broadcast booth, straight into the GM chair, with no front-office experience. A Pro Football Hall of Fame safety who won a Super Bowl with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during a 15-season playing career, he was hired in 2017 to rebuild a 2-14 team. Nine years later, that team is 9-1 and tied for the best record in the NFL.

What it means

This is a stability move, and stability is the whole point. The 49ers have had the same coach and general manager for a decade, and the league's best record is the payoff. With Shanahan locked up in September and Lynch now extended, the two men who built this roster will be the ones deciding what comes next — including the question of whether this 9-1 start turns into the Super Bowl run that has eluded them twice.

NAVI complete the miracle run, beating FUT 4-3 to win the Brawl Stars World Finals

By Matt

NAVI — in through October's Last Chance Qualifier — beat FUT Esports 4-3 in a seven-set grand final in Tokyo to win the Brawl Stars World Finals 2026 and $450,000.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

NAVI are Brawl Stars world champions. The team that only reached the World Finals through October's Last Chance Qualifier in China beat FUT Esports 4-3 in a seven-set grand final on Sunday at Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium, closing out the Brawl Stars Championship 2026 season in front of 7,000 fans and taking home $450,000 from a $1,000,000 prize pool.

A final that went the distance

NAVI carried a one-set advantage into the grand final as the upper-bracket team, then won the opening Gem Grab set to go up 2-0. FUT answered with three straight sets — Brawl Ball, Bounty and a second Gem Grab — to take a 3-2 lead and stand one set from the title. NAVI held on from there, winning Knockout and then Heist to close out the series, with the six sets actually played finishing 3-3 before the bracket advantage settled it.

It was the second time in two days NAVI had beaten FUT. The two teams had already met in the upper quarterfinals, where NAVI edged a 3-2 series that went to a deciding Hot Zone set.

The run that got them there

Nobody had NAVI penciled in for this. They arrived in Tokyo as the last team in, through the Last Chance Qualifier, and opened the group stage by beating the defending world champions, Crazy Raccoon, 3-1. A 1-3 loss to Team Elektros sent them to a decider, where they swept NOVO Esports 3-0 to reach the playoffs.

From there it was upset after upset. NAVI beat FUT 3-2 in the upper quarterfinals, knocked out HMBLE — the two-time Brawl Cup winners — 3-1 in the upper semifinals, then beat the previously unbeaten Team Elektros 3-1 in the upper final to book their place in the championship match.

The roster is Polish and British rather than Ukrainian: Łukasz "GeRo" Gerek, Edward "Enraged" Stowe and Damian "Nowy297" Nowakowski. For GeRo and Nowy297, it is a second world championship. For the 18-year-old Enraged, it is a first — and he was named the grand final MVP.

Final standings

1st: NAVI; $450,000

2nd: FUT Esports; $200,000

3rd: Team Elektros; $100,000

4th: ZETA DIVISION; $80,000

5th–6th: HMBLE, Reply Totem; $40,000

7th–8th: Tribe Gaming, Bounty Hunters; $20,000

9th–10th: NOVO Esports, Team Heretics; $15,000

11th–12th: Crazy Raccoon, RED Canids; $10,000

The defending champions finished last. Crazy Raccoon, the 2025 winners playing on home ground in Japan, went out in the group stage — beaten by NAVI in the opener and then by NOVO Esports in the elimination match.

What's next

The World Finals were the biggest edition Supercell has staged for the game, with 12 teams across three days in Tokyo. The circuit moves on quickly: the Brawl Cup heads to South Korea next, and Paris will host the Brawl Stars World Finals 2027. The new season kicks off with four regional Invitationals in January 2027.

MLB · Nov 23, 2026 · 11:45 AM ET

Mets keep spending: Paul Goldschmidt signs one-year, $8 million deal a day after the Skubal splash

By Matt

One day after landing Tarik Skubal, the Mets added former NL MVP Paul Goldschmidt on a one-year deal — a veteran bat for a first-base spot that has been a revolving door.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The Mets are not done spending.

One day after landing Tarik Skubal, New York agreed to a deal with free agent first baseman Paul Goldschmidt on Monday morning, multiple outlets reported. FanSided's Robert Murray was first to report the agreement, and Jon Heyman of the New York Post also reported the deal. The contract is for one year and $8 million, with up to $2 million more available in performance bonuses, according to Will Sammon of The Athletic and Joel Sherman of the Post.

The timing is no accident. The Mets moved fast after the Skubal signing, and with eight days left before the collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1 — and an expected lockout to follow — the market is moving at a sprint.

The player

Goldschmidt is 39 and still producing in the right role. He spent the past two seasons with the Yankees, where he largely started against right-handed pitching — and handled it well, hitting .299 with a .967 OPS against righties last season.

His full 2026 line with New York was a .252 average with 18 home runs and 52 RBIs in 105 games. The resume behind it is the reason the Mets wanted him: seven All-Star selections, four Gold Gloves, and the 2022 National League MVP award.

Across 16 big-league seasons, Goldschmidt is a career .286 hitter with 390 home runs and 1,284 RBIs in 2,179 games, spanning the Diamondbacks, Cardinals and Yankees. He turns 40 late in the 2027 season, so this is a short-term bet on a proven bat, not a long-term commitment.

The fit

First base has been a hole in Queens since Pete Alonso signed with the Baltimore Orioles last winter. The Mets finished last in the National League East at 74-88 in 2026, with Jared Young and Mark Vientos splitting time at first base — and Young, Jorge Polanco, Vientos and Brett Baty sharing the first-base and designated-hitter at-bats between them.

Goldschmidt gives them a real first baseman and a right-handed bat who has mashed right-handed pitching, which is exactly the side of the platoon the Mets were thin on. He also comes from across town: the Mets pried him away from the Yankees, where a return had been considered a possibility after he said following the season that he planned to keep playing.

What it means

This is the second Mets signing in two days, and the two moves tell one story: Steve Cohen is spending like a man who believes the window is now. Sunday brought the richest pitcher contract in baseball history. Monday brought a former MVP on a one-year deal to plug the most obvious hole in the lineup.

The luxury-tax bill stings — MLB Trade Rumors notes the Mets sit in the top penalty tier, where a 110% tax pushes the real cost of the deal to $16.8 million — but Cohen has never let the tax stop him, and a one-year commitment carries no long-term risk.

Goldschmidt is not the headline. Skubal was the headline. But championship rosters are built on moves like this one, and the Mets just made two of them in 24 hours.

NFL · Nov 23, 2026 · 9:19 AM ET

Travis Kelce just passed Rob Gronkowski — third-most touchdowns ever by a tight end

By Matt

An eight-yard touchdown from Patrick Mahomes moved Travis Kelce past Rob Gronkowski into third place all-time among tight ends — and he added a second score before halftime in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over Arizona.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The pass

It took one drive. On the Chiefs' opening possession against the Arizona Cardinals, Patrick Mahomes found Travis Kelce for an eight-yard touchdown — the 109th total touchdown of Kelce's career, and the one that moved him past Rob Gronkowski into third place all-time among tight ends.

Gronkowski finished his career with 108 total touchdowns. Kelce entered Sunday tied with him, and by the end of the first quarter he was alone in third. Only two tight ends in NFL history sit ahead of him now: Tony Gonzalez and Antonio Gates.

Kelce did not stop there. He caught a 22-yard touchdown from Mahomes in the second quarter — his 110th career score — on his way to six catches for 74 yards and two touchdowns in a 34-7 Chiefs win that moved Kansas City to 8-2.

A very short list

The second touchdown put Kelce in company that has nothing to do with tight ends. He became only the fourth player in NFL history to score two touchdowns in a half at age 37 or older, joining Jim Thorpe, Steve Young, and Jerry Rice.

It was also his first multi-touchdown game since Week 11 of the 2022 season against the Chargers — a reminder that the 37-year-old is still finding new lines for the resume in his 14th season. Sunday was his 100th regular-season game at Arrowhead Stadium, making him just the fourth player in franchise history to reach that mark since the stadium opened in 1972.

The gap to the top of the list is now small. Kelce needs five more touchdowns to tie Gonzalez, and eight to tie Gates, with seven regular-season games left on the schedule.

The Gronk comparison

The numbers behind the pass tell the story of two different kinds of careers. Kelce entered Sunday with 108 touchdowns — 104 receiving, three rushing, one return — across 226 games and 14 seasons. Gronkowski reached the same total in 165 games over 11 seasons, with 107 receiving scores and one rushing.

Gronkowski, a four-time Super Bowl champion, will be eligible for the Hall of Fame ballot for the first time in 2027. Kelce, a three-time Super Bowl champion, will join him there eventually. The list they are climbing now is the one that decides how history orders them.

A season of climbing

This is not Kelce's first record of the fall. He entered Week 11 leading the Chiefs with 512 receiving yards, and earlier this season he and Mahomes passed Gates and Philip Rivers for the most yards generated by a tight end and quarterback duo in NFL history. In Week 2 he broke Marshall Faulk's career record for yards after the catch.

Kelce ranks first among tight ends in NFL history in receiving yards including playoffs. The touchdowns were the one list where Gronkowski still stood in front of him. Not anymore.

NFL · Nov 23, 2026 · 9:19 AM ET

Jahmyr Gibbs just tied Barry Sanders — 52 rushing touchdowns before 25, and the record is one score away

By Matt

Two touchdowns against Tampa Bay gave Jahmyr Gibbs 52 career rushing touchdowns, tying Barry Sanders for the most by a player before his 25th birthday — and Gibbs doesn't turn 25 until March.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The tie

Jahmyr Gibbs needed two rushing touchdowns on Sunday to catch Barry Sanders. He got both — in a 31-21 Lions win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field — and now the two Detroit running backs share the NFL record for the most rushing touchdowns by a player before turning 25.

Gibbs walked into the game with 50 career rushing scores, level with Emmitt Smith. The brace on Sunday passed Smith and put him alongside Sanders, the greatest Lion of them all.

He finished the afternoon with 23 carries for 98 yards and the two touchdowns, plus four catches for 20 yards — 118 scrimmage yards in a win that pushed Detroit to 8-2 ahead of Thursday's Thanksgiving showdown with the Bears.

One more and it's his alone

Here is the part that makes this more than a tie: Gibbs does not turn 25 until March 20, 2027. He has the rest of this season — and the whole of next season's opening stretch before his birthday — to score one more rushing touchdown and own the record outright.

He has already done the same thing in the combined category. Back on October 11 against Arizona, Gibbs passed Sanders for the most total touchdowns by a player before 25, reaching 58 career scores in that game. Now he shares the rushing-only mark too, and the next one breaks the tie.

The season he is putting together makes it a matter of when, not if. Through ten games he has 1,502 scrimmage yards and 15 scrimmage touchdowns, and he entered Sunday tied for the league lead in touchdowns from scrimmage.

The company he keeps

The record book keeps running out of room for Gibbs. His 64 total touchdowns in 59 career games moved him past Jim Brown for the second-most by a player in his first 60 games. He is the fourth player ever to score a touchdown in 40 games within his first four seasons, joining LaDainian Tomlinson, Terrell Davis, and Maurice Jones-Drew.

And it is not just a solo act. Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown have now each scored a touchdown in the same game 25 times, tying Marvin Harrison and Edgerrin James for the third-most by a running back and wide receiver duo.

What it means

Tying Barry Sanders in anything is a career-defining line on a resume. Gibbs did it at 24, in his fourth season, on a team chasing the NFC's top seed. The Lions are 8-2, the record is one touchdown away, and the player ahead of him on the list is the one whose name is on the standard itself.

Sanders congratulated Gibbs personally when he passed him for the combined-touchdowns mark in October. The next one — the one that puts Gibbs alone at the top of the rushing list — is coming, and it will not take long.

TSL Bets: The Monday night parlay (~+414) — Higgins OVER 74.5 receiving yards, Diggs anytime TD

By Matt

Tee Higgins averages 91.6 receiving yards a game against the NFL's second-worst pass defense, and Stefon Diggs has scored in 5 of 8 games as Washington's clear WR1. Two legs, about +414.

The game

Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) at Washington Commanders (3-5-1) — 8:15 PM ET, Northwest Stadium, Landover, MD, ESPN

Bengals -6, total 54.5, moneyline -295 / +240 (BetMGM). Weather: cloudy, 56°F at kickoff, NW wind ~7 mph, 0% rain — no factor.

Injuries — Cincinnati: G Dalton Risner OUT (knee). LB Oren Burks OUT (groin, IR). WR Andrei Iosivas doubtful (thumb). CB Jalen Davis doubtful (hamstring). G Dylan Fairchild questionable (oblique — practiced fully Saturday). S Kyle Dugger questionable (quadriceps). CB Dax Hill questionable (illness). LB Swayze Bozeman questionable (forearm). G Brian Parker II questionable (knee). Joe Burrow carries no designation (illness cleared). Tee Higgins carries no designation (knee, full participant).

Injuries — Washington: RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt questionable (groin). RB Rachaad White questionable (heel). C Lucas Patrick questionable (concussion). CB Amik Robertson questionable (ankle). QB Jayden Daniels is healthy — 23-of-33 for 249 yards and 3 touchdowns last week against the Giants. WR Terry McLaurin is on IR (knee, out for the season).

Storylines: The Bengals have won five straight behind Joe Burrow's 27 touchdown passes in nine games, and Washington ranks second-worst in the NFL in passing yards allowed (244.8 a game). The 54.5 total is the highest on the Week 11 board — the market expects a shootout. Washington stayed alive in the NFC East with a late 24-21 win over the Giants in Week 10, sealed by Stefon Diggs' 32-yard game-winning touchdown catch with 57 seconds left.

Leg 1 — Tee Higgins OVER 74.5 receiving yards

Higgins has 824 receiving yards and 6 touchdowns on 53 catches through nine games — 91.6 yards a game — and needs 176 more yards to reach 1,000 on the season. His recent form is loud: 155 yards (10 catches, 2 TDs) vs. Tennessee, 148 yards (6 catches, 1 TD) at Baltimore, 32 yards (5 catches, 2 TDs) vs. Atlanta. He is Burrow's second option in an offense that just put up 409 passing yards, and he draws a Washington secondary that is second-worst in the league against the pass with its cornerback questionable. Line: OVER 74.5 receiving yards (-115, bet365).

Leg 2 — Stefon Diggs anytime touchdown

Diggs leads Washington in targets (59), receptions (36), receiving yards (386) and receiving touchdowns (6) — and he has scored in 5 of his 8 games, including the game-winner last week (6 catches, 83 yards, TD on 10 targets). With Terry McLaurin out for the season, Diggs is the clear WR1 and Daniels' first read in the red zone; he has drawn 10 targets in a game and is coming off his best yardage day of the season. Cincinnati's defense has to pick its poison between Diggs and the run game, and Washington is a 6-point underdog that will be throwing late. Line: anytime touchdown (+175, DraftKings).

The bet

Tee Higgins OVER 74.5 receiving yards (-115, bet365) + Stefon Diggs anytime touchdown (+175, DraftKings) — about +414. A $10 ticket returns about $51.40.

Why these legs

Both legs clear on their own. Higgins is a 91.6-yards-a-game receiver against the league's second-worst pass defense at a near-even price, and Diggs is a plus-money touchdown scorer who leads his team in every receiving category and just caught the game-winner. Neither leg depends on the other — different players, different sides of the ball, same shootout script. That is the juice rule working as intended: a near-even leg plus a plus-money leg, about +414 instead of the chalky +150 you get from stacking favorites.

The honest caveats

Both legs live in the same game, so they share the same risk: if this turns into a slog instead of the shootout the 54.5 total implies, both can miss together. Higgins had a 32-yard game against Atlanta two weeks ago, and the Bengals' target share tilts heavily toward Chase on any given night. Diggs' yardage is modest (48.3 a game) — the touchdown leg is about red-zone usage, not volume — and Washington's banged-up backfield could shorten Daniels' dropbacks. A parlay needs both legs, and either one can sink it alone.

The record

NFL · Nov 23, 2026 · 12:44 AM ET

Colton McKivitz's season is over — the 49ers' starting right tackle fractured and dislocated his ankle in Mexico City

By Matt

The 49ers beat the Vikings 35-10 on Sunday night to move to 9-1, but they lost starting right tackle Colton McKivitz for the season — a fractured and dislocated left ankle, confirmed by Kyle Shanahan after the game.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

McKivitz is done for the year

The San Francisco 49ers lost starting right tackle Colton McKivitz for the rest of the season on Sunday night, after he suffered a fractured and dislocated left ankle in their 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed the diagnosis after the game, telling reporters McKivitz's ankle was broken and dislocated, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner. Shanahan added that the injury is similar to the one linebacker Fred Warner suffered last year.

How it happened

The injury came in the second quarter, on a four-yard Christian McCaffrey run. McKivitz was blocking when he got rolled up in the pile, and McCaffrey landed on the back of his left leg. When McKivitz came out of the pile, his left foot was facing the wrong direction.

The reaction on the field told the story before any diagnosis did. McCaffrey dropped to a knee beside him. Left tackle Trent Williams spiked his helmet into the turf. Teammates gathered around as the medical staff put McKivitz's leg in an air cast and carted him off, to an ovation from the crowd at Estadio Banorte.

What the 49ers lose

McKivitz is not a name that shows up in highlight reels, but he is the kind of loss that changes a season. The 30-year-old has been San Francisco's starting right tackle since 2023, and Sunday night was his 61st consecutive start. He had not given up a sack all season, and Pro Football Focus had him graded as the seventh-best tackle in the league through Week 10 — second-best in run blocking.

The 49ers know it, too. They signed him to a three-year, $45 million extension in September 2025, with $27 million guaranteed, keeping him under contract through the 2028 season. He was playing the best football of his career.

Now the job falls to swing tackle Vederian Lowe, who had played only 36 offensive snaps all season before checking in on Sunday night. Lowe will get the first crack at the job, but there is no replacing a lineman who had not missed a start in three years — not in November, not with the playoffs coming.

The win came at a cost

None of this takes away from what the 49ers did on the field. Brock Purdy completed 21 of 26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns against a Vikings defense that had been the stingiest in the league, and San Francisco's 35-10 win moved them to 9-1 — one game clear of Detroit and Chicago in the race for the NFC's top seed.

But the 49ers were already the most banged-up contender in football, with 14 players on injured reserve before Sunday night. McKivitz makes 15, and he is the one they could least afford to lose on the offensive line.

What comes next

San Francisco hosts Seattle in Week 12, and holding the No. 1 seed means winning that game with a backup right tackle on Purdy's right side. The 49ers have survived injuries all season — that is how they got to 9-1 — but this one tests the depth at the exact spot where depth is thinnest.

McKivitz will have surgery, and the recovery from a fracture-dislocation is a long one. The 49ers' Super Bowl push now runs through Vederian Lowe.

NBA · Nov 22, 2026 · 11:45 PM ET

Murray's 45 and Jokic's triple-double set the NBA record for a duo — their eighth together

By Matt

Murray scored a season-high 45 and Jokic posted his 202nd career triple-double as the Nuggets outlasted the Bulls 151-145 in overtime — the eighth time the pair has combined a 40-point night and a triple-double, the most by any duo in NBA history.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The record

Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic now own a piece of NBA history no duo has ever held.

Sunday was the eighth time in their careers that Murray has scored 40 or more points while Jokic has recorded a triple-double in the same game — passing Wilt Chamberlain and Guy Rodgers (seven) and Tom Gola and Wilt Chamberlain (seven) for the most such games by a duo in NBA history, according to the NBA.

Together they scored 82 points against Chicago, the second-most the pair has ever combined for in a game, regular season or playoffs. The record is 91, set last Christmas against Minnesota.

The night

The Nuggets needed all of it to outlast the Bulls 151-145 in overtime at the United Center. Denver improved to 10-5 and won three straight for the first time this season; Chicago fell to 4-12.

Murray scored a season-high 45 points on 13-of-22 shooting, 6-of-11 from three and 13-of-14 at the free-throw line, adding seven assists, five rebounds, three steals and two blocks. He played every minute of the fourth quarter and overtime and scored 17 points in that stretch, opening overtime with a 27-foot step-back three as Denver scored the first eight points of the extra session and never trailed again.

It was Murray's fifth 40-point game of the season and the 13th of his career — fifth in franchise history, behind Jokic (35), Alex English (33), Carmelo Anthony (19) and David Thompson (18).

Jokic had 37 points, a season-high 18 rebounds and 11 assists for the 202nd triple-double of his regular-season career, seven shy of Russell Westbrook's NBA record of 209.

The 151 points were Denver's most since it put up 157 at Portland on February 20, and they tie for the fourth-most the Nuggets have ever scored on the road. The starters scored 137 of them — Christian Braun had 21 points and eight rebounds, Aaron Gordon had 18 points and eight rebounds, and Cameron Johnson scored 16 on 6-of-9 shooting.

The other side

Chicago nearly stole it anyway. Josh Giddey had 23 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high 22 assists — the first Bulls player with more than 20 assists in a game since 1985, and the first with a 20-point, 20-assist game since December 6, 1969, when Clem Haskins had 23 points and 21 assists against Boston.

The Bulls made 25 three-pointers, tying a franchise record, led by Buddy Hield's 33 points and seven threes. Jalen Smith added a career-high 26.

Chicago wiped out a seven-point deficit in the final 40 seconds of regulation — Giddey's layup tied the score at 131 with 2.1 seconds left, and Jokic's 31-footer missed at the buzzer. Then Denver's starters took over the extra session, and the Bulls never got closer than four.

NFL · Nov 22, 2026 · 11:45 PM ET

Justin Herbert in concussion protocol after Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets — Week 12 status in doubt

By Matt

The Chargers announced after Sunday's loss to the Jets that Justin Herbert has entered the NFL's concussion protocol, leaving his availability for next week's game against the Patriots up in the air.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The news

Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has entered the NFL's concussion protocol, the team announced after Sunday's 27-24 loss to the New York Jets at SoFi Stadium.

Herbert played the entire game, but a member of the Chargers' public relations team announced postgame that he would not be available to the media because he had entered the protocol. The exact play on which the head injury occurred has not been specified.

What happened Sunday

Herbert was efficient when he had the ball — 15-of-21 passing for 131 yards and two touchdowns, a 119.3 passer rating that was his best of the season — and he added eight rushes for 32 yards, including a 10-yard touchdown run on the final play of the first half.

The protection was the problem again. Herbert was sacked six times by the Jets, bringing his season total to 39, a league high. The loss dropped the Chargers to 1-9, and it came against a Jets team that had dropped five straight.

Los Angeles had only six possessions all game and came away with points on four of them. The Jets scored on five of their six possessions, milking the clock on their final drive while the Chargers couldn't get the ball back.

What comes next

Herbert will have to progress through the NFL's mandatory five-step return-to-participation protocol, which requires clearance from both the team physician and an independent neurological consultant, before he can play again.

The Chargers host the New England Patriots next Sunday, November 29. If Herbert doesn't clear the protocol in time, backup DJ Uiagalelei would be in line to start — with Trey Lance on injured reserve and Jake Browning on the practice squad.

The Chargers will provide further updates when practice resumes later this week.
