Lions and Bears both reach 8-2 before Thanksgiving

By Matt

Detroit and Chicago both moved to 8-2 on Sunday — Gibbs scored twice in the fourth quarter to close out Tampa Bay, and Caleb Williams threw two touchdowns as the Bears held off New Orleans. They meet Thursday at Ford Field with first place on the line.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The NFC North's Thanksgiving showdown is a first-place game. Detroit and Chicago both won on Sunday to reach 8-2, and now they meet at Ford Field on Thursday with the division lead on the line.

Detroit: Gibbs closes it out in the fourth

Jahmyr Gibbs ran for two touchdowns as the Lions beat the Buccaneers 31-21 at Ford Field — Detroit's sixth straight win, and the team remains undefeated at home this season.

Both of Gibbs's scores came in the fourth quarter. A 1-yard run midway through the period put Detroit up 10, and after sacks from Trevor Nowaske and Derrick Barnes ended Tampa Bay's next possession, Gibbs added a 4-yard touchdown with 1:55 left. The second score was his 13th rushing touchdown of the season.

Gibbs finished with 98 rushing yards on 23 carries and caught four passes for 20 yards. Jared Goff threw for 279 yards and two touchdowns without an interception, including a 57-yard strike to Jameson Williams and a 14-yard score to Amon-Ra St. Brown.

Baker Mayfield, playing through a foot injury, threw for 187 yards and two touchdowns — both to Ted Hurst III — but the Bucs fell to 3-7.

Final: 31; 21

Gibbs rushing: 98 yards, 2 TD; —

Goff passing: 279 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT; —

Mayfield passing: —; 187 yards, 2 TD

Chicago: takeaways set up both touchdowns

Caleb Williams threw for two touchdowns as the Bears beat the Saints 21-13 at Soldier Field — Chicago's fifth straight win.

Williams went 15 of 23 for 181 yards with one interception. Both scoring throws came in the second quarter and both were set up by takeaways: a 3-yard shovel pass to D'Andre Swift after a fumble recovery, then a 15-yard pass to Colston Loveland — who hurdled a defender on his way in — after Dillon Thieneman's interception.

The defense did the rest. Jeffery Simmons had three of Chicago's six sacks, and New Orleans never led. The Saints closed the gap late but couldn't finish the comeback.

It was a bounce-back afternoon for Williams in one specific way: his last outing, a 27-24 win over Tampa Bay on November 8, saw him throw a career-high four interceptions. This time the two touchdowns came with just the one pick.

What Thursday means

The two wins set up the cleanest possible Thanksgiving game. The Lions and Bears are tied at the top of the NFC North, and Thursday's game at Ford Field decides who spends the holiday weekend in first place. Detroit has won six in a row; Chicago has won five.

Watch

Watch the full game highlights: Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs. Detroit Lions | 2026 NFL Season Week 11 — YouTube. Full-game highlights from Ford Field, including Gibbs's two fourth-quarter touchdowns and Goff's 57-yard strike to Williams.

NHL · Nov 22, 2026 · 8:56 PM ET

Canadiens acquire Dylan Larkin from Red Wings in blockbuster — Dach, Montembeault, Hage and four picks go to Detroit

By Matt

The Montreal Canadiens acquired captain Dylan Larkin from the Detroit Red Wings on Sunday, sending Kirby Dach, Sam Montembeault, the rights to Michael Hage and four draft picks — including first-rounders in 2027 and 2029 — the other way.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The captain is gone

The Montreal Canadiens acquired Dylan Larkin from the Detroit Red Wings on Sunday, ending a month-long standoff that had the Detroit captain sitting at home, suspended without pay, waiting for a trade.

Canadiens general manager Kent Hughes announced the deal, and the price was a haul. Detroit gets forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Sam Montembeault, the rights to forward prospect Michael Hage, a first-round pick in 2027, a second-round pick in 2027, a fourth-round pick in 2028 and a first-round pick in 2029. Montreal also gets Detroit's second-round pick in 2028 and its third-round pick in 2027.

Larkin is 30, and he has been one of the most consistent goal scorers in the league — at least 30 goals in each of the last five seasons, six times in his career. He had six points (two goals, four assists) in 10 games with Detroit this season, and he led Red Wings forwards in average ice time at 21:41 a night.

What Montreal is getting

Since making his NHL debut in 2015, Larkin has 278 goals and 649 points in 818 games with Detroit, ranking tenth in franchise history in both categories. He also helped the United States win the gold medal at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Olympics and represented his country at the 4 Nations Face-off in 2025.

The fit is obvious. Nick Suzuki already commands Montreal's top line with 20 points in 17 games, and Lane Hutson leads the club with 24 points from the blue line — but the Canadiens have been hunting a second-line center all season. Larkin is that, with a track record of 30-goal seasons and a captain's resume.

His contract runs through 2030-31 at an $8.7 million cap hit.

How it got here

Larkin told Detroit in October that he would not play another game for the team. The Red Wings announced it, suspended him without pay, and he has been sitting out since October 29 — forfeiting more than $1 million in earnings along the way, according to The Athletic.

The holdup was never the package. It was Larkin's no-movement clause. In October, the Detroit Free Press reported he would facilitate a move to one of 10 teams — Minnesota, Florida, Vegas, Dallas, Washington, Carolina, Utah, Tampa Bay, New Jersey and Colorado. Montreal was not on that list, and The Athletic reported the Canadiens were frozen out despite strong interest.

So this deal needed Larkin's sign-off, and he gave it. Detroit, sitting at 8-11-3 under head coach Todd McLellan, finally got the reset it has been circling for weeks — two first-round picks, a young goalie, a former top prospect in Dach, and Hage's rights.

For Montreal, the message is just as clear. The Canadiens paid a premium — two firsts, two more picks, a roster forward, a goalie and a prospect — because they believe Larkin is the piece that turns a good young core into something more. Now he has to prove them right, in a new sweater, in the same division as the team he just left.

Bam Adebayo just tied LeBron James — and the Heat keep winning

By Matt

Bam Adebayo posted 24 points, 15 rebounds and 12 assists with zero turnovers in Miami's 123-113 win over Oklahoma City — his ninth career triple-double, tying LeBron James for the second-most in Heat history.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

A triple-double with nothing wasted

Bam Adebayo did everything on Sunday night, and he did it without giving the ball away once.

Adebayo finished with 24 points, 15 rebounds and 12 assists in the Miami Heat's 123-113 win over the Oklahoma City Thunder at Kaseya Center — a triple-double with zero turnovers, plus two steals and three blocks in 37 minutes. He shot 8-of-11 from the field and 8-of-9 from the free-throw line.

The Heat never trailed. They led by 12 after the first quarter and by 15 at halftime, and they never let the lead slip below double digits. Oklahoma City kept pushing — Jared McCain had 20 points and Bennett Stirtz added 21 — but Miami had an answer every time, and most of the answers ran through Bam.

Tied with LeBron

The triple-double was the ninth of Adebayo's career. That ties LeBron James for the second-most triple-doubles in Heat history. Jimmy Butler leads the franchise with 13. Dwyane Wade is next at five.

It is the kind of company that says more than the box score. Adebayo is the Heat's all-time rebounding leader — he passed Udonis Haslem for that mark on October 29 — and now he sits alongside LeBron on another franchise list, four triple-doubles behind Butler.

The zero turnovers are the detail that makes this one special. Twelve assists, no giveaways, while grabbing 15 rebounds and guarding everything. That is a complete game from a center who runs the offense as much as he finishes it.

Seven in a row

The win is Miami's seventh straight. The Heat came into Sunday having won six in a row, including a 137-130 win over Milwaukee on Wednesday in which Giannis Antetokounmpo had 27 points and 14 rebounds and Adebayo added 26.

Pelle Larsson helped carry the scoring load on Sunday with 21 points on 9-of-14 shooting. The Heat are 10-6, and the streak has turned a good start into the best run in the East right now.

What it means

Miami's next game is Tuesday night at home against the Philadelphia 76ers, 5:00 PM ET. The streak will be on the line, and so will Adebayo's run of form — but the bigger story is what this version of Bam looks like. He is not just the Heat's defensive anchor and rebounding king anymore. He is the player the whole offense runs through, and on nights like this one, he does not make a mistake.

NBA admits the refs missed it — Embiid stepped out of bounds, and the Bucks should have had the ball with 3.5 seconds left

By Matt

A day after Tyler Herro's career-high 50-point night ended in a 132-129 loss, the NBA's last-two-minute report confirmed what the Bucks bench saw in real time: Joel Embiid stepped out of bounds in the final seconds, and possession should have gone to Milwaukee with 3.5 seconds left.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The league confirmed it a day later

The NBA admitted Sunday that the officials missed the call that decided Saturday's game between the Philadelphia 76ers and the Milwaukee Bucks.

In its daily last-two-minute report, the league acknowledged that Joel Embiid stepped out of bounds in the final seconds of Philadelphia's 132-129 win — and that "possession should have been awarded to Milwaukee." The report also noted there should have been 3.5 seconds left for the Bucks to try and win the game afterward.

The result stands. The admission changes nothing in the standings. But it confirms the Bucks were robbed of a chance, not just a call.

How the final seconds actually went

Milwaukee had stormed back from 10 points down with just over two minutes left. A Brayden Burries three-pointer cut the deficit to one, 130-129, with 4.8 seconds on the clock. Philadelphia called timeout.

LeBron James inbounded the ball deep toward the opposite end, to Embiid. Herro chased him down to commit the intentional foul — and as Embiid tried to evade him along the baseline in front of the Bucks bench, his foot went over the line. Out of bounds, plain as day on the replay.

Only nobody with a whistle was there to see it. Every official had been watching James inbound the ball, then positioned themselves around the Philadelphia basket. The Bucks bench saw it. The fans in that corner saw it. The referees did not.

Herro saw it too — and for a split second, he pulled up, expecting the whistle. When none came, he committed the foul with 1.5 seconds left. Embiid sank both free throws, stretching the lead to three, and Herro's desperate buzzer-beating three was ruled no good — the ball was still on his fingertips when the horn sounded.

Why Milwaukee couldn't challenge

The cruelest part: the Bucks had no way to fix it. They had already used their coach's challenge with 1:42 remaining, and an uncalled out-of-bounds violation cannot be initiated by the officials. Had they still possessed a challenge, they could have challenged Herro's foul on Embiid, which would have let officials review whether Embiid committed a boundary-line violation immediately beforehand. They were out of challenges, so the play stood.

Herro, who finished with a career-high 50 points to go with 11 rebounds and 7 assists, was diplomatic about it afterward.

"Well, Embiid, he did step out of bounds," he said. "But for ref, it is a tough play. 'Cause the ball was being taken out on the other side of the court. For him to see that you've got to have a ref on that baseline. So it was a tough call, a tough play to see as a ref. So, I get that one."

One call the league says was right

The last-two-minute report did not hand Milwaukee everything. The league also determined that 76ers guard VJ Edgecombe did not foul Herro while the Bucks guard tried to get off his game-tying shot before the buzzer — a correct non-call, in the NBA's view.

So the record is now this: the Bucks should have had the ball, down one, with 3.5 seconds left and Herro — the hottest hand on the floor — ready to take the shot. Instead they got a foul, two Embiid free throws, and a 13th straight loss that dropped them to 1-16, the worst record in the league.

Philadelphia, meanwhile, survived again. The 76ers sit atop the Eastern Conference, and they keep finding ways to win the close ones — this time with a little help from the officials, who the league now admits missed the one that mattered most.

Wyatt Kaiser suspended three games for the illegal check to the head that knocked Martin Pospisil out of the game

By Matt

The NHL's Department of Player Safety suspended Blackhawks defenseman Wyatt Kaiser three games without pay for an illegal check to the head of Calgary's Martin Pospisil on Saturday night. Pospisil left the game and did not return.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The league wasted no time

The NHL's Department of Player Safety announced Sunday that Chicago Blackhawks defenseman Wyatt Kaiser has been suspended for three games, without pay, for an illegal check to the head of Calgary Flames forward Martin Pospisil.

The hit came late in the second period of Saturday night's game in Calgary, with the Blackhawks leading 3-2. Kaiser was assessed a match penalty on the play and a game misconduct, and the league scheduled a phone hearing for Sunday — which caps any suspension at five games — before handing down the three-game ban.

Under the collective bargaining agreement, Kaiser will forfeit $26,288.67 in salary. The money goes to the Players' Emergency Assistance Fund.

What the league saw

The Department of Player Safety released its usual explainer video with the ruling, and it did not leave much room for debate. The hit satisfied both elements of the illegal check to the head rule: the head was the main point of contact, and the contact was avoidable.

"First, the head is the main point of contact," the video states. "Kaiser takes a poor angle of approach and cuts across the front of Pospisil's body, missing his core and making direct contact with his head. And, it is Pospisil's head that absorbs the vast majority of the force."

The league also noted that Pospisil did nothing to contribute to the contact — while stickhandling he pulled the puck toward his body, but his head stayed level and moved predictably. He did not change the position of his head or body just before or simultaneously with the hit.

Pospisil was carrying the puck out of the Flames' zone when Kaiser stepped in at the blue line and drove his shoulder into Pospisil's head. Pospisil went down, left the game with an upper-body injury, and did not return. He is 27 and has a history of concussion problems, which makes any head shot land harder in Calgary.

Kaiser didn't see it coming

Speaking to reporters after Saturday's game, Kaiser sounded like a player expecting a fine at most — not a multi-game ban.

"Not really, to be honest," he said when asked if he was concerned about supplemental discipline. "Because at the end of the day, if they really look at it and say, hey, that's really dangerous, (then) you're suspended for a game or two, take a fine, and then you're back."

The league disagreed, and went a game longer than even Kaiser's own guess. It is the first suspension of the 24-year-old's NHL career — he had never been fined or suspended before Sunday.

What it costs Chicago

Kaiser will miss Sunday night's game at Vancouver, Wednesday's trip to Seattle, and Friday's home game against the New York Rangers. Kevin Korchinski is expected to take his spot on the blue line.

The timing is rough for a team that is already shorthanded. Captain Connor Bedard is out after shoulder surgery this week, and center Anton Frondell left the third period in Calgary with an undisclosed injury and is still being evaluated. Chicago gutted out a 4-3 overtime win on Saturday — Sam Rinzel scored with 15 seconds left in the extra frame for the Blackhawks' first road win of the season — but the blue line keeps getting thinner.

Flames coach Ryan Huska had no official update on Pospisil after the game. "I think he's doing fine, but I don't really have anything official yet," he said. For a player with his concussion history, "doing fine" the night of the hit is the start of the story, not the end of it.

Tarik Skubal signs with the Mets for nine years, $450 million — the richest pitcher deal in baseball history

By Matt

The Mets landed the winter's top free agent on Sunday, agreeing to a nine-year, $450 million deal with two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal — the richest contract ever given to a pitcher.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The biggest free agent of the winter is off the board.

Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the New York Mets on Sunday, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan, who first reported the terms. Jon Heyman of the New York Post was first to report the signing itself. Skubal passed his physical on Wednesday, November 25, and the deal is now official. The contract includes a $45 million signing bonus, a full no-trade clause, and no opt-outs or option years.

The Mets beat out the Dodgers, Padres and Blue Jays to land the Scott Boras client, according to the Post — the same three clubs that had been in the mix all month.

The number

Four hundred fifty million dollars is the richest contract ever given to a pitcher, surpassing Yoshinobu Yamamoto's 12-year, $325 million deal with the Dodgers. The average annual value works out to $50 million a year.

That is a jump from where the bidding started. The Mets' initial offer, reported last week, was nine years and nearly $400 million. The sweepstakes pushed it $50 million higher before Skubal put pen to paper.

The pitcher

The Mets are paying for the best pitcher in baseball, and the resume backs it up. Skubal won the American League Cy Young Award in both 2024 and 2025 with the Detroit Tigers, and his 2024 season included the AL Pitching Triple Crown.

Detroit traded him to the Dodgers at the Aug. 2 deadline, and he started Game 1 of the NLCS for Los Angeles in October. He hit free agency as the clear top prize of the winter — a left-hander with two Cy Youngs, a mid-90s fastball, and no real holes in his game.

What it means

For the second time in three offseasons, Mets owner Steve Cohen went out and landed the top free agent on the market. The rotation now has its ace, and the Mets did it by outbidding the team Skubal just pitched for in the postseason.

The Dodgers, meanwhile, lose the sweepstakes for the pitcher who started their NLCS opener. The winter's biggest domino has fallen, and it fell in Queens.

Tigers grab Luis Gil for $2.3 million — two days after the Yankees let him walk

By Matt

The Tigers are betting $2.3 million that the 2024 version of Luis Gil is still in there — two days after the Yankees non-tendered the former Rookie of the Year rather than pay him the same number in arbitration.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

Luis Gil was a free agent for less than 48 hours.

The Detroit Tigers agreed to a one-year deal with the right-hander on Sunday, worth $2.3 million with up to $2 million more available in performance bonuses, pending a physical. ESPN's Jeff Passan was first to report the agreement, and it was quickly confirmed by USA Today, the Detroit Free Press and the New York Post.

The number is the whole story. The Yankees non-tendered Gil on Friday rather than pay him a projected $2.3 million in arbitration — the exact figure Detroit just gave him. New York decided the bet wasn't worth it. The Tigers decided it was.

The 2024 version

This is a bet on a very recent memory. In 2024, Gil went 15-7 with a 3.50 ERA in 29 starts, striking out 171 in 151⅔ innings, and ran away with the American League Rookie of the Year award — the first Yankees pitcher to win it since Dave Righetti in 1981.

The stuff was never the question. A four-seam fastball that averaged 96.6 mph, a slider with a plus-9 run value per Baseball Savant, and a changeup he threw a quarter of the time. The walks were the flaw even then — a major league-high 77 — but at 26, cheap and throwing 97, he looked like a long-term rotation piece.

The fall

It unraveled fast. A high-grade lat strain in spring training cost Gil the first four months of 2025; he came back in August and posted a 3.32 ERA in 11 starts, but with 33 walks in 57 innings. Then right shoulder inflammation derailed his 2026: he opened the season in Triple-A, made nine appearances for the Yankees, and finished with a 4.61 ERA and more walks (18) than strikeouts (17) in 27⅓ innings.

There was a flicker at the end — a 1.13 ERA across eight innings in five relief appearances after his late-August return — but it came with seven walks and a hit-by-pitch, and he didn't pitch in the postseason. The Yankees had seen enough to walk away from the arbitration number.

It wasn't his first long road back, either. Gil had Tommy John surgery in 2022 and pitched only twice in the minors in 2023 before the breakout. In five seasons with the Yankees, he went 21-11 with a 3.61 ERA and 272 strikeouts in 269⅓ innings across 56 games, 51 of them starts.

Why Detroit

The Tigers are rebuilding a rotation from scratch. They traded Tarik Skubal to the Dodgers at the deadline, and two days before landing Gil they locked in the apparent top of the staff, giving 25-year-old right-hander Troy Melton a six-year, $46.5 million extension.

Behind Melton, the rotation shapes up as left-hander Framber Valdez, right-handers Jackson Jobe and Keider Montero, swingman Drew Anderson — who posted a 2.61 ERA in 11 starts, nine of them after the All-Star break — and River Ryan, who arrived in the Skubal trade. Gil slots in as a low-cost upside play in that mix: if he throws strikes, he's a rotation option. If he doesn't, Detroit walks away after one year.

Gil had other suitors — the Red Sox had already expressed interest, per the Boston Globe — but the Tigers moved first, and they paid exactly what the Yankees wouldn't.

MLB · Nov 22, 2026 · 3:15 PM ET

Yankees non-tender Luis Gil — two years after he won Rookie of the Year, the 2024 AL ROY is a free agent

By Matt

The Yankees non-tendered former AL Rookie of the Year Luis Gil on Friday, making him a free agent two years after his breakout 2024 season — and the Red Sox are already interested.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The New York Yankees non-tendered Luis Gil on Friday, making the 2024 American League Rookie of the Year a free agent. The Yankees also cut loose reliever Fernando Cruz, leaving both pitchers free to sign anywhere after the club declined to offer them contracts by the tender deadline.

Gil was the headliner of a 44-player non-tender class, and his name stands out for how fast the fall came. Two years ago he was the Yankees' breakout starter. This winter, New York decided he wasn't worth the roughly $2.3 million he was projected to earn in arbitration.

The door isn't fully closed — both pitchers can still negotiate a new deal with the Yankees — but for now, Gil is on the open market, and he won't be short of suitors.

The 2024 season

Gil's rookie year was the real thing. He went 15-7 with a 3.50 ERA in 29 starts, striking out 171 in 151⅔ innings with a four-seam fastball that averaged 96.6 mph. The walks were the flaw — a major league-high 77 — but the stuff was undeniable, and he ran away with the Rookie of the Year vote.

He looked like a long-term piece of the Yankees' rotation. He was 26, cheap, and throwing 97.

The fall

It unraveled from there. A lat strain sidelined Gil for much of 2025, when he went 4-1 with a 3.32 ERA in 11 starts. Then right shoulder inflammation derailed his 2026: he spent much of the season in the minors, was optioned to Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre in April after struggling in four starts, and finished the year 1-2 with a 4.61 ERA across nine appearances, four of them starts.

There was a flicker at the end. Gil returned on August 31 and posted a 1.13 ERA across eight innings in five appearances. But he didn't pitch in the postseason, and the Yankees had seen enough to walk away from the arbitration number.

His 2026 salary was $2,162,500. The club chose the open roster spot over the raise.

Cruz, too

Cruz's exit is its own story. The 36-year-old right-hander went 4-6 with a 3.13 ERA and two saves in 61 appearances, striking out 67 in 54⅔ innings — but he hasn't pitched since August 25 because of a partially torn ulnar collateral ligament, and he has said he will try to return without surgery.

New York tendered the rest of its arbitration class — Anthony Volpe, Clarke Schmidt, Austin Wells, Ryan Weathers, José Caballero, Luis García Jr. and Heliot Ramos — and earlier Friday agreed with Jonathan Loáisiga on a two-year deal. Closer David Bednar is also back, having accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer.

What's next

Gil won't wait long. The Red Sox are already interested, according to the Boston Globe's Tim Healey, and a 28-year-old with a Rookie of the Year trophy and a 97 mph fastball will draw a crowd — even one coming off two injury-marred seasons.

The team that signs him is betting on the 2024 version. The Yankees just decided that bet wasn't theirs to make anymore.

A one-of-two Blastoise sells for $630,000

By Matt

Fanatics Collect sold the 1998 Commissioned Presentation Galaxy Holo Blastoise — one of only two in existence, graded CGC 8.5 — for $630,000, a new record for the card.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The second-most famous starter is closing the gap on Charizard. Fanatics Collect sold the 1998 Commissioned Presentation Galaxy Holo Blastoise, graded CGC 8.5, for $630,000 in its November Premier auction — a new record for any Blastoise card, after 59 bids.

The card

Only two copies of this card are known to exist, and the location of the other one is currently unknown. That scarcity is the whole story: this isn't a pack pull, it's a piece of Pokémon history that was never meant to be sold at all.

Wizards of the Coast printed it in 1998 as a presentation piece — a pitch to Nintendo to show what an English-language Pokémon TCG could look like, ahead of the Base Set launch in 1999. The tells are obvious once you know them: the font on the name and text is different from the Base Set release, the Blastoise artwork by Ken Sugimori is a different image from the final printing, the corners were kept square, and the back is blank.

The copy that sold carries a CGC 8.5 NM-Mint+ grade, with 8.5s on centering, surface, and corners and a 9.5 on edges.

The price, in context

This is the same copy that sold at Heritage Auctions in January 2021 for $360,000 — so the card is up 75% in under six years. That 2021 sale was already a record at the time; the new result nearly doubles it.

The rest of the Blastoise leaderboard shows how far ahead this card sits:

1998 Commissioned Presentation Galaxy Holo: CGC 8.5; $630,000 — Fanatics Collect, Nov 2026

1998 Prototype Test Print (Magic back): CGC 6.5; $241,083.60

1996 Japanese Base Set, No Rarity Symbol: PSA 10; $231,800 — Goldin, Dec 2025

1999 Base Set 1st Edition: PSA 10; $138,880 — Goldin, Feb 2026

The gap between the top two rows tells you everything about what collectors are actually paying for: not the character, and not the grade — the story. The presentation card is the artifact that brought Pokémon cards to the English-speaking world. The next-best Blastoise is a test print that never left the factory floor in any real sense either, but it doesn't carry the same origin-story weight.

The market around it

The sale came out of Fanatics Collect's November Premier auction, which totaled $39.3 million across 604 lots. Pokémon accounted for 89 lots and $7.05 million — 18% of the auction's dollars. The Blastoise was the sixth-highest lot in the sale, sitting just below a $780,000 Jordan/Kobe dual patch auto.

Charizard is still the king by a significant margin — SI's words, and the numbers back it up. But Blastoise is comfortably in second place among the Kanto starters, and the gap is narrowing with every record result like this one.

TCU fires Sonny Dykes after five seasons — four years after the national title run

By Matt

TCU has fired head coach Sonny Dykes, four years after he took the Horned Frogs to the national championship game. The move came a day after a home loss to No. 2 Utah left TCU needing a win just to reach a bowl.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The firing

TCU has fired head coach Sonny Dykes after five seasons, sources told On3 on Sunday, ending a tenure that swung from the program's greatest high to a midseason firing in the span of four years. The Athletic's Chris Vannini also reported the decision, and theScore confirmed it through On3's reporting.

As of Sunday afternoon, TCU had not formally announced the move or named an interim coach. The timing leaves the program in limbo with one regular-season game left — a Thanksgiving night trip to face No. 12 Texas Tech, where the Horned Frogs need a win to become bowl eligible.

The fall

The final straw came Saturday night at Amon G. Carter Stadium, where No. 2 Utah beat TCU 38-17 and dropped the Horned Frogs to 5-6 on the season and 3-5 in Big 12 play.

It was a fitting end to a season that never found its footing. TCU opened 2026 in Dublin with a loss to North Carolina, and the offense never recovered from losing starting quarterback Josh Hoover to the transfer portal after last season — Harvard transfer Jaden Craig took over under center, and the Horned Frogs never looked like the same program that had been a fixture in the Big 12 race.

The decline was steady, not sudden. After the title-game run, TCU went 5-7 in 2023, then steadied at 9-4 in each of the past two seasons, with wins in the Alamo Bowl and the New Mexico Bowl. This fall erased that progress, and the home loss to Utah — TCU's sixth defeat — made the decision for the administration.

The peak

What makes the firing sting is how high Dykes took TCU, and how recently.

Hired in 2022 to replace Gary Patterson, Dykes inherited a program that had been good but never great — and immediately produced the greatest season in school history. With quarterback Max Duggan, the Horned Frogs went undefeated in the regular season, earned a berth in the Big 12 championship game, and, despite a loss to Kansas State in the title game, made the four-team College Football Playoff.

TCU upset No. 2 seed Michigan in the Fiesta Bowl for the program's first national championship berth, before No. 1 seed Georgia cruised to a 65-7 win in the title game. It remains the high-water mark for TCU football — and the standard Dykes was ultimately judged against.

What's next

TCU will immediately begin a national search for its next head coach. Early names floated in reports include defensive coordinator Andy Avalos as an internal option, along with UTSA head coach Jeff Traylor, North Texas head coach Neal Brown and Houston offensive coordinator Slade Nagle.

The cost of the move is not publicly known — TCU is a private university, so contract terms are not a matter of public record. A figure of $13.1 million has been cited for the buyout, though it is unconfirmed, and ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Sunday it could cost around $20 million. Dykes previously earned about $7 million annually after signing a multi-year extension in April.

The coach

Dykes leaves with a 107-81 overall record in 16 seasons as a head coach, with stops at Louisiana Tech, Cal and SMU before TCU. At SMU he rebuilt a program that had been an afterthought into a winner, and at TCU he delivered a national title-game appearance in year one. He just never got back there — and in college football, that is what gets a coach fired.

NHL · Nov 22, 2026 · 1:15 PM ET

Jake Neighbours ties a Blues record with five assists — and breaks a Brett Hull mark in under six minutes

By Matt

Jake Neighbours tied the St. Louis franchise record with five assists in a 9-6 win over the Devils — and needed less than six minutes to pass Brett Hull's mark for the fastest three points to start a game in Blues history.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

A night for the record book

Jake Neighbours tied a St. Louis Blues franchise record on Saturday night, recording five assists in a 9-6 win over the New Jersey Devils at Enterprise Center.

He is the seventh Blues player to record five assists in a game, and the first since Torey Krug did it against the Montreal Canadiens on Feb. 11, 2024. Neighbours assisted on all three of St. Louis' opening goals, then added two more as the Blues piled up nine in one of the wildest games of the season.

"I started to hear some rumblings (of breaking records), but I'm not too sure of what I tied or what I beat or anything like that," Neighbours said. "Just happy we pulled out the win and I can contribute."

Six minutes to pass Brett Hull

The record that actually fell belonged to a Hall of Famer. Neighbours had three assists in the opening 5:53, making him the fastest player in Blues history to record three points in a game — passing Brett Hull, who did it in 6:57 on Oct. 26, 1996.

It was nearly an NHL record, too. Only Guy Lafleur (5:37 on March 27, 1979) and Pavol Demitra (5:43 on Nov. 13, 2005) have ever reached three points faster from the start of a game.

"It's cool to be mentioned in the same company as those names," Neighbours said. "I'm not going to read into it too much. Those guys are Hall of Famers and a higher pedigree than I am, but obviously just one of those nights where things were working for me."

The helpers

Neighbours set up Jimmy Snuggerud, Robert Thomas, Brandon Carlo, Logan Mailloux and Mason McTavish. Thomas added a goal of his own for a three-point night — his third straight game with at least three points, the first Blues player to do that since Keith Tkachuk in 2005-06 — and Jonatan Berggren scored twice.

The Devils never recovered from the opening burst. Connor Hellebuyck was pulled in the first period after allowing goals on four consecutive shots, facing just six in total, and Jake Allen allowed four more on 16 shots in relief. Jordan Binnington made 37 saves at the other end.

"The season's a long year, you've got to win games all kinds of different ways," St. Louis coach Jim Montgomery said. "Sometimes the game gets sloppy. Tonight's game was sloppy by both teams."

A heater, not a fluke

The five-assist night capped a three-game run in which Neighbours has nine points, on one goal and eight assists. He now has 18 points in 23 games this season, a pace that would smash his career high.

It is also the kind of production the Blues have been waiting on from the 24-year-old winger, who is in the final year of the bridge deal he signed in October 2024 and will be a restricted free agent next summer. Nights like this one change the conversation around what that next contract looks like.

What it means

The win was St. Louis' third straight, the first time the Blues have won three in a row this season. They also tied a franchise record with 22 goals over a three-game stretch, matching a mark set in January 1991, and became just the second team in 30 years to score eight or more goals in consecutive home games.

Edmonton is next, and the Oilers just watched the Blues hang nine on one of the league's best goaltenders. If Neighbours keeps setting the table like this, the record book is going to need another look.

TSL Bets: The Sunday night parlay (~+318) — Draisaitl anytime goal, Jokić OVER 25.5 points

By Matt

Leon Draisaitl leads the NHL with 22 goals and is plus money to score again in St. Louis, and Nikola Jokić has cleared 25.5 points in 4 of his last 5 against the league's second-worst scoring defense. Two legs, about +318.

Leg 1 — the game

Edmonton Oilers (17-5-3) at St. Louis Blues (12-9-2) — 7:00 PM ET, Enterprise Center, St. Louis, BN+ / STLNHL / SNW / SN1

Oilers -110 moneyline (consensus; -118 DraftKings), total 6 (lines via BetWatch).

Injuries — Edmonton: C Ryan Nugent-Hopkins OUT (undisclosed — expected back Tuesday, November 24). LW Zach Hyman day-to-day (migraine/illness — left Saturday's game in Carolina early). C Mattias Janmark, D Alec Regula, F Matt Savoie and G Frederik Andersen on IR.

Injuries — St. Louis: LW Connor McMichael OUT (undisclosed). D Torey Krug OUT (ankle, out for the season). D Tyler Tucker OUT (knee). LW Dillon Dubé OUT (neck). F Ross Johnston day-to-day (upper body).

Storylines: The Oilers close a six-game road trip after back-to-back losses — 7-4 at Carolina on Saturday, 3-1 at Tampa Bay on Thursday — ended a six-game win streak, but they can still finish the trip 4-2. Draisaitl leads the NHL with 22 goals, has scored in 7 of his last 10 games with 10 goals over that stretch, and nine of his 22 have come on a power play converting at 34.1%, second in the league. He skates with Connor McDavid (57 points) and Vasily Podkolzin, a line that has outscored opponents 23-6 at five-on-five. The Blues are no pushover: they have won three straight and scored 22 goals in their last three games. The wrinkle is in net — Joel Hofer is the projected Blues starter, and he has saved 9.7 goals above expected, sixth-most in the league. Both teams are on the second night of a back-to-back.

Leg 2 — the game

Denver Nuggets (9-5) at Chicago Bulls (4-11) — 7:00 PM ET, United Center, Chicago, ALT / CHSN

Nuggets -8.5, total 237.5, moneyline -366 / +298 (lines via BetWatch).

Injuries — Denver: G Julian Strawther OUT (knee) — the only Nugget on the report. Jokić and Jamal Murray (24.9 points a game) are both healthy, no designation.

Injuries — Chicago: F Caleb Wilson OUT (hand). G Norman Powell day-to-day (hamstring — the Bulls' leading scorer at 20.8 points a game). C Jalen Smith day-to-day (illness). F Patrick Williams probable (thumb). F Tobe Awaka OUT (back).

Storylines: The Bulls allow 122.8 points a game, second-worst in the NBA, with a defensive rating ranked 26th — and their top scorer and starting center are both questionable. Jokić has cleared 25.5 points in 4 of his last 5 games — 26, 24, 28, 26, 27, newest first — and 6 of his last 10, averaging 25.9 points in November. Denver has won seven of its last ten and two straight, including a 133-124 win over Houston on Friday; Chicago blew a 15-point lead in a 94-98 loss to Washington the same night and is 1-5 at home.

The bet

Leon Draisaitl anytime goal (+120, FanDuel) + Nikola Jokić OVER 25.5 points (-111, Novig best price via BetWatch) — about +318. A $10 ticket returns about $41.80.

Why these legs

Both legs clear on their own. Draisaitl is the league's leading goal scorer at plus money, on the league's second-best power play, against a Blues team that has allowed 18 goals over its last four games. Jokić is the defining matchup problem in the league against the NBA's second-worst scoring defense, with Chicago's frontcourt banged up. Neither leg depends on the other — different sport, different building, same 7:00 PM window. That is the juice rule working as intended: a plus-money leg plus a near-even leg, about +318 instead of the chalky +150 you get from stacking favorites.

The honest caveats

Edmonton is on the second night of a back-to-back after being outshot 36-15 in Carolina, and Hofer is a real goalie — 9.7 goals saved above expected is not a soft matchup. On the other leg, the blowout risk is real: Denver is an 8.5-point favorite, and Jokić could sit much of the fourth quarter in a rout, and his last-10 hit rate on this line is only 60%. A parlay needs both legs, and either one can sink it alone.

NHL · Nov 22, 2026 · 3:08 AM ET

Rossi burns his old team twice in Canucks shootout win

By Matt

Marco Rossi scored twice against his former club — ending a 20-game goal drought — including the tying goal with 1:23 left, as the Canucks stunned the league-leading Wild 4-3 in a shootout.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Marco Rossi picked the perfect night to find his scoring touch again. The Vancouver center scored twice against Minnesota, his former club, including the tying goal with 1:23 left in the third period, and Jake DeBrusk scored the shootout winner as the Canucks stunned the Wild 4-3 on Saturday night at Rogers Arena.

It was a revenge game in the truest sense. Rossi and defenseman Zeev Buium both came to Vancouver from Minnesota in the blockbuster trade that sent captain Quinn Hughes to the Wild last December, and both of them scored against their old team on Saturday. Buium opened his account for the season; Rossi ended a drought that had stretched across a fifth of the schedule.

How it played out

The first period was scoreless, and Minnesota struck first in the second. Matt Boldy put the Wild ahead at 8:58 on a feed from Kirill Kaprizov, but Rossi answered on the power play at 13:13, deflecting a hard Filip Hronek pass past Jesper Wallstedt from the left slot.

The lead lasted barely a minute. Kaprizov circled behind the net and tried to center the puck; it deflected off Canucks defenseman Luke Schenn's skate and landed right on Jared Spurgeon's stick for a 2-1 Wild lead at 14:25.

Buium tied it 30 seconds into the third, his point shot bouncing off Kaprizov's stick and beating a screened Wallstedt. The game stayed deadlocked until the final two minutes, when Nick Foligno put Minnesota ahead 3-2 at 18:02 on a wrist shot from the right circle.

Vancouver pulled goaltender Leevi Merilainen for the extra attacker, and 35 seconds later the game was tied again. Brock Boeser's wrist shot from the left circle deflected off the skate of Wild defenseman Brock Faber through the crease to Rossi, who buried his second of the night to force overtime.

Neither team scored in the extra frame — Merilainen robbed Faber with a sliding left-pad save 44 seconds in — and DeBrusk was the lone scorer in the shootout, beating Wallstedt over the blocker in the second round. Merilainen stopped all three Wild shooters after making 22 saves in regulation and overtime.

The drought is over

The two goals carried extra weight because of how long Rossi had gone without one. The double snapped a 20-game goalless stretch in which he had managed only three assists, and his last goal before Saturday had come on October 1 against Edmonton.

Rossi was the ninth overall pick by Minnesota in the 2020 draft, and he spent the first years of his career with the Wild before the Hughes deal moved him to Vancouver on December 12, 2025. He arrived as part of the return for a franchise defenseman, and nights like this are exactly what the Canucks traded for — a former Wild first-rounder deciding a game against the team that drafted him.

What it means

The result snapped Minnesota's five-game winning streak, though the Wild still left Vancouver with a point and have now collected points in 14 straight games. Kaprizov added two assists of his own, extending his point streak to 14 games and tying the Minnesota franchise record he set in 2022.

For Vancouver, the upset was a third win in four games after a brutal stretch in which the club won just once in 18. Boeser assisted on all three regulation goals and stretched his point streak to a career-high 10 games. The season series between the two clubs is now tied at one win apiece.

NBA · Nov 21, 2026 · 11:45 PM ET

Wembanyama drops 50 and 19 — a stat line nobody in NBA history had ever posted

By Matt

Victor Wembanyama went for 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals as the Spurs rolled the Pelicans 114-91 — the first 50-19-5-5-4 game in NBA history.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Victor Wembanyama did something Saturday night that no NBA player had ever done before. The 22-year-old Spurs star poured in 50 points, grabbed 19 rebounds, blocked five shots, hit five three-pointers and added four steals as San Antonio rolled the short-handed New Orleans Pelicans 114-91 at Frost Bank Center — a combination of numbers that had never appeared in a single box score in league history.

He did most of the damage before halftime. Wembanyama had 32 points and 13 rebounds in the first two quarters alone, shooting 12-of-15 from the field in 18 minutes — and single-handedly outscored New Orleans' entire starting five. The Spurs led 61-45 at the break and never looked back, stretching the lead to 29 in the fourth before Wembanyama reached the half-century mark on consecutive three-pointers, the second putting San Antonio up 108-82 with 6:29 left. He checked out shortly after.

The final line: 20-of-29 from the field, 5-of-11 from deep, 5-of-6 at the line, one assist, three turnovers, and a plus-35 in 31 minutes and 51 seconds of work.

A first half for the record books

The first half alone would have been a career night for most players. Wembanyama's 32 points before the break were the second-most in a half by any Spur since the league started using play-by-play data in the 1996-97 season, and he became just the second player to compile at least 30 points, 10 rebounds, two steals and two blocks in a single half since the NBA introduced half-by-half tracking in 1997-98.

He is also the first player this season to record 30 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and three steals in a game — and he had it wrapped up by halftime.

The Pelicans tried to get physical with him, and it backfired twice. Midway through the second quarter, Jaron Pierre Jr. shoved Wembanyama from behind after a foul by Karlo Matković, drawing technicals for Pierre and for Keldon Johnson, who stepped in. Wembanyama answered by scoring the next seven points, including a spin around Yves Missi for a one-handed slam. A few minutes later, De'Aaron Fox was whistled for a technical after a two-handed shove on Jeremiah Fears — and Wembanyama responded again, scoring the next five.

"Tonight he got it going," Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley said afterward. "A lot of that was tough to guard and obviously he made some big-time shots."

The history around the night

The full line puts Wembanyama in company of three. He is only the fourth player ever to record at least 50 points, 15 rebounds and five blocks in a game, joining Wilt Chamberlain — who did it five times — Anthony Davis and Bob McAdoo. Remarkably, it is the second time he has done it this month: on November 4 he went for a career-high 52 with 24 rebounds and eight blocks in a 112-111 win over Dallas, the first 50-20-5 game in 50 years.

He also joined David Robinson as the only players to record multiple 50-point, five-block games since blocks became an official stat in 1973-74.

It was the third 50-point game of Wembanyama's career, and his second of the season. The Nov. 4 outburst against the Mavericks remains his career high by two points.

Asked afterward how special the night was, Wembanyama couldn't resist a joke at the rest of the league's expense: "It is very special. But unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at stat-padding. So, I haven't reached it yet," he said, via the Spurs' account on X.

The Spurs keep rolling

The win moved San Antonio to 14-3, tied with the Los Angeles Lakers for the best record in the Western Conference, and the Spurs have now won 14 of their last 15. They did it without Dylan Harper, who missed his second straight game with a strained left hip, and still limited themselves to 13 turnovers after committing a season-high 21 in their first game without him.

Stephon Castle added 19 points, six assists and three rebounds while tying his career high with five three-pointers. De'Aaron Fox handed out 10 assists, and Devin Vassell and Keldon Johnson each scored 10.

The numbers behind the dominance are stark. Entering Saturday, Wembanyama was averaging 28.6 points, 11.9 rebounds and a league-leading 3.9 blocks per game. San Antonio owns a plus-26.7 net rating with him on the floor this season — and a minus-14.4 when he sits.

For New Orleans, Jeremiah Fears led the way with 29 points, Jordan Poole scored a season-high 25 off the bench, and Derik Queen posted 15 points and 15 rebounds. But the Pelicans were gutted before tip: Zion Williamson was a late scratch with a left thigh contusion, Trey Murphy III sat with a knee issue, Bennedict Mathurin remained out with plantar fasciitis, and Dejounte Murray is still away from the team after having his agent request a trade on November 13. The loss was their third straight and ninth in their last 10.

The Pelicans host Phoenix on Monday. The Spurs visit Sacramento the same night — and after a night like this one, the rest of the league is running out of ways to describe what Wembanyama is doing.

NHL · Nov 21, 2026 · 10:44 PM ET

Mark Scheifele passes Dale Hawerchuk — 380 goals, and the Jets' record book is all his now

By Matt

One week after taking the Jets' points record, Mark Scheifele buried his 380th career goal to pass Dale Hawerchuk for the franchise goals lead — and now owns the Jets' goals, assists and points records outright. Winnipeg lost the night 5-4 in a shootout to Vegas, but the record is his.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The goal

Mark Scheifele's pursuit of Dale Hawerchuk is officially over.

The Winnipeg center buried a tap-in off a Kyle Connor pass at 14:36 of the second period on Saturday night, tying the game with Vegas at three — and moving past Hawerchuk to stand alone atop the Jets' all-time goal-scoring list. It is the last of the three franchise scoring records to fall to Scheifele in the span of a week.

He now leads the franchise in goals, assists and points. Only two other active players can say the same about their club: Aleksander Barkov in Florida and Alex Ovechkin in Washington.

The Jets lost the night, 5-4 in a shootout to the Golden Knights at Canada Life Centre. The record did not care.

One week, three records

This has been building all month, and it broke open in a single week.

Last Saturday in Chicago, Scheifele passed Hawerchuk for the franchise points lead with his 930th career point, then kept going — a goal and three assists in a 5-4 shootout comeback from 4-0 down — and took the assists record from Thomas Steen in the same game. He entered Saturday night in Winnipeg needing one goal to finish the set.

The goal itself had the same fingerprints as the points record a week earlier. Connor fed him, and Josh Morrissey was in on it too — the same two linemates who set up the record point in Chicago. Connor has now assisted on 111 of Scheifele's goals. Morrissey has been in on 70.

The record only became reachable this season. In September, the NHL merged the statistical history of the two Winnipeg franchises — the original Jets (1979-96) and the current club, which arrived from Atlanta in 2011 — putting Hawerchuk's marks back on top of the book. Before the merge, Scheifele had already passed Blake Wheeler in October 2025 as the points leader of the current Jets era.

Hawerchuk's goals mark stood at 379, scored across 713 games for the original Winnipeg franchise from 1981-82 through 1989-90.

Goals: 380; Dale Hawerchuk, 379

Assists: 554; Thomas Steen, 553

Points: 934; Dale Hawerchuk, 929

The mentor connection

The man whose record fell was also Scheifele's junior coach. Hawerchuk coached him with the Barrie Colts in the OHL, and the two stayed close until Hawerchuk's death in 2020.

Scheifele was the first draft pick of the current Jets era — seventh overall in the 2011 NHL Entry Draft, the franchise's first selection after the move from Atlanta. Fifteen years later, in his 16th NHL season, the 33-year-old from Kitchener, Ontario owns the record book of a franchise that spans two eras and 44 seasons.

The game got away

Winnipeg got the start it wanted. Adam Lowry redirected an Elias Salomonsson shot past Carter Hart 29 seconds in — only the eighth time this season the Jets have scored first. Vegas answered at 8:18 when Jack Eichel won a faceoff back to Brett Howden, and Mitch Marner buried a rebound shortly after to put the Knights up 2-1.

Rookie Viggo Björck tied it at two on a feed from Morgan Barron, and after Vegas went back in front, Scheifele's record goal made it three-all.

Just over four minutes into the third, Connor pounced on a Vegas turnover and rocketed a shot over Hart's glove for his 19th of the season, and Winnipeg led 4-3. It held until 16:25, when Tomas Hertl found Ivan Barbashev alone in the slot and Barbashev beat Stuart Skinner to tie it at four.

Overtime produced no winner. In the shootout, William Karlsson scored on Vegas' second attempt, and Hart shut down Scheifele, Connor and Gabriel Vilardi to close it out. Skinner finished with 29 saves. The Jets fell to 11-9-4.

A franchise record on a losing night is still a franchise record. Scheifele has spent a week rewriting a book that stood for decades — and now every line in it has his name on it.

NHL · Nov 21, 2026 · 8:44 PM ET

Rangers lose Bjorkstrand and Smits for months as the injury pileup reaches a breaking point

By Matt

The Rangers announced Saturday that Oliver Bjorkstrand and Alberts Smits will each miss two to three months with upper-body injuries, the latest blows to a roster already without Igor Shesterkin for the season.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Two more gone for months

The New York Rangers announced Saturday that forward Oliver Bjorkstrand and defenseman Alberts Smits will each miss the next two to three months with upper-body injuries.

It is the latest gut punch in a season that has tested the Rangers' depth at every position. The team has outperformed expectations so far, but the list of unavailable players keeps growing — and Sunday brings a matinee against the defending Stanley Cup champions.

How Bjorkstrand got here

Bjorkstrand's injury did not announce itself all at once. The 31-year-old winger was hurt midway through the third period of a 3-1 win over Montreal on November 16, then played the next game on Monday and practiced on Thursday. He did not take part in Friday's session, and head coach Mike Sullivan said Saturday that Bjorkstrand complaining about the injury prompted "further investigation."

That investigation ended with injured reserve on Friday and a months-long timeline on Saturday. Taylor Raddysh was recalled to take the roster spot.

The loss stings because Bjorkstrand has been one of the Rangers' most productive forwards. He is tied for second on the team in goals, and he was a steady presence in a top six that has had to carry the load while the lineup around it keeps changing.

The rookie who earned his spot

Smits' timeline is the quieter heartbreak of the two. The 18-year-old defenseman was the No. 5 overall pick and played his way onto the roster out of training camp, but he has not skated in a game since a win over Philadelphia on November 5. Until Saturday, there was no clear timeline for his return. Now there is one — and it is measured in months, not weeks.

Losing a rookie who forced his way onto the team is one thing. Losing him for the bulk of the season, when the blue line is already stretched thin, is another.

The list that won't stop growing

Bjorkstrand and Smits join a casualty list that already reads like a roster page. Joe Veleno went down with a lower-body injury four games into the season. Igor Shesterkin suffered a season-ending knee injury in the sixth game. Goaltender Joonas Korpisalo missed 16 games with a foot infection. Adam Sykora's preseason injury carries a timeline of four to five months.

Pavel Dorofeyev landed on injured reserve Saturday as well, with a lower-body injury retroactive to November 13. He could technically return as early as Sunday, but he did not practice Saturday and continues to skate on his own, and Sullivan would not say whether the stint will be short.

There is at least one player coming back: defenseman Sean Durzi, who has missed the past eight games with an undisclosed injury, is expected to return against Carolina.

Sunday is the test

The Rangers entered a five-day break on a three-game winning streak, with wins in six of their last seven games. Sunday's matinee against the Hurricanes — the reigning Stanley Cup champions and the Metropolitan Division leaders — is, in defenseman Braden Schneider's words, a game against "the team to beat."

"We've just got to have more guys step up," J.T. Miller said after practice in Tarrytown. "It's an opportunity for everybody. It's gonna be a chance to have a bigger role for maybe some guys."

Sullivan called it a next-man-up mindset, and the front office has already acted on it, acquiring center Max Sasson from the Canucks on Friday in exchange for a fourth-round pick in 2029 to boost the center depth.

The Rangers have survived every absence so far. Sunday will show whether they can survive two more.

Quinn Hughes is headed home for evaluation — and the NHL's best team just lost its best defenseman

By Matt

The Wild sent Quinn Hughes home from their road trip for evaluation of an undisclosed injury suffered Thursday in Calgary. The Norris winner is out at least two games, his 13-game point streak is over, and there is no timeline yet.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Sent home mid-trip

Quinn Hughes is headed back to Minnesota.

The Wild ruled their star defenseman out for the rest of the road trip on Saturday, November 21, and sent him home to be evaluated for an injury he suffered Thursday night in Calgary. Head coach John Hynes confirmed the move before Saturday's game in Vancouver, saying Hughes will miss at least the next two games — Saturday against the Canucks and Monday at San Jose.

What Hynes did not say is what is actually wrong. He would not say whether it is an upper- or lower-body injury, only that it is not a concussion. There is no timeline beyond the two games he has already been ruled out for, and no word on whether he will be ready when the Wild return home Wednesday to host Utah.

The hit in Calgary

The injury came late in the third period of Thursday's 4-1 win over the Flames, when Calgary forward Adam Klapka checked Hughes into the boards. Hughes finished his shift, went out for one more power play, and then left the game for good.

It was an ordinary-looking hit. That is what makes the next part concerning: a routine shove into the glass ended the night of the best defenseman in hockey, and a day and a half later the team decided he needed to go home to be looked at properly.

Before he left that game, Hughes had a goal and an assist — extending his point streak to 13 games, with six goals and 15 assists in that stretch. The streak ends now, in a building where he used to be captain.

What Minnesota loses

Hughes is not just the Wild's best defenseman. He is their engine.

He has 34 points in 24 games this season — second on the team in scoring — and leads the entire NHL in average ice time at 27:49 a night. He is the 2023-24 Norris Trophy winner and a U.S. Olympic gold medalist, and he is doing it in the final year of his contract, with no extension signed and unrestricted free agency waiting on July 1.

The timing could hardly be worse for the standings. Minnesota is 17-3-4, the best record in the NHL, riding a five-game winning streak and points in 13 straight. They have been doing it with Hughes playing nearly half of every game.

The Wild do have some cover. Brock Faber and Jared Spurgeon recently returned from injuries of their own, and David Spacek steps into the lineup alongside Zach Bogosian in Vancouver. Minnesota also recalled defenseman Viking Gustafsson Nyberg from AHL Iowa for depth, with Olli Maatta still on injured reserve.

None of that replaces 28 minutes a night from a Norris winner. The question now is what the evaluation in Minnesota finds — and whether two games is the whole story, or just the start of it.

Connor Bedard is having shoulder surgery — and the Blackhawks just lost their captain again

By Matt

Five months after surgery on his left shoulder, Connor Bedard needs the same operation on his right one. The Blackhawks' captain — and their leading scorer — is out for a significant spell, with no timeline until after the procedure.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The decision is made

Connor Bedard is having surgery on his right shoulder.

Chicago Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson announced the decision on Saturday, November 21, after the Blackhawks' 4-3 overtime win over the Calgary Flames. Bedard will go under the knife this coming week, and the team will not put a timeline on his return until after the procedure is done.

What Davidson did say: Bedard is projected to miss a significant spell. The operation is likely the same one he had on his left shoulder this past summer, which took him a little more than three months to come back from — and the team is confident he will be able to keep playing center and taking faceoffs long term.

It is the second shoulder surgery for the 21-year-old captain in just over five months.

How it happened

The injury came on Tuesday, November 17, in Chicago's 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs. Bedard hurt his right shoulder early in the third period while taking a faceoff and did not return to the game.

For a few days, the Blackhawks held out hope that rehab might be enough. On Thursday, coach Jeff Blashill ruled Bedard out of that night's game against the Columbus Blue Jackets and the three-game road trip that followed, saying the medical staff was still weighing rehab against surgery and consulting outside experts — including the specialist who operated on his left shoulder last summer.

Saturday, after the win in Calgary, the weighing was over.

The shoulder history keeps growing

This is not Bedard's first scare with his shoulders, and it is not even his first with the right one. He missed time last season after injuring the same right shoulder off a faceoff, though that one did not require surgery.

The left shoulder is the one that already went under the knife. Bedard had surgery to repair it on July 8, after injuring it in offseason training, with an initial recovery timeline of roughly four months. He beat it — returning for the season opener on October 13, 97 days after the operation, about a month ahead of schedule.

Now the right shoulder needs the same attention. Dr. Peter Millett, the surgeon who operated on the left shoulder in July, will perform this procedure as well.

What Chicago loses

Bedard leads the Blackhawks with 18 points in 15 games this season. He is the 2023 No. 1 overall pick, the face of the rebuild, and the player Chicago signed to a five-year, $75 million contract extension in July before naming him captain in September.

The Blackhawks are still finding their way — Saturday's overtime win in Calgary was their first road win of the season — and they were doing it with their best player driving the top line. Now they will do it without him for months, with no firm return date until the surgery is complete.

There is no replacing a point-a-game captain. The only question now is how long the wait is, and what the standings look like when he gets back.

MLB · Nov 21, 2026 · 5:17 PM ET

The Mets just locked up A.J. Ewing for eight years and $95 million — the biggest pre-arbitration deal in franchise history

By Matt

The Mets agreed to an eight-year, $95 million extension with 22-year-old center fielder A.J. Ewing on Saturday — the largest pre-arbitration commitment in franchise history, and a bet that their rookie-year outfielder is a cornerstone.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The deal

The New York Mets and center fielder A.J. Ewing have agreed to an eight-year, $95 million contract extension, with a club option for a ninth season that would keep him in Queens through 2035.

The agreement was first reported Saturday by SNY's Chelsea Janes and confirmed by The Associated Press, which cited a person familiar with the negotiations. The Athletic's Will Sammon reports the option year is worth $25 million, and the New York Post reports the deal includes a $2 million signing bonus plus escalators that could push the total value higher.

The biggest pre-arb bet the Mets have ever made

The $95 million guarantee is the largest pre-arbitration commitment in Mets history, surpassing the six-year, $55 million deal third baseman David Wright signed in 2007, per Spotrac. It is also the eighth-largest guarantee ever given to a player with less than a year of big league service time, according to MLB Trade Rumors.

That is the scale of the bet. Ewing made his major league debut in mid-May and stayed with the big club for the rest of the 2026 season, finishing with a .252/.324/.376 slash line, 11 home runs, 43 RBI and 25 steals in 33 attempts across 492 plate appearances. He is 22 years old.

Under baseball's labor rules, Ewing could have been eligible for arbitration after the 2028 season and free agency following the 2032 season. Instead, the extension buys out all of his arbitration years plus three free-agent seasons — and if the Mets pick up the option, they control him through 2035.

What it says about the Mets' plan

Ewing slots into a young outfield the Mets are clearly building around: Carson Benge in right field and star slugger Juan Soto in left. And the Ewing deal may be the first of several. SNY's Janes reports the Mets are open to more pre-arbitration extensions with young players like Benge — who finished second in National League Rookie of the Year voting after a 20-homer, 22-steal campaign — and pitcher Nolan McLean, who owns a 2.93 ERA across 39 career starts.

It also lands in the middle of the Mets' biggest offseason pursuit. The club is chasing free-agent ace Tarik Skubal, and locking up Ewing now sends a clear message about how the Mets intend to spend: keep the young core, then add the star on top of it.

For a franchise that has spent the last few years buying stars at the top of the market, this is a different kind of move — a $95 million vote of confidence in a 22-year-old who has played one season. The Mets are betting the best version of A.J. Ewing is still years away, and that by the time it arrives, he will already be theirs.

Tyler Herro dropped a career-high 50 — then his buzzer-beater was waved off by a fingertip

By Matt

Tyler Herro scored a career-high 50 points for the Bucks in Philadelphia, including 15 in the first quarter. He appeared to tie the game at the buzzer — but replays showed the ball was still on his fingertips when the horn sounded, and the 76ers escaped 132-129.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Tyler Herro had the game of his life on Saturday afternoon in Philadelphia — and it still wasn't enough.

Herro finished with a career-high 50 points on 15-of-23 shooting, including 7-of-12 from three and a perfect 13-of-13 from the line, plus 11 rebounds and seven assists in 40 minutes. His previous career high was 41. The Bucks noted afterward that he is the first player in NBA history to record at least 50 points, 11 rebounds, seven three-pointers and 65 percent shooting in a single game.

He set the tone immediately, scoring 15 points in the first quarter to help Milwaukee take a 30-29 lead after 12 minutes. He poured in 35 more after halftime, and by the closing minute he was carrying the Bucks' entire comeback on his back.

The ending

The final 20 seconds were as cruel as a basketball ending gets.

Herro converted a running layup with 19.2 seconds left — the basket that got him to 50 — and cut the Sixers' lead to 128-126. Rookie Brayden Burries, who had a career-high 26 points off the bench, then drilled a three with 4.8 seconds to go to make it a one-point game. Joel Embiid answered with two free throws on the other end, and with 1.5 seconds left the Bucks inbounded the ball to Herro.

His fallaway three went in at the buzzer. The building erupted. Then the officials went to the replay.

Replays showed the ball was still on Herro's fingertips as the horn sounded. The basket was overturned, the game was over, and Philadelphia walked away with a 132-129 win. Herro finished with 50 — not 53, and no overtime.

What it means for the Bucks

The loss was Milwaukee's 13th in a row, dropping the Bucks to 1-16. Herro is the first Bucks player to score 50 points since Giannis Antetokounmpo did it on November 13, 2024, against the Pistons — and Giannis now plays for Miami, which is how Herro ended up in Milwaukee in the first place.

There is no silver lining in a 13-game losing streak. But a career night like this one, in a game the Bucks had no business being in, is the kind of performance that reminds everyone what Herro is: one of the purest scorers in the league, and the one player on this roster who can win a game by himself on any given night.

The other side

Philadelphia survived because its stars did just enough. Embiid had 26 points, 17 rebounds and nine assists — one assist short of a triple-double — and LeBron James added 21 points, six rebounds and six assists. Tyrese Maxey chipped in 17, and all five Sixers starters scored in double figures. The win moved Philadelphia to 14-3.

Embiid made four late free throws in all, and everyone on the Sixers' sideline was relieved to see that Herro hadn't quite released his jumper in time.

NHL · Nov 21, 2026 · 4:44 PM ET

MacKinnon's injury is much worse than first thought — out 12 weeks, and the Winter Classic is gone

By Matt

The Avalanche thought they were losing their best player for a month. After a specialist visit, the timeline tripled — and Nathan MacKinnon will now miss the Winter Classic and the rest of 2026.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The new timeline

Nathan MacKinnon is out approximately 12 weeks.

Avalanche head coach Jared Bednar gave the update on Saturday, November 21, after practice, and it was nothing like the news Colorado was hoping for. MacKinnon saw a specialist after the team returned home, and the re-evaluation changed everything. What was first called at least a month is now three times that long, keeping the Avalanche's leading scorer out through December and January, with a return sometime in February.

Bednar said he expects MacKinnon to make a full recovery and does not anticipate the injury becoming a recurring issue. That is the one piece of good news in an update that otherwise lands like a gut punch.

How it happened

The injury came on November 12 against the Ottawa Senators. MacKinnon took a cross-check from Senators defenseman Artem Zub in the second period, went down grabbing his side, and left the game. He did not return.

At the time, the hope was a month. MacKinnon had played 20 games and still leads Colorado in scoring with 30 points — 10 goals and 20 assists — despite missing the last three. He is 31, a former Hart Trophy winner, and the engine of everything the Avalanche do offensively. Losing him for a month was already a problem. Losing him for the rest of the calendar year is a different season entirely.

The Winter Classic is off the table

The most visible casualty of the new timeline is the Winter Classic. Colorado plays the Utah Mammoth outdoors on December 31 at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City, the kind of showcase game built around stars — and the Avalanche will play it without theirs.

It is not just one game, either. Colorado does not play again until November 25, when Montreal comes to town, and the schedule from here is a long stretch of hockey without the player who drives the top line, the top power play, and most nights the outcome.

What it means for Colorado

The Avalanche have held up so far. They are 13-7-3 and third in the Central Division, and they have gone 2-1 since MacKinnon and Cale Makar went down in the same game against Ottawa. Makar, the top defenseman, was also hurt that night and is expected to be out about two weeks, until around Thanksgiving — a much shorter absence, and one the team can plan around.

MacKinnon is the harder one to plan around. There is no replacement for a point-a-game center who leads the team in scoring and plays in every situation. The Avalanche have depth, and the last three games showed they can win without him. But three games is not three months. The test now is whether a team built around its two stars can stay in the race while one of them watches from the press box until February.

He will be back. Bednar made that clear. The question is what the standings look like when he gets there.

Sports · Nov 21, 2026 · 9:45 AM ET

Mets offer Tarik Skubal nine years, nearly $400 million — the biggest pitcher offer in baseball history

By Matt

The Mets have offered free-agent ace Tarik Skubal a nine-year deal worth nearly $400 million, a reported offer that would make him the highest-paid pitcher in baseball history — if he takes it.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The offer

The New York Mets have offered two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth nearly $400 million. The report comes from former Mets general manager Jim Duquette, now an MLB Network Radio analyst, who said Friday that multiple MLB sources confirmed the terms. Reuters, USA Today, and the New York Post have all carried the report.

No deal is done. This is an offer — the first reported one of Skubal's free agency — and the Mets are not the only team at the table.

What the money means

If Skubal takes it, the deal would make him the highest-paid free-agent pitcher in baseball history. The total would pass the 12-year, $325 million contract Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers in December 2023. The average annual value, about $44.4 million, would top the $43.3 million the Mets themselves paid Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander, the current record for a free-agent starting pitcher.

Those numbers tell you how the Mets see him: not as a good arm to add, but as the ace their rotation has been missing.

Why the Mets are all in

New York entered the offseason without a veteran ace. Rookie Nolan McLean is the club's top returning starter, and the rest of the projected 2027 rotation is a mix of upside and question marks. The Mets met with Skubal in California on Monday, and owner Steve Cohen is expected to be "all in" on landing him, according to the Post's Jon Heyman.

Skubal turned 30 on Friday. He split 2026 between Detroit and Los Angeles after a midseason move, going 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA in 26 starts, and he won the Cy Young in back-to-back seasons, 2024 and 2025. Across 163 career games he owns a 3.02 ERA.

Who else is in it

The Dodgers, the incumbent after acquiring him in August, have met with Skubal, as have the Blue Jays and the Padres. MLB Network reported a fifth team met with him over Zoom. The Dodgers and Blue Jays remain in the hunt, and Skubal spoke after the Dodgers' postseason exit about his love for the city — so the Mets' offer is an opening move, not a finish.

What happens next

Skubal is expected to sign before a lockout that could begin in early December, which puts a clock on all of this. The Mets have set the market with a record number. Now the question is whether anyone tops it — or whether Skubal takes the biggest offer a pitcher has ever been handed.
