Red Sox non-tender Connor Wong, closing the book on the Mookie Betts trade

By Matt

The Red Sox non-tendered catcher Connor Wong on Friday, making him a free agent — and ending Boston's last link to the Mookie Betts trade.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The Boston Red Sox non-tendered catcher Connor Wong on Friday, making him a free agent. The decision was telegraphed earlier in the week: Boston designated Wong for assignment on Wednesday to clear a roster spot after acquiring catcher Nick Fortes from the Tampa Bay Rays, and no team claimed him or traded for him in the meantime.

Wong is now free to sign with any club. He figures to land a backup job somewhere — teams are always in the market for catching depth.

How it got here

The writing was on the wall well before this week. Wong hit .190 with no home runs in 2025, and while he improved to .233 in 2026, he never recaptured his 2024 form. His role shrank further after Boston acquired Adley Rutschman from the Orioles before the 2026 trade deadline, and the Fortes trade — Fortes for 17-year-old right-hander Angel Roa — gave the Sox a new backup catcher with better defensive metrics and a lower strikeout rate.

The money played a part too. MLB Trade Rumors projected Wong for a roughly $2 million salary in arbitration for 2027, and Boston had a cheaper, optionable alternative already on the roster in Mickey Gasper. Rather than tender Wong and stash him in Triple-A, the Sox moved on.

Wong in Boston

Wong appeared in 425 games for the Red Sox across six seasons, hitting .243/.304/.372 with 27 home runs, 128 RBI and 158 runs scored in 1,386 plate appearances. His 2026 line was .233/.308/.348 with four home runs, 25 RBI and three steals in 238 plate appearances over 77 games.

He stuck around longer than anyone else from the deal that brought him to Boston — and that is the real story here.

The last piece of the Betts trade

Wong was the last remaining player Boston acquired in the February 2020 Mookie Betts trade. The full deal sent Betts and pitcher David Price to the Los Angeles Dodgers for outfielder Alex Verdugo, shortstop Jeter Downs and Wong.

The other two pieces are already gone. Verdugo, the headliner of the return, spent four seasons in Boston (2020–23), hitting .281 with 43 home runs across 493 games — solid, but never the star the Sox gave up. He has since played for the Yankees and Braves and signed a minor-league deal with the Padres before being released after season-ending shoulder surgery. Downs played all of 14 games for Boston and hasn't appeared in the majors since 2023.

Meanwhile, Betts signed a 12-year, $365 million extension with the Dodgers and has helped them to three World Series titles since the trade. The Red Sox have reached the playoffs three times in the six years since and haven't won a playoff series since the 2021 ALCS.

Wong's departure doesn't change any of that — but it does close the book. There is now nothing left on Boston's roster from the most debated trade in modern franchise history.

What's next

Wong is a 30-year-old catcher with six seasons of big-league experience, a University of Houston product who could draw interest from Houston among others. He won't be a starter anywhere, but as a backup with pop — 27 career home runs — he should find work quickly.

Dodgers acquire Royce Lewis from the Twins for Bobby Miller and catching prospect Francisco Espinoza

By Matt

The Dodgers acquired infielder Royce Lewis from the Twins on Friday, sending right-hander Bobby Miller and 19-year-old catching prospect Francisco Espinoza to Minnesota.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The deal

The Los Angeles Dodgers acquired infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins on Friday, the clubs announced. In return, Minnesota gets right-handed pitcher Bobby Miller and minor league catcher Francisco Espinoza.

Jon Heyman of the New York Post first reported that Lewis was headed to Los Angeles, and the Dodgers confirmed the trade on X shortly after. It is the first major move of the offseason for both clubs, and it swaps one former top prospect whose career has stalled for another.

Why the Dodgers did it

Lewis is a buy-low bet on talent that has never been in question. The 27-year-old was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2017 draft, and when healthy he has shown the power and flair that made him that pick. The problem has been the healthy part — he has struggled to stay on the field throughout his career.

What Los Angeles is buying is versatility as much as upside. Lewis played three positions in 2026, logging time at first base, second base, and third base, which gives the Dodgers a right-handed bat they can move around the infield as needed. He is under club control through 2028, so this is not a rental — it is a two-year window to see if a change of scenery and a winning clubhouse unlock the player Minnesota drafted first overall.

What the numbers say

Lewis finished 2026 hitting .227 with 15 home runs, 57 RBI, 51 runs scored, and 16 stolen bases across 125 games. The average was a career low, and the Twins had explored moving him ahead of Friday's deadline to tender him a contract — he was arbitration-eligible for the first time, with MLB Trade Rumors projecting a $5.1 million salary for 2027. The Dodgers will pay a 110 percent luxury tax on him, so he will cost them more than $10 million in actuality.

Miller, also 27, heads the other way after barely pitching in the majors this year. He made three relief appearances for Los Angeles in 2026, going 1-0 with a 3.68 ERA over 7.1 innings with eight strikeouts. That is a long way from his promising rookie season in 2023, when he went 11-4 with a 3.76 ERA, and injuries and inconsistency have kept him from building on it since. Espinoza, a 19-year-old catcher who reached A-ball this past season, is the lottery ticket in the deal.

Why the Twins did it

For Minnesota, this is about the money and the roster crunch as much as the return. Lewis was a non-tender candidate, and moving him now frees up that projected arbitration salary from a payroll the Twins are trying to trim. In exchange they get a 27-year-old arm in Miller who was once one of the best pitching prospects in baseball, plus a teenage catcher to develop. It is not a haul — Twins fans made that clear within minutes of the announcement — but it beats non-tendering Lewis for nothing.

What it means

Both teams are betting on a fresh start fixing what the old one could not. The Dodgers have made a habit of turning other teams' distressed assets into contributors, and Lewis, healthy and in a lineup where he does not have to carry the offense, is exactly the kind of player that model is built for. The Twins, meanwhile, are betting that Miller still has a major league arm in there somewhere. One of these teams is going to look smart by July. The other is going to hear about it.

Manon Fiorot suspended three months by UFC after positive test for ostarine

By Matt

Manon Fiorot has accepted a three-month suspension after testing positive for low levels of ostarine at UFC Noche, with anti-doping officials tracing the result to contaminated supplements.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The suspension

Manon Fiorot has accepted a three-month period of ineligibility for a violation of the UFC Anti-Doping Policy, Combat Sports Anti-Doping (CSAD) announced Thursday, November 19.

Fiorot tested positive for low levels of ostarine, a prohibited substance in the class of Anabolic Agents, in an in-competition sample collected on September 12, 2026, at UFC Noche, where she fought Alexa Grasso at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona. Fiorot lost that bout by unanimous decision.

Why only three months

The short ban comes down to how the ostarine got there. CSAD traced the positive result to a set of supplements supplied by Fiorot's nutritionist during fight week — new to her routine, and contaminated. Investigators found no evidence of intentional use and no significant performance advantage.

Fiorot also gave CSAD her full cooperation, and a second sample she provided on October 19, before she was even notified of the adverse finding, came back negative — consistent with her account that she only used the supplements during fight week. The supplements were neither tested nor certified, so she still bears responsibility, but CSAD used its discretion to reduce the penalty.

What's next

Fiorot's period of ineligibility began on October 19, 2026, the date she was notified of her provisional suspension, and it expires on January 19, 2027, when she will be eligible to compete again. The Arizona State Boxing and Mixed Martial Arts Commission, which also holds jurisdiction over the UFC Noche bout, will recognize the suspension and impose no separate sanction.

The 36-year-old French fighter, ranked No. 4 in the women's flyweight division, does not currently have a fight booked. She is 13-3, and her lone UFC title shot to date came at UFC 315 in May 2025, when she dropped a unanimous decision to then-champion Valentina Shevchenko. A three-month layoff is about as light a landing as a failed test gets — and with the calendar on her side, she should be back in the mix early in 2027.

By Matt

Karl-Anthony Towns has cleared 37.5 points, rebounds and assists in 7 of his last 10, and Jiří Procházka is a live +160 underdog with championship experience against an unbeaten contender in his first main event. Two legs, about +377.

Leg 1 — the game

Knicks -5.5, total 217.5 (lines via FanDuel).

G Ja Morant OUT (left hamstring strain, Grade 2 — out until around December 1). G/F Shaedon Sharpe OUT (right meniscus surgery — about six months). F Vit Krejci OUT (left ankle fracture). G Chris Youngblood OUT (right heel/foot bone bruise). C Robert Williams III day-to-day (rest) — expected to be available.

Injuries — New York: F OG Anunoby questionable (left calf tightness). G Jordan Clarkson OUT (right plantar fasciitis). Other reports list the Knicks as fully healthy, so the Anunoby designation is the one to watch.

Storylines: The Knicks are the defending champions, 9-6, and winners of three straight — twice over Toronto and a 102-99 win at Minnesota on Thursday after leading by 19 in the third quarter. Jalen Brunson leads them at 26.6 points a game, sixth in the league, and Karl-Anthony Towns is the second option. Portland is 10-5 under first-year coach Micah Nori with Damian Lillard back in the fold (20.9 points a game), on the fifth stop of a six-game road trip, chasing its first win in this series since November 2022. The frontcourt matchup is the edge: Portland's only true big is Donovan Clingan, with Williams day-to-day and Avdija questionable, and Towns has cleared 37.5 points, rebounds and assists in 7 of his last 10 while averaging 39.3. He landed on 38 on Thursday at Minnesota (22 points, 12 rebounds, 4 assists).

Leg 2 — the fight

Jiří Procházka (32-6-1) vs. Navajo Stirling (11-0) — UFC light heavyweight, 5 rounds, ~3:00 PM ET, ABHA Arena, Doha, main card 1:00 PM ET on Paramount+

Procházka +160, Stirling -192 — DraftKings via Wise Guy Team, prices checked November 21, 6:55 AM ET.

Weigh-ins: Both men hit 205 pounds on Friday, and the main event is official. The only miss on the 12-fight card was Tahir Abdullayev at 172 pounds, one over for his prelim against Jake Matthews — he forfeits 20 percent of his purse and the fight goes ahead at catchweight.

Camp/availability: Procházka returns for the first time since Carlos Ulberg knocked him out in the first round at UFC 327 in April, in a fight for the division's vacant title. Before that setback he knocked out Khalil Rountree Jr. in the third round and Jamahal Hill. Stirling trains at City Kickboxing alongside Ulberg — the man who just beat Procházka — and Procházka has said openly he didn't want this matchup at first, because Stirling is the lower-ranked fighter from the same camp. Stirling is 29 and has finished three straight opponents by knockout in 2026: Bruno Lopes, Ion Cuțelaba, and former champion Jan Błachowicz in the first round at UFC Belgrade in August. Saturday is his first UFC main event.

Storylines: This is a former champion as a +160 underdog. Procházka owns the championship experience — five-round fights, title-fight pressure, the walk to the cage as the hunted — and Stirling is in his first main event against his first former champion. The MMA Junkie staff picks back the dog, 7-4 for Procházka. The market disagrees: Stirling is a 62% favorite on the exchanges, and he has finished three straight by knockout this year, including a former champion in round one. The case for the dog is experience and proven five-round pedigree; the case for the favorite is that he just starched Błachowicz in a round.

The bet

Karl-Anthony Towns OVER 37.5 points + rebounds + assists (-120, FanDuel) + Jiří Procházka moneyline (+160, DraftKings) — about +377. A $10 ticket returns about $47.70.

Why these legs

Both legs clear on their own. Towns has cleared 37.5 PRA in 7 of his last 10 while averaging 39.3, and he just cleared it on Thursday with 38 — against a Portland frontcourt that is down to Clingan with Williams day-to-day and its leading scorer questionable. The line is 37.5 at -120, and the consensus line across books is 37.5. Procházka is the upside leg: a plus-money dog with a real path, not a lottery ticket — former champion, championship rounds on his record, staff picks 7-4 his way, and an opponent in his first main event. Neither leg depends on the other — different sport, different building, different afternoon. That is the juice rule working as intended: two real edges, one ticket, about +377 instead of the chalky +150 you get from stacking favorites.

The honest caveats

Towns landed on 38 on Thursday, clearing by half a point, and one model puts the over at 37.5 at about 50% — the trend is the case here, not a model consensus. Portland's defense is seventh in the league, and if Avdija does play, the Blazers' offense stays dangerous enough to keep the Knicks honest late. On the fight side, Procházka was knocked out in the first round in April, and Stirling has finished three straight by knockout, including a former champion in round one — the favorite is favored for a reason, and a second straight early knockout loss is a live outcome. A parlay needs both legs, and either one can sink it alone.

NBA · Nov 21, 2026 · 3:09 AM ET

Harden passes Kobe with 51-point night

By Matt

James Harden dropped 51 on the Pacers to pass Kobe Bryant for third-most 50-point games in NBA history — at 37, in a season where he'd barely cracked 30 all year.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

James Harden turned back the clock on Friday night. The 37-year-old guard scored 51 points to lead the Cleveland Cavaliers past the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in an Emirates NBA Cup game at Rocket Arena — and in doing so, he recorded his 26th career 50-point game, moving past Kobe Bryant into third place on the all-time list.

Harden shot 15-of-26 from the field, 7-of-11 from three, and a perfect 14-of-14 from the free-throw line, adding six rebounds and six assists in a season-high 40 minutes. It was his first 40-point game since November 22, 2025 — when he dropped 55 for the Clippers against Charlotte, two days shy of a full year earlier — and his best scoring night since joining Cleveland near last season's trade deadline, topping the 36 he put up against Chicago.

How the night unfolded

Harden signaled what was coming early, scoring 15 points in the first nine minutes as the teams fought to a 29-29 draw. He had 24 by halftime, but Cleveland still trailed early in the third before flipping the game for good: up 74-73 four minutes into the period, the Cavs ripped off a 21-4 run, with Harden scoring 13 of those points on a perfect 4-of-4 from the field.

The third quarter belonged to him outright — 18 points on 6-of-8 shooting — and his driving layup at the end of the period pushed the total to 42 and the lead to 105-83. Cleveland outscored Indiana 43-22 in the quarter.

The Cavaliers led by 24 early in the fourth quarter, but Indiana gradually cut into the margin. Harden's flagrant foul gave the Pacers two free throws and possession — Jarace Walker made both, then assisted an Obi Toppin dunk that brought Indiana within six with 2:03 left. Donovan Mitchell answered with a driving floater, and Harden closed it himself: a three with 57.9 seconds left made it 124-113, and two more free throws with 42.3 seconds left carried him past 50 and sealed the win. He scored seven of Cleveland's final nine points.

1st: 15; 29-29

2nd: 9; 62-61

3rd: 18; 105-83

4th: 9; 128-119

Mitchell added 20 points, 3 rebounds and 3 assists. The win moved Cleveland to 2-1 in East Group B of the NBA Cup and 9-8 overall, with three wins in its last four.

Where the milestone sits in history

Only two players in NBA history have more 50-point games than Harden now does. Wilt Chamberlain leads the way with 118, and Michael Jordan sits second with 31. Bryant finished his career with 25, and Elgin Baylor rounds out the top five with 17.

The number is even more striking in context: Harden is one of only six players age 37 or older to ever score 50 in a game, joining Bryant, Jordan, LeBron James, Jamal Crawford and Steph Curry. At 37 years and 86 days, he is one of the oldest players ever to do it.

The night also moved him up another all-time list. It was his 346th career 30-point game, passing Allen Iverson and tying Dominique Wilkins for the 10th-most in NBA history. Only four guards have more: Jordan, Bryant, Oscar Robertson and Jerry West. And he has now scored 50 or more against 18 different teams, passing Jordan and Bryant, who each did it against 17.

In Cavaliers history, it was the 15th 50-point game by any player — Harden is just the sixth Cavalier ever to do it, and the first since Donovan Mitchell's 71-point night against Chicago on January 2, 2023.

Why this one hit different

This wasn't a star padding a hot streak. Harden entered Friday averaging 16.2 points per game on 38.5% shooting — a career low — and had cracked 25 points just once all season, a 32-point night at Madison Square Garden on November 11. His previous season high was that 32. He blew past it by the third quarter.

The milestone clearly meant something to him afterward. Asked about passing Bryant, Harden called him "my idol" — "the person I watched growing up. The way he cared about the game and the effort he put in is something special. So, we miss him. We miss him a lot."

Harden signed a three-year, $96 million deal to stay in Cleveland this past summer, so the chase isn't over — Jordan's mark of 31 is now five away, and a healthy season of nights like this one puts it within reach. For now, though, the story is simpler: a 37-year-old in his 18th season, in a year where the scoring had mostly dried up, went out and reminded everyone what the Beard used to do every other week.

Sports · Nov 20, 2026 · 9:30 AM ET

Berkly Catton's first career hat trick powers the Kraken past the Canucks 5-1

By Matt

Berkly Catton scored in every period — a power-play one-timer, a steal-and-score, and an empty-netter — for his first career NHL hat trick as the Kraken beat the Canucks 5-1.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Berkly Catton scored his first career NHL hat trick — a goal in every period — as the Seattle Kraken beat the Vancouver Canucks 5-1 at Climate Pledge Arena on Thursday night, snapping a three-game losing streak in their first game back from the Global Series trip to Helsinki.

Catton opened the scoring on the power play at 7:37 of the first, one-timing a Brandon Montour feed from the right dot over Leevi Merilainen's glove. He made it 3-1 at 8:54 of the second, stealing the puck from Linus Karlsson in the neutral zone and scoring unassisted, 54 seconds after Matty Beniers had restored the lead. And he completed it with 43 seconds left, taking a pass from Freddy Gaudreau — who passed up the easy empty-netter himself to set up the milestone — and snapping it home for the 5-1 final.

Catton finished with three goals on four shots in 15:17 of ice time. At 20 years and 310 days old, he is the youngest player in Kraken history to record a hat trick, eclipsing Jared McCann, who was 26 years and 228 days when he did it on January 14, 2023. Catton is the fifth Kraken player ever with a hat trick, joining Jordan Eberle, McCann, Montour and Jaden Schwartz.

The season he's having

The hat trick pushed Catton to eight goals on the season — already past the seven he scored in 66 games as a rookie last year — with 17 points in 19 games. He's on pace for 35 goals.

That pace is the story now. A year ago he was a rookie finding his way; this season he's the Kraken's breakout, scoring in every kind of situation — power play, off a steal, into an empty net — and doing it on a night when Seattle needed a response after a difficult trip to Finland.

The game around him

Seattle overwhelmed Vancouver from the opening faceoff, finishing with 43 shots on goal — tied for the fifth-highest single-game total in franchise history — including 24 in the first period alone, a franchise record for one period. Beniers had a goal and an assist, with his second-period goal standing as the game-winner, and Jordan Eberle scored on the power play in the third, four points away from 800 for his career. Montour had two assists. Philipp Grubauer made 22 saves.

Jake DeBrusk scored Vancouver's only goal, on the power play in the first period, with an assist from Brock Boeser that extended Boeser's point streak to nine games.

What it means

A first hat trick is a milestone by itself. Doing it as the youngest in franchise history, in the first game back from Helsinki, while snapping a losing streak, makes it a statement. Catton isn't just having a good sophomore season — he's becoming the player the Kraken build around.

Up next: the Kraken host the Sharks on Saturday, November 21 at 10:00 PM ET.

Sports · Nov 20, 2026 · 9:30 AM ET

Scott Wedgewood's 25-save shutout blanks the Ducks as the Avalanche end Cutter Gauthier's 10-game goal streak

By Matt

Scott Wedgewood stopped all 25 shots for his first shutout of the season as the Avalanche beat the Ducks 4-0 in Denver — and ended Cutter Gauthier's 10-game goal streak.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Scott Wedgewood made 25 saves for his first shutout of the season as the Colorado Avalanche beat the Anaheim Ducks 4-0 at Ball Arena on Thursday night. It was the 13th shutout of Wedgewood's career, and his seventh as a member of the Avalanche.

The shutout ended the story of the NHL season so far. Cutter Gauthier came into Denver on a 10-game goal streak — four hat tricks in November, 19 goals across the streak, three shy of the NHL record for goals in a calendar month — and Wedgewood stopped him cold. The Ducks rang two shots off the post and kept coming, but nothing got through.

"I think it's hard not to see it. He's on every Instagram page and every media highlight right now. I skated with him this summer," Wedgewood said of Gauthier after the game.

The game around him

Colorado broke it open in the second period. Nicolas Roy scored eight seconds into the middle frame, Brock Nelson added a power-play goal at 3:25 and another at 10:04, and Devon Toews made it 4-0 at 10:33 of the third on a give-and-go with Nelson. Nelson finished with two goals and an assist, Toews had a goal and an assist, and Martin Necas set up two. Lukas Dostal made 23 saves for Anaheim.

The shutout stretched a quieter streak, too: Colorado has now gone 165:25 without allowing a regulation home goal, dating back to November 5 against Nashville.

The Avalanche improve to 13-7-3 and have won four of their past six. The Ducks fall to 11-11-1 and have lost four of five.

What it means

A shutout is a shutout, but this one lands harder because of who was on the other side. Gauthier's streak was the hottest run in hockey — the kind of thing that had the whole league watching every Ducks game — and Wedgewood ended it with a clean sheet on home ice. Colorado didn't just beat Anaheim; it took away the one thing everyone tuned in to see.

Gauthier's November still stands at 19 goals, three short of the calendar-month record shared by Teemu Selanne (March 1993) and Joe Malone (February 1921). He'll get another crack at it — but the streak itself is over.

Up next: the Avalanche host the Canadiens on Wednesday, November 25 at 9:30 PM ET.

Sports · Nov 20, 2026 · 9:30 AM ET

Travis Konecny caps a four-point night with an OT winner as the Flyers rally from three down to stun the Senators 6-5

By Matt

Travis Konecny scored 39 seconds into overtime to cap a four-point night as the Flyers erased a 5-2 third-period deficit and beat the Senators 6-5 in Ottawa.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Travis Konecny scored 39 seconds into overtime to finish a four-point night as the Philadelphia Flyers rallied from three goals down in the third period to beat the Ottawa Senators 6-5 at Canadian Tire Centre on Thursday night.

Konecny came into the game with two goals, four assists and six points in 14 games — a slow start by his standards. He left it having factored into four of Philadelphia's six goals, including the winner. He assisted on Owen Tippett's first-period power-play goal, set up Cam York's late second-period goal that cut the deficit to 3-2, fed Tyson Foerster on a 2-on-1 in the third, and then ended it himself, racing up the left wing and wiring a shot from the circle that squeezed past former Flyers goaltender Samuel Ersson.

It was Konecny's fourth career overtime goal, tied for the eighth-most in Flyers history. Claude Giroux leads the list with 11.

The comeback

The Flyers were dead in the water six minutes into the third period, trailing 5-2. Then York swatted in a bouncing puck to make it 5-3, and fifteen seconds later Konecny fed Foerster to bring it within one. With goaltender Joseph Woll pulled during 4-on-4 play, Jamie Drysdale walked in from the blue line and snapped a shot past Ersson at 17:27 of the third — 2:33 left — to tie it 5-5 and force overtime.

Four unanswered goals, all in the third period and overtime. It was the seventh third-period, three-goal comeback victory in Flyers history, and the first since they beat the Buffalo Sabres 4-3 in overtime on March 29, 2021.

York finished with two goals, Foerster had a goal and two assists, and Drysdale had a goal and two assists. Woll made 21 saves — and picked up an assist on Konecny's overtime winner, his first of the season and the second point of his career.

The game around him

Ottawa got two goals from Dylan Cozens and two assists from Tim Stutzle, and Claude Giroux scored against his former team early. But the Senators couldn't hold a three-goal lead at home, and the Flyers — who have now won two straight and are 4-1-1 in their past six — stole two points in a building where they looked finished with 14 minutes to play.

Philadelphia improves to 8-11-6.

What it means

This is the Konecny the Flyers have been waiting on. The first 14 games were quiet for a player who is supposed to drive this team, and one night doesn't erase that — but a four-point game capped by an overtime winner, with his fingerprints on every part of the comeback, is the kind of performance that turns a season around. If this is the version of Konecny that shows up the rest of the way, the Flyers' record starts moving.

Up next: the Flyers visit the Canadiens in Montreal on Saturday, November 21 at 7:00 PM ET.

MLB · Nov 19, 2026 · 9:10 PM ET

Duran tops Boston's Friday non-tender board

By Matt

Jarren Duran's $11.1 million projected salary and crowded outfield make him Boston's biggest non-tender decision before Friday's 5 p.m. deadline.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The Red Sox have until Friday at 5 p.m. ET to decide whether Jarren Duran is still one of theirs. MLB's contract tender deadline hits then, and Boston has to tender contracts to every unsigned player on its 40-man roster or watch them become free agents immediately. Duran, the 2024 All-Star Game MVP, is the name at the top of the board — and a trade looks likelier than a straight non-tender.

The deadline

The mechanics are simple: tender a contract and the player stays under team control, with the two sides free to keep negotiating until an arbitration hearing. Don't tender, and the player hits the open market the same day. Duran is arbitration-eligible for 2027 and 2028, so the decision isn't just about next season — it's about whether Boston wants to pay a projected $11.1 million (via MLB Trade Rumors) for a player who no longer has a clear everyday role.

He isn't the only name on Boston's list. First baseman Triston Casas is among the other potential cuts, per NBC Sports Boston, but Duran is the one with real trade value still attached.

The case against paying him

Duran's 2026 season was the worst of his career, and it wasn't close. The full line:

Games: 151

Average: .207

On-base: .266

Slugging: .361

OPS: .627

Home runs: 20

Stolen bases: 21

RBI: 69

Strikeouts: 165

Walks: 41

wRC+: 69

That wRC+ — 31 percent below league average — was the second-worst mark among qualified hitters in baseball, per MLB Trade Rumors. The strikeout rate climbed to 27.1 percent, up from 24.3 percent in 2025 and 21.8 percent in his breakout year. The one thing that didn't crater was the power-speed combination: he still reached 20 homers and 21 steals, the second 20-20 season of his career, which is what makes him a change-of-scenery candidate rather than a straight release.

From All-Star MVP to the bubble

The fall is what makes this one sting. Two years ago Duran was one of the best players in baseball: a .285/.342/.492 line in 2024, an All-Star selection, and the Ted Williams Award as All-Star Game MVP after a tiebreaking two-run homer off Hunter Greene lifted the American League to a 5-3 win. He led the majors in doubles (48) and triples (14), stole 34 bases, and finished eighth in AL MVP voting. He followed that with a 4.0 fWAR season in 2025 — a step back, but still a useful everyday player.

Then came the collapse. The extra-base hits dried up — 15 doubles and five triples after 62 combined in 2024 — and the strikeouts piled up. Boston's outfield, meanwhile, got younger and more settled around him: Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela, and Wilyer Abreu are the projected starters, and the club just signed Jake Bauers to a four-year, $58 million deal to be the primary designated hitter. With Bauers at DH, Duran and Masataka Yoshida — due $18.6 million next season — are left fighting for bench at-bats at starter money.

The trade market

Boston has been shopping Duran since the GM Meetings, and the interest is real even at his lowest value. The San Diego Padres have long admired him and are doing background work again. The Seattle Mariners and Philadelphia Phillies have each poked around, per MassLive's Chris Cotillo. The Chicago Cubs evaluated him as a potential change-of-scenery addition this week, The Athletic's Patrick Mooney reported Thursday, and the Cubs are also in on posted Japanese outfielder Teruaki Sato.

The leverage is thin. Boston's own reporting has it that the Red Sox don't want to pay $11.1 million in arbitration for a player who is, at best, a fourth outfielder — USA Today's Bob Nightengale put it bluntly: "He should be as good as gone." But letting him walk for nothing would sting for a front office already criticized for not trading him when his value peaked after 2024. A trade, even for a modest return, beats a non-tender.

What happens Friday

If no deal materializes by 5 p.m., Boston faces a straight choice: tender him and swallow the arbitration number, or non-tender him and let the market set his price — almost certainly well below $11.1 million. Either way, it would be a surprise to see Duran back in a Red Sox uniform in 2027. The deadline forces the answer.

Golden Chocobo bids $85,400 at Goldin

By Matt

A PSA 8 serialized Golden Traveling Chocobo — #71 of just 77 ever printed — is bidding at $85,400 in Goldin's fall TCG auction, days after a sibling copy reportedly changed hands for $1.4 million.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The golden bird is back on the block. A PSA 8 serialized Golden Traveling Chocobo — card #71 of the entire print run — is bidding at $85,400 with buyer's premium in Goldin's 2026 Fall TCG Elite Auction, and the auction is still live.

The card

This is the 2025 Magic: The Gathering — Final Fantasy serialized Golden Chocobo (#0551f Traveling Chocobo), the gold-foiled chase card from the set. Wizards printed the serialized version in English Collector Boosters only, each copy stamped with its own number, and the odds of pulling one were under 0.1% per pack, according to CGC. ICv2 calls it one of the scarcest Magic cards in existence, and it rarely shows up at auction at all.

It's also not clear how many of the print run ever made it into collectors' hands — the rest could still be sitting in sealed product. Unopened Collector Boosters for the set are going for roughly $1,500 a box.

The timing is the story

This listing lands days after a sibling copy made headlines of its own. Copy #47 — a PSA Gem Mint 10 that also carries an MBA Gold Diamond evaluation — was reported sold in a private deal for $1.4 million, per MTG Rocks and Draftsim on November 17. The seller was named as Adam Cai, also known as Pristine_Collectibles, with the report traced to Collectr.

A note of caution on that figure: it is a reported private sale, not an auction result. No buyer identity, settlement document, or payment record has been published, and one extraordinary sale does not set a market price for the rest of the print run. The previous confirmed record for the card was $250,000 — less than a fifth of the reported number.

Recent auction comps put the Goldin bid in context. A CGC 8 copy realized $75,000 at Fanatics Collect in March, and another CGC 8 went for $67,100 at Goldin in September 2025. Draftsim notes most copies known to have changed hands have sold in the $40,000–$80,000 range, which is exactly where this listing sits right now.

The rest of the auction

Goldin's fall sale is stacked beyond the Chocobo. The current headline lots include:

Illustrator Pikachu: $488,000

1st Edition Base Set box: $231,800

Final Fantasy Collector Boosters (unopened): ~$1,500

The Chocobo is the Magic headliner, but the Pikachu is the auction's top lot by a wide margin.

Sports · Nov 19, 2026 · 12:23 PM ET

Jalen Johnson's second triple-double in five days powers Hawks past Thunder 117-112

By Matt

Jalen Johnson put up 16 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists — his second triple-double in five days — as the Hawks beat the Thunder 117-112 in Oklahoma City.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Jalen Johnson recorded a triple-double with 16 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists as the Atlanta Hawks beat the Oklahoma City Thunder 117-112 on Wednesday night at Paycom Center. It was his second triple-double in five days — he put up 27 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists at Chicago on November 13 — and it handed the Thunder their first home loss of the season.

Both teams now sit at 9-6, but the night belonged to Atlanta's balance. Onyeka Okongwu led the Hawks with 28 points and nine rebounds, Nickeil Alexander-Walker added 19 points and seven assists, and Dyson Daniels chipped in 10 points and 10 rebounds. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led all scorers with 34 for Oklahoma City, and Jared McCain added 18 off the bench.

The homecoming stole the first half of the story

The game was circled on the calendar the moment the schedule came out: Lu Dort and Aaron Wiggins were back in Oklahoma City for the first time since being traded to Atlanta this past offseason. Both helped the Thunder win the 2024-25 NBA championship, and the home crowd gave them standing ovations and video tributes — Wiggins during the first media timeout, Dort after the first quarter.

They made sure the return was more than a ceremony. Dort finished with 16 points, three rebounds and two steals, knocking down three triples. Wiggins scored 14. And when the game swung in the fourth quarter, it was the two former Thunder players who swung it.

How it played out

Oklahoma City erased a 13-point halftime deficit to tie the game at 83 entering the fourth quarter. Then, in the first 1:15 of the final frame — with Gilgeous-Alexander on the bench — Atlanta retook control with three straight three-pointers: Wiggins, then Dort, then Wiggins again. The Hawks never gave the lead back, winning the fourth 34-29.

Atlanta's shooting carried the night. The Hawks hit 20 of 50 from three-point range and outrebounded the Thunder 50-43, while Oklahoma City went 9 of 26 from deep. Gilgeous-Alexander got his 34, but he missed critical late shots as the comeback fell short, including a mid-range jumper off the front of the rim and a pull-up three in the final seconds.

Johnson is stacking them now

Five days ago in Chicago, Johnson's triple-double came in an overtime win. This one came on the road against the defending champions' building, with the game still in the balance. The 16 points were the quietest part of the line — the 12 rebounds and 11 assists were the engine, with Atlanta's ball movement and second chances built around his playmaking.

The Hawks have now won back-to-back games and six of their last eight. The Thunder have dropped four of their last five.

Gaming · Nov 18, 2026 · 9:10 AM ET

ARC Raiders 2.6 brings back Cold Snap

By Matt

Embark Studios launched Live Update 2.6.0 on November 17, bringing Cold Snap back to the map rotation, a new Outlaw Weapon Stencil Set, a 50% Black Friday discount, and a first look at Flickering Flames Part 1 arriving November 24.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Embark Studios launched Live Update 2.6.0 for ARC Raiders on November 17, 2026. The headline is the return of Cold Snap to the Major Map Condition rotation, just as the snow settles in — and the update pairs it with a new weapon stencil set, a long list of fixes, a 50% Black Friday discount, and a first look at the Flickering Flames project arriving November 24.

Cold Snap is back

Cold Snap rejoins the Major Map Condition rotation in 2.6.0. Embark's own note on it is short — "As the days get colder and snow settles in, Cold Snap is back!" — but the condition changes how every run plays: snow, reduced visibility, and the cold itself become part of the extraction, on top of the ARC machines and rival Raiders already competing for the same loot.

It is a return, not a debut. Cold Snap first arrived as the game's winter update in December 2025, and its comeback a year later lands alongside a fresh event built around the same season.

What's new in 2.6.0

Cold Snap: Back in the Major Map Condition rotation

Outlaw Weapon Stencil Set: Three weapon stencils — Taurus, Sundob, and Malocchio — now in the in-game store rotation

Buried items: The Dockmaster's Detector now finds buried items on all maps except Pendola Pass (which still needs the Mountaineer's Detector); the Beachcombing minor condition is gone from Riven Tides

50% discount: Black Friday sale on the base game and Deluxe Edition, dates vary by platform (below)

The buried-items change is the quiet quality-of-life win in the patch. What used to be a Riven Tides-only mechanic is now available almost everywhere, so detector runs are worth doing no matter which map the rotation serves up.

The 50% Black Friday sale

New players can join topside at half price, with the sale window depending on platform:

PlayStation: November 16–30; Base game only

Epic Games Store: November 17–December 1; Base game, Deluxe Edition, Deluxe Edition Upgrade

Xbox: November 19–December 3; Base game, Deluxe Edition, Deluxe Edition Upgrade

Steam: November 19–December 3; Base game, Deluxe Edition, Deluxe Edition Upgrade

The game normally sells for $40 on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC (Epic, Steam, and Nvidia GeForce NOW).

Flickering Flames Part 1 lands November 24

Update 2.7 arrives next week, on November 24, with Part 1 of the two-part Flickering Flames Raider project. The event warms Toledo in a celebration of light: with hopes of a festive gathering of all four contradas, Celeste is preparing a special dinner, and Raiders complete three steps to help her get ready. Each step pays out weapons and weapon mods, with additional cosmetic rewards coming in Part 2. The Nessuno Set — outfit, backpack, and backpack charm — is also headed to the in-game store rotation with the update.

The fixes that matter

2.6.0 is mostly a fixes patch, and several of the fixes target the kind of bug that ends a run unfairly:

• Invisible players: fixed two separate cases where a Raider could appear invisible to others — one tied to entering and quickly exiting the Gondola, one that could happen mid-round.

• Revive protection: enemies could knock a player out immediately after a defibrillator revive; being revived now properly prevents knockouts.

• Road Warrior skill: it can now recycle Weapon Amplification Modules and Candleberries during raids as intended.

• Vaulting stamina: vaulting no longer drains jump stamina, and the "Vaults on Vaults on Vaults" skill no longer drains any stamina.

• Hydra vs. lures: the Hydra now only aims some of its weapons at Lure Grenades, still targeting players with the rest.

• Snap Hook: the description now states the correct 18m range (previously listed as 20m).

• Stiletto: weight reduced from 7 to 6.

• Scoped aiming: aiming down sights with scoped weapons could shift aim sideways; aim now stays aligned with the crosshair entering and exiting ADS.

• Inventory: items can now be dropped by dragging them outside the inventory, and a gamepad looting bug that could delete a stack when interrupted is fixed.

• Outpost: the Outpost can now be correctly upgraded to Level 4, fixing a case where it could not be fully upgraded.

• Codex: a new "Times Revived By A Stranger" stat is on the player stats page.

Lighting and exposure also got a pass on Spaceport and Buried City, aimed at clearer visibility looking from interiors to exteriors and in dark interiors, and collision fixes landed across Pendola Pass, Spaceport, Riven Tides, and Stella Montis.

A year after launch, the cadence is the story as much as any single patch: 2.6.0 lands, 2.7 follows a week later, and the game keeps getting seasonal events and systemic fixes rather than coasting on its launch audience.

Sources: ARC Raiders rolls out v2.6 update with bug fixes, new content, cosmetics and sale · ARC Raiders Update 2.6.0 patch notes: Cold Snap is back

TSL Bets parlay: Nikola Jokic OVER 24.5 points + Shai Gilgeous-Alexander OVER 30.5 points (~+300)

By Matt

Two props, two scoring stars. Nikola Jokic OVER 24.5 points (-105) at home against a Boston frontcourt with no answer for him, plus Shai Gilgeous-Alexander OVER 30.5 points (+104) at home against Atlanta — about +300 combined.

The game slips

Boston Celtics (11-3) at Denver Nuggets (7-5)

Wednesday, 9:30 PM ET — Ball Arena, Denver (ESPN)

• Spread: Celtics -2.5 (-110)

• Total: 219.5 (-110)

• Moneyline: Celtics -142 / Nuggets +120

• Odds source: DraftKings via Bleacher Nation, November 18

Injury report — Celtics: No players on the injury report. Jayson Tatum (26.5 PPG) and Paul George are playing.

Injury report — Nuggets: G Julian Strawther OUT (left knee sprain). G Jamal Murray and F Aaron Gordon are both available.

Collectibles · Nov 18, 2026 · 8:02 AM ET

A serialized Golden Chocobo just sold for a reported $1.4 million — more than five times the card's previous record

By Matt

A PSA 10 Golden Chocobo, copy 47 of 77, reportedly changed hands in a $1.4 million private sale — shattering the card's previous confirmed record of $250,000. The buyer is not identified, and no settlement documents have been published, so the figure is an attributed private-sale price, not an auction result.

The sale

A serialized Golden Chocobo from Magic: The Gathering's Final Fantasy set reportedly sold for $1.4 million in a private sale — a new reported high for the card, and more than five times its previous confirmed record.

The sale was reported by Collectr, the card-tracking app, and covered by MTG Rocks on November 17. The card is copy 47 of 77, graded PSA Gem Mint 10, and it also carries an MBA Gold Diamond evaluation — a second independent grading that marks it among the best examples of its kind.

The seller was identified as Adam Cai, known as Pristine_Collectibles, who was tagged in Collectr's announcement. MTG content creator Ben Bateman posted on November 17 about meeting Cai at MagicCon: Atlanta and discussing the deal.

The caveat

This is a reported private sale, not a public auction. No buyer identity has been published, and no settlement document or payment record has been made public. The $1.4 million figure is attributed — real reporting, from a named seller and a named source, but with less public price discovery than a fully documented auction result.

That matters for what the number means. With only 77 serialized copies in existence, one sale cannot establish a reliable market price for the other 76. The previous confirmed Golden Chocobo sale was $250,000 — less than a quarter of this new figure. If the $1.4 million holds up, it resets the ceiling for the card overnight. If it does not, it is a rumor with a big number attached.

The card

The Golden Chocobo — the serialized gold-stamped version of Traveling Chocobo — is the premier chase card of the Final Fantasy set, Magic's best-selling release of all time. Only 77 copies were printed, each uniquely numbered, and they appear only in English-language Collector Boosters. The card carries no rules text at all, a first for a serialized Magic card, and no borders — just the golden bird, the number, and the art.

It is the set's answer to The One Ring: a single serialized chase card that became the face of the entire release, with every Collector Booster opened in part because it might be inside.

What it means

Whether or not $1.4 million becomes the card's settled price, the report itself is the story: a modern Magic card, printed in 2025, is now being talked about in the same breath as the game's most expensive pieces ever. The serialized-chase era that started with The One Ring has a new headline number — and every other Golden Chocobo owner just watched their card's ceiling move.

Sources

• The Mana Forge: A $1.4 million private Golden Chocobo sale is reported for copy 47/77

iShowSpeed just won Streamer of the Year at the Esports Awards — his second Streamer of the Year trophy in five days

By Matt

iShowSpeed won Streamer of the Year at the Esports Awards 2026 in Miami on Monday night, beating Kai Cenat, CaseOh, Jynxzi and Caedrel — five days after taking the same title at the Streamer Awards in Los Angeles.

The night

Darren "iShowSpeed" Watkins Jr. won Streamer of the Year at the Esports Awards 2026 on Monday night, November 17, at the Adrienne Arsht Center in Miami.

He beat 11 other nominees for the title: Kai Cenat, CaseOh, Jynxzi, Caedrel, OhnePixel, JasonTheWeen, Cinna, StableRonaldo, Snax Gaming, Coringa and TheBurntPeanut.

It is his second Streamer of the Year trophy in five days. Last Thursday, November 13, Speed won the same title at the sixth annual Streamer Awards in Los Angeles — his third straight win there — taking three trophies on the night. The Esports Awards is a separate ceremony, esports' own biggest night, and Speed just swept the top streamer prize at both of them in the same week.

The other winners

Marc "Caedrel" Lamont was honored as Esports Personality of the Year, and Jynxzi took Esports Content Creator of the Year. The ceremony returned to Miami for what the organizers call the biggest and most prestigious night in esports, with the night's winners announced across the full list of categories.

The year

The award caps a year in which Speed kept expanding past streaming. He did his World Cup Tour this year, partnering with FIFA to livestream soccer fans around the globe, and last month he became an executive producer on "The Eyes of Ghana," a documentary alongside former President Barack Obama and Michelle Obama.

He also has GTA 6 on the calendar: Speed and Kai Cenat have both announced plans to stream the game when it releases — Cenat starting at 8 p.m. ET on November 18, Speed an hour later at 9 p.m. ET.

What it means

Two ceremonies, two Streamer of the Year trophies, five days apart. Whatever you think of the awards circuit, the industry just told the same story twice in one week: right now, the biggest streamer in the world is Speed — and the gap between him and everyone else is not particularly close.

Sports · Nov 18, 2026 · 8:00 AM ET

Quentin Grimes drops a career-high 47 — 10 threes, a game-tying bomb with 1.7 left — as the Lakers rally from 18 down to beat the Hornets in OT

By Matt

Quentin Grimes scored a career-high 47 points, including 21 in the fourth quarter and the game-tying three with 1.7 seconds left, as the short-handed Lakers came back from 18 down to beat Charlotte 118-114 in overtime for their ninth straight win.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Quentin Grimes had never scored 40 points in an NBA game. Then the Lakers needed him to save one.

Grimes scored a career-high 47 points — 16-of-24 from the field, 10-of-14 from three — and buried the game-tying three with 1.7 seconds left in regulation as Los Angeles came back from 18 down to beat the Charlotte Hornets 118-114 in overtime at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday night. It was the Lakers' ninth consecutive win, and they are 13-2 with the best record in the NBA.

The shot itself was disbelief made real. Luka Doncic brought the ball up with under 10 seconds left, the Lakers trailing 111-108, and found Grimes wide open on the right wing. Grimes had already outscored the Hornets 18-17 by himself in the quarter.

"I don't know why they left me open," Grimes said after the game. "I was like, 'Oh yeah, that's cash. I was too open.'"

The 10 threes are a career high, and they put Grimes next to Kobe Bryant as the only Lakers ever to hit 10 or more in a single game. Bryant hit 12 against Seattle in 2003.

The fourth quarter

The Lakers were lifeless for three quarters. They trailed 94-81 entering the fourth, down 18 in the last minute of the third, and were missing their second- and third-leading scorers — Austin Reaves (left heel bruise) and Walker Kessler (right leg soreness) both sat out.

Then Doncic went to the bench for the first six minutes of the final frame, and Grimes took the game over. He scored 21 points in the quarter, including 15 to Charlotte's five over a six-and-a-half-minute stretch that erased a 14-point deficit. When Doncic returned, he kept calling off JJ Redick's plays just to get Grimes the ball.

"Luka, when he got back in the game in the fourth, he kept calling off every play I was calling and just saying, 'No, I'm trying to get Q the ball!'" Redick said. "He recognized what was happening. The hot-hand theory — it's a real thing. It definitely was a real thing tonight."

Doncic finished with 36 points of his own on 13-of-34 shooting, his 11th consecutive game with at least 30. The two combined for 83 points and 15 threes, and the Lakers outscored Charlotte 37-20 across the fourth quarter and overtime, holding the Hornets to three points in the extra session.

Grimes iced it himself in overtime, disrupting an inbounds pass meant for Royce O'Neale with 17.4 seconds left, then making both free throws. Matisse Thybulle added three steals, the last with 8.8 seconds to go.

The context

The win made the Lakers just the fourth team in league history with three different players scoring 40-plus through the first 15 games of a season — Grimes joining Doncic and Reaves. It also kept them unbeaten in November despite playing without two starters, on a night when the supporting cast had to carry real weight: Kevon Looney, Jarred Vanderbilt and two-way player Carson Cooper, playing his first game as a Laker, combined for 19 rebounds with Kessler out.

There was a personal layer to the night, too. Grimes' mother, Tonja Stelly, was in the stands the day after her 60th birthday. He gave her his game-worn uniform afterward and admitted he had tried to get 60 points for her 60th. He came 13 short — and nobody in the building was complaining.

He also did it a week after dislocating the pinkie finger on his shooting hand, an injury that cost him two straight games. Collin Sexton, who scored 10 off the bench, said the locker room has spent weeks telling Grimes to let it fly. Tuesday night, he finally did.

Charlotte, for its part, did almost everything right for three quarters. Brandon Miller scored 28, Naz Reid added 23 points and 11 rebounds, and the Hornets led in every period before the fourth. It is their ninth loss in 10 games.

What it means

Nine straight wins, the league's best record, and now a night where the third option became the hero. The Lakers keep finding a different guy to win the game — and Tuesday it was the one who had never scored 40 before, against a team that left him open with the game on the line.

Up next: the Lakers host the Utah Jazz on Wednesday night at Crypto.com Arena, the second night of a back-to-back.

Sports · Nov 18, 2026 · 8:00 AM ET

The Pistons just ended the Spurs' 12-game win streak — Cade's 27, Jenkins' 25, and a fourth quarter San Antonio never solved

By Matt

Cade Cunningham scored 27 points, Daniss Jenkins added 25 off the bench, and Ausar Thompson finished a rebound shy of a triple-double as Detroit rallied from 14 down to beat San Antonio 105-93, ending the Spurs' 12-game winning streak.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The San Antonio Spurs had not lost since October 23. They had won 12 straight, owned the best record in the West, and had Victor Wembanyama rolling toward another MVP case. The Detroit Pistons walked into Frost Bank Center on Tuesday night, fell behind by 14, and beat them anyway, 105-93.

Cade Cunningham led Detroit with 27 points, five rebounds and six assists. Daniss Jenkins added 25 points, five rebounds and five assists off the bench. Ausar Thompson finished a rebound shy of a triple-double with 14 points, 12 assists and five steals.

The Pistons trailed 55-54 at halftime and were down six entering the fourth, 78-72. Then they held San Antonio to 21 fourth-quarter points, led by as many as 11 multiple times in the period, and never let the Spurs' final push get closer than five. Dylan Harper cut it to five with a layup at the 2:35 mark, then slipped and fell heading downcourt with a little more than a minute left, suffering an apparent groin injury. Detroit pulled away from there.

"Have fun. Play basketball. It's another game," Cunningham said after the game. "Obviously, they're a good team, but nobody in that locker room has fear in his heart for anybody. So it's just about coming out here, playing basketball, doing what we do best, executing our game plan."

The streak

Twelve straight wins is the kind of run that starts showing up in franchise history books. Per the Spurs, it was their 25th double-digit win streak since the 1976-77 season, their first in the NBA after moving from the ABA — the most such streaks in the league, ahead of the Lakers (21), Celtics (16), Cavaliers (15) and Thunder (14). The NBA record is 33, set by the 1971-72 Lakers.

The loss drops San Antonio to 12-3, still among the strongest early-season teams in the West. It also held the Spurs below 100 points for the first time this season — 93 was their lowest scoring total of the year.

Wembanyama had 25 points and 18 rebounds in the loss, his 11th double-double of the season. He was blunt afterward: "We didn't do the right things. I think we should have been smarter. As soon as we stepped off the court after the end of the fourth quarter, things looked pretty straightforward and our mistakes looked kinda obvious."

The context

This was not a fluke night for Detroit. The Pistons shot 49 percent from the field, handed out 31 assists, and improved to 9-4 — third in the East — with a 6-2 road record. They have won three of four, and they did this one on the second night of a back-to-back, a night after Cade's 52-point game against Washington last week made him the first player in NBA history with 50 points and 10 assists and zero turnovers in a game.

Jenkins' 25 was the second-half engine: Detroit's bench outplayed San Antonio's depth all night, and the Pistons' defense held a team averaging well over 110 to its worst offensive night of the season.

What it means

Streaks end. The question was always who would be the team to do it, and Detroit answered it with defense, depth and a star who wanted the moment. The Spurs are still 12-3 and still terrifying. But the "when will they lose?" watch is over — and the team that ended it is 9-4 and playing like it belongs in the East's top tier.

Up next: the Pistons visit the New Orleans Pelicans on Wednesday night. The Spurs host the Clippers on Thursday.

Sports · Nov 18, 2026 · 3:07 AM ET

Sensabaugh drops 40 to snap Utah's skid

By Matt

Brice Sensabaugh came off the bench and scored 40 points — 25 in the fourth quarter — as the Utah Jazz beat the LA Clippers 132-107 on Tuesday night, snapping a 12-game losing streak and becoming the youngest player in NBA history with 40 points, 10 rebounds and eight threes in a game.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Utah Jazz had not won a game in nearly a month. Then Brice Sensabaugh came off the bench and took over the fourth quarter.

Sensabaugh scored a season-high 40 points — 25 of them in the final period — as Utah beat the Los Angeles Clippers 132-107 at Intuit Dome on Tuesday night. The win snapped a 12-game losing streak and gave the Jazz just their second victory of the season, improving them to 2-13. It was also their first road win of the season after an 0-6 start away from home, and their first win of any kind since a 120-119 decision over New Orleans on October 23.

The game was tight for three quarters. Utah led just 88-86 heading into the fourth, then blew it open. The Jazz outscored the Clippers 44-21 in the final 12 minutes, shooting 18-for-22 from the floor in the period. Sensabaugh sparked a game-changing 20-2 surge — including a 16-0 run midway through the quarter — with a pull-up jumper when Utah led 93-91, scoring 13 points in that stretch alone.

He finished 16-for-21 from the field and 8-for-11 from three, the eight makes a career high, adding 11 rebounds, five assists and a block. Keyonte George added 30 points and 11 assists, and Utah finished with a season-high 20 three-pointers on 38 attempts, shooting 58.3 percent from the floor as a team. Brook Lopez led the Clippers with 23 points and six rebounds in the loss, dropping Los Angeles to 4-9.

The history

The line put Sensabaugh in the record book. At 23 years and 18 days old, he became the youngest player in NBA history to total 40 or more points, 10 or more rebounds and eight or more three-pointers in a single game.

The 40 was three points shy of his career high — and his third career 40-point game — but this was his first 40-point double-double, and the first time he had done it coming off the bench. For a Jazz team that has been injury-plagued and short on bright spots during a 2-13 start, a 23-year-old reserve rewriting a record that young is the kind of night worth remembering long after the losing streak is forgotten.

What's next

Utah visits the Lakers on Wednesday, with three more games on the schedule this week. The skid is over. The question now is whether the youngest 40-10-8 night in league history was a one-off explosion or the start of something bigger for Sensabaugh.

Collectibles · Nov 17, 2026 · 9:08 PM ET

Deep Space 9 is Star Trek's breakout card

By Matt

Five Magic: The Gathering Star Trek cards have spiked since prerelease — and Deep Space 9 leads the way, climbing from $14.50 to $40 after Worlds put the new set through its paces.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The spike

Five cards from Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek have spiked in price in the few days since prerelease — and the headliner is the station itself. Deep Space 9 went from $14.50 at prerelease to $40, a jump of roughly 176% in under two weeks. A nine-mana mythic was always going to cost real money — but $40 caught everyone off guard.

The timing tells the story. Worlds, the biggest tournament of the year, kicked off on the set's release day, immediately putting the new cards to the test in high-level competitive play. The ones that performed spiked; the ones that didn't fell back. Five passed the test.

The five risers

Deep Space 9: $14.50; $40

Jadzia Dax, Living Legacy: $7.70; $23.50

Captain James T. Kirk: $6.50; $22

Anthropological Mission: $0.50; $8

The Naked Time: $0.50; $2.90

The foil market agrees with the direction: NerdSnack's TCG Market Movers board has the foil printing at $43.83, up from $18.60 over the November 10–17 window — a 136% move.

Why the station is worth it

Deep Space 9 is a nine-drop that pays you back the moment it lands. When it enters — and at the beginning of your upkeep — it exiles the top four cards of your library and puts every permanent exiled that way onto the battlefield. Up to four free permanents a turn is the kind of effect that ends games, and it's one you can cheat into play rather than hard-casting for nine.

It shines in the new spacecraft decks built around Captain Picard, sure — but the price is being driven by something wider: unlike most cards of its type, it doesn't need your deck to be all about rockets and charge counters. It fits Eldrazi shells and artifact decks, or really anything that can get to nine mana and wants a game-ender. A finisher that slots into existing shells instead of demanding a new one is exactly the kind of card that holds a price.

The Worlds effect

The other four risers all have the same fingerprint: they showed up at Worlds and did real work.

Anthropological Mission is the real shocker out of Atlanta. Stefan Schütz rode it to the Worlds title with an Izzet list running a full playset of a fifty-cent uncommon nobody had on their radar. Once it has three counters, it stops looting and starts netting a card every time you play a non-creature spell. Schütz's list leaned all the way into that: thirty instants and sorceries, zero creatures, and a deck that just buries opponents in cards once the Mission is online. A fifty-cent uncommon that won the biggest tournament of the year doesn't stay fifty cents.

The Naked Time caught the wave of Boros Pixie, the most-played deck of the weekend. It pumps a creature, gives it haste, and ramps you in red — strong enough that some players were openly asking if it should be banned. It isn't, and it's not even the set's best uncommon — but a card that strong in the format's most-played deck was never going to stay at prerelease pricing.

Captain James T. Kirk is the other half of that Boros story: an efficient, aggressive creature that generates a lot of value when your back is against the wall, and a key part of the deck that dominated Worlds weekend.

Jadzia Dax, Living Legacy is a useful ramp creature — and a beater in her own right in a long game — that has proven popular in a rising Selesnya Landfall deck, an archetype that appeared en masse at the recent tournament.

What it means

Prerelease pricing is a guess; Worlds is the answer key. The Star Trek set's early market was soft — most cards came down once packs started opening — but the five that proved themselves in competitive play went the other way, and the station went furthest of all. If the Worlds decks stay relevant, these prices have room; if the meta moves on, the uncommons that rode one tournament are the first to give it back.

Sports · Nov 17, 2026 · 8:04 AM ET

Jeremiah Fears, 20, becomes the youngest Pelican ever with a triple-double — New Orleans snaps its skid, 115-94 over Golden State

By Matt

Jeremiah Fears had 19 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists for his first career triple-double, and at 20 years and 33 days old he is the youngest player in Pelicans history to do it — passing Chris Paul's mark from April 2006 — as New Orleans snapped a six-game losing streak with a 115-94 win over Golden State.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Smoothie King Center crowd knew what was happening before the box score did. Late in the third quarter, Jeremiah Fears grabbed his 10th rebound, the building erupted, and a 20-year-old rookie had the first triple-double of his career — 19 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 115-94 win over the Golden State Warriors that snapped New Orleans' six-game losing streak.

Fears did it at 20 years and 33 days old. That makes him the youngest player in Pelicans franchise history to record a triple-double, passing a mark Chris Paul set at 20 years and 331 days on April 2, 2006 — a record that had stood for more than two decades. He is also the ninth-youngest player in NBA history to post one.

The game itself was never close. New Orleans led 35-11 after one quarter and pushed the lead as large as 31 in the third. Fears shot 6-of-13 from the field and 1-of-4 from three in 29 minutes, and by the time he sealed the milestone the only question left was the final margin.

The help around him

Saddiq Bey led the Pelicans with 23 points, hitting five threes, and Zion Williamson added 16. Yves Missi grabbed 14 rebounds in his second game back from a knee injury that sidelined him 11 games, and Derik Queen — drafted six spots after Fears — came off the bench for 17 points and 10 rebounds, tying a career high with four threes. Jeron Pierre Jr. added 10 points.

New Orleans shot 42.3 percent from the field and 15-of-40 from three, outscored Golden State 44-32 in the paint, and outrebounded the Warriors 57-50. It was the kind of complete night the Pelicans, now 5-10, have been waiting for all season.

The other side

Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg scored a game-high 28 points for Golden State, with Brandin Podziemski adding 15 and Gui Santos 12. But the Warriors shot 33.3 percent from the field and 11-of-46 from three, and this was their third straight loss — the second in a row by 20 or more, coming on the heels of a 123-85 defeat at San Antonio on Friday night.

Golden State is playing without Stephen Curry, sidelined at least two weeks with a right oblique tear suffered in a 115-108 loss at Houston on Wednesday. The gap between the Warriors with Curry and without him has been stark, and Monday night was the latest evidence.

What it means

A triple-double at 20 years and 33 days puts Fears in rare company — and passing Chris Paul to do it, in a Pelicans uniform, is the kind of line that follows a player. Paul's mark had survived every Pelican since, including Anthony Davis and Zion Williamson. Fears cleared it by nearly ten months.

The win matters too. Six straight losses had the Pelicans buried at the bottom of the West, and a 21-point win over a shorthanded Warriors team doesn't fix the season — but a franchise-record night from the seventh overall pick is exactly the kind of thing a rebuild is supposed to produce.

Up next: the Warriors visit Dallas on Wednesday, and the Pelicans host Detroit the same night.

Collectibles · Nov 17, 2026 · 7:56 AM ET

Stefan Schütz wins Magic World Championship 32 — a creatureless deck, a 3-0 sweep, and $100,000

By Matt

Austria's Stefan Schütz beat Eduardo Sajgalik 3-0 in the World Championship 32 final at MagicCon: Atlanta with Izzet Mission — a deck with zero creatures that only two players in the 128-player field dared to register.

The final

Stefan Schütz is the 2026 Magic: The Gathering World Champion.

The Austrian beat Eduardo Sajgalik 3-0 in the final of World Championship 32 on Sunday at MagicCon: Atlanta, claiming the $100,000 first-place prize and the Black Lotus trophy from a $1,000,000 prize pool. Sajgalik took home $50,000 for second.

Schütz did it with Izzet Mission, a creatureless Standard deck built around Anthropological Mission — a three-mana blue enchantment from the newly released Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek set that turns into a card-drawing engine once its requirements are met. The deck runs zero main-deck creatures, blanking opposing removal entirely, and wins with Ral, Crackling Wit.

Only two players in the 128-player field registered the deck: Schütz and Alex Rohan. It went undefeated in Schütz's hands — 7-0 in the Swiss rounds, a bye in Round 14, and three wins in the Top 8 for a perfect 10-0 record in played Standard matches. He went 3-3 in the Star Trek draft portion and still made the Top 8 as the No. 4 seed, beating Hall-of-Famer Shuhei Nakamura in the quarterfinals and James Drake in the semifinals.

The play that won it

Game 3 was the one that will be retold. Sajgalik found a Leatherhead, Swamp Stalker that Schütz had no clean answer for — his removal couldn't target it through hexproof. So Schütz pointed his removal at his own creature, sending two copies of Torch the Tower at his own Bothersome Noisemaker while holding priority, growing the Goblin Army token and drawing cards off Anthropological Mission until the token was big enough to block the Leatherhead.

A few turns later, with three Anthropological Missions in play — the perfect encapsulation of the deck — Sajgalik extended his hand.

The stakes beyond the trophy

The final was also the decider for the 2026 Player of the Year race and the Kai Budde Player of the Year trophy. If Sajgalik had won, it was his. His loss sends it to Christoffer Larsen, who finished the World Championship 9-5 but reached the finals of two Pro Tours this year, winning one.

For Schütz, the win caps a fast rise. He first burst onto the scene by winning a Magic Online Champions Series event in 2024, then earned his Worlds seat with a second Top Finish at Pro Tour Secrets of Strixhaven earlier this year. The title also earns him a likeness immortalized on a future Magic card, and everyone in the Top 8 earned invites to all Pro Tours in 2027.

A brand-new card from a brand-new set, a deck nobody else would play, and a 3-0 sweep in the final. That's how you win a World Championship.

Entertainment · Nov 17, 2026 · 7:56 AM ET

RAYE leads the Grammys with 11 nominations — and Beyoncé just hit 100

By Matt

RAYE leads the 69th Grammy nominations with 11, tying Beyoncé's single-year record for a woman — and Beyoncé herself became the first artist ever to reach 100 career nominations.

The morning

The nominees for the 69th Grammy Awards were revealed on Monday morning, and the list belongs to RAYE.

The British singer landed 11 nominations — the most of any artist this year — including nods for Record and Song of the Year for "Where Is My Husband!" and Album of the Year for "This Music May Contain Hope." Her 11 nominations tie Beyoncé's record for the most Grammy nominations earned by a woman in a single year.

ROSALÍA is next with nine, days after dominating the Latin Grammys with her album "Lux." Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers each scored seven. Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas have six apiece, Olivia Dean has six, and Taylor Swift received five.

The other record in the room

Beyoncé didn't lead the nominations this year. She did something bigger: she became the first artist in Grammy history to reach 100 career nominations, extending her standing as the most nominated artist the awards have ever seen.

The milestone nod came for "Morning Dew (Donk)" in Best R&B Solo Performance. It is the latest line on a record she already owned outright — and the number now sits at triple digits.

The race taking shape

The nominations set up an Album of the Year showdown between a veteran and a new guard. Swift is in the field, and Bruno Mars — the only male artist nominated in the category, for his album "The Romantic" — is the other established name in a race led by RAYE and ROSALÍA.

One absence is already drawing debate: no R&B or rap albums were nominated for Album of the Year, a gap that has the internet arguing about what the Academy values in its biggest category.

The eligibility period covered recordings released from August 31, 2025, through August 28, 2026. Final-round voting, in which roughly 16,000 Recording Academy members choose the winners, runs December 10, 2026, through January 7, 2027. The winners will be announced at a ceremony in downtown Los Angeles on February 7, 2027.

Extra Life Secret Lair is on sale today

By Matt

Rise of the Polygons, Magic's Extra Life 2026 Secret Lair, is on sale November 16–30 at $39.99 non-foil and $49.99 foil — five low-poly cards, with half of every purchase going to Seattle Children's Hospital.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The drop

Magic: The Gathering's annual Extra Life charity drop is live. Rise of the Polygons | Extra Life 2026 is on sale at MagicSecretLair.com from November 16 through November 30, closing at 1 a.m. PT on the 30th. The five-card set costs $39.99 non-foil and $49.99 foil — the same prices as the 2024 Extra Life drop.

Half of every purchase price, less third-party transaction fees, goes to Children's Miracle Network via Our Change Foundation, supporting Extra Life and Seattle Children's Hospital. On a $39.99 non-foil order, that's about $20 to the cause. This year's money is earmarked for mental and behavioral health care at Seattle Children's.

What's in the box

The drop is built like a lost N64 cartridge. All five pieces are illustrated by Brendan Sullivan in a late-1990s low-poly 3D video game style, and they tell a little story: the Young Pyromancer levels up through a treasure room and a legendary sword before the final boss, the Balefire Dragon.

Balefire Dragon: Mythic

Sword of Truth and Justice: Mythic

Big Score: Rare

Young Pyromancer: Rare

Elemental token (1/1 red): Token

The 2024 Extra Life drop went back to the 16-bit era. This year Wizards jumped a console generation forward, to blocky polygons and a charming sidekick with advice on how to beat that one especially tricky puzzle. The scenes were later revealed to be actual frames from a short film.

The charity behind it

Extra Life is the fundraising program where gamers raise money for Children's Miracle Network Hospitals, usually by streaming or hosting marathon game sessions and collecting donations. Wizards of the Coast has partnered with Extra Life since 2013, and at MagicCon: Atlanta this past weekend the company announced Magic players have now raised $10 million for Seattle Children's through the partnership.

Limited copies of Rise of the Polygons were sold early at the MagicCon: Atlanta merch booth from November 13 to 15 — at the convention, 100% of purchases went to Extra Life. The online sale runs at the standard 50% split.

Also on MTG Arena

The fictional video game from the drop crosses over into the real one: two bundles and a special emote are available in the MTG Arena store from November 16 to 30, including an Extra Life Secret Lair Sleeve Bundle priced at 3,000 gems with five sleeves based on the drop's art.

The bet

Jacoby Brissett OVER 215.5 passing yards (-111, DraftKings via HelloRookie) + Denver Nuggets -10.5 (-105, consensus) — pays about +270

Why these legs

Brissett is a veteran quarterback making his debut for a new team with 11 days to prepare, against the worst team in football. He's thrown for 1,719 yards this season at 214.9 per game — right at the line, which is the honest truth about this leg: the edge isn't the trend, it's the spot. A rested Baltimore offense against an 0-8 Chargers team that is missing starters on both sides of the ball, with a quarterback who has started 46 games in this league and knows how to run an offense cold. The Chargers' defense has given up points to everyone; Brissett doesn't need a career night, he needs his average.

The Nuggets leg is the mismatch. Denver has won seven straight and is at home against a Suns team that is winless on the road, has lost those road games by more than 18 points a night on average, is playing its fourth game in seven days on zero rest, and is missing its starting center. The Nuggets just won in Minnesota without two starters. The 10.5 is a big number, but the road form supports it — and it's the only big-spread leg in this parlay, as it should be.

The honest caveats

Brissett's season average sits a hair under the line, so this leg is a coin flip on the numbers alone — if the Ravens lean on Derrick Henry and the run game, Brissett might not get the volume. And the Nuggets are also shorthanded without Braun and Cam Johnson, so a flat shooting night could keep this inside the number. Two legs, two teams, two sports — that's the point of the parlay, and both legs have to clear on their own.

The record

TSL Bets is 19-32 in November, 23-53 all-time. Two-leg parlays are 4-4 in November at about +250 — the only parlay format that pays.
