Entertainment · Nov 12, 2026 · 3:36 PM ET

Fat Perez, Riggs and Bobby Ray win the Internet Invitational 5 & 3

By Matt

Blue never trailed at Payne's Valley — Fat Perez, Riggs and Bobby Ray closed out Big John, Ryan Whitney and Salim 5 & 3 to split the $4 million purse and lift the Cody 'Beef' Franke Trophy.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Blue never trailed

The Internet Invitational is over, and it belongs to Team Blue. Fat Perez, Sam "Riggs" Bozoian and Bobby Ray beat Big John, Ryan Whitney and Salim Sirur 5 & 3 in the 18-hole alternate-shot final at Payne's Valley, closing the match out on the 15th hole with three still to play.

The margin tells the whole story. Blue went 1 up on the first hole and never gave it back — 2 up after three, 3 up at the turn, 4 up after ten, and 5 up after fifteen. Red never led a single hole all day. In a format built to swing wildly, with three wildly different handicaps sharing every shot, this one never really swung at all.

Each of the three winners takes home $1,338,333 from the $4 million purse, and Bobby Ray's total runs $25,000 higher — the 9th-hole money he banked alongside The Duke back on Day 2. On top of the split, the trio also takes home a Tracker boat from Bass Pro Shops. The trophy they lifted is the Cody "Beef" Franke Trophy, named for last year's winner.

The drama: Salim, and the finale nobody could look away from

The score says Blue won 5 & 3. The internet says something else decided it — or at least ruined the watch. Salim Sirur, Red's third man, drank through the episode on camera: a tequila shot on just about every hole, beers on top of it, asking the cart girl for another round. Australian Golf Digest's episode recap named him "the drunkest man alive" and described him as "blackout drunk" going into the final, showing no signs of stopping.

It bled into the team. At one point Salim took a beer out of Big John's hand, causing real friction inside the group, and Ryan Whitney spent part of the match coaching Big John on keeping Salim's vibes up rather than letting it show. Big John, for his part, came out of it as the sympathetic figure of the finale — viewers calling him "all heart" and the MVP of a losing team.

The audience reaction has been brutal. Across Barstool's, Portnoy's and the Invitational's own posts, the comments are dominated by viewers calling the finale unwatchable, blaming Salim's drinking for costing his teammates $1.3 million each, and calling for him not to be invited back. Some of it is cruel; a smaller thread defends him or jokes about it. The dominant tone is anger that a $4 million match came down to a guy who could barely stand up straight.

There is a twist that complicates the whole thing: Salim himself has said he's on Day 87 of a 90-day sober challenge — he knew before the episode aired that he needed a lifestyle change. Golf Digest called the whole thing "an all-time drunk golf performance" while noting he's since reeled the drinking in. Whether the finale becomes a turning point for him or just the episode everyone remembers him for is the open question hanging over next year.

The trophy means something

That name is the emotional center of this whole series. Cody "Beef" Franke won the first Internet Invitational in 2025 alongside Brad Dalke and Francis Ellis, beating Paige Spiranac, Frankie Borrelli and Malosi Togisala 1 up in the final. He died suddenly at 31 in October 2025, the day before the series aired. Barstool and the Fore Play crew helped set up a scholarship fund in his name at his alma mater, Ferris State, and his family opened this year's first episode to introduce the Beef Franke Foundation, which funds golf-management scholarships and a Heart of the Course Award for the people who keep courses running. They finished by teaching the room Beef's signature send-off: two claps and a woo.

So when the trophy got handed over at Payne's Valley, it wasn't just a prop with a funny name. It was the whole point of the week.

How Blue got here

Nobody had this trio winning it when the field of 64 was drafted. All six finalists came out of Ryan Ruffels' Team White, which survived a wild three days at Big Cedar Lodge in Ridgedale, Missouri.

Day 1 at Ozarks National ended with Ruffels and Peter Finch's team tied 8–8, and Ruffels going through on a sudden-death playoff — Big John, nearly left out of the event entirely, holing the putt on the second extra hole. Defending champions Dalke's Red lost 10.5–5.5 to Wesley Bryan's Green and went home. Day 2 at Buffalo Ridge was sixteen singles matches, and Ruffels closed it out 12.5–6.5, with Salim winning the 17th and 18th to clinch it on the last.

Then came the twist: four of Ruffels' sixteen were going home that night. The captains played a sudden-death hole under the lights, and Grant Horvat's team went out when Ryan Whitney's par beat Jake Adams on the next hole — taking Horvat, Adams, Spiranac and Jon Gruden with it. The last twelve were split into four teams of three for nine holes of alternate-shot stroke play at Payne's Valley, top two through. Blue won it at two over. Red got through at four over only because Salim holed a bogey putt on the last that would have tied Green if he'd missed.

On paper, the final was close: Blue's combined handicap averaged 2.1 (Fat Perez 0.3, Riggs 4.1, Bobby Ray 2.0) against Red's 2.9 (Big John +3.1, Whitney 2.1, Salim 9.8). A million simulations gave Blue a 57% edge. On the course, it wasn't close at all.

What this event is

For anyone still catching up: the Internet Invitational is Barstool Sports and Bob Does Sports' creator golf tournament, hosted by Dave Portnoy, who runs the show as host and rules commissioner alongside Big Cat and former PGA Tour pro Kevin Kisner. The second edition filmed August 10–17, 2026 at Big Cedar Lodge and rolled out in six episodes on YouTube — Mondays and Thursdays, October 26 through today — free on the Fore Play Golf, Bob Does Sports and Internet Invitational channels, presented by Dunkin'.

The first two episodes alone drew more than 16 million combined views. It's the rare YouTube golf series that plays like a real sports event: a draft, team play, a rules committee with actual teeth — the "Gruden Rule" lets them veto any pairing that looks like a thrown match — and side pots everywhere, including a $500,000 Reese's hole-in-one prize on the par 3 each day and $25,000-a-man payouts on the Day 2 9th hole. The production team cut it from more than 24 terabytes of raw footage, and the 2025 series was a Shorty Awards finalist for Best Video Series.

It also never stops being messy, which is half the appeal. The Duke, the weakest golfer in the 64-man field, became the story of Episode 5 when his play cost Ruffels and Marissa Wenzler their shot at the final — then took to Instagram to apologize to his teammates. Portnoy spent Wednesday addressing whether The Duke gets invited back at all.

What's next

Portnoy has confirmed the Invitational will be an annual event, and the 2026 edition proved the format has legs: a bigger field, a purse four times the size of year one, and a final that delivered a clean, decisive winner. The champions list now reads two lines long — Dalke, Ellis and Beef in 2025; Fat Perez, Riggs and Bobby Ray in 2026. Three guys who started the week as long shots walk away as millionaires, and the trophy they lifted carries the name of the guy who won it first.

Streamer Awards go live tonight in Los Angeles

By Matt

Streaming's biggest night is tonight — the sixth annual Streamer Awards, live free on Twitch and YouTube, with IShowSpeed, Jynxzi, and Kai Cenat leading the nominations and one very stolen set of trophies hanging over the show.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Streaming's biggest night

The Streamer Awards go live tonight from Los Angeles, with the main show at 8:30 p.m. ET streaming free on Twitch and YouTube. The red carpet starts at 5:30 p.m. ET, and the whole night is hosted by the show's founder, QTCinderella, alongside Caroline Kwan.

This is the sixth edition of the show, and the largest one yet: 37 categories covering creators across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick. Fan voting counted for 70% of each result, with an industry panel deciding the remaining 30%. Voting ran October 16 through October 31, so tonight is purely about the reveals.

The names to watch

IShowSpeed, Jynxzi, and Kai Cenat lead the field with four nominations each. Speed is the defending Streamer of the Year, and he is on the ballot again — joined by CaseOh, Joe Bartolozzi, Jynxzi, and Stable Ronaldo in the flagship category, presented by YouTube this year.

Kai Cenat's four nominations all sit outside that flagship race: the two-time past winner is not on the Streamer of the Year ballot at all, which was one of the biggest talking points when the nominees were revealed on October 16. The other one was xQc, who got zero nominations across all 37 categories and spent the night voting for Speed instead.

Beyond the top prize, the marquee races include Best Marathon Stream — Speed and Kai's Minecraft Marathon against Cinna's Cinnathon, DDG's Hit-A-Thon, JasonTheWeen's 7 Days Stranded, and the Chained Together run from Jynxzi, Stable Ronaldo, and LosPollosTV — plus Streamer University, Kai's summer event, up for Best Streamed Event.

The trophies were stolen

Yes, really. On October 29, QTCinderella announced on X that this year's trophies had been stolen off one of the show's producers' front porches after delivery, and asked anyone in the Los Angeles area who spots them at a Goodwill or pawn shop to let her know. The good news for the results: winners' nameplates aren't attached until the night before the ceremony, so nothing was spoiled — the thief got a box of very blank trophies. QT joked the winners' plates might end up on coffee mugs instead.

The show itself was also moved up a week, from November 17 to tonight, to get clear of the GTA VI release. And for the first time, Kick streamers were eligible for nominations this year.

How to watch

The red carpet starts at 5:30 p.m. ET and the main ceremony follows at 8:30 p.m. ET, streaming free on QTCinderella's Twitch and YouTube channels. Co-streaming is open to everyone — QT confirmed on November 11 that all co-streams are welcome, on any platform, as long as "Streamer Awards" is in the title.

Red Sox inquire about Seiya Suzuki

By Matt

Boston has checked in on free agent Seiya Suzuki, per Pete Abraham — the Cubs slugger is coming off the best season of his career and would add the power bat the Sox lineup lacked.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The first bat checked

The Red Sox have checked in on free agent Seiya Suzuki, according to Pete Abraham of the Boston Globe. Free agency opened on November 2, and Suzuki is the first premier bat Boston has reportedly asked about.

The inquiry came out of the GM Meetings in Las Vegas, where Abraham also reported the worst-kept secret in the room: Boston is shopping left fielder Jarren Duran. The two moves fit together — if Duran goes, there's an outfield spot and a middle-of-the-order hole to fill, and Suzuki is the top right-handed bat on the market.

What Suzuki did in 2026

Suzuki, 32, just finished the best season of his five-year run with the Cubs. He set a career high with 5.1 wins above replacement while playing 143 games, and he did it as the middle-of-the-order bat Chicago leaned on all year.

Games: 143

Slash line: .270/.368/.473

Home runs: 26

Doubles: 31

RBIs: 86

OPS: .841

That production is exactly what Boston's lineup was missing. The Sox finished 12th in the American League in home runs last season, and the front office has made adding a middle-of-the-lineup hitter its offseason priority. This isn't the first time the two sides have been linked, either — The Athletic's Jen McCaffrey named Suzuki as a possible Boston target last week.

What it would cost

Suzuki just completed a five-year, $85 million deal he signed with the Cubs ahead of the 2022 season. Chicago extended him a one-year, $23.1 million qualifying offer, but his agent, Joel Wolfe, said at the GM Meetings that Suzuki will decline it and test the open market.

The early projections put the price in nine figures: Spotrac projects a four-year deal worth just over $109 million, while The Athletic's Jim Bowden projects five years and $120 million. Boston won't be bidding alone — the Mariners, Padres, Phillies and Blue Jays are all reported to have interest, and the Cubs are expected to make an effort to keep him.

There's also a draft-pick cost attached. Because Suzuki received a qualifying offer, signing him would cost Boston a second- and fifth-round pick in the 2027 MLB Draft plus $1 million in international signing bonus pool space.

Collectibles · Nov 12, 2026 · 7:55 AM ET

Pokémon's Day & Night boxes are trading at double retail a week after launch — and the market is already cooling

By Matt

The Pokémon TCG 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collections — Day with Espeon ex, Night with Umbreon ex — launched November 6 at $179.99. Pre-release market prices ran past three times retail, and even after a pullback they are still trading well above it.

The boxes

The peak product of Pokémon's 30th anniversary year landed on November 6: the 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collections, in two versions — Day, built around Espeon ex, and Night, built around Umbreon ex. Each one retails for $179.99 at the Pokémon Center and participating retailers.

What is inside justifies the price tag, at least on paper. Every box carries 30 packs — 29 from the 30th Celebration set plus one Classic Collection pack with three etched cards from the anniversary subset, including the Base Set Charizard reprint. Then the promos: a foil Pikachu ex illustrated by YOSHIROTTEN in a day or night version, and a foil Espeon ex or Umbreon ex depending on the box. A playmat, deck box, 65 sleeves, a metal coin and six damage-counter dice round it out.

The two versions are identical except for the theme — the featured Eeveelution, the Pikachu art, and the accessories. Espeon and Umbreon are the Gen II Eeveelutions, the pair that has anchored Pokémon collecting since Gold and Silver, and the 30th anniversary is the first time they have headlined a premium box together.

The market

The resale market did what it always does with a premium Eeveelution product: it went vertical, then started coming back down.

TCGplayer's pre-release market figures put both versions at more than three times retail — roughly 3.1 times for Day and 3.3 times for Night. At launch, market tracking had both boxes above $420. But the peak is already behind us: in the week before launch, Night fell 25% and Day fell 22.6% from their highs, as supply actually reached shelves.

Good luck choosing, though. Best Buy listed the collections with a one-per-order restriction and assigns buyers a random Day or Night version rather than letting them pick. In France, only Night released on November 6 — Day is expected November 27.

Why it matters

The 30th Celebration set itself launched September 16 — all-foil cards, 30 unique Pikachu cards with one guaranteed in every booster, a new Futuristic Rare rarity. The Day & Night boxes are the anniversary's premium capstone, and the Classic Collection pack inside is the only place to pull those gold-bordered reprints of three decades of icons.

The market cooling off a pre-release spike is normal. The question is where the floor is: at $179.99 retail with 30 packs and two exclusive promos, the box is fairly priced even before resale. If you can find one at retail, that is the buy. If you are paying $420, you are paying for the Eeveelutions, not the cardboard.

Sports · Nov 12, 2026 · 7:54 AM ET

The Warriors' win streak is over — and Curry left after six minutes

By Matt

Houston beat Golden State 115-108 on Wednesday, ending the Warriors' eight-game win streak. Stephen Curry played six minutes before leaving with right abdominal soreness, and the MRI results weren't known after the game.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Houston Rockets beat the Golden State Warriors 115-108 on Wednesday night in Houston, and the final score only tells half of it. The Warriors' eight-game winning streak — the run that started after an 0-3 opening and made them the first team ever to open a season with three losses and then win eight in a row — is over.

The bigger worry left the floor in the first quarter. Stephen Curry played six minutes before departing with right abdominal soreness. He underwent an MRI after the game, and the results weren't immediately known, coach Steve Kerr said postgame. Golden State played most of the night without the player carrying the streak — Curry was averaging 30.6 points a game, 32.3 over his last five.

Houston did not need a masterpiece to close it out. Alperen Sengun flirted with a triple-double — 19 points, 13 rebounds, nine assists — Kevin Durant led the Rockets with 20, and Amen Thompson added 19 points and seven rebounds. The Rockets pulled away in the fourth quarter for their second straight win, improving to 9-3. Golden State falls to 8-4.

Why it matters

Streaks end. That is the boring part. The interesting part is how this one ended — not with a cold shooting night or a buzzer-beater, but with the best player on the floor walking to the locker room six minutes in and the team holding on for three quarters before Houston's depth took over.

The Warriors have been shorthanded all through the run — Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody and Gary Payton II are all out — and they kept winning anyway. But there is shorthanded and then there is no Curry at all, and Wednesday was the second one. Until the MRI results come back, the streak is the smaller story. The abdominal is the story.

Around the league

Boston pulled off its own 22-point comeback on the same night, beating Toronto 98-93 behind Jayson Tatum's 24 — the Celtics' fifth straight win. James Harden scored a season-high 32 as Cleveland won 115-107 at the Garden.

Sports · Nov 12, 2026 · 7:54 AM ET

Spurs win their 10th straight after erasing a 22-point hole in Chicago

By Matt

Victor Wembanyama scored 32 and Dylan Harper added 18 points, 10 assists and four steals as the Spurs came back from 22 down to beat the Bulls 124-119 — their 10th straight win after an 0-2 start.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The San Antonio Spurs trailed by 22 points midway through the second quarter in Chicago on Wednesday night. The Bulls were 10-for-12 from three, the United Center was loud, and the Spurs looked like a team about to take its first loss in two weeks.

Then they did what they have done all month: they won anyway.

Victor Wembanyama scored 32 points and Dylan Harper — 18 points, 10 assists, four steals — ran the comeback as San Antonio beat the Bulls 124-119, closing out a 4-0 road trip. It was the second night in a row the Spurs had to dig out of a hole, and the second night in a row Wembanyama delivered: he dropped 40 with nine blocks in 25 minutes against Phoenix two days earlier.

The Bulls led 64-42 before the Spurs started chipping away, and Chicago's collapse is its own story. The Bulls have now lost eight straight to fall to 1-9, winless in four home games. Their biggest lead of the season lasted about a quarter.

The history

The record book cares about how the run started, not just how long it has gone. San Antonio opened the season 0-2. Since then, ten wins in a row — and that makes the Spurs just the second team in NBA history to start 0-2 and then win ten straight. The only other club to do it: the 2017-18 Boston Celtics, who turned an 0-2 start into a 16-2 stretch.

That is a very different kind of streak than an undefeated start. Nobody remembers the two losses in October because the response has been perfect since. Ten in a row, and the last one came from 22 down on the road.

What's next

The test gets harder immediately. Golden State comes to San Antonio on Friday night — the same Warriors team that just saw its own eight-game win streak snapped in Houston, and the same team the Spurs beat to start this run's momentum. A win there makes it eleven, and the conversation changes from "nice streak" to "how far can this go?"

Burger King is selling a Magic: The Gathering deck box with your Whopper — Italy only

By Matt

Burger King Italy has launched 'The Great Gathering' — a €19.90 bundle that comes with a rigid burger-styled Magic deck box and 100 sleeves. No promo cards, but nine restaurants are running Pauper tournaments with a final at Milan Games Week.

The bundle

Magic: The Gathering has done a lot of crossovers. A fast-food one was not on the list until this week.

Burger King Italy has launched "Burger King Quest: The Great Gathering," a bundle that runs from November 10 through November 30 at participating Italian locations. The price is €19.90 — about $22 — and it gets you a choice of sandwich, fries and a drink, plus the thing everyone is actually here for: a rigid Burger King x Magic deck box, styled to look like a burger, and a pack of 100 card sleeves.

The sandwich is your choice of the Chicken Krispper, the Double Cheese King, or a plant-based Whopper. The box itself is the prize — an orange, sesame-seed-dotted deck box with the Burger King logo on one side and the Magic logo on the other — and Polygon reports it is already being resold online, with scalpers flipping the box before the promotion is even halfway through.

There are no promo cards in the bundle. The accessories are the product.

The tournaments

This is not just a meal with a toy in it. Nine Burger King restaurants across Italy are hosting Pauper tournaments as part of the promotion — competitive Magic in the cheap, commons-only format — with qualifiers running through the month and a final at Milan Games Week & Cartoomics, November 27–29.

It is a real competitive structure wrapped around a fast-food promotion, which is exactly why it is working. The Pauper community gets a tournament circuit with a national final; Burger King gets a month of people coming through the door for something they cannot get at a card shop.

Why it matters

Wizards of the Coast has never done a fast-food partnership like this. The closest comparison is Pokémon's Happy Meal runs, and those move staggering numbers — the recent U.S. Pokémon Happy Meal launch had McDonald's locations selling out within days. Burger King is betting the same energy works for an older, tournament-playing audience, and the resale market says they were right to try.

The math is worth noting, too. A regular Burger King meal in Italy runs around €11.50. The bundle at €19.90 means the deck box and sleeves are effectively costing about €8.40 — less than most standalone deck boxes, and this one looks like a burger.

The catch, of course, is that it is Italy only. No U.S. dates, no wider European rollout announced. If you want one, you either know someone in Milan or you pay the reseller price — which, given how this promotion is going, is not going down.

Gaming · Nov 11, 2026 · 7:56 AM ET

Ubisoft makes it official: the Tubarão-Noor combo is banned for the rest of the Osaka Major

By Matt

Ubisoft has ruled on the Rainbow Six Siege combo that dominated the BLAST R6 Major Osaka's opening days: the Tubarão-Noor gadget interaction is banned until the end of the event, and any team that uses it loses the round.

The ruling

The BLAST R6 Major Osaka had a problem before it really got started, and on Wednesday Ubisoft finally put it in writing.

The interaction between Tubarão's Zoto Canister and Noor's Horus Lance is banned from now until the end of the event. Any team confirmed using it loses the round. The ruling is not retroactive — results from the opening days stand — and neither operator is banned. Tubarão and Noor are still playable; their gadgets just cannot be used together anymore.

The ruling comes under section 4.6 of the Osaka Major rulebook, and it closes a saga that began the moment the tournament opened.

How it worked

Here is the combo: Tubarão's Zoto Canister freezes both a Horus Lance and a hard breach gadget. When the freeze ends, the Lance disables the gadget it was touching. The result is a hard-breach denial that is, on paper, perfectly legal — and brutally effective.

The players knew what it was the second they saw it. On the tournament's opening day, teams raised it with BLAST, and BLAST confirmed with Ubisoft that the interaction was intentional — not a bug. That is where the trouble started. If Ubisoft knew the interaction existed, the players wanted to know why nobody said anything before the Major began. The patch notes said nothing. The teams found out on stage.

The gentlemen's agreement

Four days ago, the players took it into their own hands. All twenty teams at the Major agreed — a voluntary gentlemen's agreement, announced publicly by Team Liquid in-game leader Felipe "FelipoX" Lucia on November 7 — not to use the interaction at all. It was, by most accounts, the first agreement of its kind in Rainbow Six Siege esports in years.

Now the agreement is a rule. Ubisoft's official ruling, published Wednesday, matches the players' position almost exactly: banned from November 11 until the end of the event, round loss for confirmed use, operators still playable separately.

It is a strange way for a major to be decided — the players agreed on the competitive integrity of the tournament before the publisher did — but the important part is that the question is settled before the weekend. The grand final is this weekend, and the Season 4 update gets its reveal there too. The players can finally go back to playing the game instead of arguing about it.

Entertainment · Nov 11, 2026 · 7:56 AM ET

Kai Cenat says he's 'genuinely terrified of human beings' as the Clover Boys fallout spills over

By Matt

Dezz says Kai Cenat cut off the Clover Boys. Kai answered on his GTA marathon stream — then admitted on camera that he's 'so scared to meet new people.' Here's what we actually know.

What happened

The Clover Boys are the group Kai Cenat built — Dezz, Tylil, Punga, RaKai, Ray and Reggie, a streaming circle that goes back to college. This week, one of its founders said it was falling apart in public.

Dezz hosted a TikTok livestream on November 9 and accused Kai of cutting off communication with him and the other Clover Boys streamers. His line, as it made the rounds: Kai "don't speak to none of us gang." He also said Kaiya Cenat — Kai's sister — had stopped talking to him as well.

Kai addressed it the same day, during his GTA marathon stream. He was not having it. He told his chat he was "tired of the bull**" and that people should "leave him alone" — the kind of answer that says more by what it does not say than by what it does.

Then, on November 10, a different clip started circulating — shared by X user @scubaryan_ — where Kai talked about why he pulls back from people at all. "I'm genuinely terrified of human beings," he said. "I'm so scared to meet new people." It was not a response to Dezz, exactly. It was the context underneath the whole thing.

Why this one stings

Kai and Dezz go back further than most people in this scene. They met in college, and Dezz helped produce Kai's early videos — he was there before the fame, before the numbers, before the marathon streams. The Clover Boys were supposed to be the answer to the lonely-at-the-top problem: a group that grew together instead of one star outgrowing everyone around him.

But the fractures have been visible for a while. Reggie distanced himself from the group in September, and Kai said in October that he has invested $3.7 million into the Clover Boys. When the money and the distance both get that big, a group of friends starts to look like a business — and businesses have arguments that friendships do not survive.

What we don't know

The important part: neither Kai nor Kaiya has confirmed Dezz's account of being cut off, and the full picture is murkier than one livestream makes it sound. Kai streamed with Ray in Japan recently, which cuts against the idea that he has shut everyone out. The "cut off everyone" claim, in other words, is one person's telling of it — and Kai's own words on stream read less like a denial of the distance and more like an explanation of why it exists.

This is not a story with a villain. It is a story about a streamer who got famous faster than anyone in his circle expected, and a group that is finding out what that does to a friendship.

ARC Raiders passes 17 million copies sold

By Matt

ARC Raiders has sold more than 17 million copies, Nexon said in its third-quarter earnings release — up from 16.3 million at the end of June, with the October Frozen Trail update pulling lapsed players back a full year after launch.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

ARC Raiders has sold more than 17 million copies. Nexon put the total in its third-quarter earnings release on November 10, 2026, and credited the October Frozen Trail update for pulling lapsed players back a full year after launch.

The numbers

Copies sold to date: More than 17 million

Copies sold at the end of June 2026: 16.3 million

Copies sold by May 2026: 16 million

Matches played in year one: Six billion

Average raids per day in year one: 16 million

Frozen Trail did the work

Nexon's earnings letter calls Frozen Trail, released by Embark Studios on October 8, "the largest update since the 2025 launch" — and says it was "successful in re-engaging lapsed players and driving incremental unit sales." That is the story behind the new total: the game did not just hold its audience, it won back players who had drifted away and sold new copies to players coming in fresh.

The pace tells the rest of it. The gap between the May figure and this one is roughly a million copies over about six months, after the launch rush did the heavy lifting in the first seven. Nexon also said third-quarter revenue from the game came in within its outlook, and that it expects fourth-quarter revenue to stay broadly flat against the third quarter while falling year over year — an honest comparison, since the same quarter last year was launch season.

What a year looks like

The game launched October 30, 2025, on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. By its first anniversary it had six billion matches played — an average of 16 million raids a day — and Nexon said in August it had generated more than 88 billion yen since launch. It is a buy-to-play game, so every active player is a paying player, which makes the retention story matter more than it would for a free-to-play title: nobody is padding the numbers with free downloads.

A year after launch, the question for an extraction shooter is never whether the launch was big. It is whether anyone is still raiding. Frozen Trail answered that, and the sales total is the receipt.

Magic's Star Trek set beams onto Arena today — tabletop lands Friday

By Matt

Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek hits MTG Arena today, with the tabletop release following Friday. Four Commander decks, signed Headliner cards from seven Star Trek actors, and a full event schedule are live.

What happened

Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek arrives on MTG Arena today, Tuesday, November 10. The tabletop release follows on Friday, November 13, with prerelease events running November 6–12. It's the 60th anniversary of Star Trek, and Wizards of the Coast is marking it with a full Universes Beyond set — Standard-legal, with new mechanics and a Commander lineup built around the franchise's biggest names.

The Arena schedule is live now: Premier Draft runs November 10 through February 2, Sealed runs November 10 through December 8, and Arena Direct Sealed runs November 13–22, where seven wins earns a Collector Booster box. There's also a Draft Night four-player Pick-Two kit for the tabletop side.

What's in it

Four Commander decks anchor the set: Federation Fleet, led by Jean-Luc Picard; Landing Party, led by Spock; Klingon Fury, led by Worf; and We Are the Borg, led by the Borg Queen. New mechanics include Assimilate, Face a Dilemma and Federation, and Scene cards recreate iconic moments across the franchise.

The chase cards are the Headliners: signed cards from seven Star Trek actors, roughly 250 copies of each, available only in Collector Boosters. One note for the tabletop release — Commander decks are delayed in North America and may arrive after November 13, so check with your local shop before Friday.

Magic's Star Trek Secret Lair superdrop beams in today — five drops, $29.99 each, and a sixth still to come

By Matt

Secret Lair x Star Trek: Set Phasers to Superdrop goes on sale today at noon ET on MagicSecretLair.com — five drops at $29.99 non-foil or $39.99 foil, from full-art lands to a full Klingon-language set, with a sixth drop still unrevealed and the main set landing Friday.

What happened

The transporters are warmed up. Secret Lair x Star Trek: Set Phasers to Superdrop goes on sale today, Monday, November 9, at 9 a.m. PT / noon ET on MagicSecretLair.com, with a pre-queue opening an hour earlier. Wizards of the Coast revealed five of the six drops on October 27. The sixth is still to be revealed.

Each drop costs $29.99 in non-foil or $39.99 in foil, while supplies last. All five revealed drops run $149.95 non-foil or $199.95 foil before tax and shipping, and spending $199.99 earns a foil copy of Return of the Wildspeaker, reskinned as "Transporter Boondoggle." Orders over $99 ship free.

The five drops

New Worlds — full-art basic lands from new worlds, the kind of drop that ends up in decks for years after the set itself is forgotten.

Beam Me Up — the transporter drop, and the cleverest of the five: four reversible cards. Eerie Interlude becomes Beam Us Up, Momentary Blink, Essence Flux becomes Materialize, and Conjurer's Closet becomes The Transporter. Every card in the drop is reversible.

tlhIngan maH — a full Klingon-language set, with Klingon-script cards developed with help from Marc Okrand, the linguist who created the language for the films. This is the one collectors will be talking about longest.

KHAAAAAAAAN — the Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan drop, which Wizards itself notes knows exactly how many A's belong in the title.

Lower Decks — the chaos of Star Trek: Lower Decks, for the people who want their Magic cards to be funny.

Why the timing matters

The superdrop lands four days before the main event: Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek hits tabletop on Friday, November 13, with prereleases running November 6–12 and the MTG Arena release on November 10. All four Commander decks have been revealed, each a ready-to-play 100-card deck with 32 new-to-Magic cards. The set is the next Universes Beyond release, and Wizards is treating it like one — a Secret Lair superdrop, a full Commander lineup, and a set code (TRK) collectors already know by heart.

The business behind it is worth a line, too. Hasbro reported that Magic: The Gathering set a quarterly revenue record of $616.1 million in Q3 2026, up 34 percent year over year, with The Hobbit as the fourth-best-selling set in Magic history and the highest prerelease participation ever for a Universes Beyond set. Star Trek is walking into the biggest moment the game has ever had.

What to watch

Secret Lair sales are queue-based and while-supplies-last, and the pre-queue opens at 8 a.m. PT — an hour before the sale. Adding a drop to your basket does not reserve it, so the drops that sell out will sell out fast, and the Klingon set is the obvious candidate. The unrevealed sixth drop is the other thing to watch: Wizards has not said what it is or when it appears, and a surprise sixth drop in a superdrop like this has a way of becoming the chase card of the whole release.

Set phasers, indeed.

The details

Sale opens: Today, Nov 9 — 9 a.m. PT / noon ET

Pre-queue: 8 a.m. PT / 11 a.m. ET

Where: MagicSecretLair.com

Price: $29.99 non-foil / $39.99 foil per drop

Bonus: Foil "Transporter Boondoggle" per $199.99 spent

Main set: Nov 13 (tabletop), Nov 10 (Arena)

Pokémon printed 10 billion cards a year — and still sold out

By Matt

The Pokémon Company printed roughly 10 billion cards in the fiscal year ending March 2026 — past 85 billion lifetime — and it still wasn't enough. Output has been flat for three years because the printers are already at maximum capacity, and the next big plant doesn't open until 2028.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

The Pokémon Company printed roughly 10 billion Pokémon TCG cards in the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026. The lifetime total is now past 85 billion cards since the game launched in 1996. The cards are printed in 16 languages and sold in more than 90 countries.

And it still was not enough. Shops are still selling out on day one.

That is the number at the center of the story: 10 billion sounds like a flood, but it is a ceiling. Output has been flat at around 10 billion a year for three years — the high-water mark was about 11.9 billion in fiscal 2023/24 — because the company has been printing at maximum capacity since January 2025. There is no more room on the presses. The only way to make more cards is to build more presses, and that takes years.

The sellout problem

The demand side is not a mystery. A London shop's allocation rose 40% and still sold out on day one, according to a Brit Brief report from a London Comic Con panel on November 6. That is the pattern everywhere: allocations go up, demand goes up faster, and the shelves are empty by the afternoon.

The timing makes it worse. Mega Evolution – Delta Reign and the 30th Celebration set launched on November 6, right into the holiday season, when demand is at its peak. New sets used to be a restock event. Now they are a race, and the race is over before most people get to the store.

The fix is coming — slowly

The Pokémon Company is building a new printing campus: 1.27 million square feet, due for completion in 2027, with full operation expected in late 2028. When it is running, it would roughly double the company's printing capacity.

That is a real fix, and it is also two years away. Between now and then, the math does not change: 10 billion cards a year, flat, against demand that keeps growing. The company is not holding back supply to create hype — it is printing as fast as it physically can, and it is still not enough.

What it means

For collectors, the takeaway is simple: the scarcity is structural, not artificial. The cards are not hard to find because the company is being cute with supply. They are hard to find because the printers are maxed out and the next plant is two years from full operation. That means day-one sellouts are the normal state of things until 2028, and the secondary market is where the action is — for better and for worse.

Ten billion cards a year. Eighty-five billion lifetime. And still sold out. That is the Pokémon economy right now.

Oregon scores 38 straight to stun Ohio State 41-28

By Matt

No. 23 Oregon trailed No. 12 Ohio State 14-0 in Columbus, then scored 38 unanswered points — sparked by a fake punt, a freshman interception, and a quarterback who wasn't supposed to be the starter — to win 41-28 and climb back into the Big Ten title race.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

No. 23 Oregon beat No. 12 Ohio State 41-28 on Saturday at Ohio Stadium, and the score does not tell you how absurd this game was.

The Ducks fell behind 14-0 in the first quarter. Ohio State's offense was rolling, the Horseshoe was loud, and Oregon looked like a team that was about to get run out of Columbus. Then the Ducks scored 38 consecutive points — four touchdowns on five drives, a fake punt, an interception, and a direct-snap touchdown as time expired in the first half — and by the time Ohio State scored again, more than two hours of game time had passed.

Quarterback Dylan Raiola finished 25 of 40 for 257 yards and two touchdowns, no interceptions. Dierre Hill Jr. ran 13 times for 75 yards and two touchdowns, including a 48-yard score to open the second half — the biggest run of Oregon's season. Dakorien Moore caught seven passes for 56 yards and a one-handed touchdown grab in the corner of the end zone. Brandon Smith added a 15-yard touchdown catch that made it 38-14.

The turning points

It is hard to say exactly when the game turned. Take your pick.

The fake punt: down 14-0, Oregon ran a fake on which Teitum Tuioti completed a pass to Matayo Uiagalelei for 30 yards. The drive ended in points, and the Ducks never looked back.

The interception: freshman safety Devin Jackson picked off Ohio State just before halftime, and Oregon turned it into a direct-snap touchdown from Jamari Johnson as time expired in the first half. The Ducks took the lead into the locker room.

The second half: Hill's 48-yard touchdown on the opening drive of the third quarter, then Moore's one-handed grab, then Smith's score. Ohio State's offense, meanwhile, managed 39 total yards in the second and third quarters — under 1.5 yards per play. The Buckeyes did not score for over two hours.

It was the first time Ohio State had allowed 38 consecutive points since 1999 against Wisconsin. The Buckeyes lost two straight games for the first time since 2011, and lost a third game in a regular season for the first time in 15 years.

The quarterback who wasn't supposed to be here

Raiola was not Oregon's quarterback to start the season. Dante Moore was. But Moore suffered a season-ending concussion in a 41-27 win over USC, Raiola struggled the following week in a loss to UCLA and was benched in the fourth quarter, and then — against Nebraska, the team Raiola had previously played for — he entered as the backup to Brock Thomas and rallied the Ducks to victory.

He has been Oregon's quarterback since. And on Saturday, in the biggest game of his season, he was the best player on the field.

"We were just confident in our plan," Raiola said. "We saw seams everywhere in their defense when we were game planning for them, and a couple of those first couple drives were self-inflicted wounds."

Head coach Dan Lanning, whose team is now 2-1 against the Buckeyes, put it more simply: "We're like cockroaches, man. We won't die."

Ohio State's side

Freshman Luke Fahey made his second career start for the injured Julian Sayin and threw for 360 yards and two touchdowns on 36-of-50 passing, with one interception. Jeremiah Smith caught a 13-yard touchdown pass. But the Buckeyes' offense vanished for two quarters, their defense gave up 395 yards to a Ducks attack led by a quarterback they could not contain, and the loss likely knocks Ohio State out of the College Football Playoff — and probably cost Smith the Heisman.

What it means

Oregon (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten) is back in the thick of the Big Ten title race and the playoff picture, with a second consecutive win in the Horseshoe — long considered one of college football's most intimidating stadiums. Ohio State (6-3, 4-2) is reeling, with two straight losses and a season that has slipped away in the span of a week.

The Ducks outgained the Buckeyes on the ground 108-53, won the turnover battle without giving the ball away once, and turned a 14-0 deficit into a 41-28 win that nobody saw coming — except, apparently, the quarterback who saw the seams all week.

The box score

Final score: Oregon 41, Ohio State 28

Raiola: 25-40, 257 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT

Hill: 13 carries, 75 yards, 2 TD

Moore: 7 catches, 56 yards, 1 TD

Fahey: 36-50, 360 yards, 2 TD, 1 INT

Records: Oregon 6-3 (4-2 Big Ten); Ohio State 6-3 (4-2 Big Ten)

Johnny Walker TKOs Waldo Cortes-Acosta in chaotic UFC Vegas 124 main event

By Matt

Johnny Walker was knocked down in the first round and lost the first two rounds on the scorecards — then landed a question-mark kick, a backfist, and a right hook to become the first man ever to knock out Waldo Cortes-Acosta, stopping him in the third round at UFC Vegas 124.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

Johnny Walker just pulled off the kind of comeback that makes heavyweight MMA the most unpredictable division in the sport.

Walker (24-10 MMA, 10-7 UFC) stopped Waldo Cortes-Acosta (17-5 MMA, 10-5 UFC) by TKO at 2:27 of the third round in the main event of UFC Vegas 124 (UFC Fight Night 293) on Saturday night at the Meta APEX in Las Vegas — becoming the first man ever to knock out Cortes-Acosta.

The finish came out of nowhere, which is exactly how Walker fights. After being knocked down in the first round and losing the first two rounds on MMA Junkie's scorecards (10-9, 10-9 Cortes-Acosta), Walker uncorked a question-mark kick, followed it with a backfist, and then landed the right hook that ended the fight. Cortes-Acosta, who had never been stopped by strikes before, went down and the fight was over.

A short-notice main event that delivered

This fight almost didn't happen — at least not like this. Walker took the main event on nine days' notice after the original headliner, Sean Brady vs. Michael Morales, was canceled when Brady suffered an injury. It was Walker's second heavyweight fight, and his second heavyweight win by knockout: he beat Mick Parkin by first-round KO in October.

That is the Johnny Walker experience in a nutshell. He is chaos in human form — a light heavyweight who moved up to heavyweight and has now finished both of his fights there by knockout, in a division where one clean shot ends everything. He was losing this fight. Clearly losing it. And then he wasn't.

Cortes-Acosta's loss is his third straight, after defeats to Alexander Volkov and Curtis Blaydes. The man who had never been knocked out now has that on his record, and the man who did it was supposed to be the short-notice replacement.

The co-main

In the co-main event, Tatiana Suarez beat Virna Jandiroba by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28), a strong performance in a strawweight fight with title implications. Suarez controlled the fight on the scorecards, and the win keeps her firmly in the mix at 115 pounds.

What it means

Walker is now 2-0 at heavyweight with two knockouts, and he did it the hard way — taking a fight on nine days' notice, getting dropped early, and finishing a man who had never been finished by strikes. Heavyweight is a division where momentum is everything, and Walker just grabbed a fistful of it. The question now is who the UFC matches him with next, because a heavyweight who can end a fight from anywhere, at any moment, is appointment viewing — even when he's losing.

The result

Winner: Johnny Walker (24-10 MMA, 10-7 UFC)

Loser: Waldo Cortes-Acosta (17-5 MMA, 10-5 UFC)

Method: TKO (punches), Round 3, 2:27

Event: UFC Vegas 124 (UFC Fight Night 293), Meta APEX, Las Vegas

Co-main: Tatiana Suarez def. Virna Jandiroba by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28)

Notre Dame stuns No. 1 Miami 31-24 behind C.J. Carr's 319 yards

By Matt

C.J. Carr threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns as No. 11 Notre Dame knocked off No. 1 Miami 31-24 in South Bend — the Irish's first win over the nation's top-ranked team in six years, and their first over the Hurricanes in a decade.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

No. 11 Notre Dame beat No. 1 Miami 31-24 on Saturday night at Notre Dame Stadium, and it was not a fluke, a gift, or a game the Irish stole. They built a 24-3 lead, survived a furious Miami rally, and made the plays that mattered in the final four minutes to hand the Hurricanes their first loss of the season.

Quarterback C.J. Carr had the best game of his season — 29 of 40 for 319 yards and three touchdowns, no interceptions, spreading the ball to 10 different receivers. It was his first 300-yard game since a 36-7 win over N.C. State on October 11, 2025, and it came against the No. 1 team in the country with Notre Dame's playoff life on the line.

The Irish jumped out fast. Spencer Porath opened the scoring with a 44-yard field goal, and Carr found Jordan Faison for a 27-yard touchdown and Micah Gilbert for an 18-yarder just before halftime to make it 17-3. Gilbert's second touchdown — a 20-yarder to open the third quarter — pushed it to 24-3, and for a while it looked like a rout.

The comeback that almost was

Miami did not go quietly. Darian Mensah, the Heisman Trophy favorite, threw three touchdown passes between the third and fourth quarters — one to tight end Elija Lofton, two to Cooper Barkate — and suddenly the Hurricanes had the ball back down seven with a chance to tie.

The ending was chaos. With 3:36 left, Mensah appeared to hit Lofton for the game-tying touchdown, but officials ruled the tight end did not retain possession after bobbling the ball while landing both feet in the end zone. Notre Dame safety Luke Talich — who had already picked off Mensah for just the second interception of his season — knocked the ball loose on the fourth-down attempt. Miami's last gasp, a hook-and-lateral on the final play, ended in a fumble recovered by Jaiden Ausberry.

Mensah finished 24 of 43 for 276 yards and three touchdowns with the interception, plus 11 carries for 28 yards. He did it without his top target — star wideout Malachi Toney is out for an extended period after ankle surgery — and with Barkate stepping up for 10 catches and 92 yards. Miami's top-ranked offense managed just 74 passing yards and three points in the first half, and the Hurricanes were outgained 251-145 before the break.

Why this one matters

This was a statement game in the most literal sense. On Tuesday, the College Football Playoff committee ranked Notre Dame 11th — seven spots below its No. 4 AP ranking — and made it clear the Irish needed a win like this one to be taken seriously. They got it, and now they head into Week 11 in a near-lock position for the playoff.

The history is just as loud. It is Notre Dame's first victory over Miami in a decade, and the Irish are now 10-1 against the Hurricanes in South Bend and 19-9-1 in the series. It is Marcus Freeman's first victory over the AP's top-ranked team, and the 10th such win in program history (10-17-1 overall). And it came six years to the day after Notre Dame's most recent win over the nation's No. 1 team — the 47-40 double-overtime thriller over Clemson on November 7, 2020.

Gilbert finished with nine catches for 98 yards and two touchdowns. Faison added six catches for 77 yards and a score. Nolan James Jr. ran 16 times for 52 yards and a one-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, set up by Mensah's interception. Miami head coach Mario Cristobal told reporters afterward he was "beyond upset" about the incomplete ruling on Lofton's would-be tying score — which tells you how close this one was.

What it means

Miami (8-1, 6-0 ACC) still has a clear path to the playoff — it was the No. 1 overall seed in last week's CFP rankings, and a season-ending three-game homestand starts next week against Duke. But the Hurricanes' margin for error is gone, and they will be doing it without Toney.

Notre Dame (8-1) is the story. The Irish went from committee afterthought to playoff near-lock in one night, and they did it the way Freeman's teams are supposed to do it: a quarterback playing the game of his life, a defense that bent and then broke Miami's last two drives, and a stadium that got louder as the night went on. Next up: Boston College, back in South Bend, Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET.

C.J. Carr: 29-40, 319 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT

Micah Gilbert: 9 catches, 98 yards, 2 TD

Jordan Faison: 6 catches, 77 yards, 1 TD

Nolan James Jr.: 16 carries, 52 yards, 1 TD

Darian Mensah: 24-43, 276 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT

Cooper Barkate: 10 catches, 92 yards

Final score: Notre Dame 31, Miami 24

Records: Notre Dame 8-1; Miami 8-1 (6-0 ACC)

Pokémon TCG enters the National Toy Hall of Fame

By Matt

Thirty years after it debuted in Japan, the Pokémon Trading Card Game is a Hall of Famer — inducted Thursday alongside bingo, Care Bears, and the playground slide.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

The Pokémon Trading Card Game is officially a member of the National Toy Hall of Fame. The Strong National Museum of Play in Rochester, New York, announced the 2026 class on Thursday, November 5, on the Today show — and Pokémon TCG made the cut in its first year as a finalist.

It joins three other inductees: bingo, Care Bears, and the playground slide. The four winners came out of a field of 12 finalists that also included Bop It!, Mahjong, Monster High dolls, Mouse Trap, Polly Pocket, Sorry!, Tickle Me Elmo, and Yahtzee. All four are now enshrined and on display at The Strong.

Thirty years, 85 billion cards

The timing is the story. The Pokémon TCG debuted in Japan in 1996 — thirty years ago this year — after the Game Boy games turned monster-collecting into a phenomenon. The Hall of Fame, established in 1998, recognizes toys that "have inspired creative play and enjoyed popularity over a sustained period." Few inductees can match this one on the sustained part: the game has never really left the cultural conversation since.

The numbers back it up. As of March 2026, more than 85 billion Pokémon cards have been printed and distributed worldwide. The Strong's own write-up calls the game "renowned for its relative accessibility compared to other collectible card games" — a big reason it spread from schoolyards to a global hobby that now supports grading companies, billion-dollar resale markets, and release-day lines at every major retailer.

"Pokémon TCG's widespread appeal and global presence are undeniable," curator Mirek Stolee said in the announcement.

A very good week to be a Pokémon collector

The induction lands on the same week as the biggest release day of the anniversary year. Mega Evolution—Delta Reign hits shelves today, November 6, alongside the final wave of 30th Celebration collections. It is the kind of week that shows exactly why the Hall of Fame came calling: thirty years in, the game is still setting release-day records instead of coasting on nostalgia.

The other inductees tell their own version of the same story. Bingo descends from an Italian lottery played around 1530 and is now played virtually worldwide. Care Bears, like Pokémon, got a boost from an active fan community that mobilized around the nomination. And the slide — the simplest toy on the list — was honored for its role in child development and a century of playground use.

What to watch

The Strong says the induction will likely lead to new exhibits and events around the Pokémon TCG in the new year. For collectors, the near-term watch is simpler: this is the third piece of institutional recognition the hobby has picked up in a year when the cards themselves keep breaking records. The game is not just popular. It is, officially, historic.

Godzilla is coming to Apex Legends: Storm Point takeover starts November 10

By Matt

Godzilla stomps into Apex Legends on November 10 — a Storm Point Wildcard takeover, a heat-ray Devotion, ten kaiju Legend skins, and a mythic Dorsal Dagger, running through December 1.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Godzilla is coming

Godzilla is stomping into Apex Legends. Respawn announced the Apex Legends | Godzilla Event today, November 5, and it runs November 10 through December 1 — three weeks of the King of the Monsters tearing up Storm Point. The tagline says it all: survive the monster, become a monster.

This is not a skins-only crossover. Godzilla is on the map, and you cannot kill it. You can only survive it.

Storm Point becomes Godzilla's stomping ground

The centerpiece is a Wildcard takeover of Storm Point. The map is mid-attack: damaged buildings, burnt trees, fallen signs, and destruction scattered across the island, with Godzilla looming above it all.

When Godzilla marks an area for destruction, a countdown starts before its Heat Ray strikes. Players brave enough to run into the blast zone before the beam hits can grab a Care Package holding a custom Devotion — a heat-ray weapon that tracks enemies on hit. It is the one piece of Godzilla's power you can actually take for yourself.

There is also a new Kaiju Zone on Storm Point to explore for Kaiju Energy, Kaiju Crates, and kaiju-themed finishers.

The loot: ten kaiju skins and a mythic melee

Ten Legends are getting Godzilla-themed skins drawn from across the franchise, including some deep cuts: Octane, Fuse, Ash, Horizon, Wattson, Ballistic, Valkyrie, Wraith, Loba, and Sparrow. The monsters represented include Godzilla, Mechagodzilla, Mothra, and Destoroyah.

The headline prize is the Dorsal Dagger, a new Universal Mythic Melee inspired by one of Godzilla's dorsal fins, with a matching Deathbox. It is Wraith's first mythic melee and the game's second universal mythic melee. Nine Legendary weapon skins are in the mix too, for the Devotion, Hemlok, Rampage, CAR, Havoc, Longbow, Wingman, Prowler, and Sentinel.

The Godzilla Event Pass runs on challenges: the free track earns rewards like the Jet Jaguar Octane skin and Godzilla Event Packs, while the Premium Track (950 Apex Coins) unlocks the Iconic Ghidorah 1991 Catalyst skin, the Legendary Gravity Beam Prowler skin, Epic Apex Packs, and more. Twitch Drops run November 10–17 with select creators.

Why now

The event is tied to Godzilla's return to theaters — Godzilla Minus Zero hits theaters this week, with a 3D re-release in IMAX and large format on November 6. The timing is no accident: the movie brings the monster back to the big screen, and Apex brings it to the Outlands the same week.

Respawn teased this one first. On November 2, the official Apex account posted a 17-second clip captioned "Something big is coming…" — a glowing Apex logo splitting into a row of shapes that turned out to be Godzilla's dorsal plates, with a roar at the end. Three days later, the full reveal landed.

The details

• Event: Apex Legends | Godzilla Event

• Dates: November 10 – December 1, 2026

• Mode: Wildcard takeover on Storm Point

• Headline weapon: custom Heat Ray Devotion from blast-zone Care Packages

• Skins: 10 kaiju Legend skins, 9 Legendary weapon skins

• Mythic: Dorsal Dagger universal melee + matching Deathbox

• Platforms: PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, PC (Steam, EA App, Epic Games Store)

GameStop's $10,000 Pokémon pack gives you a 44.8% chance of pulling a card worth $6,000–$8,000

By Matt

GameStop's new Riptonium Power Pack costs $10,000 for one PSA-graded Pokémon card — and GameStop's own odds say nearly 75% of pulls come back worth less than the pack. The top chase is a $156,000 Lugia.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

GameStop has gone all in on the digital pack. The retailer announced Riptonium on October 10 — its biggest Power Pack tier yet — and the price is exactly what it sounds like: $10,000 for a single digital pack that reveals one PSA-graded Pokémon card.

The catch is right there on GameStop's own listing. According to the odds GameStop publishes for the pack, 44.8% of pulls land in the $6,000–$8,000 estimated value band. That is at least $2,000 less than the pack costs, before resale fees or the gap between an estimate and what a buyer can actually get for the card.

The odds, straight from GameStop

Here is the full value chart for Riptonium, as reported from GameStop's listing:

$6,000–$8,000: 44.8%

$8,000–$10,000: 29.9%

$10,000–$20,000: 22.9%

$20,000–$40,000: 1.5%

$40,000–$80,000: 0.5%

Above $80,000: 0.4%

Add it up and 74.7% of pulls come back worth less than the $10,000 pack price. Only 2.4% of pulls land above $20,000. The top pull currently listed is valued at $156,000 — a PSA 10 2005 #105 Lugia ex-Holo, per Resell Calendar's report on the pool.

GameStop warns on the listing that values can fluctuate and that the probabilities update every five minutes. The estimates are calculated from market data and feed GameStop's instant buyback offers, which pay 90% of the estimated value. So even a "break-even" pull at $10,000 is worth $9,000 the moment you take the buyback.

How Power Packs work

Riptonium is the top rung of a ladder GameStop has been building all year. Power Packs are digital mystery packs made in partnership with PSA: you buy a pack online, it opens digitally to reveal a real, physical, PSA-graded card, and that card goes into your PSA Vault — a secure, insured storage facility in Delaware — until you decide to ship it, sell it, or keep it stored. Every card was already graded and slabbed before you spent a dollar.

The platform launched to the public on April 15, 2026 with four categories — Pokémon, football, basketball, and baseball — and nine price tiers: Starter ($25), Silver ($50), Gold ($100), Sapphire ($250), Platinum ($500), Diamond ($1,000), Lunar ($2,500), Neutronium ($5,000), and Riptonium ($10,000). Higher tiers buy a deeper card pool and a higher ceiling. The category list has since grown to include One Piece and themed Pokémon packs like Rewind and On Fire.

GameStop added the $5,000 Neutronium tier after announcing its bid for eBay, and Riptonium now pushes the ceiling to $10,000. It is, by a wide margin, the most expensive single digital pack in the hobby.

Why people are buying it anyway

The math says most buyers lose money. The hobby says that was never the point.

Power Packs sell the rip — the moment of the reveal, live on a creator's stream, with a real slab on the line. GameStop publishes live pull data, so collectors can watch in real time what other people are hitting. And for the 0.4%, there is a $156,000 Lugia sitting at the top of the pool.

That is the same logic that has powered the hobby's biggest nights all year, from Logan Paul's $1.2 million vintage rip to the record $16.49 million Pikachu Illustrator sale. The difference is that GameStop has industrialized it: nine tiers, published odds, a vault, and a buyback button. The casino is open, the odds are printed on the door, and the line is still forming.

VeeFriends goes luxury: the Treasure Chest packs gemstone pins and graded coins into 5,555 boxes for Black Friday

By Matt

Gary Vaynerchuk's VeeFriends is going physical in the biggest way yet — a premium Treasure Chest with sapphire gemstone pins, NGC graded coins, and Super Stickers, limited to 5,555 boxes and launching Black Friday.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

VeeFriends is ushering in a new era of premium collecting. The Gary Vaynerchuk-founded brand has unveiled the all-new physical Treasure Chest, a luxury collectible box that launches on Black Friday — and with only 5,555 chests in existence, it is the most exclusive VeeFriends Super Stickers and pin release yet.

Each Treasure Chest holds a randomized assortment of four premium collectibles, built around 21 VeeFriends characters. This is not another sticker drop. This is VeeFriends dressing up for the high-end shelf.

What's inside

Every chest contains four treasures, each featuring one of 21 possible VeeFriends characters:

• Sapphire gemstone pins framed in 18K gold plating

• NGC graded coins crafted in various metals, including pure silver and gold

• Debut Super Stickers in new sapphire colorways

• Classic pins

The scarcity is the point. Every collectible inside the chest — except the coins — is limited to 99 or fewer. The 5,555 chests break down into 555 sealed cases of 10 boxes each, and the sealed-case sale is the only chance to buy a case as a case.

How the sale works

The release rolls out in five waves, and the order matters — holders get first crack, the public gets last:

• Wave 1 — Sealed case sale: Monday, November 24 at 12 p.m. ET through Tuesday, November 25. Exclusive to select Series 1 holders, based on an account snapshot taken Monday, November 24 at 9 a.m. ET. One case per account. Price: $1,999.99 (43% off). Cases ship starting Friday, November 28.

• Wave 2 — Series 1 holder sale: Tuesday, November 25 at 12 p.m. ET through Wednesday, November 26, if inventory remains.

• Wave 3 — Series 2 and Iconics holder sale: Wednesday, November 26 through Friday, November 28 at 12 p.m. ET, if inventory remains. Price: $249.99 (29% off). Boxes ship the week of December 3.

• Wave 4 — Black Friday weekend live breaks: Friday, November 28 through Monday, December 1. VeeFriends goes live to break 55 reserved cases on Whatnot.

• Wave 5 — Public sale via EQL: Week of December 3, if inventory remains.

Series 1 Spectacular holders of the 21 featured characters also get a two-week window to claim one Treasure Chest. Hobby retailers have the box listed for preorder at $399.95, with a 10-box case at $3,989.95.

Why this one matters

VeeFriends started as an NFT project, but its physical collecting arm has been building for years. The Super Stickers line debuted at The National Sports Collectors Convention in July 2023, and the brand has been steadily turning its characters into real, hold-in-your-hand collectibles ever since — including a Spectacular Series boxed sticker set whose public pre-order draw ran November 4–5 at $99 a box, and a Monster Squad collaboration with Crocs for Halloween.

The Treasure Chest is the loudest statement of that direction yet: gemstones, gold plating, graded coins, and a print run smaller than most card-shop allocations. It lands as VeeFriends approaches its five-year anniversary in 2026, and as the brand takes a bigger live role in the hobby — VeeFriends joins Goldin, TikTok, and AFA at the Coins, Cards & CHAOS live shopping event at Valley Forge Casino Resort in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania, on November 14–15.

For collectors, the math is simple. There are 5,555 boxes, a holder-first sale ladder, and a public window that only opens if anything survives. If the Treasure Chest sells the way VeeFriends' last few drops have, the week of December 3 may not come at all.

By Matt

Mega Evolution—Delta Reign launches Friday, November 6 alongside the 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collection, Ditto Premium Collection, and Figure Collection — the biggest single release day of Pokémon's 30th anniversary year.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

Friday, November 6 is the biggest release day of Pokémon's 30th anniversary year. The new Mega Evolution expansion, Delta Reign, launches alongside a trio of 30th Celebration products — and after weeks of shortages and raffles, this is the day collectors have been circling.

Here is everything hitting shelves.

Mega Evolution—Delta Reign

Delta Reign is the new Mega Evolution expansion, headlined by the return of Mega Rayquaza ex. The set brings new Mega Evolution Pokémon ex, more than 35 Pokémon and Trainer cards with special illustrations, and a brand-new mechanic: Legendary Stadiums.

The products out Friday are the Booster Display Box and the Elite Trainer Box. The ETB carries a $49.99 MSRP, though expect to pay more wherever stock is tight — Walmart's raffle this week listed it at $60.00.

The 30th Celebration wave

The anniversary line gets its final batch of products on the same day:

• 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collection (Day and Night) — the Eevee-themed centerpiece of the anniversary line. MSRP is $179.99, but the market has already spoken: Target and Barnes & Noble list it at $249.99, GameStop at $399.99, and Walmart's Wednesday raffle offered it at $224.97.

• 30th Celebration Ditto Premium Collection — MSRP $39.99, listed at $49.97 in Walmart's raffle.

• 30th Celebration Figure Collection — the Mew and Mewtwo figure collections round out the wave.

UK retailers have flagged that the Ultra-Premium and Ditto collections may arrive in waves, with allocation shortages pushing some stock past the November 6 date — so if your shop does not have them Friday, it may not mean you missed out.

How the Walmart raffle went

Walmart ran its weekly Wednesday collectibles raffle on November 4, and this one was loaded: six Pokémon products, five of them pre-orders for Friday's releases, including the Ultra-Premium Collection, the Ditto Premium Collection, the Delta Reign ETB, a Delta Reign 3-pack blister at $15.97, and a Prismatic Evolutions Elite Trainer Box at $69.00 against a $49.99 MSRP.

Entry opened at 2:00 p.m. PST and lasted exactly one hour, with winners drawn at random. It cost nothing to enter — and with the UPC going for more than double its MSRP at some retailers, it was the cheapest shot anyone got at one this week.

What to watch

Delta Reign is the set, but the Ultra-Premium Collection is the story. It is the most hyped product of the entire 30th Anniversary lineup, it has not had a clean retail release yet, and Friday is the first real test of whether supply can meet demand. If the UPC sells through at the big retailers on day one, the secondary market does what it always does — and the $179.99 MSRP becomes a memory.

Get to your shop early on Friday. This is the one to be in line for.

Call of Duty: Warzone ends on PS4 and Xbox One on November 6

By Matt

When Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 starts on Friday, Warzone stops working on PlayStation 4 and Xbox One — ending the battle royale's run on the consoles it launched on.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

Call of Duty: Warzone is ending support on PlayStation 4 and Xbox One on Friday, November 6, when Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 begins. From that point on, the battle royale will no longer be playable on either last-gen console.

It is the end of an era in the most literal sense. Warzone launched on PS4 and Xbox One in March 2020, and for more than six years those consoles have been its home base. Season 1 moves the game exclusively to current-generation hardware — PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC — and November 6 also marks the first time Warzone is available on a Nintendo console.

What Season 1 brings

The new season is not just a platform cull. It adds 33 new weapons from Modern Warfare 4 and introduces a new battle royale map, Hajin, as the game enters its next chapter.

For players still on last-gen hardware, though, the headline is simple: one more day. Warzone remains playable on PS4 and Xbox One through Thursday, November 5. After the Season 1 update lands, that is it.

The last-gen farewell tour

Sony gave the PlayStation 4 one last nod this week, releasing system firmware 14.02 on November 4 — a security-only patch, with no new features. It is the kind of quiet maintenance update a console gets when the industry has already moved on.

The timing is hard to ignore. GTA VI arrives on PS5 on November 19, and PlayStation has already pushed the PS5 firmware update required to play it. The last generation is not being switched off overnight, but the biggest games are done building for it.

Warzone's departure is the clearest marker yet. When the most-played free-to-play shooter on the planet stops supporting your console, the generation is over in every way that matters.

What to do if you still play on PS4 or Xbox One

If Warzone is your game and you are still on last-gen, Friday is the deadline to make a plan — upgrade to a current-gen console or PC, or find your next game. Your account, progress, and unlocks carry over to current-gen platforms, so nothing you have earned is lost. Only the old hardware is being left behind.

Sports · Nov 3, 2026 · 7:41 PM ET

Rosas Jr. Taps Covington in 43 Seconds in Rome Shocker

By Matt

Raul Rosas Jr. needed just 43 seconds to submit Colby Covington with a rear-naked choke in the Hype Italy main event in Rome.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Raul Rosas Jr. just pulled off one of the wildest results of the year. The UFC bantamweight submitted former interim welterweight champion Colby Covington with a rear-naked choke just 43 seconds into their submission-only grappling main event at Hype Italy in Rome on Tuesday night.

The finish

It was over almost before it started. Rosas pressured Covington immediately, secured an early takedown, and quickly worked his way onto the bigger man's back. Covington couldn't clear the choking arm before Rosas locked up the rear-naked choke and forced the tap 43 seconds into a match scheduled for 10 minutes.

The size gap made it even more stunning. Rosas competes at 135 pounds in the UFC; Covington used to fight at 170. None of it mattered once the action started.

One timing note: Hype's own announcement and the ESPN graphic going around tonight round it to 40 seconds. The 43-second figure comes from MMA Fighting's report of the finish, and it's the number most outlets have settled on.

Three days' notice

Rosas wasn't even supposed to be in this match. Covington was booked to face Dillon Danis in the main event, but Danis withdrew — MMA Mania reports it was an injury — and at Sunday's press conference, the promoter asked if anyone in attendance would step in. Rosas, sitting in the audience, raised his hand.

"I'll do it, f—k it," he said. "Chiwiwis!"

That gave the 22-year-old roughly three days to prepare for a much larger opponent with elite NCAA Division I wrestling credentials. He needed less than a minute to finish the job.

The reaction

The broadcast cut to Conor McGregor at ringside laughing as the tap came, and both men referenced him afterward. McGregor, a teammate of Danis, was a special guest at the show.

Covington owned it. He said he started slowly and had been focused mainly on his wrestling rather than jiu-jitsu — he hadn't trained Brazilian jiu-jitsu in years — but offered no excuses for the loss.

Rosas thanked Covington for accepting the last-minute matchup and reiterated that his primary goal remains becoming the youngest champion in UFC history. He rides a six-fight MMA winning streak into whatever comes next, fresh off his first UFC main-event win over Raoni Barcelos in September.

What's next

Covington isn't slowing down. He wrestles Khamzat Chimaev for the RAF Cruiserweight Crossover Championship in Abu Dhabi on November 14, and his next Hype match is already set against UFC lightweight Ignacio Bahamondes on December 20.

Rosas Jr. Steps In as Danis Pulls Out, Faces Covington Tonight in Rome

By Matt

Dillon Danis is out of tonight's Hype Fighting main event in Rome, and Raul Rosas Jr. volunteered from the press-conference audience to face Colby Covington in a 10-minute, submission-only grappling match.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Dillon Danis is out, and Raul Rosas Jr. is in. Tonight's Hype Fighting main event in Rome has a new headliner after Danis pulled out of his scheduled grappling match with Colby Covington — and his replacement volunteered on the spot, from the audience.

The switch

Hype Fighting CEO Armand Martirosian announced Danis' withdrawal at Sunday's press conference in Rome. No official reason has been given for the pullout. It is Danis' third withdrawal from a signed bout in under a year.

Rosas Jr. was in the room. When Martirosian called for a replacement, the UFC bantamweight walked down from the audience, accepted the match, and faced off with Covington right there at the press conference.

"Unfortunately, Dillon Danis could not come," a Hype Fighting organizer told the room. "If there's someone who wants to wrestle with Colby, we can organize it."

The matchup

Covington vs. Rosas Jr. headlines Hype Fighting's Italy debut at the PalaPellicone in Ostia, Rome, tonight, Tuesday, November 3. It is a 10-minute, submission-only grappling match — no striking, no judges' decision, no points. The only way to win is to force the other man to submit, by choke or joint lock. Takedowns and dominant positions alone will not earn a victory.

The size gap is real. Rosas Jr. normally competes at bantamweight, around 135 pounds, while Covington is a former interim UFC welterweight champion who usually fights around 170. Covington praised Rosas Jr. for taking the match on short notice.

The backstory

Rome was originally booked as a rematch of sorts. Covington defeated Danis by 14-4 technical fall at RAF 7 in Tampa in March, and the Hype booking was pitched as Danis' chance to answer back under a different ruleset. Danis has since lost on the RAF mat to Khamzat Chimaev and Arman Tsarukyan as well.

Rosas Jr. is no stranger to this stage. He previously went the full 10 minutes with former UFC flyweight champion Deiveson Figueiredo at an earlier Hype FC event, a match ruled a draw. He is a top-10 UFC bantamweight contender riding a six-fight winning streak in MMA, fresh off his first UFC main-event win over Raoni Barcelos in September.

How to watch

Hype Fighting Rome streams live and free on DAZN and YouTube, with coverage starting at 1:00 p.m. ET (7:00 p.m. local time in Rome). The main event closes the show, so Covington vs. Rosas Jr. lands later in the evening, depending on how long the preceding bouts run. The rest of the 11-bout card mixes in bare-knuckle boxing and dirty boxing.
